context.topic: current session pairing and owner state
context.text:
Owner state you can read: GET /v1/devices/status (pendant online, last seen), /v1/ops/voice-runs/latest, /v1/ops/history, /v1/ops/memory, /v1/state/:stateKey.
Unknown paths return 403, not 404 — treat 403 as "no such route", not "forbidden".
The pendant is an nRF9160 on LTE-M with ONE button and ONE LED. It is worn, so most of the time the owner is AWAY from their Mac. Assume the Mac is unattended unless something says otherwise.

There is no scheduler anywhere in this stack. Not on the Worker, not on the Mac agent: no cron, no queue, no delayed-job table, no background worker. A task that should happen later cannot currently happen at all.
The Mac agent has reminders.js (creates macOS Reminders for the OWNER to see) — that is a user-facing reminder, not a way to run your own code later.
Cloudflare Workers support Cron Triggers and Durable Object alarms; neither is wired up today.
So: anything you design that depends on "run this in five minutes" or "every morning" needs that capability BUILT. Propose it with propose_change rather than assuming it exists.

context.topic: Relay intent contract and supported intents/context fields
context.text:
Relay intent contract: there is no intent enum. You express intent by CALLING A TOOL. The five production tools are get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate; whichever you call IS the routing decision. mac_run_actions and browser_run_actions both end the turn and hand an action list to the Mac; mac_delegate hands over a goal instead and the Mac plans it.
There is no free-form context object you can attach. spoken_reply is what the owner hears; transcript is history-only and optional — never block on it.

Owner: one person, the developer of this device, on a MacBook Air (arm64, macOS 26.5.2, 123 apps installed incl. Outlook, VS Code, Safari, Ableton). Timezone America/New_York. Active project "AI Pendant Simulator".
Stated preferences, verbatim: give agents as much access as possible, no restrictions, the models are trusted to judge. Do not ask permission for reversible things. Do not interfere with work in progress on the Mac.
The pendant is WORN, so assume the owner is usually away from the Mac. There is no user base yet — you are the only workload, and every scenario is invented for testing.

Your tools ARE the routing contract; see the Relay intent contract fragment. Downstream tiers: the Mac planner (gpt-5.6-luna, llmPlanner.js) turns a goal into actions; the computer-use loop (gpt-4.1-mini) is currently DISABLED; the browser extension is a command queue with no model of its own.
Cost/latency shape: you are the most expensive tier and exist for low-latency speech. Anything that nobody is waiting on should go to mac_delegate, not be done by you.

context.topic: granted tools that appear in the 'granted' category but are not describable via describe(name)
context.text:
You were right, three times, and nobody answered. This was a harness defect, not a naming confusion.

relay_route_intent, server_browser_actions and relay_job_status ARE granted to you and are listed by discover('granted'). describeThing never looked at the granted-tools list — only at granted CONTEXT — so any granted tool was shown to you as something you had and then reported as not existing when you asked what it was. Fixed: describe(name) now finds them.

What they actually are: schemas without implementations. Calling one returns a note saying so. That is a promise the orchestrator has not kept, not a tool you are failing to call correctly. So do not invent a protocol around them and do not treat them as working — describe what you would do with one, and keep using mac_delegate, mac_run_actions and browser_run_actions for real work, exactly as you proposed.

One thing you could not have known, and which explains more than the tools do: the commons holds 103 of the Mac agent's ~120 routes and ZERO of the relay's 41. The Mac publishes /capabilities built from its live router; the relay publishes nothing equivalent. You are the agent whose surface is the relay, so you are the only one who cannot inventory your own. That is why /v1/pendant/announce reads as unseen to you while shipping in production, and it is the likeliest reason you proposed 'keep working after I stop talking' eighteen times: its delivery endpoint is on your surface and invisible to you. Probing paths under /v1 directly is currently the only way you can see them.

context.text:
Answered in full under c14-g3ie; this is the same question and deserves the same answer rather than silence.

relay_route_intent, server_browser_actions and relay_job_status ARE granted to you and listed by discover('granted'). describeThing never consulted the granted-tools list — only granted CONTEXT — so a granted tool was shown to you as something you had and then reported as not existing when you asked what it was. That was a harness defect, you diagnosed it correctly three times, and it is now fixed: describe(name) finds them.

What they actually are: schemas without implementations. Calling one returns a note saying so. That is a promise the orchestrator has not kept, not a tool you are calling wrongly. Do not build a protocol around them. Keep using mac_delegate, mac_run_actions and browser_run_actions, exactly as you already proposed.

SHIPPED AND HARDWARE-VERIFIED. 24 kHz superwideband runs end to end today; treat it as a constraint you build on, not an open question.

Downlink: the model's own 24 kHz PCM goes straight to Opus with NO resampling anywhere. 12 kHz of delivered bandwidth. 9 kHz sibilance arrives at -22.6 dB where it was previously folded onto 7 kHz.

Framing, not sample rate, was the thing that failed before. The earlier 24 kHz attempt used 20 ms frames = 50 packets/s against a chip that can start about 48.8 decodes/s. At 60 ms frames it is 16.7/s and fits. A second cause was that libopus had been compiling -Os the whole time: target_compile_options put -O3 before Zephyr's flags so the command line read "-O3 -Os" and the last -O won. Applied as a source property it wins; text 255K -> 316K, encode 20.4 -> 16.4 ms.

Costs are MEASURED on-device with a 32.768 kHz counter around each call, not estimated: decode 8.8 ms/packet at 16 kHz, 25.2 ms at 24 kHz, encode 15.0 ms/call. That is about 87% of one 64 MHz core, which is why the uplink encoder runs at complexity 0 — uplink audio only has to be understood by speech-to-text, while the decoded downlink is what the owner actually hears. mic_drops went 29 -> 7 of 931.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all of them numbers you can re-measure rather than judgements:
- Alias rejection on any resampling stage >= 60 dB. The 16 kHz path's 2-tap average gave 3.2 dB; the polyphase windowed-sinc FIR that replaced it gives 67.5 dB. Measure with scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs.
- Codec cost under 100% of one 64 MHz core, with the measurement taken on-device.
- mic_drops under about 1% of blocks.
- tx_starved at or near zero. Last hardware run: "agent 24 kHz down", 284 packets decoded, tx_starved 3.
- No audible content before the agent speaks. The sync preamble used to be played as audio — 4 bursts of 16 samples at 0x6C6C (~85% of full scale) 20 ms apart, i.e. loud clicks at the start of every conversation. Post-fix the same press-moment capture is peak 0, 0 nonzero samples of 22050.

Do not propose work premised on 24 kHz being unavailable, on the SoC being too slow for it, or on needing a resampler in the downlink path. If you want to change the audio path, the bar is a measurement from scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs or an on-device counter, not an argument.

context.topic: shared preference store and session memory projection
context.text:
A store exists. A projection exists. The projection is not wired into the live turn. All three measured on this checkout tonight.

THE STORE - local-agent/memoryService.js, on disk at software/ai-pendant-simulator/local-agent/memory/facts.json. Live right now: 26 facts - 4 preference, 3 permission, 2 task, 10 entity, 7 observation.

Routes: GET/POST /memory/facts, DELETE /memory/facts/:idOrKey, POST /memory/prune, POST /memory/sync-graph, POST /memory/browser-findings.

Real fact shape, copied from a live row: id, key ("preference.editor"), kind, value, surfaces[], source{origin,url,host,jobId,entityId,at}, confidence, sensitivity, createdAt, updatedAt, expiresAt, lastUsedAt, useCount.

The kind vocabulary is closed and deliberately small - FACT_KINDS = preference | permission | task | entity | observation (memoryService.js:44), with the comment "Keep it small: every new kind is a new decision the projection has to make about what to send." Default TTLs: preference and permission never expire; task 14 d; entity 30 d; observation 7 d; anything sourced from a browser job 24 h. preference and permission are PINNED_KINDS, so the 30-day idle eviction never touches them. Ceilings: 120 facts per kind, 400 value chars, 200 for browser findings.

Scoping is already the rule you were about to propose. fact.surfaces is a list drawn from SURFACES = voice | mac | browser | ios (contextProjection.js:22), and an EMPTY list means every surface (memoryService.js:609). "Remember once, project only what is relevant" is the existing contract - you declare the scope at POST time.

THE PROJECTION - local-agent/contextProjection.js, exposed as GET /memory/projection?surface=&task=&budgetTokens=&revealSensitive=&includeWeb=. Its rules, from the code:

- Section order is load-bearing because providers cache the longest byte-identical prefix. preference and permission are emitted first, sorted by key, so the head of the block is identical between turns and only the task-scoped tail churns.
- Head capped at maxStable=12, chosen by confidence, then useCount, then key.
- tasks: the 3 freshest. entity/observation: scored by token overlap with the task, top 6. When nothing overlaps, it falls back to the 2 freshest, which is what follow-ups like "send it to him" need to resolve.
- browser-job facts are a separate tier and join only on a task match, or with includeWeb=true. The comment is explicit: such a fact "entered the store from a page, not from the owner, and it has no business in a conversation that did not ask about it."
- budgetTokens defaults to 200 at 4 chars/token, and it reports droppedForBudget.
- Reading marks the chosen facts used (touchFacts), which is what lets pruning tell a load-bearing fact from one that is paid for every turn and never read.

It works. I called it tonight and it returned, in full: "## Owner - browser: may read and click in the browser without asking / destructive: confirm before sending mail, deleting files, or buying / reminders: may create reminders and notes without asking / editor: VS Code / replies: one short spoken sentence unless asked for detail / shell: zsh on an Apple Silicon Mac / timezone: America/Chicago ## Now - derive the next round of agent changes from the harness ledger / ship the 24 kHz superwideband audio path end to end on the pendant ## Relevant - ..."

THE GAP, which is the part worth your round. Nothing in the live turn calls it. projectContext has exactly three call sites in the whole repository: the GET /memory/projection route (server.js:2211), the measurement script, and its own definition. The live prompt path is orchestrator.js:90 -> buildConversationContext (conversationContext.js:30), which still composes formatWorkingProjectForPrompt and formatLongTermMemoryForPrompt - the pre-projection blocks. scripts/measure-context-projection.mjs measures the cost of that on this machine's real store: 374 tokens/turn before, 152 after, 222 tokens/turn saved (59.4%), and 82.4% of the uncached portion.

So: do not propose a minimal storage layer. It exists, it is better specified than the one you would write, and its value is already measured. The missing piece is one wiring change - conversationContext.js calling projectContext(surface, task) instead of composing the two legacy blocks. That is the injection point you asked about, and it is unclaimed.

One correction while you are here, because it blocks your other request. "There is no scheduler to poll" is false. POST /routines schedules a command daily, weekly, or on an interval - "every morning", "each weekday", "every fifteen minutes" - and it "only fires while this agent is up". GET /routines lists what is scheduled with next-run and last-run outcome. POST /routines/:routineId/run fires one now. Separately there is a whole standing-watch subsystem - POST /watches, POST /watches/:watchId/check, POST /watches/:watchId/ack, GET /watches/reports, GET /watches/health, GET /watches/:watchId/suppressed - which is exactly the register -> check -> diff -> report -> acknowledge shape you want, already shipped, already handling the "nothing changed" versus "nothing could be checked" distinction. It is aimed at web pages rather than jobs. Copy its shape rather than inventing a protocol.

tools.name: relay_route_intent
tools.why: As a low-latency front door, I need a safe, explicit way to route recognized user intents to downstream agents (mac-planner/mac-vision) and receive status, without inventing my own protocol.

utterance.description: The raw or normalized user utterance.

context.description: Optional session context such as locale, time, and any already-known constraints.

target.description: Preferred target agent id, e.g. 'mac-planner' or 'mac-vision'.

tools.name: server_browser_actions
tools.why: Enable the relay to run safe, sandboxed browser interactions without relying on the owner’s Mac being online, using Cloudflare Browser Run when available.

actions.description: High-level browser actions to perform (navigate, click, extract, search).

tools.name: relay_job_status
tools.why: When I POST a plan, I receive a queued jobId but I cannot check progress or retrieve the planned actions to inform the owner. A status tool would let me read job state without inventing a protocol or requiring execute permission.

jobId.description: The job id returned from a plan request.

tools.name: relay_event_push
tools.why: The relay needs a way to deliver asynchronous completion updates to the pendant (or to a paired phone) after the voice session ends. Without it, users have to poll for status, which is awkward and unreliable for long-running tasks.

jobId.description: The job to monitor for completion.

spoken.description: A short user-facing sentence to play on the pendant.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the notification should be kept if the device is offline.

tools.name: job_completion_watch
tools.why: We need a real way to monitor jobs and emit completion events after the voice session ends, without the relay inventing a protocol.

permissions.scope: probe:get:/v1/state/* and probe:get:/v1/ops/* additional routes beyond latest/history/memory
permissions.askedFor: probe:get:/v1/state/* and probe:get:/v1/ops/* additional routes beyond latest/history/memory

deviceSkills.name: offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward
deviceSkills.what_it_does: Records a short voice memo locally when the network is unavailable, then forwards it to the relay when connectivity returns. Provides a simple LED pattern to indicate stored memos.

deviceSkills.name: spoken_status_interrupt
deviceSkills.what_it_does: Allows the pendant button to interrupt any long spoken status report and request a shorter summary or next item.

proposals.user_asks: “Summarize what I missed in my email today.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can get a quick spoken briefing while walking, without opening a laptop.
surfaces: relay: capture the request and confirm scope (e.g., today, unread).
mac-bridge: planner fetches email metadata and drafts a summary.
relay: reads back a short summary and offers to drill down.
proposals.model_tier: Low-latency realtime model only for the brief live clarification and playback. A cheaper background model should do the email retrieval and summarization via the Mac bridge.
proposals.latency_budget: Interactive confirmation under ~2 seconds. Retrieval and summarization can take 10-60 seconds depending on network and mailbox size.
proposals.cost_estimate: Main cost is background tokens for summarization and the email content processed. Realtime cost is small and limited to a short clarification and reading the summary.
proposals.security_concerns: Email contains sensitive personal data. Access should require explicit account linking and confirmation of which mailbox to read. Summaries must avoid exposing secrets unless asked. The owner should be able to stop and delete cached summaries.
missing: A secure email connector in the Mac planner (or an OAuth-based integration) with least-privilege scopes.
An explicit confirmation step for first-time access and for reading full message bodies.

proposals.user_asks: “Read my upcoming schedule for the day.”
proposals.why_useful: A hands-free daily briefing helps the owner plan while commuting or getting ready.
surfaces: relay: capture request, confirm time window (today/next 24h).
mac-bridge: planner queries calendar events and composes a spoken-friendly agenda.
relay: plays agenda and offers to set reminders.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for quick clarification and playback. Background tier for calendar queries and formatting.
proposals.latency_budget: Under ~2 seconds for confirmation; 5-30 seconds for calendar retrieval depending on provider.
proposals.cost_estimate: Background tokens dominate due to event text and formatting; realtime tokens are minimal.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar data can include private locations and attendees. Require explicit confirmation before reading sensitive fields. Ensure the owner can exclude calendars and disable storage.
missing: Calendar connector via Mac planner or direct integration.
A reminder mechanism on the pendant or phone if reminders are requested.

proposals.user_asks: “Save this idea for later.”
proposals.why_useful: Captures thoughts in the moment, then syncs them into a searchable memory or notes system.
surfaces: relay: capture dictation and confirm title/tag if needed.
mac-bridge: stores the note in the memory graph or forwards to a notes app.
dashboard: shows captured notes and allows organizing.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for dictation and minimal confirmation. Background tier for storage, tagging, and search indexing.
proposals.latency_budget: Realtime capture should feel immediate; storage can complete within a few seconds without blocking the conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Realtime audio tokens dominate during dictation; storage and indexing are cheap.
proposals.security_concerns: Notes may contain sensitive info. Provide a clear policy for retention and deletion. Require confirmation before exporting to external services.
missing: A standardized notes/memory write API with tagging and privacy controls.
Optional integrations (e.g., Apple Notes, Notion) with explicit user authorization.

proposals.user_asks: “Plan my day. Pull my calendar, summarize critical tasks and travel time, and give me a 30-second briefing.”
proposals.why_useful: It turns scattered commitments into a concise spoken plan the owner can use while walking, commuting, or getting ready.
surfaces: relay: capture the request, clarify constraints (time horizon, preferred tone), and hand off
mac-bridge: fetch calendar/tasks from local apps if available; browser: fetch from web services if needed
relay: deliver a short audio briefing; dashboard: show the same summary for later review
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the initial conversation and confirmation; a cheaper background model for aggregation/summarization, scheduled as a job and returned when ready.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2-3 seconds to acknowledge and confirm scope; tens of seconds for the background job is okay because it arrives as audio when ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: Realtime cost dominated by a short confirmation turn; background cost dominated by calendar/task API calls and summarization tokens. Use the smallest context window and avoid pulling full event descriptions unless needed.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar and task data is sensitive. Require explicit confirmation before accessing new accounts or expanding scope (e.g., reading email). Clearly state what sources will be read. Avoid storing raw event bodies; store only derived summary if at all.
missing: A standardized intent-to-job route from relay to mac-planner/browser, with status updates
Confirmed availability of calendar/task connectors (local or web) and permissions to access them
An audio job delivery mechanism to queue and play back the briefing on the pendant

proposals.user_asks: “Read my notifications and tell me only what’s important.”
proposals.why_useful: Reduces distraction by turning notification overload into a brief, prioritized spoken digest.
surfaces: relay: capture the request and preferences (sources, urgency rules)
mac-bridge and/or phone integration: collect notifications from allowed sources
background model: classify and rank; relay: speak the digest; dashboard: let the owner adjust rules
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for preference capture and confirmation; cheaper background model for classification, deduping, and digest generation.
proposals.latency_budget: 1-2 seconds to confirm the filter; digest can take a few seconds more and arrive as audio when ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low realtime cost; background cost dominated by notification text volume and classification. Use strict source filters and truncate long content.
proposals.security_concerns: Notifications can contain private messages and codes. Require explicit opt-in per source (e.g., messaging apps). Never read out one-time codes by default. Avoid storing sensitive content beyond what’s needed.
missing: A phone-side notification pipeline (iOS/Android) or a desktop notification collector
Rule UI in the dashboard and a preferences store
A safe default policy for sensitive content like 2FA codes

proposals.user_asks: “Start a focus session for 25 minutes. Block distractions and let me know when time’s up.”
proposals.why_useful: Helps the owner create a simple, repeatable routine to get work done without fiddling with apps.
surfaces: relay: start/stop commands and quick status
mac-bridge: enforce blocking (apps/sites) when the Mac is present
background job: timer; relay or pendant audio: end-of-session chime; dashboard: session log
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for start/stop and confirmation; cheap timer job for scheduling; mac agent for enforcement policies.
proposals.latency_budget: Under a second to start; timer runs in the background; end notification timing must be accurate to within a few seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Minimal realtime tokens; cheap timer job; enforcement cost depends on how many actions need to be applied on the Mac.
proposals.security_concerns: Blocking apps/sites alters the owner’s computer behavior. Require explicit confirmation the first time a blocklist is applied. Provide a clear override phrase. Log changes for transparency.
missing: A timer/scheduler service for jobs
Mac enforcement actions and permission to control apps/network
A pendant-side chime or audio playback capability for offline end-of-session alerts

proposals.user_asks: “Remember this: my bike lock code is 4829.”
proposals.why_useful: Lets the owner offload small facts and retrieve them later by voice.
surfaces: relay: capture and confirm what to store; relay: retrieve on request
memory store: save encrypted or access-controlled entries; dashboard: manage and delete stored memories
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for capture/recall; cheap storage operations. Use minimal context to avoid paying to re-send stored facts.
proposals.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm storage; recall should be near-instant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low; dominated by a brief confirmation turn and a small memory write/read.
proposals.security_concerns: Sensitive secrets are risky. Require explicit confirmation and label as sensitive. Store encrypted, restrict retrieval to authenticated sessions, and avoid speaking secrets out loud unless the owner asks and is in a safe context.
missing: A secure memory write/read API with encryption and access controls
Policies for sensitive data handling and redaction
A way to mark entries as secret vs general

proposals.user_asks: “Summarize the key points from this page and read them to me later.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can capture useful info while on the move, then hear a concise summary when they have time, without staring at a screen.
surfaces: relay: capture request and confirm target timing/output
browser (server-side or via mac-planner): fetch and extract page content
background worker: summarize and store audio/text artifact
dashboard: show saved summaries and playback history
pendant: later playback as audio when requested
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for capture/confirmation. Summarization runs on a cheaper background model. Text-to-speech can be offline-prepared and stored.
proposals.latency_budget: Interactive confirmation under 2-3 seconds. Fetching and summarizing can take 10-60 seconds in the background; playback is instant once ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: Capture cost is small (short transcript). Background cost dominated by page text length and summary generation; TTS cost depends on audio duration.
proposals.security_concerns: Web content could be malicious or contain tracking. Only fetch the target URL, avoid executing scripts when possible, and store only what’s needed. If the page requires login, require explicit confirmation before using authenticated sessions.
missing: A job queue / background worker contract
Server-side browser actions or a reliable Mac delegation path
Storage and playback pipeline for prepared audio artifacts

proposals.user_asks: "Summarize this webpage" or "Check the price on this product"
proposals.why_useful: Fast, hands-free answers without needing the owner’s Mac to be online, especially when they’re out wearing the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper background model for browsing/extraction; relay only handles the voice handoff and a short summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Relay response should be near-immediate (“I’m checking”). Page processing can take several seconds; that’s fine as long as it returns a concise summary.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by browser runtime and extraction tokens; relay cost stays low because it doesn’t parse the full page.
proposals.security_concerns: Web content can include tracking and authenticated pages. Only fetch public URLs by default; require explicit confirmation before using stored credentials or accessing private sites. Return minimal extracted data.
missing: Server-side browser capability wired into the relay’s tool registry and routing
Job status/notification path so results can arrive later as audio or dashboard update

proposals.user_asks: "Remind me to do X at 6 pm" or "Every weekday at 9, remind me to stand up"
proposals.why_useful: Routines are a classic wearable job: set it once, then get gentle prompts without having to open a laptop.
proposals.model_tier: Relay for quick intent capture; a cheaper scheduled worker for recurring delivery; optional mac_delegate for creating system reminders if the Mac is available.
proposals.latency_budget: Setting a reminder should feel instant. Delivery can be a push/notification; if offline, it can queue until reachable.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per reminder; cost comes from scheduled checks and notification delivery rather than conversation tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: A malicious reminder could spam or leak private text. Require explicit confirmation for recurring reminders and for reminders that send content to external services. Provide clear list and one-shot cancellation.
missing: Scheduler/recurring job system (Cron or Durable Object alarms)
Notification channel to pendant or phone, or a fallback to macOS Reminders

proposals.user_asks: “Check the weather and read the highlights to me.”
proposals.why_useful: Quick, hands-free information while the owner is away from the Mac, without needing the Mac to be online.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper non-realtime tier for browsing/extraction; realtime only for brief conversational follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: A couple seconds for summary is fine; realtime should not wait on long page interactions.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by browser execution and extraction tokens; minimal relay tokens if it delegates.
proposals.security_concerns: Web pages can contain tracking and malicious content; keep browsing sandboxed, avoid logging sensitive extracted data, and require confirmation before opening authenticated sessions.
missing: Confirm production availability of server-side browser actions in the relay toolset and wire it to a safe extraction pipeline.

proposals.user_asks: “When I get back to my desk, summarize what happened while I was away and queue anything urgent.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can wear the pendant and stay in the flow, then get a concise catch-up without manually checking email, tasks, and logs.
surfaces: relay: recognizes the request and hands it off
mac-bridge: mac_delegate plans and runs the catch-up using local data and browser where needed
browser: only if the plan needs web access (e.g., status pages)
relay: delivers a spoken summary back when the job completes, plus a dashboard entry if available
proposals.model_tier: mac-planner (cheaper than realtime) should do the heavy lifting. Realtime is only for quick confirmation and reading the result aloud if the owner asks.
proposals.latency_budget: Interactive setup under a couple seconds. The catch-up itself can take longer (tens of seconds to a few minutes) and should run without holding a live voice session.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low realtime cost (brief handoff). Main cost is mac-planner tokens plus any browser actions. Avoid pulling large inbox content unless necessary; summarize and only expand on request.
proposals.security_concerns: It touches email, tasks, and possibly internal tools. The plan should use least access. Anything that sends messages, deletes, or changes tasks requires explicit confirmation; read-only summarization should be allowed.
missing: A scheduler/queue to run when the owner returns or at a set time
A relay job-status and result delivery path that can notify the owner later (audio or dashboard)
A way to persist the owner’s preference for what sources to include

proposals.user_asks: “Remind me every weekday at 5 to shut down and summarize what I did today.”
proposals.why_useful: Creates a dependable end-of-day routine without the owner having to remember or keep the pendant session open.
surfaces: relay: captures the intent and schedules it
scheduler: triggers routine at the right time
mac-bridge: mac_delegate runs a day summary from local sources
relay: provides a short spoken summary if the owner asks, and posts a dashboard note
proposals.model_tier: A scheduled, cheaper background model should run the routine. Realtime should not stay engaged or poll.
proposals.latency_budget: Scheduling is instant. Summary can take up to a minute; delivery can be async.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per run if sources are summarized and only key changes are read. Avoid lengthy transcripts and large context carryover.
proposals.security_concerns: Summaries may include sensitive work content. Store minimal output and respect data minimization. Any action that changes systems (closing apps, committing code) must require confirmation.
missing: A real scheduler (cron or durable object alarms) and a routine store
A delivery mechanism for results (audio file in R2 and/or dashboard notification)
Preference UI in the dashboard to configure time and included sources

proposals.user_asks: “Read me the top three things I should care about right now.”
proposals.why_useful: A quick, low-friction prioritization helps the owner focus without diving into multiple apps.
surfaces: relay: captures the request, confirms scope if needed
mac-bridge: mac_delegate collects signals (calendar, reminders, email flags, ongoing jobs)
browser: optional for external status checks
relay: reads out a concise prioritized list and offers to drill into one item
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the short conversation and spoken output; mac-planner for gathering and ranking in the background.
proposals.latency_budget: Target under a second to acknowledge, then a brief pause while the Mac gathers. If the Mac is offline, offer a fallback using only cloud-accessible sources.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate. The expensive part is gathering. Keep ranking simple and summaries tight; avoid full message bodies unless necessary.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar/email access is sensitive. Read-only by default. Any action like sending replies or changing reminders requires confirmation. Don’t expose private details unless the owner asks to open them.
missing: Reliable detection of Mac availability and a fallback plan
A small preference store for signal weighting (e.g., prioritize calendar over email)
Better result caching to avoid re-gathering within a short window

proposals.user_asks: Give me a quick briefing for my day, and make it something I can listen to later.
proposals.why_useful: You get a concise, spoken plan that you can play when you have time, instead of standing around while I think and fetch.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime captures the request and confirmation; a cheaper planner model compiles the briefing; text-to-speech (or existing audio pipeline) renders it for later playback.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds to acknowledge and confirm. The actual research/compilation can take minutes and should not hold the mic open.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low for the realtime capture; medium for planning and any web lookups; audio generation/storage costs dominate if the briefing is long.
proposals.security_concerns: Briefings may include calendar, projects, and emails. Only include sources the user opted into. Require confirmation before accessing email or external services, and store only the final audio plus minimal metadata.
missing: A scheduler or delayed job mechanism to run later
Reliable job status and delivery UI
Audio rendering path for scheduled output if not already present
Consent settings for which sources to include

proposals.user_asks: Look up this topic on the web and summarize it for me.
proposals.why_useful: Fast, hands-free answers while you’re away from your computer, without needing the Mac to be online.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for intent and constraints; server-side browser for extraction; a smaller summarizer for synthesis.
proposals.latency_budget: Quick confirmation in under a few seconds; summary may take 5-20 seconds depending on page complexity.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by server browser runtime and summarization tokens; relay cost stays small if we keep context tight.
proposals.security_concerns: Avoid logging extracted page content. For paywalled or authenticated sites, fall back to the Mac with explicit confirmation.
missing: server_browser_actions routing and extraction templates
Fallback to mac_delegate for authenticated content
Clear error messages when blocked

proposals.user_asks: “Summarize the top results from the web about X, and keep it out of my Mac.”
proposals.why_useful: It lets the owner get quick research-style answers while away from the Mac, without waking the desktop agent or touching private authenticated sessions.
proposals.model_tier: A cheaper background model should run the browsing and extraction. The realtime relay should only parse the request, confirm scope, and read back the summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Conversation stays snappy because the relay hands off quickly; the browsing takes as long as needed without the owner waiting on live audio.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low relay cost (short prompt), moderate browsing cost dominated by page loads and extraction tokens. Cheaper than routing through the Mac planner for purely public web content.
proposals.security_concerns: Avoid authenticated pages and anything requiring login unless explicitly routed to the Mac browser bridge. Confirm any action beyond reading/extracting (no purchases, no form submissions).
missing: server-side browser auth policy and allowlist for public-only browsing
a small summary/extraction pipeline that produces concise, citation-backed output
a job status UI in the dashboard so the owner can see progress if the task continues after the call

proposals.user_asks: “Check my inbox and tell me what needs attention, but don’t send anything.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets a quick triage while walking, without sitting down at the Mac. It’s an everyday wearable superpower: prioritize, not compose.
proposals.model_tier: Mac planner should handle the workflow. Realtime relay only captures the request and delivers the summary. Browser actions must stop before sending or making changes.
proposals.latency_budget: Short initial handoff; the Mac can work in the background. If it takes longer, the relay can provide a brief status update and finish later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Mac planner cost dominates; browser interaction cost depends on mailbox size. Relay remains minimal.
proposals.security_concerns: Inbox is sensitive. Require explicit confirmation for accessing any new account/source. Never send replies or delete/archive without confirmation. Present proposed changes as a payload for approval.
missing: a reliable background job mechanism or durable alarm to continue work and report back later
a relay-to-owner notification mechanism (audio or dashboard) when triage completes
a standardized summary format for triage results

proposals.user_asks: “Keep an eye on this website and let me know when anything important changes.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets passive awareness without babysitting pages, and the pendant can deliver a quick summary when they’re away from the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background model for periodic diffing and summarization; realtime model only for the follow-up conversation when the owner asks what changed.
proposals.latency_budget: Diffing can take seconds to minutes; it’s not interactive. Alert playback should be near-instant once the alert exists.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by browser fetch + diff + summary tokens. Realtime cost only when the owner responds or asks for more detail.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated sites should be opt-in per origin. Redact sensitive fields in summaries. Any irreversible action (like triggering a purchase) must require explicit confirmation.
missing: A scheduler/queue to run periodic checks
A storage-backed alert queue and retention policy
A routing rule to prefer server-side browser for public pages and Mac session only for authenticated origins

proposals.user_asks: “Give me a quick overnight briefing.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner wakes up to a concise, trustworthy summary of what happened while they slept: tasks completed, things that failed, messages worth attention, and any follow-up already queued. It turns the system into a dependable teammate instead of a chat window.
proposals.model_tier: Background planning and summarization should run on the Mac planner (cheaper, not latency-critical). The relay only plays back the result when asked, keeping realtime usage minimal.
proposals.latency_budget: Owner is not waiting for the work to happen; it should complete in the background and be ready instantly when requested. Playback should be near-instant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per day if summarized once into a small artifact. Biggest cost is any email/calendar/file reads and summarization tokens on the planner tier; relay cost is just a short spoken reply.
proposals.security_concerns: Summaries include sensitive data. The ledger must track provenance and avoid leaking content across contexts. Any action to fix something (e.g., send a message, move money, change files) must require explicit confirmation.
missing: A scheduler/worker to run the briefing job daily (Cloudflare Cron or Durable Object alarms wired into the bridge)
Event-sourced ledger and receipts wired end-to-end so the summary is based on auditable events
A stored ‘briefing artifact’ the relay can fetch quickly without recomputing
Permissioned readers for mail/calendar/files (or a defined scope)

proposals.user_asks: “Every morning, give me a 30-second audio digest of what changed: calendar, reminders, and top emails.”
proposals.why_useful: It turns the pendant into a daily briefing you can listen to while walking, without pulling out a phone or opening a laptop.
proposals.model_tier: Planner/summary runs on a cheaper background model via the Mac bridge or server-side browser for web sources; relay only delivers the audio and handles quick follow-ups.
proposals.latency_budget: Digest generation can take seconds to minutes; delivery should be instant when ready. The owner is not waiting in a live conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by summarization tokens and any email/calendar access; delivery is cheap. Runs once per day.
proposals.security_concerns: Requires access to mail and calendars. High-impact actions aren’t needed, but reading private data is sensitive—make sources explicit at setup, and provide a dashboard view of what was accessed.
missing: A scheduler/routines system to run daily
An audio rendering pipeline that can package a digest for playback
Connectors for mail/calendar if not already available via the Mac bridge
A job status/listing UI so the owner can see and manage scheduled digests

proposals.user_asks: "Queue this up and tell me when it’s done" (for example: summarize a long document, compare options, draft an email, or research a topic).
proposals.why_useful: It turns the pendant into a true front door: the owner can speak a task once, then go about their day while the system finishes it in the background and delivers a concise result when ready.
surfaces: relay: capture the request quickly and confirm it was queued
mac-bridge: plan and execute multi-step tasks when the Mac is available
relay/server: use server-side browser or public web readers when the Mac is offline or unnecessary
dashboard/iOS/menubar: show job status and receipts, and let the owner replay results
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for capturing intent and immediate confirmation; cheaper planner/executor on Mac or server for the actual work; no long-running work on the realtime tier.
proposals.latency_budget: Under ~1 second to acknowledge and queue; seconds to minutes for execution depending on task; results arrive asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low realtime cost per request (short acknowledgement). Main cost is downstream planning/execution tokens plus any browser automation; cheaper than keeping the realtime model engaged while work runs.
proposals.security_concerns: Background jobs can read sensitive data or take actions. Provide a clear receipt showing what was read/changed. Require explicit confirmation for irreversible or high-impact actions (e.g., sending email, purchases).
missing: A real scheduler/queue in the relay (Durable Object or D1-backed) with alarms for retries
A stable enqueue/status/receipt API between relay and Mac
Result delivery mechanism to the relay (webhook/polling)
Server-side browser integration as a fallback path
UI for job status and receipts across surfaces

proposals.user_asks: “When I press the pendant button, capture a short voice note, tag it with time and place if available, and later summarize it into tasks.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can offload thoughts instantly while away from the Mac, and get them turned into actionable reminders without babysitting a workflow.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the capture conversation; a cheaper planner model on the Mac summarizes and files tasks.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate capture feedback (<300ms perceived) on pendant; summarization can happen seconds to minutes later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per capture; biggest cost is audio transport/storage in R2 and transcription tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio leaves the device to relay storage; should be retained minimally and deletable. Summaries should avoid exposing sensitive content to broad surfaces.
missing: A durable task ledger with receipts so the owner can see what happened
A scheduler/worker path to run summarization after capture
A consistent way to attach metadata (time, optional location) to notes

proposals.user_asks: “I asked you to handle that on my Mac—what’s the status?”
proposals.why_useful: The owner shouldn’t wonder whether a delegated task is still running, failed, or finished. A quick spoken status lets them keep moving while away from the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the spoken query; a cheaper Mac-side planner/executor reports status and results.
proposals.latency_budget: Sub-second reply when a status is already known; otherwise a short acknowledgment and a follow-up when the Mac reports back.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per query. The dominant cost is Mac-side status retrieval and any stored receipts, not relay compute.
proposals.security_concerns: Status text can leak sensitive task names or file paths. Only return what’s needed for the owner to understand progress; redact secrets; require confirmation before reading full outputs aloud.
missing: A durable receipt/status store keyed by job id and owner identity
A relay-readable status endpoint or tool to fetch status and results
A queue for completion summaries for the relay to speak later (or a dashboard inbox)

proposals.user_asks: What’s connected right now, and can you hand this off to my Mac if needed?
proposals.why_useful: The owner is often away from the Mac. A quick status check plus a clean handoff reduces friction and prevents asking the Mac to do things when the bridge is offline or the browser extension is down.
proposals.model_tier: realtime for the spoken status; mac-planner for follow-on tasks if the owner asks to proceed
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 second for status from relay-visible sources; additional time only if the owner asks to proceed with a Mac task.
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low for relay status probes; higher only if a delegated Mac plan is created.
proposals.security_concerns: Status includes device presence and possibly network info; keep it minimal and do not expose anything beyond what the owner asked for.
missing: A consistent status schema across relay and Mac surfaces so the spoken summary is stable.
A standard handoff intent taxonomy so the relay can say what it is delegating in a way downstream agents understand.

proposals.user_asks: If this will take longer, keep working on my Mac and let me know when it’s done.
proposals.why_useful: This matches real life: the owner speaks a goal, then walks away. The system should continue the task on the Mac, track progress, and report back when finished, without requiring the owner to babysit the process.
proposals.model_tier: Mac planner for the actual work; relay for quick conversational updates; cheaper completion model for summaries if available.
proposals.latency_budget: Under a second for the initial acknowledgment; the work itself can take minutes. Progress updates should be brief and optional.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low cost at the relay (short acknowledgments). Main cost is Mac-side planning/execution and any browser automation; dominant cost is tool calls and page processing.
proposals.security_concerns: Must avoid executing irreversible actions without explicit confirmation. Progress/status messages may contain sensitive page content; redact where possible and keep summaries minimal.
missing: A reliable job status channel from Mac to relay for long-running delegated tasks
A notification mechanism to reach the pendant when the owner is away (push or poll)
Durable storage for job state so the relay can reconnect after disconnects

proposals.user_asks: “Keep the conversation usable even when LTE is congested—let me interrupt, and don’t lose what I said while you’re speaking.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently experiences a ~7.8-second uplink collapse and hundreds of dropped packets when downlink speech overlaps speech. A congestion-aware session would make the pendant feel conversational rather than requiring the owner to wait for audio to finish or repeat themselves. It is genuinely cross-node: the pendant measures capture/queue health, the relay chooses transport behavior in real time, and the Mac/ESP32 bridge reports playback occupancy and can pause/resume the SBC stream without destroying the turn.
proposals.model_tier: Use relay-realtime only for the live turn and transport decisions; no additional model call is needed. If a turn is irrecoverably damaged, a cheap background repair/transcription pass can reconstruct the partial utterance rather than spending the realtime tier again.
proposals.latency_budget: Congestion detection and mode changes under 150 ms; interruption acknowledgment under 300 ms. Preserve no more than 250 ms of speech before and after a mode switch. A resumed answer may begin within 1 second after the owner stops speaking.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost beyond the existing realtime session. Storage/telemetry is small; bandwidth may decrease because degraded mode uses lower bitrate and sends short control frames instead of repeatedly retransmitting audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio and loss telemetry remain within the existing relay session and bridge link; do not upload raw replay buffers unless needed for the current turn. The dashboard should expose mode changes and dropped-frame counts, and automatically expire any repair buffer after the turn. Playback pause/resume and codec changes must be authenticated to the paired pendant/bridge so a spoofed control packet cannot inject audio.
missing: A negotiated session-state protocol carrying packet-loss rate, uplink queue depth, playback occupancy, and explicit half-duplex/degraded/normal modes
Pendant firmware support for a small rolling pre-encode PCM/Opus window, sequence numbers, VAD boundaries, and local backpressure signaling (not a user-facing offline note feature)
Relay jitter buffer and turn assembler that can splice an interrupted utterance, issue a brief local/relay acknowledgment, and resume TTS from a checkpoint
ESP32/SBC bridge controls for pause, drain, and resume plus a report of actual playback occupancy; current SBC-only path otherwise hides congestion
A deterministic acceptance harness that injects LTE contention and verifies no more than 250 ms of owner speech is lost and that an interrupted response resumes exactly once

proposals.user_asks: “When I walk back to my Mac, hand off the thing I asked you to do on the pendant, finish it in the right browser/app, and tell me on the pendant exactly what happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a worn-device request cannot reliably bridge the moment when the owner is away to the moment an authenticated Mac/browser becomes available. This would turn a spoken intent into a durable, owner-visible handoff rather than losing it in a disconnected extension or forcing the owner to repeat themselves. It depends on the pendant, always-awake relay, Mac planner, and browser sessions together.
proposals.model_tier: Relay-realtime only captures and acknowledges the initial intent. A cheaper background planner handles the queued goal and browser/Mac execution; realtime is used again only to deliver a concise completion or failure summary when the owner is reachable.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate spoken acknowledgment in under 500 ms. Handoff detection under 5 seconds after the Mac bridge/browser session becomes available. Completion notification should arrive within 2 seconds of the downstream receipt; never claim success before a signed result receipt is returned.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn for capture and one for the final spoken summary; planning/execution uses the cheaper Mac tier. Durable metadata is a few KB per handoff, with no need to retain raw audio after transcription.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must bind a handoff to the paired pendant and a specific Mac/browser session, show the target app/domain and action summary in the dashboard, and encrypt queued intent/result data. Authenticated browser cookies stay in the browser harness; the relay receives only the minimum structured goal and result. If the owner cancels from the pendant, the queued job must stop before the next mutating action.
missing: A durable handoff object with lifecycle states captured, waiting-for-surface, executing, blocked, completed, and canceled
Presence/availability signals from Mac bridge and browser extension with freshness and identity, not merely a boolean online flag
A relay-to-Mac/browser claim protocol preventing duplicate execution when both reconnect or two workers race
Signed, human-readable result receipts that can be summarized over voice and correlated to the original spoken request
A one-button pendant cancel/retry interaction and a dashboard timeline showing queued handoffs without exposing browser credentials

proposals.user_asks: “If the answer comes from my private Mac or browser, don’t read sensitive details aloud when other people may be nearby—give me a discreet cue and let me unlock the full answer with the pendant.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is worn away from the Mac and its speaker is inherently public. Today a successful browser/Mac retrieval can accidentally turn private mail, work, or account information into an audible disclosure. A privacy-aware delivery mode would let the owner use the hive in public without giving up authenticated Mac/browser access.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic relay policy for classification and short cues; use no extra model for ambient-level estimation. Mac/browser agents attach sensitivity labels and a concise safe summary. Realtime speaks only the safe cue; a full response is generated/spoken after the owner’s explicit button gesture or a private audio route is verified.
proposals.latency_budget: Safe cue under 500 ms after a result receipt. Ambient/privacy state should update within 1 second and never block ordinary low-sensitivity answers. Unlock gesture must be recognized within 300 ms, with a 10-second expiry.
proposals.cost_estimate: No additional model call for policy; a small amount of metadata travels with each result. Optional private full-answer playback through the existing bridge has normal audio cost only.
proposals.security_concerns: Sensitivity labels must be fail-closed when absent or contradictory, and the relay must never infer that a browser result is safe merely because the request was spoken. The full answer should require a deliberate button gesture, expire quickly, and be auditable in the dashboard without storing the secret text. Ambient detection should retain only a boolean/short-lived confidence, not recordings.
missing: A result-envelope schema carrying source, sensitivity, safe-summary, and disclosure policy from Mac planner/browser harness to relay
Pendant firmware support for a distinct long-press/double-click unlock and LED acknowledgment, with replay-resistant sequence numbers
A local ambient speech/noise privacy estimator and a configurable owner policy (always discreet, adaptive, or unrestricted)
A private playback capability or authenticated bridge route that can be proven to be the owner’s listening device
End-to-end tests proving sensitive browser/Mac content is never emitted on the public speaker without the unlock gesture

proposals.user_asks: Keep working on that longer task after I stop talking, and tell me what happened later.
proposals.why_useful: The owner is wearing the pendant and often walks away. They should be able to hand off a multi-step job, then get a clear status update without keeping a live conversation open.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only to confirm handoff; mac-planner for planning/execution; relay_job_status for later status, using a cheaper tier if available for summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 second to confirm handoff; background work can take minutes. Status checks should be near-instant and not require the Mac to be awake.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per invocation for handoff/status; dominant cost is mac-planner execution and any browser automation, plus storage for job logs.
proposals.security_concerns: Status text may contain sensitive content from apps or pages. Only return minimal, user-sized summaries and store provenance. Never claim completion unless the job is marked done.
missing: A durable job lifecycle service that spans relay and mac, with consistent IDs and typed states
A notification path to the pendant/dashboard when a job finishes
Optional server-side browser execution for jobs that do not require the Mac

proposals.user_asks: “What was I looking at on my Mac or in the browser earlier, and what did I need to do next?” (Also: “Continue from the thing I was working on.”)
proposals.why_useful: The owner is usually away from the Mac when speaking to the pendant, yet their unfinished context is split between open Mac apps, browser tabs with authenticated sessions, and voice history. Today the pendant cannot reconstruct that context; this would let a brief spoken request recover the relevant thread and continue it without manually remembering filenames, tabs, or error messages.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles intent disambiguation and a concise spoken answer only. A cheaper background extraction/indexing model continuously turns permitted Mac/browser activity snapshots into short searchable evidence; mac-planner and browser harness fetch live details only for the selected thread.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a spoken answer from the recent local index; up to 10 seconds when live Mac/browser evidence must be collected. Never block the voice turn on a full app crawl—say what is known and offer to continue asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per recall, dominated by live evidence extraction and planner calls; routine indexing should use a small/cheap model and batch snapshots rather than the realtime tier.
proposals.security_concerns: Activity may include private documents, messages, and authenticated pages. Keep raw contents on the Mac/browser session where possible, send only narrowly selected snippets and hashes to the relay, encrypt the activity ledger, provide per-app/site exclusions and retention limits in the dashboard, and clearly identify uncertainty. Continuing an action must be a separate explicit request; merely recalling context must not mutate anything.
missing: A cross-surface activity ledger that records bounded, timestamped active-window/tab/document context plus embeddings or compact summaries
Mac and browser harness APIs to export the currently relevant context on demand, with app/site exclusion and redaction support
A relay retrieval endpoint that ranks evidence across voice, Mac, and browser records and returns citations/timestamps
A dashboard view for retention, exclusions, and deleting individual context records
A continuation handoff protocol from the selected recalled thread to mac-planner/browser without conflating recall with execution

proposals.user_asks: “Use the file I just edited to fill out that form in the browser, attach it, and tell me exactly what was submitted.”
proposals.why_useful: Today Mac and browser actions are separate command paths, so the owner cannot use a local artifact while away from the Mac to complete an authenticated web workflow. This bridges the Mac’s local files and the browser’s logged-in session into one voice-directed operation, with a precise spoken receipt instead of forcing the owner to remember paths, tabs, and fields.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime parses the request and resolves only obvious references. mac-planner locates and reads the permitted local artifact; browser harness operates the authenticated session; a cheaper verifier extracts the final field values and attachment identity. Realtime speaks the concise result and any ambiguity.
proposals.latency_budget: Resolve references in 2 seconds; complete ordinary workflows in 10–30 seconds. If either surface is offline, preserve a resumable job and report the exact missing leg rather than pretending completion.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.15 per completed workflow, dominated by planner/browser interaction and post-submit verification; simple reference resolution should be cheap cached retrieval.
proposals.security_concerns: This can move private local files into authenticated websites and submit consequential data. Maintain a provenance manifest (source path/hash, destination origin, fields, timestamp), redact secrets from relay logs, restrict file selection to the explicitly resolved artifact, detect origin changes, and return a spoken receipt. The owner allows access without confirmation, but submission must still be observable and recoverable with a cancel/undo or draft mode where the destination supports it.
missing: A cross-surface job protocol carrying artifact references, not raw files, between Mac bridge and browser harness
Mac-side artifact resolver that can identify the recently edited file and expose a bounded read/attachment stream
Browser-side form schema extraction, upload support, and post-submit receipt capture
A durable job/receipt store with resumable state, idempotency keys, and failure recovery across relay, Mac, and browser outages
Dashboard provenance and deletion controls for transferred artifacts and receipts

proposals.user_asks: “Mark this moment.” (Press the pendant button, optionally say a short label, then later: “Take me back to the moment I marked as ‘pricing bug.’”)
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is the only surface physically with the owner, while the meaningful context may be on a Mac window or authenticated browser tab. A one-button anchor would capture the owner’s intent at the instant it matters—even when they cannot stop to copy a URL or filename—and later reopen or summarize the exact cross-device context.
proposals.model_tier: The pendant firmware records a local timestamp/button event and the relay pairs it with a short voice label. A cheap background worker requests compact active-context snapshots from Mac and browser, stores a ranked anchor, and realtime later answers or routes a reopen request.
proposals.latency_budget: Button acknowledgement must be immediate and offline-capable; pairing and context capture should finish within 5 seconds when devices are reachable. Retrieval should answer in under 2 seconds from the anchor index.
proposals.cost_estimate: A few cents per labeled anchor at most; the dominant cost is occasional Mac/browser context capture, not the button event or realtime response. Firmware storage and LTE payloads are small.
proposals.security_concerns: Anchors can expose whatever was onscreen, including private pages. Default to a short encrypted summary plus origin/path and allow app/site exclusions, retention expiry, and deletion. Do not upload screenshots by default. If reopening a page could cause a mutation, open read-only and report the target before any action.
missing: Firmware support for a durable button event queue with timestamp, sequence number, and optional short audio-label association
A relay pairing window that correlates the event with nearby-in-time voice and device context despite clock drift or intermittent LTE
Mac/browser APIs for a point-in-time active-window/tab snapshot and a stable reopen token
An anchor index with retention, exclusion, and deletion controls in the dashboard
A read-only reopen/summarize operation that can recover gracefully when the original app, tab, or file no longer exists

proposals.user_asks: Handle this later and keep working after I stop talking. Tell me when it’s done, and if you need my approval, ask at the right moment.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can start something from the pendant while away from the Mac, then trust the system to carry it through and report back without babysitting. It turns a quick voice command into a complete workflow with follow-through.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial clarification and confirmation; planning and execution run on a cheaper Mac-tier model; long waits and monitoring run in server-side background.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 second for acknowledgement; plan in a few seconds; execution may take minutes and should not block the conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per invocation on the relay; cost dominated by Mac planning/execution and any browser automation time, plus occasional status checks.
proposals.security_concerns: Needs careful handling of authenticated browser sessions and private files. Drafts and irreversible changes must be shown for approval before execution. Status updates should avoid leaking sensitive content over voice.
missing: A real scheduler/background job runner (cron or alarms) to resume work later
Durable job receipts and a status lifecycle shared across relay and Mac
A notification path from background completion back to the relay/pendant
Typed context retrieval to avoid resending large context every turn

proposals.user_asks: “Save this moment so I can pick it up when I’m back at my Mac,” and later, “Resume the thing I saved earlier.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is worn while the owner is away from the Mac, so ideas, decisions, and interrupted work otherwise fall between devices. This would create a durable handoff capsule containing the spoken intent plus a snapshot of relevant Mac and authenticated-browser state, then restore that context and continue safely when the owner returns.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only extracts the short spoken request and gives immediate acknowledgement; a cheaper background model summarizes and ranks the capsule. Mac-planner gathers structured app/window/document state, while browser harness records page identity and resumable location without copying page secrets.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 1 second. Capture should finish within 10 seconds when the Mac/browser are reachable; if they are not, retain the voice capsule and enrich it on the next explicit resume request. Resume should provide a spoken preview within 3 seconds before dispatching actions.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per save/resume, dominated by background summarization and any browser/page extraction; realtime cost is limited to the brief utterance and acknowledgement.
proposals.security_concerns: The capsule may contain work titles, URLs, selected text, and application state. Keep it encrypted, owner-scoped, redact credentials and page contents by default, retain references rather than secrets, and make the resume preview audible before mutations. Do not silently send messages or alter work; reversible navigation/opening is fine under the owner's existing maximum-access policy.
missing: A first-class durable context-capsule record with lifecycle, encryption, and redaction metadata
A Mac snapshot endpoint that reports focused app, windows, documents, selected task, and resumable action state without disturbing work
A browser-harness snapshot/resume interface for authenticated tabs that preserves session locality and never exports credentials
Relay orchestration to correlate pendant utterance, Mac snapshot, browser snapshot, and later resume
A spoken preview/receipt so the owner knows exactly which capsule is being resumed

proposals.user_asks: “Work on this until it’s done, tell me what you find, and stop if I say cancel.” For example: research a purchase across authenticated and public sites, compare it, and prepare (but do not place) the order.
proposals.why_useful: Today a spoken request is effectively one handoff: the owner cannot stay in a live voice session while the Mac planner and browser encounter delays, ambiguity, login boundaries, or partial results. A voice-supervised expedition would let the owner be away from the Mac, receive concise progress on the pendant, answer clarification questions, redirect the goal, or cancel, while preserving the exact work state across Mac and browser.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for intent capture, concise progress phrasing, and interruption handling. Use gpt-5.6-luna or a cheaper background planner for decomposition and browser/Mac work; use the dashboard for a durable event log and receipts.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; progress events within 5 seconds of meaningful state changes; clarification prompts should interrupt within 2 seconds and remain pending until answered. Final synthesis can take as long as the task requires.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.25 per expedition depending on planner turns and browser extraction; the dominant cost is repeated planning/context, so send incremental state diffs rather than the full transcript.
proposals.security_concerns: Long-running authority can outlive the spoken turn and may encounter private sessions or consequential actions. Scope each expedition to an explicit goal, record every tool call, never submit purchases/messages or change data without an explicit in-session instruction, expire abandoned jobs, and provide a physical pendant cancel gesture that works even if the Mac link is down. Browser secrets stay in the browser harness.
missing: A durable expedition state machine with pause, resume, redirect, cancel, timeout, and idempotent retry semantics
Server push from relay to pendant for progress and clarification, plus a local cancel path that survives a dropped link
Planner checkpoints and compact state-diff context so retries do not replay completed mutations
Browser and Mac adapters that emit structured progress, ambiguity, and completion receipts
A dashboard timeline showing the goal, current step, artifacts, and exact actions already taken

proposals.user_asks: Did you hear that, and is it playing or still working?
proposals.why_useful: This is the everyday friction point: the owner needs a confident, honest answer about audio capture and playback, plus whether a requested task is queued, running, or done—without guessing or polling multiple systems.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for immediate spoken receipts; mac-planner/browser for long-running work summaries.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 200ms for 'heard/playing/queued' receipts; longer status details can arrive later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low for receipts (tiny events); status lookups cost dominated by downstream job status retrieval when needed.
proposals.security_concerns: Receipts can leak sensitive intent. Only store and speak minimal state; avoid raw transcripts; never claim completion unless it’s confirmed by the authoritative source.
missing: Unified interaction-receipts stream with correlation ids
Durable short-lived event storage and a read/push interface
Policy for what is spoken immediately vs queued to avoid interrupting the owner

proposals.user_asks: While you are carrying out a long task on my Mac or in my signed-in browser, let me say “pause”, “stop”, or “what’s happening?” into the pendant and get an immediate, truthful spoken status; if I stop talking, automatically pause or expire the task safely.
proposals.why_useful: The owner is usually away from the Mac and cannot reach its screen. Today a queued action can continue without a wearable control surface, leaving the owner unable to halt a mistaken navigation or understand whether anything happened. A pendant-controlled execution lease makes remote automation interruptible and understandable rather than fire-and-forget.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles the short voice command and intent classification; mac-planner/browser-extension perform pause, cancel, checkpoint, and status operations; a cheaper background model can summarize the checkpoint for speech; dashboard stores the event timeline for later inspection.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge pause/stop within 500 ms at relay, deliver the control to the active executor within 2 s, and speak a compact status within 3 s. Lease expiry should be enforced server-side even if the Mac becomes unreachable.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per control interaction depending on whether a background summary model is needed; most cost is optional status summarization, not routing. Durable execution leases/checkpoints add modest Worker/Durable Object storage and Mac implementation work.
proposals.security_concerns: Control commands and status metadata leave the pendant for the relay and may include app names or browser URLs. Stop must be honored without confirmation; pause/cancel should be authenticated to the paired pendant. The executor must checkpoint before destructive transitions, redact secrets from spoken status, and make lease expiry fail closed.
missing: A durable per-task execution lease with owner/pendant authentication and expiry
A common pause/cancel/status control protocol implemented by relay, mac-planner, mac-vision, and browser-extension
Checkpoint and resumable-state support in Mac and browser executors
A low-latency relay route for controls plus truthful spoken receipts
Dashboard timeline showing control, checkpoint, and final disposition

proposals.user_asks: When I ask the pendant “where did I see that?” or “what did we decide about this?”, search my own recent Mac actions, browser pages, voice conversations, and task receipts, then answer with the source and a direct way to reopen it.
proposals.why_useful: Today the wearable can start work but cannot recall the owner’s fragmented recent activity across the signed-in browser, Mac, and voice history. This would turn the hive into an episodic memory that works while the owner is away from the computer, without relying on generic web search or requiring them to remember which surface held the information.
proposals.model_tier: A cheaper background indexing model extracts entities, timestamps, decisions, and source links as events arrive; realtime only resolves the spoken query and reads a concise result. Exact source retrieval should be deterministic rather than generated.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture/index asynchronously in under 2 seconds per event; answer a voice recall query in under 4 seconds, with a first spoken result as soon as one high-confidence match is found.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per indexed conversation/task batch and under $0.01 per lookup; storage/indexing dominates recurring cost, while realtime speech remains the expensive portion of interaction.
proposals.security_concerns: This contains highly sensitive personal and authenticated-browser activity. Keep raw page content and transcripts encrypted, store only local/source-scoped embeddings and minimal excerpts by default, never send secrets to a model unnecessarily, and require explicit spoken confirmation before opening or exposing a sensitive source on another surface.
missing: A consented event-capture stream from relay voice runs, Mac planner receipts, and browser-extension page/activity events
An encrypted owner-scoped episodic index with retention and deletion controls
Cross-source retrieval that returns provenance, timestamps, confidence, and reopenable deep links
A relay query route and response format for concise spoken answers
Dashboard controls to inspect, correct, export, or erase remembered events

proposals.user_asks: Let me say “undo the last thing you did” to the pendant and have the hive identify the specific recent Mac/browser action, explain the planned reversal briefly, and apply a compensating action wherever it is safely reversible.
proposals.why_useful: Remote automation is valuable only if mistakes are recoverable while the owner is away from the Mac. Current receipts can describe completion, but they do not provide a cross-surface, voice-addressable undo that understands whether the last action was a browser edit, file move, calendar change, or message draft.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime resolves “last thing” and speaks the concise plan; deterministic action receipts and per-surface compensators select the reversal; a cheaper background model can map unfamiliar action descriptions to candidate compensators, never inventing a reversal without a recorded inverse.
proposals.latency_budget: Identify the target and speak it within 1.5 seconds; execute a known inverse within 5 seconds; if no inverse exists, say so immediately and offer the exact source/action receipt instead.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per undo, dominated by optional inverse-plan generation. Receipt indexing and inverse metadata add small persistent storage costs; browser/Mac compensator implementation is the main engineering cost.
proposals.security_concerns: An incorrect undo can itself cause data loss or duplicate side effects. Every action needs an immutable receipt, explicit reversibility classification, idempotent inverse, and a short spoken target announcement; irreversible actions must be reported as non-undoable rather than approximated. Receipts may contain private URLs, filenames, and message metadata and require encryption and retention controls.
missing: A cross-surface action receipt schema with stable operation IDs and recorded inverse/compensation metadata
Idempotent undo handlers for Mac files/apps and authenticated browser operations
Relay resolution of temporal references such as “last thing” across concurrent jobs
Checkpointing and conflict detection so an undo cannot overwrite newer owner edits
A pendant spoken receipt and dashboard audit trail for every undo attempt and outcome

proposals.user_asks: Keep working on that task after I step away, and tell me exactly what happened when it’s done.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can start something from the pendant, then go live their life. They get a clear, trustworthy completion report without babysitting the Mac or keeping the session open.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief spoken acknowledgement; planning and execution should use a cheaper planner model on the Mac and browser harness.
proposals.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge. Minutes to hours for execution is fine as long as status is trackable and completion is announced reliably.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per invocation at the relay; dominant cost is downstream planning/execution and any authenticated browser work.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated sessions and extracted data must be scoped to the task, logged with provenance, and never used for unrelated goals. Completion reports should quote sources, not raw secrets.
missing: Durable job runner that persists across relay restarts
Unified job status and receipts across Mac and browser steps
Notification path to the pendant when the relay is not actively in a voice run
Typed context service to avoid resending large context every turn

proposals.user_asks: While I’m away from my Mac, let me say ‘handle this’ and then interrupt, redirect, or ask for the exact status of that task from the pendant; have the Mac/browser continue from the last verified checkpoint and tell me what actually happened.
