proposals.model_tier: Realtime model extracts only a task envelope and sensitivity label; encryption, presence checks, and release policy are deterministic. Use a cheaper background model to summarize the sealed queue after release.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local acknowledgement in under 500 ms; release and confirmation within 5 seconds after the paired device is detected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible per task beyond one short realtime classification, roughly $0.002–$0.01; storage and cryptographic key management dominate engineering cost, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: This is specifically about keeping secrets sealed. Use device-bound keys, nonce-protected records, expiry and explicit deletion, and never put plaintext dictated content in logs, analytics, or spoken notifications. Presence must be cryptographic pairing, not merely a network IP.
missing: Pendant-side encrypted sealed-record support and a physical release gesture
Relay encrypted-at-rest queue with device-bound key exchange and expiry
USB/LTE pairing and presence attestation for the real nRF9160 and ESP32-connected setup
Mac/browser release endpoints that acknowledge exact record hashes and receipt them

proposals.user_asks: “Run this as a reversible experiment.” — Before changing my files, settings, browser state, or messages, show me a spoken prediction of the observable changes and a rollback plan; execute in an isolated snapshot or transaction where possible, then report which predicted changes actually occurred and let me revert the whole experiment with one phrase.
proposals.why_useful: The owner wants maximum access, but maximum access without a way to understand blast radius is hard to trust. A whole-experiment boundary is more useful than a per-click confirmation: it preserves speed while making multi-step changes inspectable and collectively reversible.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model frames the experiment and speaks the result; deterministic planners and shell/browser adapters perform snapshots, diffs, and rollback. Use a cheaper background model for large diffs.
proposals.latency_budget: Prediction in under 3 seconds for a short plan; execution can run asynchronously, with a compact pendant update as soon as the first verified receipt arrives.
proposals.cost_estimate: One realtime framing call plus optional background diff summarization, roughly $0.01–$0.08 depending on changed files/page state; storage for snapshots is the dominant cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Snapshots can duplicate secrets. Store locally where possible, encrypt relay-held artifacts, redact spoken diffs, expire snapshots, and make rollback idempotent. Do not pretend arbitrary external side effects (sent mail, purchases) are reversible; label them as irreversible before execution.
missing: Transaction/snapshot adapters for filesystem, macOS preferences, browser storage and app state
A cross-action experiment ID joining /plan, /execute, receipts, observations and rollback
A diff-and-rollback planner with explicit irreversible-side-effect detection
A pendant command path for “revert experiment <recent description>”

proposals.user_asks: “Use my personal lens for this.” — Let me switch, from the pendant, which private context the hive may use (personal, work, travel, or no-history), and have the relay enforce that lens consistently across its speech context, Mac actions, browser tabs, logs, and follow-up notifications until I switch it back.
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot safely wear a context-free agent everywhere. A single spoken privacy mode should prevent accidental mixing of work and personal material, rather than relying on each downstream agent to remember a preference or on the owner to explain it every turn.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model recognizes only the explicit lens switch and confirms it; enforcement is deterministic at the relay and adapters. No expensive model is needed for ordinary routing.
proposals.latency_budget: Mode change acknowledgement in under 1 second; enforcement must apply before the next transcript or action leaves the pendant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost after setup; roughly $0.001 or less per switch. Engineering cost is policy propagation and audit testing.
proposals.security_concerns: A lens must fail closed when missing or stale, be visible in every spoken confirmation, and never be inferred from location or calendar. Redact excluded context at ingestion rather than merely hiding it in prompts; retain an audit trail of mode changes without retaining excluded content.
missing: A relay-owned, versioned context-lens state with TTL and explicit reset
Ingress filtering for audio/transcripts and egress filtering for Mac/browser actions and notifications
Mac/browser adapters that expose and enforce lens-scoped app/tab/session allowlists
Pendant LED/audio confirmation and offline persistence of the selected lens

proposals.user_asks: Do that on the Mac, and if you need details, ask me.
proposals.why_useful: This is a smoother handoff for multi-step tasks: the relay captures intent, the Mac plans, and the owner only answers clarifying questions when necessary.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for intent capture; mac-planner for the workflow.
proposals.latency_budget: Intent capture should be immediate; planning can take a few seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate: one plan call plus execution. Keep the relay’s role minimal.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not execute irreversible actions without a clear plan and receipts. Keep a job record for traceability.
missing: A resolvable intent-routing mechanism (relay_route_intent is currently unresolved).
An enum-based intent contract tied to real action types (so routing can resolve).
Relay capability manifest for discoverability.

proposals.user_asks: “When my pendant is physically with my Mac, let this button press authorize the next powerful action I say—open the authenticated portal, send the prepared message, or change the setting—without another confirmation. If the pendant is not present, only prepare and report.”
proposals.why_useful: It gives the owner fast, deliberate control over high-impact remote actions while preventing a replayed voice request or a compromised relay session from acting later. The same wearable that hears the request becomes a short-lived physical authorization key.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only parses the spoken request and reports the result; the Mac planner performs the action, while browser-extension handles authenticated browser state. No expensive model is needed for the cryptographic check.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 500 ms to establish the challenge when USB-attached, then the normal 1–3 s action latency; the pendant should say “authorized” immediately and stream the result when complete.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one realtime turn plus one planner/action call, roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on the action; cryptographic challenge traffic is negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: A nonce-bound challenge must be signed by the pendant over USB or LTE and scoped to one normalized action, one Mac session, and a short expiry. Never treat mere historical pairing or an audio recording as authorization. Show a distinct LED pattern before commit and log the signed receipt; losing the pendant requires revocation.
missing: pendant challenge-response firmware and secure key storage
relay authorization verifier and nonce ledger
Mac/browser enforcement that refuses the commit without a fresh pendant signature
a physical-presence signal that works over the currently live USB serial links

proposals.user_asks: “Tell me what is actually true right now, even if the Mac, browser, and relay disagree—what changed, what is still a draft, and what evidence proves it.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has to trust a single completion message. This would reconcile independent observations: for example, the Mac reports a send attempt, the authenticated browser still shows a draft, and the relay has no receipt. It speaks the contradiction instead of confidently claiming success.
proposals.model_tier: A cheap background perception pass gathers structured observations; a judgment model compares timestamps, identities, and source reliability. Realtime only turns the final verdict into a short spoken answer.
proposals.latency_budget: 2–5 seconds for a normal live query, with an immediate “checking three sources” acknowledgement; never block the voice turn on an unavailable source.
proposals.cost_estimate: One small perception/judgment pass, approximately $0.01–$0.04 per query; browser and Mac reads dominate neither tokens nor bandwidth.
proposals.security_concerns: Only return content already authorized for the owner’s paired Mac/browser session. Preserve source timestamps and hashes rather than copying whole pages into relay memory. Explicitly say “unverified” when sources conflict or are stale; never synthesize a successful state from an action request alone.
missing: a common observation envelope with source, timestamp, object identity, and confidence
a reconciliation/judgment route that can request parallel Mac and browser reads
spoken provenance formatting and a contradiction receipt in the job ledger

proposals.user_asks: “Take this outcome, work across my Mac and my authenticated browser, and keep going through ordinary interruptions. If one step fails, use the partial result to continue, and come back with exactly what was done, what was not, and the one choice you need from me.”
proposals.why_useful: This is an outcome-level assistant rather than a brittle one-turn command: it can collect a file locally, use a logged-in web service, reconcile the returned identifiers, and recover from a dropped Mac or browser connection without making the owner repeat the whole request.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime extracts the goal and handles brief clarifications. A cheaper planner owns the durable state machine; use the vision model only for a browser/UI step that has no reliable structured action.
proposals.latency_budget: A spoken acknowledgement within 1 second; each step may take seconds or minutes. The owner can end the conversation and receive a concise completion or blocked-choice alert later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.20 per multi-step outcome, dominated by planner iterations and occasional vision calls; retries should reuse observations rather than resend full context.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only the minimum goal, action receipts, and opaque remote IDs. Every retry must be idempotency-keyed so reconnects cannot duplicate a send or purchase. A blocked destructive choice is reported, not guessed; all completed steps remain auditable and undo metadata is retained where available.
missing: durable cross-surface workflow state and idempotency keys
a coordinator that can resume after Mac/browser disconnects
event delivery to the pendant for completion or needs-attention
structured partial-result handoff between planner and browser session

proposals.user_asks: If you can’t reach the internet, save my request and try again when connectivity returns.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can speak a task once and trust the system to eventually deliver it, instead of failing silently or asking them to repeat themselves.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for immediate acknowledgement and fallback messaging; queued retry logic should live in firmware/relay and run cheaply.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1s; retry is opportunistic.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low; dominant cost is durable storage and retry attempts.
proposals.security_concerns: Queued items may contain sensitive speech. Encrypt at rest where possible and minimize payloads.
missing: Typed durable outbox for non-audio requests beyond the existing voice memo failure path
A retry policy shared between pendant and relay
Conflict handling to avoid duplicate execution when retries overlap

proposals.user_asks: “Turn what I just said into the right finished artifact—update the project file, prepare the browser form or message, and tell me exactly what changed.”
proposals.why_useful: This is the most useful missing end-to-end ability: the owner can speak an intent while away from the desk and receive a completed, inspectable result rather than a memo or a plan. The relay preserves the utterance and constraints, the Mac edits local material, and the browser handles a session the Mac agent alone cannot safely reconstruct.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay extracts the short intent and constraints; mac-planner performs the multi-step plan with the cheaper planner tier; browser harness executes authenticated browser steps; relay returns a concise spoken receipt while dashboard exposes the artifact and provenance.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 500 ms; first spoken progress within 3 s; completion can take 30–120 s asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per request depending on planner/browser turns; browser and Mac execution dominate, not the short realtime interpretation.
proposals.security_concerns: The utterance, selected local files, and browser page data leave the pendant and may cross the relay. The owner policy permits trusted execution, but the result must include exact files/pages touched, action receipts, and an easy voice undo for reversible edits; never claim completion without verification.
missing: A typed artifact-intent envelope shared by relay, mac-planner, and browser harness
A cross-surface execution journal that links each mutation to its source utterance and verification
A result handoff that can deliver a compact receipt to the pendant after the live turn

proposals.user_asks: “I’m leaving now—keep working on this task across my Mac and browser, recover from a transient failure, and tell me only when there is a real result or a decision you need from me.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently must remain in a voice turn or manually poll. This would make the pendant a true handoff point: it can launch a long, cross-surface job while the owner walks away, distinguish a recoverable failure from a decision, and deliver a useful result later.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only classifies the handoff and captures constraints; a background planner/executor and browser worker do the work; a small summarizer turns verified receipts into a spoken alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acceptance under 1 s, durable job start under 5 s, completion notification whenever finished; retries should not require the owner to reconnect.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.20 per job, dominated by multi-step planner calls and browser retries; idle waiting should cost near zero via alarms/queues.
proposals.security_concerns: Long-lived credentials and unattended mutations are the main risk. Persist least-needed job context, redact secrets from receipts, make retry idempotent, and notify on ambiguity rather than guessing. Data must be encrypted in transit and expire after completion.
missing: A real durable queue with retries and idempotency keys
Worker Cron/ Durable Object alarms or equivalent background execution
A job state machine with blocked/needs-owner states and durable event delivery
Browser and Mac leases so two workers cannot mutate the same session concurrently

proposals.user_asks: If I start a task, keep an ear on it and warn me if it stalls or needs my input.
proposals.why_useful: Completion notifications are not enough. A task can hang, fail early, or wait for a login/permission. Early warnings save time and prevent silent failure.
proposals.model_tier: background model for monitoring; realtime only to confirm the watch was started
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate confirmation, then alerts within seconds to a couple minutes depending on polling interval and urgency.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low to moderate; dominated by periodic status checks and occasional short alert generation.
proposals.security_concerns: Alert content may expose sensitive app or document names; keep summaries minimal unless the owner asks for detail. Ensure alerts are delivered only to the owner’s paired session/device.
missing: A real job-monitoring mechanism with stall heuristics (status age, no progress receipts, repeated errors)
A relay-to-pendant alert delivery implementation (could reuse the existing inbox concept)
A small policy layer to decide when to alert vs. wait

proposals.user_asks: Run a spoken hardware self-test: "Check whether my pendant audio is healthy right now."
proposals.why_useful: The owner can diagnose the actual worn device from anywhere in seconds instead of guessing whether silence comes from the microphone, LTE/USB link, Opus path, bridge, or speaker. It turns the currently attached, testable hardware into a trustworthy daily instrument and reports concrete measurements, not a generic online/offline answer.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay interprets the short request and speaks the result; mac-terminal performs the hardware probe and parses measurements deterministically; no expensive model is needed for signal analysis.
proposals.latency_budget: 20 seconds for a full test; speak an early "testing" acknowledgement within 500 ms and stream a concise result when complete.
proposals.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per invocation; dominated by one short realtime turn, with shell probes and serial capture essentially free.
proposals.security_concerns: The probe reads device diagnostics and may access the USB serial endpoints, but does not modify owner files. It must redact serial identifiers from spoken/dashboard output and clearly distinguish stale LTE health from the live USB-attached test.
missing: A Mac allowlisted hardware-test action that can flash/run the audio probe, capture serial output, and return structured metrics
A relay result schema for measured audio/uplink/bridge health rather than prose
A pendant button/LED convention for a test-in-progress state
built_from: the shipped 24 kHz audio acceptance measurements

proposals.user_asks: Let me say "Make this ready for tomorrow's client call" and have the hive prepare, but not send, everything it can find.
proposals.why_useful: One natural request would turn scattered preparation into a reviewable package: calendar details and local project context from the Mac, relevant authenticated browser pages, and a short spoken briefing on the pendant. The owner gets a useful deliverable while away from the desk without delegating the judgment or risking an external send.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles intent and clarifying one missing constraint; mac-planner and browser harness do the long multi-step collection; a cheaper background summarizer produces the packet; relay only speaks the headline and review link.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; preparation may take 1–3 minutes. The owner should receive a completion alert and be able to ask for a spoken three-item summary.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.05–$0.30 depending on browser pages and document volume; model summarization and authenticated page extraction dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: Browser sessions and local documents leave their originating surfaces only as narrowly scoped excerpts. No message, calendar invite, upload, or external send is allowed in this mode. The dashboard must show every source and generated artifact, with explicit expiry and a prominent discard control.
missing: A cross-surface preparation job that can fan out to Mac files/calendar and the authenticated browser session
A durable artifact bundle with source citations and a review-only state
A relay notification path that can announce the finished bundle while the voice session is over
A deterministic no-send policy enforced by the executor

proposals.user_asks: When I say "What am I looking at?", have the pendant and Mac jointly identify the thing in front of me and tell me only what helps me act next.
proposals.why_useful: The pendant alone has no camera and the Mac alone cannot know what the owner is pointing at. A coordinated mode would use a deliberate phone/desktop or browser capture, voice context, and local visual analysis to answer practical questions such as which cable, menu, document, or error is in view—without making the owner narrate it.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay keeps the dialogue short; mac-vision handles image grounding; mac-planner performs a follow-up read or reversible action only when requested. Use a small vision model for ordinary frames and escalate only on ambiguity.
proposals.latency_budget: First acknowledgement under 700 ms; visual answer within 5 seconds; allow a follow-up correction such as "the other one" without restarting capture.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.08 per frame, dominated by vision inference; local capture and relay transport are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Capture is strictly button- or spoken-command initiated, never ambient. Frames are ephemeral by default, not added to memory, and browser credentials/face-like content are blurred or excluded from dashboard logs. Any action inferred from the image remains a separate spoken request.
missing: A real camera source and capture contract reachable by the relay while the pendant is worn
A mac-vision endpoint that accepts an image plus the owner's utterance and returns grounded regions/confidence
A low-bandwidth image transport and retention policy
A relay dialogue state that can bind one captured frame to several follow-up questions
built_from: the pendant's existing button-triggered voice session

proposals.user_asks: Keep an eye on the thing I just asked you to do, and tell me when it’s done.
proposals.why_useful: This is the single most useful behavior: the owner can ask for work, walk away, and still get a clear completion signal without polling or staring at a screen.
proposals.model_tier: realtime for the initial promise; cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarizing completion
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement in under a second; completion notification can arrive minutes to hours later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per job after start; the expensive part is keeping context and summarizing results, which should run off the realtime tier.
proposals.security_concerns: Job status and short summaries leave the device; avoid including sensitive content in spoken alerts, and require confirmation before speaking anything potentially private out loud.
missing: A reliable completion-event path that resolves to real delivery targets
A relay-to-pendant alert delivery that uses the existing unified inbox rather than a new queue
A summary renderer that can produce a short spoken line from receipts

proposals.user_asks: Summarize what you know about what I’m working on right now, and keep it short.
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets a quick, consistent snapshot of the active project or task without dumping noisy history, perfect for voice.
proposals.model_tier: realtime for spoken summary; cheaper tier for gathering and structuring context
proposals.latency_budget: Under a second for a short summary; longer only if it must fetch fresh machine context.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate; dominated by context retrieval and summarization, not by speech.
proposals.security_concerns: Context may include sensitive data; summarize conservatively and avoid quoting private content unless the user asks.
missing: Live prompt path must use the memory projection instead of legacy context blocks
Task-scoped context selection for voice surface

proposals.user_asks: Use the Mac as a bridge right now and act on what I say, even if the pendant isn’t on LTE yet.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can test real workflows immediately: the pendant is physically connected to the Mac, so the system should be useful today, not after registration.
proposals.model_tier: realtime for intent capture; mac-planner for planning and execution
proposals.latency_budget: Fast: acknowledgement under a second; execution time depends on the task.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low to moderate; planning and execution dominate cost, not the relay.
proposals.security_concerns: Avoid interrupting active work; confirm before destructive actions.
missing: Reliable USB-bridge operational status reporting to the relay
A clear fallback policy: Mac-online path preferred when LTE is not registered

proposals.user_asks: When I say “panic stop,” stop every action this system has started, tell me exactly what was stopped, and leave a recoverable record of anything that could not be interrupted.
proposals.why_useful: A worn button and voice are the only controls the owner can reach when away from the Mac. Today an active Mac/browser job can outlive the conversation with no single owner-facing kill switch. This turns the pendant into a genuine emergency brake across relay, Mac, and browser rather than merely another status query.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime classifies the utterance and immediately issues cancellation; no model should deliberate before stopping. Background reconciliation verifies each downstream job and summarizes partial effects.
proposals.latency_budget: Begin cancellation acknowledgement in under 500 ms; reconcile all known jobs within 5 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference beyond the live turn; dominant cost is one short realtime turn and status polling for active jobs.
proposals.security_concerns: A false trigger could cancel useful work, so require the explicit phrase or a deliberate long button hold, never ordinary speech. Cancellation is safer than continuing but may leave partial mutations; retain immutable receipts and expose an undo path where available. No audio needs to leave the pendant beyond the normal turn.
missing: A relay-wide active-job registry keyed to the owner session
A cancellation fan-out from relay to Mac planner, computer-use loop, and browser command queue
A pendant emergency gesture and a spoken/LED confirmation state
A structured cancellation receipt that distinguishes cancelled, already-completed, and uninterruptible actions

proposals.user_asks: What is happening right now? Give me one concise situation report that combines my pendant connection, active Mac/browser work, queued jobs, and the last verified result, and call out contradictions instead of guessing.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must ask separate status questions and cannot tell whether silence means completion, a dead Mac, a stale browser session, or a disconnected pendant. A cross-surface truth report is uniquely valuable from a worn front door: it turns a fragmented hive into one dependable answer with explicit uncertainty.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic aggregation for health, job, and receipt facts; use the realtime model only to compress the already-collected evidence into one spoken sentence. No background model is needed.
proposals.latency_budget: Parallel probes and a spoken answer in 2 seconds when surfaces respond; state exactly which surface timed out rather than waiting indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short realtime synthesis turn per request; probe and aggregation costs are negligible. The main cost is retaining compact, timestamped receipts rather than resending full transcripts.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not read page contents or private Mac data merely for health. Scope browser evidence to URL/title/command state unless the owner explicitly asks for content. Include timestamps and freshness so a stale result cannot be presented as current.
missing: A relay aggregator that concurrently reads device health, active jobs, Mac status, browser inspection, and execution receipts
A common freshness/contradiction schema across pendant, Mac, and browser reports
A compact spoken renderer that names uncertainty and source timestamps
A live pendant health route, since the known /v1/devices/status route must be made authoritative for this USB/LTE split

proposals.user_asks: Only carry out this sensitive request while I am physically holding my pendant: have it prove my presence, then let the Mac and authenticated browser act, and tell me if the proof expires before completion.
proposals.why_useful: A spoken voice session alone is not a reliable presence signal when the owner is away from the Mac. This would make the pendant a physical authorization token that spans relay, Mac, and browser without imposing confirmation on ordinary reversible work. It is especially useful for an owner who wants maximum access but still wants a deliberate boundary for rare, consequential operations.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime identifies the requested presence-bound operation; cryptographic verification, expiry, and enforcement are deterministic. The model only explains the resulting receipt.
proposals.latency_budget: Challenge/response under 300 ms over the live USB path and under 2 s over LTE; leases should expire automatically after 60 s or completion.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost; engineering cost is key provisioning, challenge verification, and enforcement adapters. No recurring API cost beyond a normal voice turn.
proposals.security_concerns: Private keys must never leave the pendant. Bind each lease to a nonce, operation digest, target surface, and expiry to prevent replay or confused-deputy use. A lost pendant needs revocation through the relay. This is opt-in per utterance and must not silently gate normal actions.
missing: A pendant secure-element or protected key slot and firmware challenge-response command
Relay-side operation-digest leases and revocation
Mac and browser adapters that refuse lease-bound actions when the lease is absent or expired
A visible/haptic/LED acknowledgement that the physical proof succeeded

proposals.user_asks: “If that task finishes, tell me on my pendant even if I’ve stopped talking.”
proposals.why_useful: This is the biggest quality-of-life feature: the owner can fire off a long Mac job and walk away. No polling, no staring at a screen, and no lost updates if the link drops.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial voice command; a cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial acknowledgement under a second; completion alert can arrive minutes later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per event; the expensive part is job monitoring. Most of the time should run in a cheaper background context or a relay worker, not the realtime model.
proposals.security_concerns: Alert text must be accurate and sourced from job status. Sensitive content should be redacted or require confirmation before being spoken aloud.
missing: A real completion-event delivery path (relay_event_push is unresolved).
A durable watch mechanism in the relay for job state transitions.
A delivery target that can render speech on the pendant without storing audio by default.

proposals.user_asks: “What’s the status of the thing you sent to my Mac?”
proposals.why_useful: Owners ask this constantly. It should work even when the Mac is asleep and should speak a concise, truthful answer.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime, since it’s a quick conversational check-in.
proposals.latency_budget: Sub-second; no Mac round trip.
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low; reads existing relay job records.
proposals.security_concerns: Never summarize beyond the tool output. If the status is unknown or failed, say so verbatim.

proposals.user_asks: “Tell me what’s going on with my setup right now.”
proposals.why_useful: A quick health snapshot helps the owner trust the system: what’s online, what’s paired, and what’s missing, spoken in a friendly way.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for quick spoken summary; deeper diagnosis should go to a cheaper tier.
proposals.latency_budget: Under two seconds for a summary; deeper checks can be deferred.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low; relies on existing status endpoints and job records.
proposals.security_concerns: Avoid leaking sensitive account details; only report operational state.
missing: A reliable pendant registration/status endpoint (previously 404).
A relay self-capabilities endpoint for inventory.

proposals.user_asks: “I just finished a conversation. Turn the commitments I spoke into the right follow-ups: check my calendar and authenticated browser context, draft the needed messages and reminders on my Mac, and tell me exactly what is waiting for my approval.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can leave a conversation with actionable follow-ups without reconstructing details later. The pendant supplies the fresh spoken commitments, the browser supplies context the relay cannot see, and the Mac produces concrete drafts rather than a generic transcript. It preserves control over sending while eliminating the clerical work.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime extracts only commitments and urgency from the utterance; mac-planner performs the slower cross-app planning, browser-extension/mac-vision gathers evidence, and a cheaper background model normalizes duplicate commitments.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; gather context and create drafts within 30–90 seconds. The pendant can speak a queued completion summary after the session.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per invocation depending on browser/vision turns; most cost is Mac/browser evidence gathering, not realtime speech.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar, authenticated pages, and spoken private content leave their local surfaces only to the relay/orchestrated agents. Never send or delete without the owner's existing policy/explicit approval; attach source snippets and confidence so inferred commitments are visible.
missing: A commitment-extraction and deduplication job that links one voice utterance to browser/calendar evidence
A cross-surface draft bundle with per-artifact provenance and approval state
A single completion/approval summary that can be delivered to the pendant inbox
built_from: mac-planner action types create_reminder, browser_read_page, type_text

proposals.user_asks: “While I’m away from my Mac, watch the specific page and local app state I name. If the condition becomes true, prepare the next action, but wait until I tap the pendant to carry it out; if it becomes false again, discard the stale plan.”
proposals.why_useful: This gives the owner a safe hands-free trigger for changing real-world conditions rather than a one-shot command. The important behavior is state validity: a plan is based on a fresh observation, expires when the observed state changes, and requires only a physical tap at the final moment.
proposals.model_tier: A cheap scheduled/watch evaluator compares page and screen observations; mac-planner creates the candidate action; realtime is used only to explain the trigger and receive the tap.
proposals.latency_budget: Checks on the configured interval; speak or queue an alert within 10 seconds of a qualifying transition, then execute within 5 seconds of a tap while the Mac/browser is reachable.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.02 per check depending on whether text inspection or visual reasoning is needed; the dominant cost is repeated visual/browser capture.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents and screen images remain scoped to the watch. The tap is an explicit physical commit, and every queued action carries an observation timestamp, expiry, and target fingerprint to prevent acting on stale UI.
missing: A watch type that can combine browser page predicates with Mac app/screen predicates
Versioned observation snapshots and invalidation of queued plans when state changes
Pendant tap-to-commit delivery for a pending, attested action

proposals.user_asks: “If you cannot complete my request on the first surface, recover across the hive: use the browser if the Mac app is unavailable, use the Mac if the browser session is unavailable, and give me one honest spoken result that says what was tried, what actually changed, and what remains.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a disconnected Mac, expired browser session, or changed UI turns a useful request into a dead end. This makes the system's physical diversity useful: it can route around a failed node instead of pretending success, while the owner receives one concise outcome rather than debugging logs.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime classifies the request and speaks the immediate acknowledgement; a background planner runs the fallback graph and a small verifier compares receipts and observations. Use vision only on the branch that needs it.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; fallback attempts complete within 1–2 minutes, with a queued pendant update when the session has ended.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.10 for a failed-first-surface invocation; cost is dominated by extra browser/Mac attempts and verification, so stop after a bounded fallback graph.
proposals.security_concerns: Fallbacks must not silently broaden scope: preserve the original target, arguments, and owner policy across surfaces. Report partial completion and never claim success from an attempted action; include receipts and before/after evidence in the dashboard.
missing: A capability graph that maps equivalent operations across Mac and browser surfaces
Cross-surface idempotency keys and a verifier that detects partial/duplicate mutations
A user-facing failure/partial-success summary renderer tied to the existing pendant inbox

proposals.user_asks: “I’m away from my Mac. Tell me exactly what I was in the middle of, gather the relevant browser and Mac state, and let me resume it from the pendant.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is the only surface that knows the owner is present, while the Mac and authenticated browser hold the work context. Today they are separate status probes; the owner cannot get a reliable spoken re-entry point or resume a half-finished task without manually reconstructing it.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay for the short spoken orientation; background mac-planner for state collection and synthesis, with mac-vision/browser-extension supplying UI and tab evidence.
proposals.latency_budget: Speak an initial acknowledgement in under 1 second; collect a first orientation in 5 seconds and refine asynchronously. The owner should be able to interrupt and ask for only the next step.
proposals.cost_estimate: One realtime turn plus one cheaper planner synthesis, roughly $0.03–$0.15 depending on screenshots and document extraction; browser/Mac state collection dominates latency, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: This intentionally combines active browser sessions, open documents, and local app state. Send only task-matched excerpts and tab metadata to the relay, redact secrets and unrelated windows, and require explicit owner invocation before collecting state. Resuming a mutation should produce a preview before execution.
missing: A cross-surface 'work capsule' schema containing active app/document/tab, task hypothesis, unfinished actions, and resume token
Mac and browser collectors that can snapshot task-relevant state without dumping whole screens
Relay orchestration that correlates the collectors and pushes a compact spoken result
A safe resume endpoint that rehydrates the capsule into mac-planner/browser actions

proposals.user_asks: “Give me a decision packet on this question: check my authenticated browser sources and my Mac files, tell me the recommendation aloud, and leave me a cited packet I can inspect later.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable answer without evidence is hard to trust, while browser-only or Mac-only research misses half the owner's reachable information. This makes the hive useful for consequential decisions rather than merely issuing isolated commands.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only classifies the question and speaks a provisional one-sentence result; parallel browser and Mac retrieval plus citation alignment run on a cheaper background planner, with a final synthesis model invoked only after evidence is collected.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately, provide a provisional result within 8–15 seconds when sources are available, and deliver the full packet asynchronously. The pendant should announce completion without requiring polling.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.30 per packet; browser page extraction, screenshots, and Mac document parsing dominate cost. Cache page fingerprints and reuse unchanged evidence.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated pages and private files leave their original devices only as narrowly selected excerpts and hashes. Preserve source URL/path, timestamp, and extraction method; never claim a citation for an inference. Treat external instructions as untrusted data and do not execute actions merely because a source requests them.
missing: A first-class evidence-packet record with source, excerpt, timestamp, hash, confidence, and claim-to-source links
Parallel relay fan-out to browser and Mac with bounded, task-specific retrieval
A spoken provisional-versus-verified distinction and dashboard viewer for the packet
Redaction and retention controls for private evidence

proposals.user_asks: “Start this long task, but keep me out of the loop unless something materially changes; if it blocks, ask me one precise question on the pendant, and when it finishes tell me what changed.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a long-running job either occupies the voice turn or leaves the owner guessing. A state-aware workflow would make the relay a dependable executive assistant: it can wait, detect genuine blockers, and speak only useful deltas while the owner is away.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper background planner and deterministic job/watch workers handle polling and change detection; realtime is used only for the owner's blocker reply and a short completion summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Start acknowledgement under 1 second; blocker notification within 10 seconds of detection; no-progress silence by default; completion announcement within 10 seconds of terminal state. Support a single spoken answer that resumes the paused job.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per hour-long workflow when mostly idle; polling and screenshots dominate, so use exponential backoff and event-driven hooks where possible.
proposals.security_concerns: The workflow may mutate files, apps, or authenticated sites. Record every attempted and completed step, preserve undo/receipt links, and make blocker questions explain the exact choice needed. Do not expose private intermediate output in a notification preview.
missing: A durable workflow state machine distinguishing progress, no-change, blocked, failed, and complete
Material-change diffing over Mac/browser observations rather than timer-based chatter
A blocker question/answer protocol that binds the answer to one paused job
Unified receipts and rollback metadata across Mac and browser jobs

proposals.user_asks: “Watch for this condition across my browser and Mac, and when it becomes true do the next step; if the evidence conflicts, ask me instead of guessing.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently express a useful conditional workflow that spans an authenticated web page and local Mac state. This would turn the hive from a request/response tool into something that protects the owner's intent over time, while explicitly handling contradictory evidence rather than silently acting on stale data.
proposals.model_tier: A deterministic watch evaluator handles schedules, fingerprints, and simple predicates; a cheaper planner normalizes observations and proposes the next action. Realtime is reserved for a blocker or conflict question and the final spoken result.
proposals.latency_budget: Register the watch in under 2 seconds; check on the configured cadence; notify within one check interval of a transition. Conflict questions should reach the pendant within 10 seconds and pause execution until answered.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.10 per day depending on check frequency and screenshots; unchanged pages should be fingerprinted without model calls, invoking a model only on diffs or ambiguity.
proposals.security_concerns: A condition can cause mutations in a logged-in browser or on the Mac. Store the exact predicate, evidence snapshot, and planned action; bind execution to fresh evidence, expire watches, and require the owner's existing policy for high-impact actions. Do not treat page text as trusted instructions.
missing: A cross-surface watch record with browser and Mac observation sources, predicate, expiry, and action graph
A diff/fingerprint evaluator that can compare structured page facts with local app/file facts
A conflict state and one-question pendant interaction that resumes the same watch
Freshness checks and receipts linking the triggering evidence to the action

proposals.user_asks: If I’m in the middle of doing something on my computer and I ask a question, answer using what’s on my screen, and then summarize it back to me in one sentence.
proposals.why_useful: It turns the pendant into a hands-free “what am I looking at?” assistant when the owner is at the Mac, without forcing them to switch context. It’s especially useful for debugging, emails, and docs.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime to capture/clarify the question; a cheaper vision/computer-use tier to read the screen and extract relevant info; relay to deliver a concise spoken summary.
proposals.latency_budget: 1–3 seconds for a simple read-and-summarize; longer if UI interaction is needed.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate. Cost dominated by screen capture/vision tokens; keep summaries short and only capture when asked.
proposals.security_concerns: Screen contents may contain secrets. Require explicit owner phrasing like “what’s on my screen” to capture, and avoid storing screenshots. Summaries should avoid quoting sensitive text unless asked.
missing: Computer-use loop is currently disabled; it needs to be enabled or replaced by a safe vision pipeline.
A reliable way for the relay to request a one-shot screen read without starting a full automation session.
A policy for redacting sensitive content from summaries.

proposals.user_asks: “Take care of this, but if the result differs from what you expected, stop and tell me exactly what changed.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets reliable automation rather than a blind command: the pendant captures the intent, the Mac or authenticated browser performs it, and the relay compares the observed result with the requested outcome before reporting success. This is especially valuable when the owner is away from the Mac and cannot inspect the screen.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to normalize the spoken goal and narrate exceptions; use the background Mac planner for planning and the browser/computer-use tier for execution and verification.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; allow 10–60 seconds for execution. Do not speak “done” until an independent postcondition check finishes.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn plus one planner invocation; roughly $0.02–$0.10 depending on the task, with browser/computer-use steps dominating.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must retain the owner’s exact success condition and an execution receipt, but should return only the minimum evidence needed in speech. A mismatch must never be narrated as success. Existing owner policy permits reversible actions without prompting; irreversible actions follow the owner’s established policy rather than inventing a new gate.
missing: A first-class postcondition/verifier in the Mac planner that accepts an explicit expected outcome and emits pass/fail/unknown evidence
A result schema that carries observed state and evidence through the job lifecycle
Pendant delivery of a mismatch explanation through the existing alert inbox

proposals.user_asks: “Give me a private heads-up when something important needs me, but do not interrupt me for routine progress.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can stay away from the Mac without missing a genuinely urgent change. The relay and browser/Mac surfaces classify events, collapse repeated updates, and deliver only an actionable exception to the worn device; routine completions remain available without turning the pendant into a noisy notification stream.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background classifier for event ranking and deduplication; use realtime only when converting a selected event into one short spoken sentence.
proposals.latency_budget: Classify within one polling/check cycle; deliver a selected alert within 2 seconds of its report. Suppress unchanged and low-confidence events.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low ongoing cost: background checks and classification dominate; realtime is invoked only for delivered alerts, roughly $0.005–$0.03 per alert.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents and Mac state must remain scoped to the originating task and never leak into unrelated voice turns. Every alert needs provenance, urgency, expiry, and a reason for interruption so the owner can audit false alarms.
missing: A shared urgency-and-deduplication policy spanning Mac, browser, and relay reports
A private delivery mode with haptic/LED signalling distinct from spoken playback
A durable event identity so the same change is not announced by multiple surfaces

proposals.user_asks: “Use what I just told you for this task, but do not remember it or let it appear in future conversations.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can safely dictate sensitive one-off details while still getting cross-surface help. The relay would mark the utterance and all derived browser/Mac artifacts as task-confined, preventing accidental promotion into durable memory or unrelated prompts.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles the explicit privacy directive and attaches a short-lived scope token; downstream agents use cheaper models under that token. No extra model call is needed unless the spoken directive is ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Apply the scope before dispatching any downstream work, within the normal conversational turn. Expire it at task completion or a fixed short TTL.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible inference overhead; the main cost is carrying a compact scope token and filtering context. No background model is required.
proposals.security_concerns: The scope must cover transcripts, planner prompts, browser findings, receipts, logs, and derived memory—not merely the final answer. It needs an explicit exception for operational metadata (job ID, failure reason) and a deletion audit so the owner can trust that sensitive content was not retained.
missing: A conversation/task privacy lease propagated across relay, Mac, browser, and memory services
Write-time filtering and deletion for transcripts, browser findings, receipts, and derived facts
A spoken confirmation when a downstream surface cannot honor the lease

proposals.user_asks: When you finish something on my behalf, let me say “undo that” and have you reverse the last reversible change, even if it touched both my Mac and a browser tab.
proposals.why_useful: A wearable assistant becomes safe to use at conversational speed when mistakes are recoverable without finding the right app or remembering what happened. The relay can identify the exact completed job, explain any irreversible portion, and dispatch compensating actions across surfaces.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the short undo utterance and selects the latest job; a cheaper background planner derives a compensation plan from action receipts; Mac/browser agents execute and verify it.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 500 ms; begin reversal within 2 s; completion may take as long as the original job, with a short pendant result and durable inbox fallback.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per undo depending on whether compensation needs planning; latency and cost are dominated by receipt interpretation and postcondition verification, not the spoken turn.
proposals.security_concerns: The system must never claim an irreversible send, purchase, deletion, or external side effect was undone. Every action needs before/after evidence, a reversibility class, and an explicit partial-undo report. Receipt data may contain URLs and document names, so dashboard retention should be bounded.
missing: A durable before-state/compensation record for each Mac and browser action
A compensation planner and verification loop
A single undo endpoint that can correlate the latest job across relay, Mac, and browser
A user-visible distinction between fully reversed, partially reversed, and irreversible

proposals.user_asks: What was the thing I saw about [topic]? Search my open and recently used browser pages and my Mac files, then tell me the answer with where each piece came from.
proposals.why_useful: Today web search can find public information, but the owner's useful context is often behind their own browser sessions or in local files. This would make the pendant a truthful memory of the owner's working world rather than a generic search box, while preserving citations so an uncertain match is obvious.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay extracts the topic and gives a concise answer; browser and Mac retrieval run in parallel with a cheaper model for ranking and deduplication; realtime is used only to narrate the final evidence-backed result.
proposals.latency_budget: Speak an acknowledgement immediately; return a first answer in 3–8 seconds and continue with a later alert if local indexing or a locked browser tab takes longer.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.12 per query, mostly retrieval/reranking and any Mac planner turn; a local text index would reduce both cost and latency after initial indexing.
proposals.security_concerns: Never send private page or file contents to public web search. Retrieval must be scoped to explicitly requested personal sources, redact secrets from the spoken summary, retain source URLs/paths only as long as needed, and clearly say when a source could not be opened.
missing: A Mac-side local full-text index with permission-aware file and browser-history connectors
A browser command to export searchable page text and timestamps from the owner's authenticated session
A relay retrieval/ranking endpoint that merges Mac and browser evidence with provenance
A compact spoken citation format and dashboard transcript showing exact excerpts

proposals.user_asks: Put me back into my work context from yesterday.
proposals.why_useful: The owner should be able to leave the Mac, use another machine, or recover after a crash without manually reconstructing apps, browser tabs, documents, and the exact page positions that mattered. A worn-device request can restore a meaningful working state while the owner is away, then report what could not be recovered.
proposals.model_tier: A background Mac agent captures and normalizes context snapshots; realtime only resolves the spoken snapshot name and gives a result. The Mac planner restores apps/files and the browser extension restores authenticated tabs, with computer vision reserved for pages whose URL/state is insufficient.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; restore the first useful state in 5–15 seconds and continue asynchronously for large sessions. Speak a compact list of restored and skipped items.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.20 per restore, dominated by planner/vision turns; snapshot storage and local indexing are the larger ongoing costs, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Snapshots can expose private URLs, document names, and scroll context. Store them encrypted on the Mac, keep only explicit named snapshots plus bounded retention, never replay passwords or form contents, and make the spoken result omit secrets. A restore must not silently submit or send anything.
missing: A Mac context snapshot service for app windows, file URLs, browser tabs, scroll/selection metadata, and timestamps
A named snapshot store and diff format shared by Mac and relay
Browser extension save/restore commands for authenticated tabs without serializing cookies
A restore planner with idempotent actions and per-item receipts
A pendant command/result path that can survive the owner walking away

proposals.user_asks: “If I say ‘that’s wrong’ right after you summarize a result, fix the task or roll it back.”
proposals.why_useful: Voice-first correction turns the pendant into a real control surface: the owner can recover from mistakes quickly without digging into apps or logs.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for interpreting the correction; mac-planner for choosing a safe rollback or edit; cheaper tier for audit trail.
proposals.latency_budget: Under ~2 seconds to acknowledge; rollback execution depends on the job but should be queued immediately.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low for the voice interpretation and job lookup; moderate if it triggers a new plan and execute cycle.
proposals.security_concerns: A rollback is a destructive action. Require confirmation for high-impact changes and rely on receipts/audit logs to prove what changed.
missing: A standardized mapping from natural-language corrections to actionable rollback/edit operations
Reliable job receipts rich enough to reconstruct side effects
A safe default strategy when multiple changes are eligible for rollback

proposals.user_asks: “I’m away from my Mac. Tell me exactly what I was in the middle of, across my Mac, browser, and pendant, and let me say ‘continue’ to pick it back up.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant currently starts new conversations, but it cannot reconstruct a truthful working set from the other surfaces. This would make the wearable a reliable handoff point: current app and window, active browser tab and page state, unfinished Mac jobs, recent owner-scoped facts, and device connectivity become one short spoken answer. “Continue” would resume the identified reversible workflow rather than forcing the owner to remember which surface held it.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model only for the short spoken synthesis and disambiguation; a cheaper background planner should gather and normalize the context, while mac-planner performs the resumed workflow.
proposals.latency_budget: First answer under 3 seconds when Mac and browser are online; up to 10 seconds for a fresh cross-surface snapshot. Resume acknowledgement under 2 seconds, with asynchronous progress thereafter.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per handoff, dominated by one realtime turn; context gathering and job polling should use cheap non-realtime calls.
proposals.security_concerns: The answer must only include facts scoped to voice and the current owner session, never arbitrary browser page contents. Resuming must be limited to the previously identified workflow and produce an auditable job receipt; destructive or external-send steps should be surfaced as pending rather than silently inferred.
missing: A cross-surface context assembler that joins machine context, browser state, live jobs, and projected memory into a stable checkpoint
A durable checkpoint identity and resume endpoint mapping one spoken ‘continue’ to the exact planner goal and prior constraints
Mac/browser adapters that report the current task, not just raw tabs or installed applications

proposals.user_asks: “Don’t just tell me the Mac task finished—verify the result independently and tell me what is actually true.”
proposals.why_useful: Planner success is not the same as world-state success: an app may have rejected a save, a browser command may have acted on the wrong tab, or a network request may still be pending. The relay should commission a separate perception pass after an action, compare the observed state with the requested outcome, and speak a calibrated result such as verified, partially verified, or could not verify. This is the single most valuable trust feature because it prevents the owner from acting on a confident but false completion report while away from the screen.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background perception and deterministic checks first; realtime is used only to explain the verdict in one sentence or ask a narrowly scoped follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial acknowledgement under 2 seconds; verification within 5–15 seconds depending on app/browser state, with an asynchronous pendant update for slower checks.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per verified action, dominated by screenshots or page extraction and only occasional model adjudication; deterministic receipts should handle the common case.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification may inspect private screens and authenticated pages, so retain only hashes, selected evidence, and redacted snippets. Never claim verified from a planner receipt alone. If evidence conflicts, say so and preserve both the requested intent and observed state for audit.
missing: A post-execution verification contract linking requested outcome assertions to concrete observable predicates
A faculty-perception endpoint that can inspect Mac/browser state after execution and return evidence with confidence
A relay-owned verdict record and pendant delivery path that distinguishes complete, partial, failed, and unverified

proposals.user_asks: “Pin this thought to whatever I’m currently looking at, and bring it back when I return to that page or file.”
proposals.why_useful: A spoken idea is usually lost because the owner cannot type while wearing the pendant. This is not another audio memo: the relay should transcribe the utterance, identify the active Mac document or authenticated browser page, store a short semantic note with that entity and surface scope, and later surface it when that same work context returns. It turns the worn device into a context-aware annotation tool rather than an inbox of orphaned recordings.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model performs concise transcription/entity clarification; a cheaper background model extracts a title, entities, and retrieval keywords. No expensive model is needed on recall unless the owner asks for a synthesis.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the pin in under 2 seconds; attach it within 8 seconds when the Mac/browser is online. If the target cannot be identified, retain the note as unassociated and say that plainly.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per pin, mostly transcription plus a small extraction call; retrieval should be deterministic keyword/entity matching.
proposals.security_concerns: Page titles, document names, and note contents may be sensitive. Store only the minimum excerpt, encrypt at rest, scope facts to voice/mac/browser, and never attach to a page or file based on a weak match without saying “I’m not sure what you meant.” Browser-originated content must remain a separate low-trust memory tier.
missing: A live-turn call to the existing scoped memory projection/store
A Mac/browser ‘current work entity’ endpoint returning stable document/page identifiers and confidence
An entity-linked pin record plus a trigger that surfaces matching pins when the owner revisits the context

proposals.user_asks: If a task needs my approval or extra info, ask me at the right moment, even after the session ends.
proposals.why_useful: This turns stalled jobs into a smooth conversation. The owner doesn’t have to remember to check; the system prompts them when it’s actually blocked, and only for what’s needed.
proposals.model_tier: Background tier monitors and detects needs_attention; realtime handles the follow-up question when the owner responds.
proposals.latency_budget: Monitoring can be slow; once blocked, the prompt should arrive within a few seconds to a minute depending on connectivity.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by periodic job-state checks and a second short conversation turn.
proposals.security_concerns: Prompts may reveal sensitive context; keep them minimal and avoid reading content unless requested. Confirm before doing anything destructive.
missing: A reliable delivery channel for needs_attention events to pendant/phone/dashboard.
An implemented relay event API (current relay_event_push is schema-only).
A policy for how long to keep blocked prompts and how to avoid duplicate nags.

proposals.user_asks: “Make this a one-sentence decision for me: compare the document on my Mac, the relevant authenticated browser page, and my previous notes, tell me what conflicts, and recommend what I should do.”
proposals.why_useful: Today each surface can be queried, but nobody fuses local files, live browser state, and durable memory into a grounded conflict report. This would turn the pendant into a decision front door while preserving evidence and avoiding a vague chatbot answer.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to clarify the owner's question; use mac-planner and browser automation for collection, then a background faculty-judgement pass for comparison and recommendation.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; gather in 10–45 seconds; speak a one-sentence recommendation first and queue evidence for follow-up.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.03–$0.15 per invocation, dominated by planner/vision turns and browser extraction; no need to resend full documents to the realtime model.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated browser content and local files leave their surfaces and enter the relay's job context. Keep source locators and hashes rather than duplicating full content where possible; never claim a conflict without quoting both source snippets. No destructive action occurs without a separate request.
missing: A cross-surface evidence bundle/job schema that can reference Mac files, browser pages, and memory facts without flattening everything into the realtime prompt
A faculty-judgement comparison worker with provenance-aware contradiction output
A spoken-result plus dashboard evidence view

proposals.user_asks: “Keep working on that investigation while I walk away. If you hit an ambiguity, ask me one short question on the pendant; let me answer and continue without restarting or losing the work.”
proposals.why_useful: The current system can queue work and eventually report completion, but a long Mac/browser task either blocks the conversation or forces the owner to restart after an ambiguity. This makes the wearable a real remote control for an ongoing agent rather than a one-shot command button.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background planner/computer-use tiers for execution; use realtime only for the short clarification exchange and final spoken update.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; ambiguity question within 5 seconds of detection; resume within 2 seconds of the owner's answer; tolerate multi-minute total execution.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.05–$0.30 per task, mainly planner/computer-use turns; clarification turns are small and should not resend the whole job transcript.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must bind every answer to the exact paused job and expire unanswered questions. Do not let a stale spoken answer mutate a later job. Browser pages and local files remain in the job's existing security boundary; dashboard should show the pending question and action history.
missing: A resumable job state machine with explicit pause/question/resume transitions and a compact state checkpoint
A relay-to-pendant question channel and answer correlation that works after the original voice session ends
Planner support for returning a single ambiguity instead of guessing
A user-visible timeline showing what was done before and after the answer

proposals.user_asks: “Undo the last thing you did for me—wherever it happened—and tell me exactly what was restored.”
proposals.why_useful: Computer and browser actions can span apps, tabs, files, and settings, yet the owner has no single spoken recovery command. A durable inverse-action record would make the system safer to trust and dramatically reduce the cost of a mistaken voice command.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic inverse handlers first; use a background planner only to assemble a multi-step rollback. Realtime should identify the target receipt and speak the result, not reason over raw action history.
proposals.latency_budget: Resolve the most recent eligible receipt in under 1 second; execute a simple inverse in under 5 seconds; for compound rollback, report progress and finish within 30 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for typed inverse handlers; $0.01–$0.10 when a planner must reconstruct a rollback. Storage and receipt indexing dominate rather than model tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Some operations are inherently irreversible (sending mail, external purchases, destructive deletes). Mark them non-undoable instead of pretending. Store inverse data locally where possible, redact secrets, bind rollback to the original job and owner session, and provide a spoken preview for ambiguous multi-action undo.
missing: Receipt records need explicit inverse operations and before-state snapshots, not just success text
Browser and Mac action adapters that expose atomic undo/restore endpoints
A deterministic selection rule for 'last thing' across concurrent jobs and surfaces
A rollback result that the pendant inbox can deliver after a dropped connection

proposals.user_asks: What happened to the thing I asked you to do?
proposals.why_useful: A quick spoken status check reduces anxiety and prevents duplicate actions. It’s perfect for voice: short, immediate, and reversible.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only; it’s a short read.
proposals.latency_budget: Fast, ideally under a second; no need to wake other surfaces if job status is already recorded.
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low. One status read and a short spoken reply.
proposals.security_concerns: Status should name the job in a user-friendly way and avoid exposing sensitive paths or content unless requested.
missing: A stable way to reference the last job (aliasing "that thing" to jobId) across turns if context is thin

proposals.user_asks: Run a quick pendant-to-Mac audio check and tell me if the link is healthy.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can verify the wearable setup before a demo or work session, catching mic, bridge, or pipeline issues early.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for guidance; diagnostics can be automated without heavy reasoning.
proposals.latency_budget: A few seconds end-to-end; short spoken steps if manual intervention is needed.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low. A small diagnostic payload and a brief report.
proposals.security_concerns: Diagnostics should avoid recording real content; use synthetic audio and discard it after the check.
missing: A defined diagnostic verb on the USB bridge and relay pipeline to run loopback tests
Permissioned endpoint to invoke bridge work when attached

proposals.user_asks: Move this conversation to my Mac, keep the context and unfinished plan, and let me continue there (or bring the result back to my pendant).
proposals.why_useful: The owner should not have to repeat a long spoken request when they reach the Mac. This creates a real handoff between the worn front door and the machine with the browser session, rather than treating each surface as a separate chat.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the handoff command and a short acknowledgement; mac-planner performs the work; a cheaper background summarizer compresses the transcript and pending decisions.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant in under 1 second; make the Mac session available within 3 seconds; later work may be asynchronous.
proposals.cost_estimate: About one realtime turn plus one inexpensive summarization call per handoff; the dominant cost is the context compression, not the relay acknowledgement.
proposals.security_concerns: The handoff must preserve the owner's existing authorization but not broadcast private browser contents to an untrusted surface. Require an explicit target (Mac versus pendant), expire handoff tokens, and redact secrets from the summary. No destructive action should be inferred merely because a conversation moved surfaces.
missing: A durable conversation-handoff object containing transcript summary, unresolved questions, planned actions, and target surface
A Mac-side endpoint/UI to claim a handoff and return progress or a result
A pendant-visible return path for the final result, beyond ordinary job completion alerts

proposals.user_asks: Use my already-open browser session to check this, but do not send the page or its sensitive contents through the relay; tell me only the answer and what action, if any, is needed.
proposals.why_useful: The browser can reach authenticated information while the relay is the always-awake voice front door, but today a browser result is effectively treated as ordinary relay context. A privacy-preserving answer capsule would let the owner use private sessions without making the relay a copy of every page.
proposals.model_tier: A small local browser-side extractor computes a narrowly typed answer; the realtime relay only verbalizes that answer. Use the expensive model only when the extractor cannot map the page to the requested fields.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds for a simple page predicate or field extraction; fall back to an asynchronous job for a complex page.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low for structured extraction; occasional model cost for ambiguous pages. Bandwidth and storage fall substantially because page HTML and screenshots do not leave the Mac.
proposals.security_concerns: The browser extension must enforce an allowlisted output schema and never return cookies, tokens, full DOM, screenshots, or unrelated nearby fields. Display an audit record locally showing exactly which fields were released. The owner must be able to revoke the capsule.
missing: A browser-local extraction primitive that returns typed fields or predicates rather than page text
A relay contract for schema-constrained, redacted result capsules
Per-session data-retention and revocation controls for browser capsules
built_from: browser_* action types including browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_read_page, browser_list_tabs

proposals.user_asks: Do not interrupt me for every update; learn my interruption rules and deliver one short, ranked digest when something truly matters, based on what I am doing on the Mac and what is waiting in my browser.
proposals.why_useful: The wearable is uniquely able to reach the owner while away, but unsolicited speech is costly and annoying. A policy-driven interrupt arbiter would combine job completions, page watches, and Mac state into one decision instead of making each subsystem compete for the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic urgency, quiet-hours, deduplication, and active-application rules first; use a cheap background model only to rank genuinely ambiguous items. Realtime is reserved for the final spoken digest.
proposals.latency_budget: New alerts should be classified in under 500 ms; a digest should be available on the next button press or within 2 seconds of a high-urgency event.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for rule-based events, with occasional low-cost ranking. This avoids paying a realtime turn for every background completion.
proposals.security_concerns: The arbiter must never infer that a low-priority browser or work item is safe to speak aloud in public. Store policies and sensitivity labels, expose a local audit trail, and make the owner able to mute or clear the queue physically. Do not silently change an action's execution policy.
missing: A single event bus that accepts job, watch, browser, and Mac-context events
A persistent interruption-policy model with quiet hours, sensitivity, deduplication, and escalation rules
A priority-aware delivery scheduler that can target the existing pendant inbox without speaking immediately
A feedback loop recording skip, replay, and interrupt outcomes without treating silence as consent

proposals.user_asks: If my Mac is online, use it to do the heavy lifting, but keep the voice interaction snappy.
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets fast conversational control without paying realtime costs for multi-step planning, browsing, or long workflows.
proposals.model_tier: realtime to interpret and hand off; planner tier for multi-step execution
proposals.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge and hand off; variable for completion.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by Mac planning/execution; relay cost is minimal routing and status updates.
proposals.security_concerns: Handing off should preserve the owner’s wording and intent; avoid expanding scope. High-impact actions should still respect existing confirmation rules.
missing: A reliable, explicit relay routing tool that resolves to real action types/enums (current relay_route_intent schema is a stub)
A stable way to report the chosen plan back to the relay for logging and user confirmation in complex cases

proposals.user_asks: Run a quick pendant and bridge audio self-check over USB while I’m at my Mac, and tell me what’s broken.
proposals.why_useful: This is the fastest path to trust: a daily-wear device needs a one-minute confidence check that audio, decoding, and the USB chain are healthy.
proposals.model_tier: realtime for spoken guidance; local tools or firmware for measurements
proposals.latency_budget: Under a minute end-to-end; results summarized in one sentence.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low; dominated by a short capture/playback loop and metrics collection.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio captured during a test could contain speech. The test should use synthetic tones/loops and avoid storing user audio.
missing: A device skill to run a self-test and report measured counters (decode/encode timing, packet loss, tx_starved)
A Mac-side tool to command the bridge and gather results over USB serial
A relay-visible status endpoint for the test results

proposals.user_asks: Let me start a task on the pendant, pause it, and continue the exact same conversation on my Mac (or resume it on the pendant) without repeating myself or risking the action twice.
proposals.why_useful: The owner is often away from the Mac. Today a voice session and a Mac job are separate worlds: moving between them loses conversational state or invites duplicate execution. Seamless migration would make the wearable, relay, and Mac feel like one reliable assistant rather than three endpoints.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short spoken handoff and intent extraction; a cheaper background model summarizes the session and reconstructs context when the surface changes. The Mac planner remains responsible for planning and execution.
proposals.latency_budget: A handoff acknowledgement under 500 ms; migration state available within 2 s. No model call is needed for a simple resume if the prior normalized intent and job state are already stored.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per migration; dominated by one small background summarization call only when the context exceeds the compact transcript/state record.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must bind a migrated session to the authenticated device/account and never expose the transcript to an unpaired surface. Every mutating action needs a stable idempotency key, with the user-visible state distinguishing planned, started, and completed rather than claiming success from a handoff.
