missing: Reliable cross-surface context handoff (what was open, what was selected, what ‘next’ means)
A standardized ‘continue’ intent that can map to Mac actions, browser actions, or a follow-up plan

proposals.user_asks: “Handle this sensitive task end to end, but show me exactly what will be sent before anything leaves my devices.” I speak the request on the pendant; the relay gathers the relevant authenticated browser/Mac context, produces a redacted preview, and I can accept or revise it by voice before execution.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must either trust a large opaque planner action or manually shuttle private context between devices. This would make the hive useful for email, forms, messages, and uploads without leaking unrelated page text or committing an accidental interpretation.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay for the short clarification and spoken preview; background gpt-5.6-luna for planning and a cheaper verifier for field-level redaction/diff.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview in 3–8 seconds for a single page/form; execution after a brief spoken accept/revise turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.15 per request, dominated by planner context and one verification pass; no recurring cost beyond existing Worker/browser traffic.
proposals.security_concerns: Raw authenticated page content must remain on the Mac/browser wherever possible. The preview must identify destination, recipients, attachments, and changed fields; execution must not occur until an explicit spoken accept. Redaction errors could expose secrets, so fail closed for credentials, tokens, and unrelated page regions.
missing: A field-level provenance/redaction service that can turn browser/Mac observations into a stable preview
A spoken accept/revise state machine spanning the relay and the existing pendant inbox/outbox
Structured dry-run receipts and an execute-after-accept link between plan and execution

proposals.user_asks: “Watch my real work, not just a page: if a meeting, message, or document changes in a way that affects the task I told you about, interrupt me with the one decision I need to make.” The relay correlates authenticated browser changes, Mac state, and my standing task, then asks only when the change crosses my configured importance threshold.
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has to remember to ask again after a task is handed off. A cross-surface watch would turn the pendant into an always-available executive filter: it notices a changed deadline, reply, build failure, or approval request even while the owner is away from the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap scheduled/standing-watch checks and deterministic diffs first; gpt-5.6-luna only for relevance ranking and a one-sentence decision prompt; realtime only when speaking the alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Changes surfaced within 1–5 minutes of a check; spoken alert under 2 seconds once selected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per check depending on page/document volume; relevance calls dominate, so deterministic hashing and local extraction should be the default.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated content and task correlations are sensitive. Store hashes/excerpts and provenance rather than whole pages, scope each watch to an explicit task, expire findings, and never speak message contents aloud until the owner requests detail. The owner must be able to pause a watch from the pendant.
missing: A unified watch adapter for Mac apps, browser sessions, and local files, rather than page-only watches
A durable scheduler/worker that runs while the relay is awake and retries offline-device delivery
Task-scoped change correlation and a pendant pause/ack control

proposals.user_asks: “Teach me what I am seeing without sending the scene or my voice to the cloud.” I press the pendant while looking at an object or screen; the Mac camera/screen and the pendant audio are joined locally, the Mac returns a concise spoken explanation, and only the final question and answer are retained if I ask.
proposals.why_useful: This is the single most useful new behavior: the pendant becomes an immediate, private accessibility and troubleshooting companion while the owner is away from the desk. It can read a label, explain a tool, identify a cable, or diagnose a screen without uploading a continuous camera feed.
proposals.model_tier: Local Mac vision/audio preprocessing and gpt-4.1-mini computer-use/vision loop for ordinary frames; realtime relay for turn-taking and 24 kHz speech; escalate to gpt-5.6-luna only for difficult reasoning.
proposals.latency_budget: First spoken answer in 2–4 seconds after the press; subsequent “look closer” turns under 2 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.005–$0.05 per turn if frames are downsampled and processed locally; relay speech and occasional escalation dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: Camera and screen capture must be visibly active only during a press-held session, with a hard local indicator and automatic frame discard. Never upload frames by default; faces, documents, and passwords need local masking. Retention is opt-in and should use existing capture provenance.
missing: A Mac-local camera/screen capture bridge with press-scoped lifetime and local redaction
A bidirectional low-latency audio/vision session protocol between pendant, relay, and Mac
A mac-vision loop that can return image-grounded claims with coordinates/confidence, not just click actions
A pendant-side ‘repeat/closer’ control compatible with its one-button interaction

proposals.user_asks: “Reconcile these systems and tell me what is inconsistent.” I name a project, person, or event on the pendant; the hive compares the authenticated browser, Mac apps, and local files, identifies contradictions with evidence, and offers one repair plan rather than silently choosing a source.
proposals.why_useful: Real work is full of stale calendar invites, conflicting documents, duplicate contacts, and status messages. No single browser or Mac action can establish cross-system truth; this would save the owner from manually checking every surface and prevent the assistant from acting on stale context.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper deterministic extraction and entity/time matching first; gpt-5.6-luna for contradiction classification and repair planning; realtime only for the concise spoken finding and follow-up question.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial comparison in 10–30 seconds for three sources; speak the first conflict as soon as found, then continue in background with a completion alert.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.05–$0.30 per reconciliation, dominated by multi-source extraction and planner context; cache stable document fingerprints to keep repeated checks cheap.
proposals.security_concerns: Cross-source joins can reveal more than any individual app. Keep source excerpts local, attach provenance and timestamps to every claim, scope access to the named entity, and never overwrite a source without an explicit repair selection. A missing source must be reported as unknown, never treated as agreement.
missing: A cross-surface entity and contradiction graph with timestamped evidence
Connectors that extract structured facts from Mac apps/local files as well as authenticated browser pages
A repair-plan format that lists every affected source and supports partial execution
A spoken/background continuation channel for reporting conflicts discovered after the initial answer

proposals.user_asks: Start this on my Mac, then keep it going even if I stop talking, and give me a short summary later.
proposals.why_useful: This is the whole promise: the pendant can initiate work, the Mac executes, and the relay closes the loop asynchronously.
proposals.model_tier: realtime to interpret intent; mac planner for execution; cheaper background watcher for status
proposals.latency_budget: Fast start (a few seconds). Completion can happen anytime; summary delivery should be prompt.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate. Planning/execution dominates; status watching is cheap.
proposals.security_concerns: High-impact actions (email, purchases, deletion) must require confirmation. Summaries should avoid exposing sensitive content to bystanders.
missing: Implemented event delivery from relay to pendant/phone
A durable watch that survives voice-session end
A concise summary generator that runs server-side

proposals.user_asks: “I’m on a phone call—stay with me, tell me who is speaking and what they just asked, and when I say ‘reply’, draft or send the response I dictate.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can conduct a difficult call without staring at the Mac: the pendant is the conversational front door, while the Mac/iPhone are the only surfaces that can actually carry and control the call. This would make the system useful in one of the highest-value moments for a wearable.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay for low-latency turn-taking and short spoken summaries; mac-planner for call control and deterministic actions; a cheaper background model for rolling transcript compression and speaker/topic tracking.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 700 ms for a spoken ‘what did they ask?’ summary; under 2 s for a dictated draft; sending or changing call state must wait for the owner’s explicit verbal command, not an inferred intent.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per five-minute call, dominated by realtime audio transcription/summarization; call-control actions are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Phone-call audio and transcripts leave the phone/Mac and pass through the relay; retention must be off by default and visibly indicated. The system must distinguish ‘draft’ from ‘send’, never claim a reply was sent without an iOS receipt, and require an explicit utterance for muting, hanging up, or sending.
missing: A Mac audio bridge that can capture the remote call leg and return a mixed, consent-marked stream to the relay
A phone-mirroring call-control contract with call audio routing, speaker attribution, and receipts
A relay realtime session mode for a bounded rolling transcript plus pendant interruption
A pendant UX for entering and leaving call-copilot mode without ambiguity

proposals.user_asks: “When I’m away from my Mac, let me ask what changed in my authenticated browser sessions since I last looked, and read me only the changes that require my attention.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently cannot use the wearable to query a logged-in work site while the Mac is offline or unattended. A durable browser-session mirror would let the pendant answer high-value change questions without pretending that a stale page or a failed check is current.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper background extraction/diffing for watched pages; realtime relay only for the owner’s question and concise prioritization.
proposals.latency_budget: A spoken answer in 3–5 s when a fresh snapshot exists; otherwise state plainly that the session is unavailable rather than hallucinating. Initial session capture may take 10–30 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per page check plus encrypted storage; cost is dominated by browser execution and change extraction, not speech.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated cookies and page contents are highly sensitive. Use an end-to-end encrypted, device-bound session handoff or a Mac-local encrypted snapshot service; never expose cookies to the model, redact secrets before diffing, keep short retention, and report ‘could not check’ separately from ‘no changes’.
missing: A browser-extension session mirror that can produce encrypted, redacted snapshots while the Mac is online
A relay-held encrypted snapshot/diff store and an offline query path
A durable browser watch that can resume from a Mac reconnect and bind results to the correct account/session
A pendant-readable alert/query protocol for prioritized diffs

proposals.user_asks: “Remember the commitments I make in conversation, resolve them against my calendar, mail, browser and notes, and tell me before I miss one—without me having to say ‘remind me’.”
proposals.why_useful: People routinely promise things without creating a reminder. The pendant is present at the moment of commitment, while the Mac and browser hold the evidence needed to resolve a person, deadline, thread, and completion state. This turns fleeting speech into reliable follow-through rather than another capture inbox.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay extracts a candidate commitment in one pass; a cheaper background model resolves entities, checks evidence, and ranks urgency; realtime is used only when the owner asks for the current commitment list.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge a detected commitment in under 1 s without interrupting the owner; reconciliation can take minutes. Notifications should arrive before a deadline, with quiet suppression when evidence shows it is already done.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.05 per commitment over its lifetime, dominated by background reconciliation across mail/calendar/browser evidence.
proposals.security_concerns: This processes private speech and personal/work records. Store only the commitment and minimal evidence pointers, allow correction/deletion, never infer a commitment from background audio after button release, and clearly label uncertain matches instead of asserting completion.
missing: A commitment-specific entity and lifecycle model distinct from generic tasks
Cross-surface evidence joins for calendar, mail, browser and iOS with provenance and confidence
A scheduler/standing-watch policy that can recheck commitments and suppress duplicates
A reliable pendant notification path that carries a short spoken escalation and supports correction

proposals.user_asks: If the Mac can’t complete what I asked, tell me why and offer the next-best alternative I can approve by voice.
proposals.why_useful: Owners don’t want a dead-end failure. They want a concise explanation and a safe fallback, like “Safari isn’t open and the browser agent is offline; I can set a reminder or draft an email instead.”
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the conversational fallback; mac-planner for generating alternatives when the workflow is complex.
proposals.latency_budget: Short spoken failure reason immediately, then a single suggested fallback within a second or two.
proposals.cost_estimate: Mostly cheap status reads and a small plan generation when needed. No continuous monitoring.
proposals.security_concerns: Alternatives may involve sending messages or modifying files; require confirmation for high-impact actions and avoid exposing private data in spoken output.
missing: A structured error taxonomy from mac-planner jobs to map failures into suggested fallback actions
A small library of fallback templates mapped to tool availability and device state

proposals.user_asks: “Make this change everywhere it needs to be changed, but show me the differences before anything irreversible.” Then, after I say “do it,” carry the same change across my Mac files, authenticated browser session, and iPhone, with one coherent result.
proposals.why_useful: Today each surface can act, but no single request can maintain one intended change across them. This would prevent half-finished edits such as updating a document but not the linked portal or phone setting, and would give the owner one spoken confirmation of what actually changed.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay extracts the invariant goal and speaks a concise diff; mac-planner (slower background tier) builds a cross-surface dependency plan; mac-vision/browser/iOS perform the concrete actions and return receipts.
proposals.latency_budget: A first spoken scope/diff within 3 seconds; planning may take 10–30 seconds; execution can continue asynchronously with a short pendant update at each surface boundary.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.03–$0.20 per request depending on screenshots and planner turns; computer-use screenshots and browser/iPhone verification dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must not expose raw credentials or browser page contents unnecessarily. The diff must identify destructive or externally visible changes, and execution must be explicitly requested after preview; retain per-surface receipts and recover by replaying only failed steps.
missing: A cross-surface transaction/intent ID and dependency graph spanning Mac, browser, and iOS
A preview/diff response that can be rendered as a short spoken summary and kept for a later approval
Idempotent action receipts and compensation/retry semantics across POST /execute surfaces
A local planner/computer-use path that is reliable for iPhone Mirroring and browser verification

proposals.user_asks: “Keep this request private: transcribe and act on it without sending my words or the screen contents to the relay or any hosted model.” Use the pendant as the microphone and let my nearby Mac do the sensitive work locally, then return only the result to the pendant.
proposals.why_useful: A wearable is present for secrets precisely when the owner is away from a keyboard, yet the current low-latency path necessarily sends audio to the relay. This would make private banking, health, work, and household requests usable without making the owner choose between convenience and cloud disclosure.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay handles only an opaque session token and transport state; a local Mac model/planner performs transcription, reasoning, and computer use. Use the expensive realtime tier only for a short fallback if the Mac disappears.
proposals.latency_budget: Local USB-attached operation should begin feedback within 500 ms and return ordinary requests in 2–8 seconds; LTE-to-Mac private tunneling, when available, may take 1–3 seconds before local processing starts.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero hosted inference cost in the local path; the main cost is a local model process and encrypted relay bytes. Optional fallback incurs normal realtime cost only after an explicit privacy-policy failure.
proposals.security_concerns: The pendant and Mac need mutually authenticated keys, replay protection, encrypted audio frames, explicit private-mode indication, and zero transcript/screenshot persistence on the Worker. The owner must be told if the Mac is unavailable rather than silently falling back to cloud. Browser credentials remain inside the Mac/browser agent.
missing: A firmware and Mac pairing protocol over the live USB serial links, with a secure session-key handshake
A relay transport mode that forwards opaque encrypted frames without decoding, logging, or model-injecting them
A local speech-to-text and response-audio path on the Mac, including Opus/PCM conversion compatible with the shipped 24 kHz downlink
A durable owner privacy-mode preference and a clear pendant indication when private mode is active

proposals.user_asks: “Send that to them,” while I am looking at something on my Mac or phone. Figure out what “that” and “them” mean from the current screen, browser tab, iPhone, and my recent spoken context, tell me your interpretation in one sentence, and carry it out.
proposals.why_useful: Short wearable commands fail today whenever the owner omits nouns that are obvious from the screen in front of them. This would make the pendant feel situated rather than forcing the owner to dictate URLs, filenames, contact names, and message bodies while away from a keyboard.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the utterance and asks the local perception tier for a compact candidate set; mac-vision and browser/iOS adapters extract visible labels and stable object IDs; a cheaper planner resolves candidates, while realtime speaks only the selected interpretation.
proposals.latency_budget: Candidate interpretation in 2–4 seconds, with a spoken “I mean X to Y” before external sending; screen capture should be one bounded snapshot, not a continuous stream.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.10 per request; one local screenshot and OCR/vision pass dominate, with a second model turn only when candidates conflict.
proposals.security_concerns: Only the active-window crop and explicitly needed browser/iPhone labels should leave the Mac; redact passwords and payment fields before relay use. Never infer a recipient from hidden page state without stating the chosen identity. Keep a short-lived object map and delete it after the action.
missing: A perception endpoint that returns stable object references and visible text from the active Mac, browser tab, and mirrored iPhone in one timestamped snapshot
A cross-surface referent graph linking screen objects to planner action arguments
A confidence/ambiguity response contract that can speak the interpretation before an external side effect
Reliable mac-vision and iOS snapshot adapters, since the current computer-use loop is disabled

proposals.user_asks: While I’m away from my Mac, check my authenticated sessions and summarize what changed that I should care about.
proposals.why_useful: This becomes a daily superpower: the wearable can summarize changes across sessions the owner is already logged into, without manual checking.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper model for periodic checks and diffing; realtime only for delivering a spoken summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Background checks can take their time; summaries should be short and quick to deliver.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate. Dominated by browser automation time and page reads, not LLM tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Sensitive data in authenticated sessions. Keep summaries minimal, avoid copying content, and require confirmation for actions.
missing: A server-side browser capability (server_browser_actions is unresolved) or a reliable always-on browser node.
A scheduling mechanism that works even when the Mac is offline, or a durable relay-side watcher using existing watch/routine primitives.

proposals.user_asks: “I’m about to walk away—finish the task I have open, but tell me if the result differs from what I asked.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can hand work to the Mac, but cannot leave with confidence that the browser/UI actually reached the requested end state. This would make the pendant a trustworthy handoff point: the Mac acts, the browser proves the visible result, and the relay reports only a meaningful mismatch.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime relay for intent and a one-sentence response; mac-planner for the action plan; mac-vision for visual verification; browser harness for DOM/session evidence; background verification should use a cheaper model.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; action may take up to 60 seconds; speak completion or mismatch immediately when evidence arrives.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per handoff depending on planner/vision retries; browser and Mac calls dominate latency, not relay speech.
proposals.security_concerns: The request can mutate authenticated sites. The owner has explicitly allowed trusted agents to act without extra gates, but the system must retain the exact utterance, planned effect, and before/after evidence. Page contents and screenshots leave the Mac only to the relay/dashboard.
missing: A first-class job contract containing intent, expected postcondition, and evidence requirements
Mac-vision execution/verification loop enabled in production
Browser result evidence attached to the same job rather than emitted as unrelated commands
A relay reducer that classifies verified, contradicted, and inconclusive outcomes

proposals.user_asks: “When I tap the pendant, tell me the one thing on my Mac or in my open browser that deserves my attention right now.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant currently answers explicit requests, but it cannot perform a cross-surface attention scan while the owner is away. A single ranked answer would replace checking several apps and tabs with an actually wearable interruption filter.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background perception gathers active-app/window and browser facts; a judgement model ranks urgency and novelty; realtime relay only handles the tap, cancellation, and spoken one-sentence result.
proposals.latency_budget: First spoken acknowledgment under 500 ms; ranked result within 8 seconds, with an asynchronous inbox alert if inspection takes longer.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.04 per scan; most cost is browser/page inspection and summarization. Cache unchanged surfaces to avoid paying for repeated scans.
proposals.security_concerns: This intentionally reads authenticated tabs and local app state. Scope must be explicit (active window plus opted-in tabs/apps), redact secrets before storage, and never treat page text as an instruction. Nothing should be sent or changed without a separate command.
missing: A permissioned cross-surface snapshot endpoint for active Mac UI plus selected browser tabs
Stable content hashes and timestamps so unchanged items are not repeatedly ranked
A priority/novelty judgement prompt and an owner-tunable attention policy
A wearable push path for a result that completes after the tap

proposals.user_asks: “Remember this page as evidence for the project, and next time I ask, quote the exact passage and tell me when it was captured.”
proposals.why_useful: A browser page can be read today and facts can be stored, but the owner cannot reliably ask the pendant for provenance-grade recall: exact excerpt, URL, capture time, and whether the page has since changed. This turns fleeting browsing into trustworthy project memory rather than an unsupported summary.
proposals.model_tier: Background browser extraction and deduplication; realtime relay handles the spoken save/retrieve request; a cheaper retrieval model selects passages, while the relay reads a short answer and offers the citation on the dashboard.
proposals.latency_budget: Save acknowledgment under 2 seconds; retrieval under 5 seconds for indexed pages; if the page is unavailable, say so rather than hallucinating.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per save/retrieval after hashing; extraction and re-checking dominate, with stable pages reused from storage.
proposals.security_concerns: Store only the owner-selected page and a bounded excerpt, never credentials or whole authenticated pages by default. Preserve source URL, host, timestamp, content hash, and sensitivity; require explicit confirmation before sharing a stored excerpt externally.
missing: A provenance record distinct from ordinary browser facts, including excerpt offsets/content hash and capture timestamp
An exact-quote retrieval route that can distinguish captured text from a fresh page read
Change detection and versioning for pages that later differ
Voice-accessible citation formatting and dashboard drill-down

proposals.user_asks: When I say “fill this out from my voice,” have the pendant capture a structured answer, the relay validate and normalize it, and my Mac’s authenticated browser fill the current form field-by-field, read back a compact receipt of every value and leave the form unsent until I explicitly say “submit.”
proposals.why_useful: Dictating a long form while away from the keyboard is a real wearable advantage: the browser session supplies authenticated context, the Mac supplies UI reach, and the relay supplies low-latency clarification. It prevents silent transcription mistakes without imposing confirmation on ordinary reversible edits.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for capture, clarification, and read-back; mac-planner/browser actions for deterministic field filling; no expensive model for straightforward normalization.
proposals.latency_budget: First field within 2 seconds; each clarification under 1 second; receipt within 5 seconds of the final field.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one realtime turn plus a small planner/browser job, roughly $0.02–$0.10 depending on form length; browser latency dominates.
proposals.security_concerns: Form contents and authenticated page state leave the Mac only as structured field metadata/transcript needed for relay confirmation. Never submit or upload without the explicit spoken submit phrase; redact password/card fields from read-back and logs.
missing: A form-schema extractor that maps browser controls to labels, types, requiredness, and sensitive-field flags
A streaming field-fill protocol with pause/resume and idempotent field receipts
An explicit submit boundary in the browser action executor

proposals.user_asks: Let me say “keep an eye on this page and tell me only if the meaning changes,” then have the authenticated browser snapshot the page on a schedule, compare semantic sections rather than pixels, and deliver one prioritized spoken alert to my pendant with the before/after evidence and a way to dismiss or snooze it.
proposals.why_useful: This turns the wearable into an always-available attention filter for pages the owner already has open: price changes, appointment slots, project dashboards, or policy updates become actionable without repeatedly checking a screen. It uses the browser’s session, the relay’s availability, and the pendant’s inbox together.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background model or deterministic DOM diff for extraction and change scoring; realtime only when the owner asks follow-up questions or receives the short alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Checks may run on a minute-scale cadence; alert delivery under 10 seconds after a meaningful change is detected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per check with DOM extraction/diff; roughly $0.001–$0.02 per check, with model cost only for ambiguous semantic changes.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page content stays in the browser/Mac path and only a minimal diff is sent to the relay. Require per-watch domain and retention controls, suppress secrets and personal fields, and make alerts explain which section changed.
missing: A scheduler that can run while the Mac/browser session is online
A semantic DOM snapshot and field-redaction layer
A durable watch-to-pendant alert binding with deduplication, snooze, and evidence retention

proposals.user_asks: Give me a “walk-away handoff”: while I am wearing the pendant, let me dictate a goal and constraints, have the relay preserve the exact task contract, let the Mac and authenticated browser work whenever they become available, and later let me ask “what is the next decision?” to hear only unresolved choices with the relevant evidence—not a generic completion summary.
proposals.why_useful: The owner is usually away from the Mac, so ordinary computer automation fails at the handoff boundary. This makes a spoken request survive disconnection and resume safely, while prioritizing decisions that actually need the owner instead of replaying logs or announcing routine completion.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only to capture the contract and answer follow-up questions; background planner and cheap summarizer maintain the task state and extract unresolved decisions.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 2 seconds; resume automatically on reconnect; decision query under 3 seconds from stored state.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short realtime capture plus background planning, about $0.01–$0.08 per handoff; storage and browser polling dominate at scale.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only the spoken contract, constraints, and task artifacts needed to resume; encrypt sensitive browser evidence; never infer approval from silence or a reconnect. The owner must explicitly choose among surfaced decisions, while routine reversible work may continue.
missing: A durable task-contract record separate from transient job logs
Checkpoint/resume semantics for Mac and browser jobs with idempotency keys
A decision extractor that cites evidence and exposes only unresolved branches
A pendant query path into task state after the original voice session ends

proposals.user_asks: Be my eyes for what’s happening on my Mac and tell me only the important changes while I’m away.
proposals.why_useful: This is the kind of thing only a multi-surface assistant can do: the Mac can observe and summarize, the relay can speak it, and the pendant makes it effortless to receive. It cuts down on constant checking and helps the owner focus.
proposals.model_tier: Mac planner/observation loop for change detection and summarization; relay only for low-latency delivery.
proposals.latency_budget: Observation runs in the background; spoken delivery should be under a second once an alert is ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: Most cost sits on the Mac observation and summarization. Relay cost is a short spoken delivery.
proposals.security_concerns: Summaries must be scoped to what the owner opted into observing. Sensitive content should be redacted and delivered to the right surface (pendant vs dashboard).
missing: A Mac-side change detection pipeline that can watch sources (files, apps, logs, browser) and produce a prioritized summary.
A delivery mechanism that can queue alerts when the pendant is offline and deliver later.
A way to configure what counts as important (rules, ML ranking, or both).
built_from: offline_alert_inbox (existing inbox mechanism described in system prompt)

proposals.user_asks: When I say “show me the choices,” have the pendant let me browse a live set of Mac/browser results with the rotary wheel, hear one item at a time, and say “do this one” to carry out the selected action.
proposals.why_useful: A wearable voice interface is poor at presenting five search results or emails and asking the owner to remember an index. This makes the pendant useful while walking: the relay keeps the active result set, the Mac/browser supplies authenticated content, and a physical wheel provides reliable selection without a phone screen.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model only interprets the short spoken commands and generates item summaries; mac-planner performs retrieval and action planning, while browser automation extracts authenticated results.
proposals.latency_budget: First list within 3 seconds; wheel-to-next-item audio under 500 ms; action completion may take longer but must stream a short state update.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per interaction depending on spoken summaries; Mac/browser calls and Opus audio dominate rather than the realtime model.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must bind the result cursor to the owner session and expire it quickly so an old list cannot trigger a later action. Sending an item must use the existing owner policy and produce an explicit target summary; no new confirmation gate is required for reversible actions.
missing: A rotary encoder and second deliberate action button in the pendant enclosure/firmware (the current single button cannot distinguish navigation from stop).
A relay-side cursor/result-set resource with expiry and reconnect recovery.
A low-latency downlink command for wheel events and an audio item-summary cache.

proposals.user_asks: After you act on my Mac or in my logged-in browser, tell me not merely that it succeeded but what changed, using a before/after proof: “the draft was sent to Alex with subject X,” or “nothing changed because the page rejected it.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a spoken success claim can be detached from reality, especially when the owner is away from the Mac. A before/after evidence bundle lets the owner trust a remote action, distinguishes a blocked workflow from an unchanged page, and makes failures actionable without opening a laptop.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to turn the final structured evidence into one short spoken sentence. The Mac planner and browser harness collect deterministic state; a slower background model may summarize large diffs for the dashboard.
proposals.latency_budget: A terse acknowledgement in 1 second, followed by a verified result within 10 seconds for ordinary UI actions.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per completed action. The dominant cost is two page/app observations and optional screenshot or DOM diff storage, not language generation.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence may contain private email, page text, or screenshots, so retain only redacted structured fields by default and encrypt short-lived artifacts. The proof must never claim success from an intent receipt alone; require a postcondition observation or report “unverified.”
missing: A transaction wrapper that captures normalized preconditions, action receipt, postcondition, and verification state across Mac and browser jobs.
Mac-side before/after snapshots for non-browser actions (mail, files, reminders) with secret redaction.
A relay spoken-result schema and short-lived evidence store; the dashboard can expose the full diff.

proposals.user_asks: If I say “undo that” right after a remote action, reverse the last change on my Mac or in the browser—even if I am no longer looking at the screen—and tell me exactly what was restored and what cannot be undone.
proposals.why_useful: Remote voice control is dangerous mainly because a mistaken click is hard to repair from a pendant. A short-lived, cross-surface undo journal would make experimentation safe: undo a moved file, reverted reminder, edited draft, or browser form change without making the owner reconstruct the original UI.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles only the spoken reference and disambiguation. A deterministic inverse-action engine on the Mac/browser harness performs reversals; a background model can propose an inverse when no static inverse exists, but must label it as unavailable rather than bluff.
proposals.latency_budget: Resolve “that” against the last completed action in under 300 ms and start reversal immediately; speak the outcome within 3 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per undo. Cost is primarily journal storage and occasional Mac/browser verification; model usage is limited to ambiguous natural-language references.
proposals.security_concerns: The journal must store sensitive arguments encrypted and expire entries after a short window. Never silently substitute a different target when multiple actions match. Non-invertible operations (send, purchase, delete) should return “cannot undo” plus the safest available compensating action, consistent with the owner's maximum-access policy.
missing: An inverse-action vocabulary and durable, encrypted last-action journal shared by Mac and browser execution.
Pre-action snapshots or compensating operations for files, reminders, browser forms, and app state.
A relay endpoint that resolves relative references such as “that” across sessions and returns reversal status to the pendant.

proposals.user_asks: When I ask what is on a private page, let me choose the disclosure level—“just counts,” “subjects only,” “read the details,” or “nothing aloud, put it on the dashboard”—and enforce that choice while the authenticated browser session is inspected.
proposals.why_useful: A worn speaker is easy for nearby people to overhear, and a single spoken answer cannot safely serve a public street and a private room. This gives the owner useful browser and Mac awareness without forcing them to expose full email, health, or work content aloud.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime interprets the terse disclosure command and speaks only the already-redacted result. Browser/Mac workers perform deterministic field extraction and redaction; a slower model may summarize only after the chosen ceiling is applied.
proposals.latency_budget: Counts or subjects within 3 seconds; dashboard-only delivery should acknowledge in under 1 second and complete asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.005–$0.04 per request, dominated by browser inspection and optional dashboard rendering; avoid sending full page text to the realtime model.
proposals.security_concerns: Disclosure level must be an explicit per-turn ceiling, never inferred upward from context. Redaction must happen before content reaches audio generation or model logs, and dashboard artifacts need short TTLs. If the page cannot be safely field-extracted, say so rather than read raw text.
missing: A structured browser extraction/redaction contract that returns counts, metadata, subjects, and bodies as separate fields.
A relay session disclosure ceiling shared by browser, Mac, transcript, logs, and speech synthesis.
Dashboard-only result delivery and expiry for sensitive page excerpts.

changes.change: Introduce a clear tiering rule: realtime relay model only handles conversational intent capture, clarification, and short confirmations. Any task that can run asynchronously (web search, email, file operations, automation, long summaries, scheduled reminders) should be routed to a cheaper background model via mac-planner or a server-side browser/search worker. Provide a standardized intent envelope and status updates so the relay doesn’t keep long context or poll for completion.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, cheaper interactions. The pendant feels responsive, while longer work finishes in the background and returns when ready without burning tokens in a live conversation.
changes.effort: Medium. Requires routing contract and status UI, plus background workers for web/search if not already present.
changes.risk: Misrouting could cause delays or partial completion. Mitigate with explicit confirmation for high-impact actions and a fallback to tell the user when a task can’t run in the current tier.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces per-second audio and token usage by moving heavy work off the realtime model. Costs shift to cheaper background tokens and occasional status messages.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency for the owner. Background work may take longer overall but doesn’t block conversation.
changes.security_impact: Limits the blast radius of the realtime agent. High-risk actions stay behind mac-planner’s risk scoring and confirmation gates.
depends_on: Authoritative tool/routing contract from orchestrator
mac-planner job queue/status primitives exposed to relay

changes.change: Introduce a clear tiering policy: relay-realtime handles only intent capture, brief clarification, and immediate safety checks; everything else becomes a job executed by cheaper background models via the Mac bridge or a server-side browser, with status updates streamed back.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, more reliable voice interactions and lower cost, because long-running work happens elsewhere without tying up the live conversation.
changes.effort: Medium: define intent schema, job queue contracts, and status events; update orchestrator routing.
changes.risk: Misrouted intents could cause wrong actions. Mitigate with explicit confirmation for destructive or high-risk actions and a visible job log.
changes.cost_impact: Lower ongoing cost by reducing realtime tokens and audio time; background jobs pay only for what they use.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency for conversation; background work may take longer but doesn’t block the user.
changes.security_impact: Better isolation if high-risk operations are confined to mac-vision/planner with risk scoring; still requires strong auth and audit.
depends_on: Confirm the five agent tools listed in hardware spec exist and are wired, or update the spec/tooling to match reality

changes.change: Add a server-side browser harness (Cloudflare Browser Run) so the relay can perform read-only web tasks without requiring the Mac to be online, with strict allowlists and output sanitization.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Web lookups and account-independent tasks work even when the Mac is asleep or away, making the pendant more useful on the go.
changes.effort: Medium: implement harness, allowlists, and fallback to Mac browser bridge when needed.
changes.risk: Web automation can leak data or trigger unintended actions. Keep it read-only by default, require confirmation for form submissions, and log actions.
changes.cost_impact: Potentially cheaper than waking the Mac; cost dominated by browsing time and model tokens.
changes.latency_impact: Removes dependency on Mac availability; web page loads still dominate.
changes.security_impact: Strict origin allowlists, content stripping, and no credential use unless explicitly authorized.

changes.change: Align the stack spec and orchestrator tool registry for the realtime agent, and publish a single authoritative capability manifest (tools, endpoints, permissions, and model routing) that both the runtime and documentation derive from. Add a health endpoint that returns the active manifest so agents can reason safely about what exists.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer routing errors and less back-and-forth. When I say I can do something, it actually works, which means faster help and lower cost.
changes.effort: Medium. Requires orchestrator changes plus docs/tests for manifest generation and validation.
changes.risk: If manifest generation is wrong, agents could lose access to tools. Mitigate by rolling out behind a flag and validating against a golden manifest in CI.
changes.cost_impact: Low. Mostly engineering time; runtime cost is a small extra manifest fetch or cached config.
changes.latency_impact: Low. A cached manifest avoids per-turn overhead; improves reliability.
changes.security_impact: Positive. A single manifest makes permission boundaries explicit and auditable.

changes.change: Add explicit, cheap tiers: relay captures intent and hands off to mac_delegate or server_browser_actions. Introduce job creation, status, cancellation, and completion notifications (audio and dashboard) so the relay doesn’t stay in the loop.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for something and get on with their day; results arrive later without tying up a live conversation.
changes.effort: Medium: add job APIs, status polling/DO, and notification plumbing; update dashboard UI.
changes.risk: Jobs could run with stale context or the wrong scope. Use scoped confirmation tokens, show what will run, and allow cancellation.
changes.cost_impact: Lower relay token/audio cost; background work uses cheaper models.
changes.latency_impact: Better perceived latency; relay returns quickly while work continues elsewhere.
changes.security_impact: Centralizes execution control. Require explicit confirmation for high-risk actions (spending money, sending email, accessing private data).
depends_on: Job status endpoint/tool and notification mechanism
Server-side browser for web tasks or Mac availability for desktop tasks

changes.change: Implement adaptive duplex behavior: when downlink audio is playing, reduce or pause uplink capture/encoding to avoid LTE contention; resume capture after playback. Add LED state to indicate “receiving” vs “recording.”
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer dropped speech packets and clearer conversations when they and the agent talk at the same time.
changes.effort: Medium: audio pipeline changes and state management; careful testing with half-duplex LTE behavior.
changes.risk: Could miss user speech while the agent is speaking. Mitigate with a short buffer and a quick “hold on” prompt; allow a button press to force recording.
changes.cost_impact: No new cloud cost; firmware development time only.
changes.latency_impact: Improves reliability; may add slight delay when switching modes.
changes.security_impact: Low; local behavior only.

changes.change: Add a Worker-side scheduler using Cron Triggers and Durable Object alarms to run routines even when the Mac is asleep, with a simple queue that delegates to the Mac when it’s online or performs server-side tasks when possible.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Time-based routines (daily summaries, reminders, check-ins) actually happen reliably, not only when the Mac is awake.
changes.effort: Medium: new Durable Object for routine state, Cron wiring, and execution routing logic.
changes.risk: Duplicate runs if both Mac and Worker schedulers fire; mitigate with idempotency keys and a last-run ledger.
changes.cost_impact: Low per routine tick; costs dominated by downstream model/tool usage.
changes.latency_impact: No realtime latency impact; runs in background.
changes.security_impact: Worker can trigger actions; require explicit confirmation for irreversible actions (sending email, purchases), and keep least-privileged credentials.

changes.change: Add a first-class scheduler/queue for delayed and recurring work in the relay, backed by Durable Objects (alarms) or Worker Cron. Provide a routine store (D1) and a delivery mechanism that can produce an audio summary stored in R2 and a dashboard notification.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can set routines once (daily brief, end-of-day shutdown, weekly review) and receive results later without keeping a live voice session open.
changes.effort: Medium to high: design routine schema, permissions, delivery, and failure handling; wire Mac agent polling or push for execution.
changes.risk: Missed alarms or duplicate runs if clocks drift or retries happen; recover with idempotency keys and run logs. Provide a manual “run now” command.
changes.cost_impact: Adds storage and occasional scheduled compute. Saves money overall by shifting work off the realtime tier and avoiding long live sessions.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency for users by making long tasks asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled tasks can touch sensitive data; require explicit confirmation for non-reversible actions and provide clear audit logs.
depends_on: Ground truth stack confirmed via get_hardware_spec(stack)
A job status/result path (e.g., relay_job_status) and a delivery mechanism

changes.change: Add a real scheduling layer for delayed and recurring work in the relay: use Cloudflare Cron Triggers for recurring jobs and Durable Object alarms for per-user delayed jobs. Jobs should enqueue a plan to mac-planner when appropriate, or run server-side web tasks when the Mac is offline. Provide a job table in D1 with status and receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: You can say “remind me every morning” or “check that thing in an hour” and it actually happens, even if the Mac is asleep. Briefings and research can arrive later as audio you play on your own schedule.
changes.effort: Medium: new worker routes, durable object, D1 migrations, job schema, and UI to list scheduled jobs.
changes.risk: Jobs could run unexpectedly or duplicate. Mitigate with idempotency keys, clear user-visible schedule list, and a hard limit on frequency. Provide cancel/disable controls.
changes.cost_impact: Low per job: a small D1 write and an occasional cron/alarm wakeup. Most cost is downstream model tokens when the job actually runs.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency because expensive work happens off the live conversation path.
changes.security_impact: Scheduling can trigger actions later; require explicit confirmation for any destructive or external spend, and log receipts for audit.
depends_on: D1 job table and receipts
relay_job_status endpoint/tool for monitoring
mac-planner plan/execute endpoints already present

changes.change: Default web reading and extraction to a server-side browser (Cloudflare Browser Run) via server_browser_actions when the task is purely web and does not require local files or accounts. Use mac_delegate only for tasks that need local access or app control. Keep the realtime model focused on intent capture and confirmation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Web lookups become more reliable when you’re away from your Mac, and the pendant feels faster because the heavy lifting moves off the live voice loop.
changes.effort: Medium: add routing rules, timeouts, extraction templates, and fallback to Mac when server browser fails.
changes.risk: Server browser may hit anti-bot blocks or render differently. Provide graceful fallback and clear errors.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate: server browser runtime plus tokens, but saves repeated relay turns and avoids waking the Mac.
changes.latency_impact: Often faster end-to-end for web tasks; slower for pages with heavy scripts. Use timeouts and partial extraction.
changes.security_impact: Web content is public, but it can still leak sensitive data if logged. Don’t store page contents unless needed; redact URLs and query terms in logs when appropriate.

changes.change: Add a lightweight intent-routing policy that uses relay_route_intent to label the request and target mac-planner or server browser explicitly, and emits a short spoken confirmation when an action could change state or spend money. Keep a small, pruned context window and store summaries in memory instead of replaying long transcripts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant feels predictable and safe: you hear what will happen, and you don’t pay for extra tokens carrying irrelevant history around.
changes.effort: Low to medium: new policy module, small memory summaries, and confirmation prompts for a handful of risky categories.
changes.risk: Over-confirmation could feel annoying. Tune for reversible actions to proceed without prompts, and destructive/external actions to require confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: Lower ongoing token cost by pruning context and summarizing. Small added cost for confirmation prompts.
changes.latency_impact: Slight overhead for confirmation, but avoids expensive misroutes.
changes.security_impact: Reduces accidental destructive actions and limits data exposure by minimizing context.

changes.change: Add a scheduler layer using Worker Cron Triggers and Durable Object alarms for delayed and recurring jobs, with a job table in D1 and a relay job-status endpoint. Jobs can target relay, server browser, or mac-bridge, and can emit a completion notification to the dashboard and optionally an audio snippet to play later.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for things like “every morning summarize my calendar” or “remind me in two hours,” and it actually happens without them keeping a session open.
changes.effort: Medium to high: wiring cron, durable alarms, persistence, idempotency, and status reporting.
changes.risk: Jobs could run unexpectedly or repeatedly. Mitigate with clear job listing, pause/disable controls, and per-job confirmation for first run.
changes.cost_impact: Adds storage reads/writes and occasional cron invocations; overall cost controlled by keeping job payloads small and using cheaper models for execution.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency by moving work off the realtime path; adds no delay to immediate conversations.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled jobs can access data without the owner present. Require explicit confirmation, scope limits, and readable audit logs in the dashboard.
depends_on: Define job schema and status API; notification channel to dashboard/audio

changes.change: Introduce a confirmation gate for high-risk actions: relay summarizes intent, shows/reads a payload (e.g., draft email, purchase order, form submission), and requires a clear “confirm” before sending. Provide a reversible safe mode for exploratory actions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: It prevents accidental spends or messages while keeping quick tasks fast. The owner stays in control, especially when away from the Mac.
changes.effort: Low to medium: implement payload generation conventions and a consistent confirmation phrase.
changes.risk: Too many prompts could frustrate. Keep it for high-risk actions only; allow reversible actions without confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: Small extra tokens for summarizing payloads.
changes.latency_impact: Tiny delay for confirmation; worth it for risky operations.
changes.security_impact: Reduces risk of unintended data changes and spending; creates auditable checkpoints.
depends_on: Standard payload format from mac-planner/browser actions

changes.change: Add a relay-owned job scheduler using Cloudflare Cron Triggers plus Durable Object alarms to run periodic tasks (web diffs, inbox checks, maintenance), with a small job table in D1 and a per-job state machine. Jobs create alert artifacts (text + optional audio) stored in R2 and indexed for the pendant.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can set routines once and get results later without keeping the Mac awake or being online. It turns the system into something that works while they live their life.
changes.effort: Medium to high: new DO, D1 schema, retry semantics, idempotency, and an alert format shared across surfaces.
changes.risk: Bad scheduling could spam, duplicate, or miss jobs. Mitigate with idempotency keys, backoff, and a dashboard view of upcoming/failed jobs. Provide a kill switch per job.
changes.cost_impact: Low per run; cost scales with job count and browser usage. Storage costs for alerts in R2.
changes.latency_impact: Background work; realtime unaffected except for quick status checks.
changes.security_impact: Jobs can touch authenticated sessions; require per-origin enrollment and confirmation gates for irreversible actions.
depends_on: Define a job schema and alert artifact format
Implement origin allowlist and auth mode selection

changes.change: Adopt a strict routing policy: realtime relay only for intent capture, clarification, and immediate reversible actions; mac_delegate for multi-step tasks; server_browser_actions for public web research; background model for scheduled diffing and summarization. Add a confirmation checkpoint for any irreversible action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Lower latency and lower cost: they get fast conversational control without paying for the expensive tier to do slow work, and risky actions get a clear yes/no moment.
changes.effort: Low to medium: define policy, implement in planner/relay, add guardrails.
changes.risk: Over-routing could send tasks to a tier that lacks context. Mitigate with receipts and fallback to mac_delegate when the job fails or needs auth.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces expensive realtime usage; shifts work to cheaper tiers.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived responsiveness; background tasks may complete later by design.
changes.security_impact: Confirmation checkpoints reduce harm from misinterpretation; origin allowlists limit data exposure.
depends_on: Handshake schema for job receipts and status reporting
Policy enforcement in mac-planner and browser harness

changes.change: Add a scheduling layer using Cloudflare Cron Triggers (for daily/weekly routines) and Durable Object alarms (for per-user delayed tasks and retries). Jobs emit ledger events and produce artifacts (e.g., briefing summaries) stored in D1/R2 with ids and provenance.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The system can do useful work while the owner sleeps or is away, and the result is ready when they ask — without burning realtime tokens or requiring the Mac to be awake at that moment.
changes.effort: Medium to high. Requires wiring Cron/alarms, defining job schemas, idempotency keys, and artifact storage; plus observability for failures.
changes.risk: Jobs could run at the wrong time or duplicate. Mitigate with idempotency keys, explicit timezones, and a replay-safe event log. Provide a ‘disable routine’ control in the dashboard.
changes.cost_impact: Adds cheap scheduled compute and storage reads/writes. Saves realtime cost by shifting work off the expensive tier.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency because results are precomputed; adds background job latency but nobody is waiting.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled jobs can touch sensitive data. Require scoped readers and audit logs; high-impact follow-up actions must still require explicit confirmation.
depends_on: Event-sourced ledger/receipt system already proposed by mac-planner to be implemented end-to-end

changes.change: Give the relay a server-side browsing path using Cloudflare Browser Run for public web tasks, with a policy to prefer server_browser_actions over routing through the Mac when the target is public and doesn’t require the user’s authenticated sessions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Web lookups and extraction can happen even when the Mac is asleep or disconnected. The pendant becomes more reliable for quick questions and research on the go.
changes.effort: Medium. Needs action schema, extraction patterns, error handling, and a fallback to mac-planner/browser extension when authentication is required.
changes.risk: Automated browsing can click the wrong thing or misread content. Mitigate with read-only defaults, explicit extraction, and clear provenance in the returned artifact.
changes.cost_impact: Adds server-side browser runtime cost; offsets by reducing mac round-trips and planner tokens for simple extraction tasks.
changes.latency_impact: Often faster than waiting for the Mac; still not realtime, so relay should present as ‘working’ and return when done.
changes.security_impact: Public browsing is lower risk, but still needs URL allow/deny policies and content sanitization. Never treat it as authenticated unless explicitly configured.

changes.change: Add a real scheduler: a Durable Object-backed job queue with delayed execution and recurring rules (cron-like). The relay can enqueue jobs, and a workers cron/alarm runner executes them, delegating to mac_delegate or server_browser_actions as needed. Include idempotency keys, retry with backoff, and cancellation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can say things like “Remind me tonight” or “Check for new messages every morning and summarize” and it actually happens without them keeping a Mac awake or staying online.
changes.effort: Medium to high: new Durable Object, queue schema, runner, and integration with existing job status/result reporting.
changes.risk: Jobs could run unexpectedly if time zone or recurrence rules are wrong; mitigate with clear job listings, pause/disable, and a dry-run mode. If a job fails repeatedly, quarantine it and notify the owner when they next connect.
changes.cost_impact: Adds storage and compute cost for queued jobs and periodic runs; cheaper than keeping realtime model sessions open. Most cost is in downstream model invocations when jobs execute.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on conversational latency; jobs run out of band.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled tasks can read data or take actions without the owner present. Require explicit confirmation for high-impact actions at scheduling time, and show what data sources will be accessed.
depends_on: A status endpoint or tool to list scheduled jobs and results (for transparency)

changes.change: Unify memory across surfaces: replace hand-written prompt sections per surface with a shared, versioned memory API that returns small, purpose-built summaries (profile, preferences, current projects, recent tasks) plus a citation trail. Add write paths with confidence and decay/TTL to prevent prompt bloat.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Tell the system something once, and every agent uses the same up-to-date understanding without growing context cost every turn.
changes.effort: Medium: define schemas, summaries, and citations; update each surface to fetch memory via the API; add pruning and summarization workers.
changes.risk: Bad memory writes could lock in wrong facts. Mitigate with confidence scores, recency bias, and user-visible correction commands.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces per-turn token cost by keeping prompts small; adds occasional background summarization cost.
changes.latency_impact: Small additional fetch latency on first use; cache summaries per session.
changes.security_impact: Central memory is sensitive. Encrypt at rest, audit writes, and separate private vs shareable facts.

changes.change: Wire up a server-side browser path using Cloudflare Browser Run and a routing rule: web reads/extraction default to server_browser_actions; only fall back to Mac browser bridge when authentication requires the owner’s existing Mac session.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Web tasks work even when the Mac is asleep, and they start faster because they don’t need to wake another machine.
changes.effort: Medium: implement routing, translate existing browser_run_actions to server_browser_actions, normalize results.
changes.risk: Server-side browsing may not share the owner’s authenticated sessions; tasks could fail silently. Detect auth walls and automatically escalate to the Mac path with a clear reason.
changes.cost_impact: Adds server browser runtime cost; likely less than launching and coordinating Mac-side browser automation for simple reads.
changes.latency_impact: Lower startup latency for many web reads; no impact on voice latency.
changes.security_impact: Server-side browsing touches third-party sites; restrict to allowed domains where possible and log what was accessed for transparency.
depends_on: Clear contract for extracted data format shared by both browser paths

changes.change: Add a relay-owned durable work queue with retries and a receipt log, implemented as a Durable Object (or D1 + Durable Object alarms). The relay exposes enqueue/status endpoints, persists intent payloads, and emits receipts when downstream nodes complete. Jobs can be routed to Mac or server browser based on availability and task type.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can hand off tasks by voice and trust they will finish even if they walk away, the network drops, or the Mac goes offline. They get a clear record of what happened.
changes.effort: Medium to high: queue design, idempotency keys, retries, backoff, receipt schema, and UI changes.
changes.risk: Queue bugs could duplicate work or lose jobs. Mitigate with idempotency keys, explicit job states, and receipts. Provide manual cancel/retry controls.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate: storage in D1, occasional Durable Object alarms; cheaper than keeping realtime sessions open.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency: quick acknowledgement, work happens asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Must authenticate enqueue calls and protect stored payloads. Receipts should avoid logging sensitive content; store references when possible.
depends_on: A receipt schema shared across relay and Mac harness
Status reporting from Mac harness back to relay

changes.change: Use the new server-side browser capability for public web tasks directly from the relay, reserving the Mac harness for authenticated sessions and local data. Add routing logic: public pages -> server browser; authenticated workflows -> Mac browser bridge.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster results when the Mac is away, and fewer points of failure. The pendant can answer more questions without depending on the laptop being online.
changes.effort: Medium: implement server browser actions, extraction patterns, and routing heuristics.
changes.risk: Automation could break on site changes; implement robust extraction and fallback to web_search/read_web_page.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate: browser automation is more expensive than a simple search, but avoids Mac dependency and can reduce retries.
changes.latency_impact: Often faster than waiting for the Mac to come online, but slower than simple search; choose accordingly.
changes.security_impact: Keep it to public web unless explicit authentication support is added. Avoid storing scraped personal data unnecessarily.

changes.change: Introduce a unified, cross-node memory write API with schema (entities, events, preferences, tasks) and TTLs, plus a pruning policy. Replace hand-written per-surface prompt sections with retrieval-based context assembly.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Tell the system something once and every node knows it. Less repetition, better continuity, and lower token costs over time.
changes.effort: High: schema design, migrations, retrieval, and updates to all surfaces.
changes.risk: Bad memory writes could propagate errors. Mitigate with confidence scoring, source attribution, and easy correction commands.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces prompt bloat and repeated context over time; storage costs increase modestly.
changes.latency_impact: Small overhead for retrieval; overall faster than shipping large prompts every turn.
changes.security_impact: Memory can contain sensitive data; enforce access control per node and encrypt at rest where possible.

changes.change: Introduce a lightweight scheduler using Durable Object alarms or Cloudflare Cron to trigger queued jobs (summarize notes, send digests, retry failed uploads).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Things the owner asks for can actually happen later, reliably, without keeping the Mac awake or waiting in a live call.
changes.effort: Moderate: define job types, persistence, retry policy, and alarm wiring; coordinate with mac-planner for work handoff.
changes.risk: Misfires or duplicate runs could create duplicate reminders; mitigate with idempotent receipts and job state checks.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing cost; alarms are cheap, storage reads/writes dominate.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on live voice; background tasks run when scheduled.
changes.security_impact: Jobs carry user content; needs strict access control and minimal retention.
depends_on: A durable task ledger and job status API across relay and Mac

changes.change: Introduce a typed, minimal context service for the relay: given an utterance and a desired outcome (status query, dictation, mac task), return only relevant facts (device online state, last job ids, last spoken receipts), each with TTL and provenance, capped to a small token budget. Cache between turns and invalidate on updates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, more accurate voice responses without re-sending bulky state every turn, lowering latency and cost while keeping answers grounded.
changes.effort: Medium. Needs a small service/schema and adapters in relay and mac-bridge, plus caching and invalidation rules.
changes.risk: Wrong or stale context could misroute a task or reference the wrong job. Mitigate with TTLs, provenance, and explicit job ids in receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate initial build; ongoing savings by reducing prompt/context size per turn.
changes.latency_impact: Improves response time by avoiding large context assembly; small overhead for cache lookup.
changes.security_impact: Centralizes sensitive state; must enforce strict per-owner isolation and audit logging. Encrypt at rest.
depends_on: A durable store for receipts/state and cache invalidation hooks from mac-bridge

changes.change: Add a typed discovery registry for granted tools and capabilities. When the orchestrator grants a tool, it registers under a stable name with a version and a canonical describe() entry so relay can reliably introspect and route without guessing names or relying on system prompt text.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer voice failures and faster handoffs. If I can always find what exists, I can route requests correctly instead of stumbling on missing descriptors.
changes.effort: Medium: define a registry schema, have the orchestrator populate it, and have list_capabilities/discover return canonical names that describe() resolves.
changes.risk: Low. Main risk is backward incompatibility with existing tool names; mitigate with alias support and deprecation windows.
changes.cost_impact: Small API cost per discovery call; reduces wasted tool calls and retries.
changes.latency_impact: Improves responsiveness by avoiding failed describe calls and misroutes.
changes.security_impact: Low; registry contains metadata, not secrets.
depends_on: list_capabilities/discover/describe must support canonical naming and aliases

changes.change: Add a typed capability registry that maps discovered tool names and surfaces to stable internal identifiers. The registry should reconcile differences between what’s granted, what’s discoverable, and what’s actually callable, and expose a single describe(name) namespace so newly granted tools are immediately describable without guessing the right category.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Prevents the assistant from getting stuck when a tool is granted but not discoverable under the expected category, so voice requests keep working and upgrades don’t break the conversation.
changes.effort: Medium: requires changes to discovery/registry wiring and tests for backwards compatibility.
changes.risk: Low: risk is misrouting if mapping is wrong; mitigate with explicit validation against a simple health probe and a fallback to known-good tools.
changes.cost_impact: Small API overhead for registry sync; negligible runtime cost after cache.
changes.latency_impact: Slightly higher on cold start to reconcile, then faster because describe calls stop failing.
changes.security_impact: Low; must ensure registry cannot be poisoned by untrusted inputs and that tool metadata is not leaked across tenants.

changes.change: Add a relay-visible, read-only telemetry endpoint and typed status schema for live audio path health (uplink packet loss, LTE contention, half-duplex state, codec/sample-rate currently negotiated, buffer depth, and whether mac bridge/browser extension are online). Include last-updated timestamps and a minimal rolling window for trend. Provide a matching tool in the relay to fetch it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When speech starts breaking up or responses are delayed, the pendant can tell the owner what’s happening (“your network is congested; I’m switching to a safer mode”) instead of guessing or failing silently.
changes.effort: Medium: define a schema, implement read-only aggregation on the relay, wire metrics from modem/bridge where available, and expose a tool.
changes.risk: Low. Biggest risk is exposing sensitive diagnostics; mitigate by returning only coarse metrics and avoiding user-identifying data. If metrics are missing, return nulls rather than blocking.
changes.cost_impact: Low per call. A small JSON payload; dominated by whatever upstream collection already costs.
changes.latency_impact: Small improvement. Faster, clearer failure modes; avoids expensive retries.
changes.security_impact: Diagnostics could reveal environment details; restrict to authenticated relay and avoid precise location or network identifiers.
depends_on: A metrics collection hook on the pendant/bridge to publish uplink loss and contention signals (or a firmware shim that emits them).

changes.change: Add a low-power audio front end between the pendant microphone/speaker path and the nRF9160: an external I2S/PCM codec with DMA-backed ring buffers and hardware sample-rate conversion, plus a small control channel for congestion/occupancy telemetry. Keep LTE and application logic on the nRF9160, but move continuous capture/playback buffering and resampling out of the 87%-busy application core. Expose independent capture and playback queues so the relay can interrupt or resume speech without corrupting the shared full-duplex stream.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets substantially more reliable natural conversation and true 24 kHz playback while speaking over an answer, instead of clipped words, long pauses, or repeated requests. It also makes the pendant less sensitive to the current single-I2S/CPU contention and gives the adaptive transport a truthful measure of audio that is actually heard.
changes.effort: Board respin, codec selection, power and EMC validation, nRF9160 driver/firmware work, bridge protocol updates, and end-to-end contention testing. Moderate-to-high hardware effort; prototype first on an external codec breakout before committing to a PCB.
changes.risk: Added component or clocking faults could introduce noise, latency, or battery drain; a failed codec must fall back to the existing direct I2S path. Require a boot-time self-test, watchdog bypass, and firmware feature flag so the current audio path remains recoverable.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $3–$10 per unit for codec, clocking, passives, and PCB changes; likely tens of milliwatts additional draw depending on codec. No meaningful per-call API cost; reduced retransmission and fewer repeat turns may lower total model usage.
changes.latency_impact: Adds an estimated 5–20 ms buffering latency, but removes multi-second stalls caused by contention and CPU starvation. Tune ring-buffer depth dynamically rather than adding a fixed large delay.
changes.security_impact: No new cloud data path. Codec telemetry is non-content metadata; ensure debug captures are disabled by default and firmware updates are signed.
depends_on: Define the negotiated audio/congestion session-state protocol
Add relay/bridge playback occupancy and pause/resume controls
Validate codec clocking against the existing 15.625 kHz capture and 24 kHz decode requirements

changes.change: Introduce a scheduler layer (cron-like) with durable job definitions, per-job cadence, retry policy, quiet hours, and a wake/dispatch mechanism that can target mac-planner, server browser, or relay summaries. Use Cloudflare Cron/Durable Object alarms as the first backend, with a queue abstraction so the Mac and future services can share it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Unlocks everyday conveniences like morning briefs, page watches, and follow-up tasks without keeping a session open. The owner can trust the system to act later, then report back.
changes.effort: High. Requires new storage tables, dispatch code, and job state transitions; plus UI to manage jobs.
changes.risk: Misfires (duplicate runs, wrong time zone, runaway retries). Mitigate with idempotency keys, per-job rate limits, and clear audit logs. Provide a kill switch and manual rerun.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate ongoing compute/storage; biggest cost is scheduled runs and external automation. Cloudflare cron/alarm costs are small compared to model execution.
changes.latency_impact: Adds no latency to live conversations; improves perceived latency by doing work ahead of time.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled jobs may access private data. Needs strict scoping, stored consent, and auditability.
depends_on: Typed job schema with provenance and idempotency
Notification/receipt mechanism to deliver results back to the owner

changes.change: Add a scheduling layer that supports delayed and recurring jobs for both the relay (via Durable Object alarms/Cron Triggers) and the Mac agent (via a persistent queue), with a shared job schema and idempotency keys. Jobs should be resumable and report status back to the relay without requiring the Mac to stay online.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for something to happen later (or repeatedly) and trust it will actually occur, even if they walk away, lose connectivity, or the Mac sleeps.
changes.effort: Medium to high: requires new infrastructure wiring and a shared job contract.
changes.risk: Jobs may fire at the wrong time or duplicate. Mitigate with idempotency, clear logging, and safe defaults. Allow cancellation and pause.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate: persistent storage for jobs and occasional background compute; relay cost remains low per request.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency by decoupling long-running work from live conversation.
changes.security_impact: Requires careful access control to ensure scheduled tasks can only act within the owner’s permissions and do not expose private data in logs.

changes.change: Introduce a typed context service that stores compact facts with provenance, sensitivity, TTL, and last-used timestamps, and delivers only task-relevant facts to each agent. Provide a small, stable schema and token budgeting per surface.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Conversations stay fast and accurate because agents stop re-sending and re-deriving the same context every turn, and they only see what they need.
changes.effort: Medium: new service plus migration of per-surface prompt context into structured retrieval.
