args.user_asks: “When I say ‘make this safe,’ use the pendant as my physical presence signal: immediately mute Mac microphones, pause recording/streaming apps, hide or lock authenticated browser tabs, and tell me what was changed; when I return and press the button, restore only the state you recorded.”
args.why_useful: A worn, always-available control is the one surface that can react when the owner notices a privacy risk, even away from the Mac. It turns the pendant into a practical emergency privacy switch rather than another voice remote.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the short intent and confirmation speech; deterministic Mac/browser executors perform the state snapshot and reversible changes. No expensive model is needed for the actual safety action.
args.latency_budget: Start muting and tab isolation within 2 seconds of the utterance; spoken acknowledgement within 4 seconds. Restoration can take up to 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one short realtime turn (about $0.01–$0.05 depending on audio duration); execution is dominated by Mac/browser round trips, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The pendant credential becomes a physical privacy token, so replay protection, device sequence numbers, and an append-only before/after receipt are required. Never expose tab contents in the spoken acknowledgement or logs. Restore must be limited to the exact recorded resources and tolerate apps having been changed manually.
missing: A relay-to-Mac emergency command with priority over queued work
Mac adapters for microphone/recording state snapshots and reversible pause/lock operations
Browser extension support for bulk authenticated-tab isolation and exact restoration
Pendant presence/sequence and button-event authentication
A durable encrypted restoration receipt and an owner-visible recovery screen

args.user_asks: “While I was away, tell me exactly what changed on my Mac and in my open browser sessions, grouped by project, with links and a one-sentence reason for each change.”
args.why_useful: The owner can leave the computer unattended without losing situational awareness. This is not merely job status: it reconstructs a trustworthy, project-grouped change narrative from Mac action receipts, browser mutations, and the relay's voice history, then lets the owner ask follow-up questions hands-free.
args.model_tier: A cheap background summarizer builds the diff after each receipt; realtime is used only to answer the owner's spoken query and read a compact result.
args.latency_budget: Precompute incrementally after each action; spoken answer in under 3 seconds, with deeper drill-down under 8 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: One small background summarization per changed batch, roughly $0.01–$0.08/day for normal use; realtime query cost roughly $0.01–$0.03.
args.security_concerns: The report must distinguish observed facts from model inference, preserve source links and timestamps, redact secrets and page contents from audio, and never claim a change without a receipt or browser inspection. Retain only hashes and short summaries by default.
missing: A durable cross-surface event ledger joining Mac receipts, browser request IDs, pendant sessions, and project labels
A browser mutation observer that records typed outcomes rather than only current inspections
Incremental background summarization (currently there is no scheduler or worker)
Relay query endpoint that streams cited, bounded results to the pendant
A project-label resolver and dashboard timeline with source drill-down

args.user_asks: “Turn the open project page into a ready-to-review decision packet: extract the relevant facts from my authenticated browser tabs, compare them with the project files on my Mac and my calendar, draft the reply and a proposed follow-up task, and read me only the conflicts or missing facts.”
args.why_useful: Today each surface can inspect one silo, but the owner still has to manually reconcile web evidence, local files, calendar commitments, and communication. This produces a reviewable packet without sending or committing anything, so the owner can make a decision from the pendant while away from the desk.
args.model_tier: Use a slower background planner for extraction, comparison, and draft generation; realtime only captures the request and speaks the concise conflicts summary. Deterministic adapters provide citations and calendar/file facts.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; packet in 30–90 seconds for four tabs and a modest project folder, with progress updates if it exceeds 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.05–$0.30 per packet, dominated by document extraction and the planner context; subsequent spoken follow-ups are pennies.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page and local-file contents cross the relay, so encrypt in transit, minimize retained content, attach source citations, and make the packet private to the paired pendant. Drafting is reversible; sending, editing files, or creating calendar events must remain separate explicit actions.
missing: A single job type that can fan out to browser and Mac reads and then join typed results
Bounded project-folder and calendar readers with citations
Conflict detection for dates, quantities, and contradictory facts
An artifact store for draft reply/task plus provenance and expiration
Pendant-accessible packet retrieval and a separate execute-draft action

args.change: Add a tiny low-power vibration motor and driver to the pendant, with firmware patterns for acknowledgement, urgent result, failure, and incoming completion. Expose a relay command that can request a pattern with a correlation id, and queue at most one completion pattern while the link is down.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know that a spoken request completed or failed without staring at the pendant or keeping audio enabled. This makes unattended, pocketed, or noisy use dependable and gives the wearable a private notification channel instead of relying on the single LED.
args.effort: Moderate hardware revision and enclosure change: motor, transistor/driver, flyback protection, firmware PWM pattern table, and relay delivery semantics. Prototype can be wired onto the currently USB-connected nRF9160 pendant before a board revision.
args.risk: Added vibration and current spikes could reset the modem or shorten battery life; rate-limit patterns, budget peak current, and fall back to LED/audio. A stuck driver needs thermal/current protection. Recovery is firmware-safe default-off and a physical disconnect option.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$3 in components and under 20 mA peak while vibrating; negligible API cost because patterns are tiny events.
args.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement under 100 ms when USB/LTE link is live; queued completion may be delayed until reconnect.
args.security_impact: Patterns must not encode sensitive content; only generic states and opaque correlation ids should cross the device link.
depends_on: A reliable pendant event/push transport over the present USB serial connection
Firmware event queue and modem/USB power-budget measurement
Relay correlation of long-running Mac/browser jobs to device notifications

transcript.text: I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out the missing pieces.

args.user_asks: What's happening with the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?
args.why_useful: The owner can get a quick, accurate status update even when the Mac is asleep, instead of guessing or re-running tasks.
args.model_tier: realtime for the spoken response; status lookup is cheap and should avoid a full planner
args.latency_budget: Under a second to respond with a status sentence; no Mac round trip.
args.cost_estimate: Low. A small relay-side status lookup dominates; no expensive model work.
args.security_concerns: Avoid revealing sensitive task content beyond what the status tool returns. Do not upgrade wording or claim success without a success state.
missing: A working implementation of the relay_job_status tool (currently schema-only).

args.user_asks: Can you check this site and tell me the key updates, even if my Mac is offline?
args.why_useful: Lets the pendant answer web questions without depending on a nearby Mac, which is perfect when the owner is out and about.
args.model_tier: realtime for voice; a cheaper, sandboxed browser runner for the browsing and extraction work.
args.latency_budget: A few seconds is acceptable for page load and extraction; response should stream if possible.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate. Browser automation and extraction dominate; model cost is small.
args.security_concerns: Only run in a sandbox. Do not log credentials. Restrict actions to read-only unless explicitly allowed.
missing: An implemented server_browser_actions tool with a safe browser environment and result schema.
Policy and limits for allowed domains and read-only actions.

args.user_asks: Start a wearable session and keep it going after I stop talking—watch for events and update me hands-free.
args.why_useful: This would be the single most useful capability: a persistent assistant that can monitor and summarize relevant changes while the owner moves through their day.
args.model_tier: realtime for the voice front door; cheaper background models for monitoring and summarization.
args.latency_budget: Voice interactions should stay snappy; monitoring can be eventual but should notify quickly when thresholds are met.
args.cost_estimate: High overall. Persistent monitoring and multi-surface coordination dominate; should use cheaper tiers and event-driven updates.
args.security_concerns: Clear consent and scope for what is monitored. Minimize data retention, encrypt stored summaries, and provide a one-tap stop.
missing: A relay-side event push mechanism and subscription model.
Device skills for local event buffering and session state.
Background scheduling (cron/alarms) and durable subscriptions.
A cross-surface session and notification protocol.

args.change: Publish a relay-side capability inventory endpoint (e.g., GET /relay/capabilities) and a minimal job-status endpoint for the Worker itself, mirroring the Mac agent’s /capabilities and /jobs views.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster diagnosis and fewer failures: the voice agent can reliably tell the owner what it can do right now and whether a request is queued, stuck, or impossible.
args.effort: Medium. Add route wiring, durable storage reads, and docs; no model changes required.
args.risk: Exposure of internal routes if auth is misconfigured. Mitigate with bearer auth and only exposing capability names and health, not secrets.
args.cost_impact: Low. A small read path; negligible runtime cost.
args.latency_impact: Improves responsiveness by avoiding blind probing and failed attempts.
args.security_impact: Requires strict auth and redaction; audit logs for access.
depends_on: Durable object or D1 schema for relay job records if not already present.

args.change: Route long-running monitoring, research, and summarization tasks to cheaper background models, with the relay acting only as a conversational front door and notification presenter.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Keeps voice interactions snappy and reliable while still enabling richer capabilities without burning budget.
args.effort: Medium to high. Needs a task taxonomy, routing rules, and receipts for results.
args.risk: Misrouted tasks could be slow or incomplete. Mitigate with receipts and fallback to Mac delegation.
args.cost_impact: Potentially large savings by avoiding expensive realtime usage for background work.
args.latency_impact: Improves voice latency; background tasks become less jittery with proper queues.
args.security_impact: Ensure data minimization and strict scoping when tasks leave the device.
depends_on: A queue/scheduler and status reporting across surfaces.

args.why_useful_to_owner: Gives the owner confidence and control: they know what’s being watched, for how long, and how to stop it instantly.
args.effort: Medium. Needs UX rules, session state, and consistent cancellation semantics across surfaces.
args.risk: If stop fails, the system could keep monitoring. Mitigate with timeouts and kill-switch precedence.
args.cost_impact: Low to moderate. Mostly state management and messaging.
args.latency_impact: Minimal for voice; monitoring latency depends on downstream surfaces.
args.security_impact: Strongly positive: explicit consent boundaries and easy revocation.

args.user_asks: “Put me on a phone call with Alex, tell them the short version of what I said, and let me interrupt or stop it from the pendant.”
args.why_useful: The owner can delegate a real-time call while away from the Mac: the pendant is the consent and interruption surface, the relay keeps the conversation low-latency, and the Mac supplies the telephony and contact access. This is materially different from composing a message because the owner can hear, correct, and abort the live interaction.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for turn-taking and interruption; mac-planner for call setup and contact lookup; mac-vision only when the telephony app exposes state visually.
args.latency_budget: Speech turn recognition and relay response under 700 ms; call-control commands under 1 s; transcript summaries can lag 2–3 s.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per spoken minute depending on transcription/synthesis; telephony provider charges dominate any external call.
args.security_concerns: The call audio and transcript leave the pendant and may contain third-party private speech. Require an explicit spoken start command, announce that an AI is participating, provide an always-available pendant stop gesture, and retain only a short-lived transcript unless the owner asks to save it.
missing: A telephony bridge reachable by the Mac or relay
A duplex audio-call stream and interruption protocol
Pendant firmware support for a distinct stop gesture during an active call
A live-call session record with participant disclosure and stop status

args.user_asks: “When I am in a noisy or public place, keep the answer private: show me a short code on the pendant and send the full answer to my phone or Mac instead of speaking it aloud; switch back when I hold the button.”
args.why_useful: The owner can use the system around other people without broadcasting private mail, work, navigation, or health information. It uses the worn device as a physical privacy control rather than relying on the owner to remember a setting in an app.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay classifies sensitivity and chooses a terse spoken/LED response; a cheaper background path can render the full answer into a paired phone/Mac notification.
args.latency_budget: Privacy mode must engage within 200 ms of the button gesture; the terse code within 500 ms; full-screen delivery within 3 s.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for mode selection; notification transport and optional phone integration dominate implementation cost.
args.security_concerns: The code must not reveal the sensitive content to someone observing the pendant. Pairing and device authentication are required; the full answer must not be sent to an untrusted browser tab. If the relay cannot verify the private destination, it must remain silent rather than fall back to speech.
missing: A persistent privacy-mode state shared by pendant and relay
A device-authenticated notification sink for the owner’s phone/Mac
A pendant LED/display or deterministic short-code protocol
Sensitivity classification and redacted spoken-response policy

args.user_asks: “Start an incident record now. Keep the next five minutes of pendant audio, my Mac’s active window and browser tab, and timestamps together, then give me one private package I can review or share.”
args.why_useful: A single physical gesture would preserve what actually happened during a confusing support call, software failure, threatening encounter, or lost train of thought. Today those observations live separately or disappear; the owner cannot reliably reconstruct them later.
args.model_tier: No expensive reasoning while recording; relay coordinates timestamped streams. A background model later produces a short chronology and redaction suggestions, with realtime used only for the start/stop acknowledgement.
args.latency_budget: Start acknowledgement under 300 ms; clock alignment under 1 s; package assembly within 10 s after stop.
args.cost_estimate: Storage and upload dominate; optional post-event transcription/summary is roughly $0.01–$0.10 per five-minute incident.
args.security_concerns: This can capture bystanders and private screens. The pendant must give an unmistakable recording indicator, enforce a hard maximum duration, encrypt each stream to the owner, and default to local deletion after export. Sharing must be a separate explicit action and support redaction before upload.
missing: A pendant-local ring buffer and unmistakable recording indicator
Clock synchronization and a multiplexed incident manifest across audio, Mac, and browser
Encrypted bundle storage/export and retention controls
A post-event review UI with transcript, timeline, and redaction

args.change: Add a low-power coin vibration motor and a protected driver to the nRF9160 pendant, with firmware patterns for acknowledgement, private notification, urgent stop, and recording-active status. Keep the existing LED as a secondary visual indicator rather than the only output.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive and control the assistant silently in public, in a pocket, or where speech is impossible. Distinct tactile patterns make it possible to know whether a command started, finished, failed, or is still recording without looking at the pendant.
args.effort: Hardware spin for a tiny motor, transistor/driver, and board routing; firmware event-pattern table; relay event mapping; enclosure and battery testing.
args.risk: Motor noise may be audible and vibration can annoy the wearer; provide intensity limits and a disable pattern. Added current can shorten battery life. Recovery is to fall back to LED/audio and expose battery-aware pattern selection.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$4 in component and assembly cost per unit, plus a few mA only while pulsing; no model/API cost.
args.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms local feedback for button and link events; no added conversational latency.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by reducing required speech, but patterns must not encode sensitive content. Firmware update must be signed and pairing state preserved.
depends_on: A defined pendant event vocabulary shared with the relay
A device-authenticated command channel for relay-to-pendant pushes
Battery and enclosure validation

args.user_asks: “Translate this conversation for me in real time, privately, and translate my reply back; stop when I tap the pendant.”
args.why_useful: The worn microphone can stay with the owner while the relay handles low-latency turn detection and the Mac/browser can provide language models or reference terminology. This gives the owner an in-person interpreter without handing a phone back and forth.
args.model_tier: Realtime speech recognition/translation for short turns; a cheaper background model can maintain glossary and speaker context. The Mac/browser is used only for language packs, terminology lookup, or fallback computation.
args.latency_budget: Partial translation within 1.5 s after each speaker turn; stop gesture locally effective within 200 ms; never wait on Mac for the stop path.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.15 per conversation minute depending on language pair and speech synthesis; audio bandwidth is the main non-model cost.
args.security_concerns: The system records another person without necessarily knowing their consent and may translate sensitive content. Make recording/translation visibly indicated, auto-delete raw audio, keep only opt-in text, and provide a local-only mode when the network is unavailable.
missing: Duplex speaker-turn detection and streaming translation
A private output path (earbud/phone) or a pendant tactile/text fallback
Language selection and glossary controls accessible by voice
Consent indicator, raw-audio retention policy, and interruption-safe stop handling

transcript.text: Got it — I’ll quickly map what’s available now, then I’ll point out the missing pieces I’d ask for next.
I’m going to outline a few high-impact things this system should be able to do, and flag what’s missing to make them real.

args.user_asks: Keep listening and keep the thread going across my devices—if I stop talking on the pendant, pick back up on the Mac or browser without losing context.
args.why_useful: This would feel like a single conversation that follows the owner, instead of a bunch of disconnected sessions. It’s the most useful thing because it removes the biggest friction: context loss when switching surfaces.
args.model_tier: Realtime for turn-by-turn speech; cheaper planner models for continuation and tool use when the owner isn’t actively speaking.
args.latency_budget: Sub-second while the owner is speaking; seconds are fine when resuming on another surface.
args.cost_estimate: Low for voice turns; higher when summarizing long context or querying sessions. Cost dominated by context transfer and session reconciliation.
args.security_concerns: Conversation history is sensitive. Only the owner’s surfaces should be able to resume. Needs explicit session binding and audit logs.
missing: A relay-visible session inventory endpoint so the relay can see its own conversations
A durable conversation state store keyed to the owner and session
A reliable event channel to notify the Mac/browser to resume

args.user_asks: If I say “remember this”, capture the last few seconds of speech, store it with a label, and later let me ask for it back.
args.why_useful: It turns fleeting spoken context into a usable memory. That’s uniquely valuable for a wearable because it’s hands-free and happens in the moment.
args.model_tier: Realtime for detecting the intent; a cheaper text model for summarizing and indexing.
args.latency_budget: Fast capture (under a second). Retrieval can take a few seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Small per memory; dominated by audio storage and transcription.
args.security_concerns: Stored audio/text is sensitive. Needs clear retention rules, encryption at rest, and a way to delete memories by voice.
missing: On-device circular audio buffer or a relay-side short grace buffer
A memory index with labels and timestamps
Voice command to delete or list stored memories

args.user_asks: Tell me if I’m talking but nothing is being sent—like the mic is muted, the bridge is down, or LTE is failing—and help me fix it.
args.why_useful: This is a daily-wear reliability feature. It prevents silent failure, which is frustrating and hard to diagnose while you’re out and about.
args.model_tier: Realtime for feedback; cheap diagnostics when needed.
args.latency_budget: Under a second for alerts while speaking; a few seconds for troubleshooting steps.
args.cost_estimate: Low; mostly event telemetry and occasional diagnostics.
args.security_concerns: Telemetry should be minimal and not include content. Only status and error codes should be sent.
missing: A consistent health heartbeat from pendant and bridge
Standardized error codes for audio pipeline failures
A guided recovery flow (reconnect bridge, restart audio path)

args.user_asks: When I ask “is this legitimate?” about a message, invoice, offer, or webpage, have my pendant return a short verdict with the exact evidence it checked across my authenticated browser, Mac files/apps, and recent conversation context.
args.why_useful: The owner gets a trustworthy answer to high-consequence everyday questions without manually copying information between devices; the worn front door, browser sessions, and private Mac data each contribute evidence no single node can reach.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the spoken question and final concise reply; a cheaper background planner performs evidence extraction and comparison, with faculty-judgement synthesizing confidence and conflicts.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 500 ms; return a preliminary answer in 5 seconds and refine within 20 seconds if browser/Mac evidence is slow.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.03–$0.15 per investigation; authenticated page extraction and Mac-context retrieval dominate, while realtime speech should see only the compact question and final evidence summary.
args.security_concerns: Sensitive browser pages and local files leave their surfaces only as narrowly scoped excerpts; citations and uncertainty must be retained. Never claim legitimacy from one source, and clearly say when evidence is unavailable. Require explicit confirmation before sending, paying, deleting, or replying.
missing: A cross-surface evidence broker that accepts one question, queries browser and Mac in parallel, and returns typed cited evidence
A durable per-investigation record with source provenance, conflict detection, and expiration of sensitive excerpts
A relay response path that can deliver a multi-stage result to the pendant without making the owner repeat the question

args.user_asks: Press the pendant button once during a conversation or while reading something and say “save this moment”; later ask “what did I save?” and hear a time-ordered, searchable digest that links the audio moment to the relevant Mac window, calendar event, browser tab, and any follow-up I mentioned.
args.why_useful: This turns an intentionally marked real-world moment into durable memory even when the owner is away from the Mac, instead of forcing them to take notes or remember which device held the context.
args.model_tier: A small background model segments and labels the captured moment; realtime is used only for the save command and later spoken retrieval. Vision/browser adapters attach optional context rather than transcribing everything continuously.
args.latency_budget: Button acknowledgement under 300 ms; save confirmation under 3 seconds; retrieval under 4 seconds for the first digest, with deeper source expansion on demand.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per saved moment plus storage; audio transcription and optional screenshot/page metadata are the dominant costs.
args.security_concerns: Capture must be visibly indicated by the pendant LED and be bounded to a short pre/post window, not ambient recording. Store encrypted, owner-scoped records with retention controls; browser page text and screenshots require source-level deletion. Never silently capture other people’s conversations.
missing: A local short rolling audio buffer and explicit button-triggered capture window
A cross-device context correlator using timestamp, active Mac window, calendar, and browser tab identity
A searchable memory index and spoken retrieval endpoint with source links and deletion by voice

args.user_asks: While I am away from my Mac, let me ask the pendant “what changed since I left?” and get only material changes across my open browser workspaces, Mac notifications/files/calendar, and any relay jobs—grouped by urgency, with a spoken explanation and a way to say “handle the first one.”
args.why_useful: The owner can stay oriented while mobile without opening every device or receiving noisy notifications; the pendant supplies presence and speech, while the browser and Mac provide private state that the relay cannot see alone.
args.model_tier: Background comparison and ranking use a cheaper model against compact snapshots; realtime only interprets the query, gives the ranked digest, and routes a selected item to action.
args.latency_budget: Return a cached baseline summary in 2 seconds; refresh browser/Mac sources within 10 seconds; acknowledge selected action immediately and report completion asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.10 per refresh, dominated by page/file diffs and Mac snapshot collection; caching avoids resending unchanged context.
args.security_concerns: Snapshots must be encrypted, scoped to the owner, and diffed locally where possible. Redact secrets and unrelated content before model submission. “Handle” must preserve the exact selected item and action receipt so the owner can tell what changed and what was done.
missing: A departure/return checkpoint that captures compact, content-redacted snapshots from Mac and authenticated browser tabs
A diff-and-urgency engine that understands semantic changes rather than raw timestamps
A pendant-friendly notification/status channel and action correlation from spoken selection through Mac/browser execution

args.user_asks: When my spoken request is ambiguous, have the pendant silently ask my Mac and authenticated browser what I am currently looking at, then ask me exactly one useful clarification (“the Outlook draft or the Safari page?”) before carrying out the right action.
args.why_useful: A worn voice interface cannot see the owner’s visual context, while the Mac and browser cannot hear intent reliably. This eliminates the most frustrating failure mode—an action on the wrong app, tab, or document—without making the owner explain context they already have on screen.
args.model_tier: Realtime interprets the utterance and speaks the one clarification; low-cost perception workers inspect active-window and tab metadata, while judgement resolves candidate referents. Action runs only after the answer is received.
args.latency_budget: Silent context probes in 1 second; clarification within 2 seconds of the utterance; execute within 5 seconds after the owner answers.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per ambiguity, primarily Mac/browser context extraction; most requests need no extra model turn if confidence is high.
args.security_concerns: Only inspect the foreground Mac window and explicitly connected browser tabs; do not transmit full screen contents unless needed. Show a visible pendant LED during inspection, expire candidate context quickly, and preserve an action receipt identifying the resolved target.
missing: A low-latency context probe that joins active Mac window identity with browser tab identity
A referent-resolution contract returning ranked candidates and one safe clarification question
A relay conversation state that pauses execution, accepts the spoken answer, then resumes the same intent without losing target identity

transcript.text:
Recorded four new capabilities. The owner still needs:

1. **Cross-device legitimacy checks**  
   The pendant should investigate a message, invoice, offer, or webpage across authenticated browser sessions and Mac data, then return a cited verdict with uncertainty and conflicting evidence.

2. **Marked-moment memory**  
   A button press plus “save this moment” should preserve a bounded audio segment and correlate it with the active Mac window, calendar event, browser tab, and follow-up context for later spoken retrieval.

3. **Semantic change digest**  
   The owner should be able to ask “what changed since I left?” and receive only important changes across the Mac, browser, and relay jobs, with the ability to select an item verbally for action.

4. **Context-aware clarification**  
   When a request could refer to multiple visible documents or tabs, the relay should inspect active Mac/browser context and ask one precise clarification rather than guessing.

The main missing pieces are not individual actions; they are cross-surface coordination:

- bounded, locally indicated audio capture and retention;
- timestamped context correlation across pendant, Mac, and browser;
- semantic evidence/diff indexes with citations and expiration;
- conversational state that pauses an intent, asks one clarification, and resumes safely;
- asynchronous result delivery back to the pendant;
- provenance-rich receipts tying each answer or action to its sources.

The first capability—evidence-backed legitimacy checking—is the most valuable: it combines the wearable’s immediate access, the browser’s authenticated sessions, and the Mac’s private local context into something no single surface can provide today.
I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out what’s still missing.

args.user_asks: Keep an ear on what I’m doing and step in when I’m stuck, then hand off to my Mac or browser if needed.
args.why_useful: This becomes a real daily co-pilot: the pendant hears confusion, repeated failed attempts, or a request for help, and routes to the right surface without the owner having to explain the whole situation.
args.model_tier: Realtime for detection and prompting; cheaper Mac planner for execution; browser only if a web session is required.
args.latency_budget: Under a second for the nudge; seconds to minutes for Mac/browser follow-up.
args.cost_estimate: Low per minute for detection; execution cost dominated by Mac planning and any browser actions.
args.security_concerns: Audio stays on-device/relay for detection; only task summaries and necessary context are sent. Avoid sending raw audio unless the owner explicitly says so.
missing: Implemented relay_route_intent for explicit routing and status callbacks
A lightweight event stream from pendant/bridge to relay for interaction signals
Policy for what counts as 'stuck' and a safe fallback when detection is wrong

args.user_asks: If I say 'summarize what just happened', give me a concise recap and what’s next.
args.why_useful: Owners can finish a voice interaction and get a clear, spoken summary and a suggested next step—great for walking, commuting, or multitasking.
args.model_tier: Realtime to assemble the spoken recap; Mac for pulling receipts and context when available.
args.latency_budget: 1-2 seconds for a recap, longer if receipts need fetching.
args.cost_estimate: Cheap if using existing job receipts; cost rises with extra context retrieval.
args.security_concerns: Summaries should avoid sensitive content unless it was part of the task; receipts can be referenced without exposing raw data.
missing: A durable, cross-surface 'interaction log' that the relay can query without resending context
Standardized receipt formats across Mac actions and browser actions

args.user_asks: Run this workflow even if my Mac is asleep, and tell me when it’s done.
args.why_useful: This is the big one: it turns the system into an always-on assistant that can complete tasks across surfaces without the owner babysitting.
args.model_tier: Cheaper background model for long-running orchestration, realtime only for updates and interruptions.
args.latency_budget: Seconds to start, minutes to hours to finish depending on task.
args.cost_estimate: Dominated by browser/cloud execution time and retry logic; relay cost is low.
args.security_concerns: Must strictly scope credentials and data access; browser actions need isolated sessions and explicit permission boundaries.
missing: Implemented server_browser_actions for cloud browsing
A durable orchestrator with retries, timeouts, and completion events
A notification pathway to the pendant when work finishes

args.change: Add a self-describing /capabilities endpoint for the relay surface, including granted tools, available routes, and current wiring status (implemented vs schema-only).
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster diagnosis when something fails. The assistant can tell the owner what’s actually possible right now instead of guessing or wasting turns.
args.effort: Medium: add route, hook into build metadata, expose wiring flags.
args.risk: Low. Risk is leaking internal details; mitigate by returning only capability names and statuses, not secrets.
args.cost_impact: Low per call; small maintenance cost.
args.latency_impact: Negligible.
args.security_impact: Ensure output is sanitized and excludes tokens, session identifiers, and private config.

args.change: Implement relay_route_intent as the explicit routing path from realtime to mac-planner/mac-vision, with status callbacks and a durable intent id.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Natural voice commands reliably land on the right agent, and the owner can ask what happened without re-explaining.
args.effort: High: needs backend wiring, intent id propagation, and job record linkage.
args.risk: Medium. Misrouting would be confusing; include clear fallback to mac_delegate when ambiguous.
args.cost_impact: Low per intent; main cost is development and testing.
args.latency_impact: Small overhead; reduces costly retries.
args.security_impact: Log intent metadata only; avoid storing raw utterances unless needed for debugging and explicitly allowed.

args.change: Implement server_browser_actions using an isolated, ephemeral browser session with strict allowlists and artifact capture (DOM snapshot, extracted text, evidence links).
args.why_useful_to_owner: Lets tasks continue even when the Mac is offline, and gives verifiable results the owner can trust.
args.effort: High: needs Browser Run integration, session isolation, and evidence capture.
args.risk: High. Browser automation can leak credentials or take unintended actions; enforce allowlists and read-only modes by default.
args.cost_impact: Moderate per run; dominated by cloud browser time.
args.latency_impact: Higher than local actions; acceptable for unattended workflows.
args.security_impact: Strong isolation, no credential reuse across tasks, explicit user authorization for write actions.

args.user_asks: When I say “meeting mode,” have the pendant listen for the next conversation, continuously extract only decisions, commitments, and names/deadlines, then send me a short spoken recap and create dated follow-up items in the right Mac app, with links to the relevant authenticated browser page when one is mentioned.
args.why_useful: The owner can leave the Mac behind and still turn a real-world conversation into actionable, attributable work instead of manually reconstructing it later. The pendant supplies proximity audio, the relay supplies low-latency capture and recap, the Mac supplies durable artifacts, and the browser supplies session-aware source links.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for start/stop cues and a compact rolling transcript; background cheaper model for diarization, decision extraction, and deadline normalization; Mac planner only for final artifact creation.
args.latency_budget: Start acknowledgement under 500 ms; spoken interim cue within 3 s after a detected commitment; final recap within 30 s of stopping. Processing can be batched every 10–20 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.15 per 30-minute meeting depending on audio transcription and extraction; audio upload and transcription dominate.
args.security_concerns: Conversation audio and extracted names may leave the pendant and be retained. Require an explicit button/voice start and stop, a visible LED while recording, automatic deletion of raw audio after extraction, and a local-only mode when no uplink exists. Browser links must be citations, not copied page contents unless requested.
missing: A pendant recording session primitive with explicit LED state and bounded raw-audio retention
Streaming audio segmentation/transcription and speaker/decision extraction worker
A cross-surface artifact API that can create dated follow-ups and attach browser citations
A reliable way to associate spoken page names with the owner’s currently authenticated browser tabs

args.user_asks: Let me say “make this a brief” while wearing the pendant: have the relay collect the current authenticated browser tabs and the relevant Mac project files, reconcile contradictions, and deliver a cited one-page brief as a file in the project folder plus a spoken three-sentence summary.
args.why_useful: Today browser research, local files, and the wearable conversation are separate worlds. This would produce a useful artifact that combines sources the owner can reach only through different physical nodes, rather than merely answering from one surface.
args.model_tier: Cheap background synthesis model for retrieval, source normalization, and drafting; realtime tier only handles the spoken command and completion summary; planner/terminal perform bounded file creation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; deliver within 60–120 s for up to eight tabs and one project directory. If source collection exceeds that, provide a partial cited brief rather than blocking the conversation.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.30 per brief; context ingestion and synthesis dominate, with browser extraction and file scanning kept bounded.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated tab contents and local project files are sensitive. Never broaden beyond explicitly selected tabs/project; preserve source URLs and local paths in the artifact; redact credentials and tokens; keep an audit record and make the generated file reversible.
missing: A single request-scoped source selector spanning browser sessions and Mac paths
A bounded local-project indexing/read route exposed to the relay
A citation-preserving synthesis worker that can reconcile conflicting sources
An artifact delivery route with atomic write and receipt semantics

args.change: Add a physical conversational checkpoint protocol: after the relay hands a multi-surface task to Mac or browser, it emits a compact spoken 'contract' (goal, scope, expected artifact, and expiration), accepts a single spoken correction during a short grace window, and otherwise lets the downstream plan continue. The contract and correction become immutable metadata on the resulting receipt.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can correct a misunderstood request while walking away without repeating the entire task, while still knowing exactly what the remote agents were told to do. This is materially safer and more usable than silent handoff or a long clarification dialogue.
args.effort: Medium-high: relay session state, audio playback/interruption handling, downstream request metadata, and receipt display all need coordinated changes.
args.risk: A late correction could race an action already executed. Use monotonic request versions, stop accepting corrections once execution begins, and clearly speak when the window closes; recover by issuing a compensating action or undo where available.
args.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; one extra short response per delegated task. Storage is tiny per request.
args.latency_impact: Adds 1–3 seconds only when the owner chooses to correct; normal delegation remains immediate.
args.security_impact: Improves transparency but places task scope in receipts. Encrypt or minimize spoken contract metadata and never include secrets from browser pages.
depends_on: A durable request/job identity shared by relay, Mac planner, and browser command queue
A pendant audio interruption or short-grace playback mechanism
Receipt records that store request version and spoken correction

args.user_asks: When I approach my Mac wearing the pendant, let me tap its button and say “handoff,” then move the active voice task, transcript context, and browser tab focus from the remote relay onto the Mac; when I leave, the pendant remains the conversational control and the Mac locks the handoff context.
args.why_useful: The owner should not have to restart or repeat a task when moving between walking and desk work. The physical pendant provides an unambiguous proximity gesture, the relay preserves continuity, the Mac takes over rich execution, and the browser extension transfers the authenticated tab context.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the tiny handoff dialogue; no expensive synthesis is needed. Mac and browser agents resume the existing task state rather than re-planning it.
args.latency_budget: Button acknowledgement under 200 ms; handoff complete within 3 s over USB and under 8 s over LTE/Wi-Fi. Context transfer must be resumable if the link drops.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per handoff; dominated by a small context transfer, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The handoff token is effectively a physical bearer credential. Bind it to a rotating device key, require a fresh button press, expire tokens quickly, and never transfer raw browser secrets or full audio history. Lock or revoke the Mac-side session when the pendant disconnects.
missing: Firmware device-key identity and button gesture for handoff
A relay session-transfer endpoint with resumable, minimal context snapshots
Mac USB/serial presence detection and a handoff/resume consumer
Browser extension support for exporting/importing tab focus without exposing cookies

transcript.text: Got it — I’ll quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few genuinely useful capabilities and call out what’s still missing.

args.user_asks: Keep working on that and tell me what happened when it’s done.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful behavior: the owner can start something by voice, walk away, and later get a precise status without guessing. It turns the system into a reliable assistant instead of a live-only toy.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the handoff; cheaper planner/executor for background work.
args.latency_budget: Handoff must feel immediate (<1s spoken acknowledgment). Work may take minutes; status must be available instantly when asked.
args.cost_estimate: Low per handoff; main cost is downstream planning/execution plus receipts storage.
args.security_concerns: Status should reveal only what the owner asked it to do. No cross-account leakage; include task names, timestamps, and receipts.
missing: A working intent routing implementation (relay_route_intent schema exists but is unimplemented).
Durable background job runner and queue (scheduler currently absent).
Reliable receipt storage and retrieval wired end-to-end.

args.user_asks: Watch this page for meaningful changes and tell me only when it matters.
args.why_useful: Cuts noise while giving the owner confidence they won’t miss important updates in authenticated accounts, orders, or dashboards.
args.model_tier: Planner for watch definition and extraction; cheap periodic checker when scheduling exists.
args.latency_budget: Definition is interactive; notifications can be delayed but should be timely (minutes to hours depending on cadence).
args.cost_estimate: Dominated by browser session maintenance and extraction; minimized by semantic fingerprints and change thresholds.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated content is sensitive. Store only extracted fields and hashes when possible; never exfiltrate full pages unnecessarily.
missing: Durable watch definitions with cadence and quiet hours.
Authenticated browser session binding and reattachment.
Scheduler or durable alarms to run checks.
Semantic diffing and volatile field rules.

args.user_asks: Get me ready for my next meeting.
args.why_useful: A wearable assistant that can pull calendar context, open relevant docs, summarize threads, and prep a short spoken brief is a daily habit-forming feature.
args.model_tier: Planner for context gathering; realtime only to deliver the brief and take quick follow-ups.
args.latency_budget: Prep can take up to a minute; spoken output should be under 30 seconds by default.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; mostly context retrieval and summarization. Cached results reduce repeats.
args.security_concerns: Calendar and documents are private. Summaries must stay within the owner’s context and avoid sharing beyond the session.
missing: Cross-surface context assembler with provenance and freshness.
Reliable access to calendar/email/doc sources via Mac agent.
Audio queue support for pendant playback.

args.user_asks: If the connection gets choppy, keep the conversation going smoothly and don’t lose what I said.
args.why_useful: Right now the LTE-M link can saturate when both sides speak, causing dropped audio packets and a frustrating experience. A voice-first device needs graceful degradation.
args.model_tier: Realtime for interaction; local buffering on-device to survive brief drops.
args.latency_budget: No added latency for normal turns; buffering should cover a few seconds without noticeable delay.
args.cost_estimate: Small runtime cost; dominant cost is implementation complexity in firmware and relay buffering.
args.security_concerns: Buffered audio is sensitive. Keep buffers short, encrypted in transit, and discard automatically after delivery.
missing: Device skill for short-grace audio buffering and retransmit.
Relay support for packet reordering/ack and partial transcript repair.
Optional local VAD to avoid buffering silence.

args.user_asks: "Give me a spoken, evidence-backed answer about what is currently on my Mac screen and in my active browser tab, then let me say 'do it' to act on that exact context."
args.why_useful: The owner can be away from the keyboard yet recover the precise situation they are looking at instead of receiving a generic Mac or web answer. The pendant supplies the voice and intent, Mac vision supplies pixels and application state, and the browser harness supplies authenticated page content; the relay can cite which surface each claim came from before any action.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for the short spoken exchange; gpt-4.1-mini vision for a screenshot/UI grounding pass; gpt-5.6-luna only for the follow-up multi-step action; browser extraction locally in the extension where sessions are already authenticated.
args.latency_budget: Answer in 3-5 seconds for inspection, with a second short turn for execution. The owner tolerates a few seconds because this replaces walking back to the desk.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01-$0.05 per inspection depending on screenshot and page-token size; the expensive part is vision/context serialization, not relay routing.
args.security_concerns: Screen pixels and authenticated page text leave the Mac only to the relay/model path and may contain secrets. Minimize to the active window/tab, redact password fields, retain the evidence bundle briefly, and make 'do it' explicitly target the displayed bundle rather than silently re-inspecting a changed page.
missing: A relay endpoint that atomically snapshots active Mac window plus active authenticated browser tab and returns a cited evidence bundle
mac-vision support for a stable snapshot id and compact UI facts
A two-turn confirmation/context binding in the voice session

args.user_asks: "I’m leaving my desk—snapshot the work context. When I come back and press the pendant, tell me only what changed in my editor, terminal, and authenticated browser tabs, and take me back to the exact place I left."
args.why_useful: This turns the wearable into a genuine continuity surface across physical absence: the owner does not need to remember which window, tab, or command mattered. It is event-driven rather than a scheduled briefing, and it works across the Mac and browser session boundaries that no single node can see.
args.model_tier: Cheap background summarization of the two bounded snapshots; realtime relay only handles the return question and spoken delta. Use Mac planner/vision to restore exact app/tab/scroll anchors, not a language-model guess.
args.latency_budget: Snapshot under 2 seconds on departure; return delta under 5 seconds, with restoration immediately after the owner says 'take me there'.

args.user_asks: "I found a bug—use my voice to investigate it across the project, reproduce it, make the smallest fix, run the relevant tests, and tell me what changed and whether the test actually passed."

It removes the current gap where delegation can act but cannot reliably explain verified completion.

args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 2 seconds, then run asynchronously. Typical completion may take 1-10 minutes; the owner should be able to ask for a spoken checkpoint without restarting the work.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05-$0.40 per issue, dominated by planner context and any vision/browser reproduction; tests themselves have no model cost.
args.security_concerns: Repository contents, logs, and potentially authenticated web data are sensitive. Keep execution on the Mac, send only targeted excerpts, record exact commands and diffs, and never claim success unless an actual exit code and test artifact are attached. args.risk: False negatives could leak sensitive text; false positives could make a task frustrating. Recover with visible/ spoken placeholders, a per-session audit trail, and explicit one-shot reveal rather than silently disabling the whole workflow.
args.cost_impact: Small per-request classifier/token cost; roughly $0.005-$0.02 for OCR/DOM sensitivity checks, with no new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds about 100-400 ms for DOM checks and lightweight OCR; full-screen vision may add 1-2 seconds only when a screenshot is requested.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves data minimization, but the classifier itself sees the raw content locally. Keep classification on the Mac/extension, transmit only redacted artifacts and sensitivity labels, and expire reveal artifacts immediately.

a session-scoped spoken one-shot reveal command

transcript.text:
Recorded four new capabilities/changes:

1. **Exact-context voice inspection and action** across the active Mac screen and authenticated browser tab, with evidence-bound follow-up execution.
2. **Departure/return work continuity**: snapshot the active editor, terminal, and browser context when leaving, then report only meaningful changes and restore the exact location on return.
3. **Voice-driven bug repair loop**: investigate, reproduce across Mac/browser, patch, run tests, and report only verified results.
4. **Sensitive-content guardian** for screenshot, browser extraction, and spoken readback, with local redaction and explicit one-shot reveal.
5. **Pendant haptic/touch feedback** for private status, completion, redaction, and immediate local cancel/mute.

What is still needed is primarily the connective layer: stable cross-surface snapshot IDs, event delivery from the pendant, durable evidence/job bundles, streamed Mac test output, browser-to-terminal handoff, and local privacy classification before data reaches the relay.
I’m going to take a quick inventory of what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out any missing pieces.

args.user_asks: Tell me what’s happening with that thing I asked the Mac to do.
args.why_useful: It gives the wearer a quick, hands-free status update even when the Mac is asleep or far away, without guessing or overpromising.
args.model_tier: realtime for the spoken turn; no downstream model needed for the read
args.latency_budget: Under a second for a simple status read; no waiting for Mac wake or network round trips to the Mac agent.
args.cost_estimate: Low. A single relay read of job history dominates; no browser or model planning costs.
args.security_concerns: Status text is sensitive because it can reveal tasks and filenames. Keep outputs verbatim and minimal; never fabricate completion.
missing: relay_job_status implementation (currently schema-only)
built_from: route: GET /jobs/:jobId (as a fallback if implemented on relay)

args.user_asks: When I say “remember this exactly” on the pendant, save a time-and-location-stamped voice clip together with the Mac’s current app/window and any relevant authenticated browser tab, then later let me ask “what was I looking at when I said that?” and hear a cited answer.
args.why_useful: A fleeting spoken thought would become reliably recoverable context, not an isolated transcript. The answer would tie the owner’s physical utterance to the exact digital state they were working in, which no Mac-only or browser-only agent can reconstruct.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the short capture acknowledgement and retrieval dialogue; a cheaper background model should extract entities and generate the later citation bundle.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge capture in under 500 ms; collect Mac/browser snapshots opportunistically within 5 seconds; retrieval response in under 4 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per captured/retrieved item, dominated by transcription and background summarization; raw audio storage dominates bytes, not API spend.
args.security_concerns: Audio, screen metadata, URLs, and possibly page text leave the pendant and may contain secrets. Encrypt at rest, retain raw audio briefly, make authenticated-tab capture explicit in the utterance, and never expose page secrets in spoken output.
missing: A pendant capture endpoint that preserves the original audio and timestamp
A relay correlation record joining voice, Mac foreground-window snapshot, and browser tab inspection
A durable searchable memory index with source citations and retention controls
A browser extension snapshot API callable at capture time

args.user_asks: Use my pendant as a physical presence key: when I say “use my private browser,” only a currently-attached or recently authenticated pendant can authorize the relay to operate my authenticated browser tabs, and the pendant immediately tells me if that presence expires while work is running.
args.why_useful: It lets the owner safely delegate real authenticated work while away from the Mac without relying on a typed password or a vague cloud session. Stealing a browser cookie alone would not be enough; the worn object becomes the human-presence boundary.
args.model_tier: No expensive reasoning for authorization; use deterministic firmware/relay checks. Realtime speech is only for the owner’s command and concise expiry warning.
args.latency_budget: Presence verification under 200 ms over USB or under 2 seconds over LTE; browser commands should start within 3 seconds; expiry warning immediately on loss.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; approximately $5–$20 for a secure-element-backed pendant revision, plus tiny relay storage and heartbeat traffic.
args.security_concerns: A compromised Mac, relay, or pendant could impersonate presence. Use challenge-response keys, nonce-bound job tokens, replay protection, short leases, revocation, and never speak secrets aloud. This is an authorization boundary, not a claim that the pendant proves identity at a distance.
missing: Hardware-backed key storage and challenge-response firmware on the nRF9160 pendant
A relay presence-lease service that binds each browser/Mac job to a nonce and expiry
Browser and Mac command handlers that reject jobs whose lease is absent or stale
A visible pendant LED pattern and dashboard audit trail for lease state

args.user_asks: Before carrying out a consequential multi-app request, have the Mac planner and browser agent independently reconstruct what will happen, compare their predicted effects, and tell me the disagreement in one spoken sentence; if they agree, execute and return a receipt plus the evidence each used.
args.why_useful: The owner gets a dependable end-to-end operator rather than a single model confidently misreading a page or app. Independent disagreement is especially valuable when the owner is away from the Mac and cannot visually inspect the action.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to normalize the request and speak the result. Use cheaper planner/vision/judgement models in parallel; reserve a stronger model for resolving only genuine disagreements.
args.latency_budget: Parallel predictions in 5–10 seconds for ordinary workflows; a disagreement explanation within 2 seconds after both return; execution and receipt can continue asynchronously with spoken completion later.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.30 per workflow, dominated by duplicated planner/vision inference and browser extraction; far cheaper than recovering from a wrong external action.
args.security_concerns: Independent agents may share the same blind spot, and page content can be malicious prompt injection. Keep predictions in typed effect schemas, isolate untrusted page text, retain both evidence sets, and never claim agreement means safety. Owner policy currently permits execution without a confirmation gate.
missing: A relay fan-out/fan-in coordinator for one spoken request
A common typed predicted-effects and evidence schema across Mac, vision, and browser agents
A faculty-judgement comparison route that can explain disagreements without taking over execution
An execution lock ensuring the action uses the exact plan that was compared
A spoken completion/status channel for results after the owner stops talking

args.user_asks: If I double-press the pendant and say “stop,” immediately halt the active Mac or browser workflow, cancel any not-yet-started steps, and tell me exactly which steps already happened and which were prevented.
args.why_useful: The owner can recover from a mistaken command while away from the Mac, using the one control surface they physically have. This is an emergency brake, not a confirmation gate, and it makes autonomous multi-step work materially safer.
args.model_tier: Deterministic pendant gesture and relay cancellation path; realtime model only interprets the short spoken stop phrase and summarizes receipts. No expensive planning model is needed.
args.latency_budget: Cancel signal should leave the pendant within 300 ms and reach the active executor within 1 second; spoken step accounting within 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost; modest durable job-state and event storage. Hardware needs only firmware gesture support on the existing one-button device.
args.security_concerns: Cancellation must be authenticated to the active job and idempotent. A lost link may prevent stopping already-running local processes, so the Mac/browser executors need cooperative checkpoints and a clearly reported last-known state. Do not pretend external side effects can be undone.
missing: Pendant firmware double-press/long-press emergency event and local LED acknowledgement
A relay cancellation endpoint and fan-out to Mac and browser executors
Checkpointed execution with cancellation polling between actions
Receipt semantics that distinguish completed, cancelled, and unknown-in-flight steps
A short spoken-status interrupt path that works while no normal turn is active

The most actionable gap for you is typed cancellation checkpoints and receipt states across Mac/browser jobs.

transcript.text:
Recorded four capabilities:

1. **Voice bookmarks tied to digital context** — save a spoken note with the Mac’s active app and authenticated browser state, then retrieve it later with citations.
2. **Pendant-backed physical presence** — require a cryptographic pendant lease before operating authenticated browser sessions.
3. **Independent cross-node verification** — have Mac and browser agents predict effects independently, report disagreements, then execute with evidence and receipts.
4. **Pendant emergency stop** — double-press and say “stop” to cancel active Mac/browser workflows and hear exactly what completed versus what was prevented.

What remains needed is primarily new coordination and device support: durable cross-surface correlation, cryptographic pendant firmware, typed prediction/evidence schemas, cancellation checkpoints, and a relay path for spoken status outside an active conversation.
I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few useful owner-facing capabilities and call out any missing pieces.

args.user_asks: If I stop talking, keep working on it and tell me what happened when it’s done.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing for a wearable assistant: the owner can start something, walk away, and still get a trustworthy outcome summary without babysitting.
args.model_tier: relay for conversation; mac-planner for planning/execution; cheaper background model for long-running monitoring.
args.latency_budget: Fast spoken acknowledgment (<300ms) at the relay, then asynchronous execution and status updates as they complete.
args.cost_estimate: Low per spoken interaction; execution costs dominated by downstream planning/actions and any browser automation.
args.security_concerns: Must not claim success unless receipts say done. Status messages must be sourced from job records; avoid leaking private page contents in spoken summaries.
missing: Durable job runner for relay-issued work
Implemented relay intent routing and status streaming
Background worker/scheduler for follow-ups and retries

args.user_asks: Tell me what’s urgent across my stuff right now, and only the top three things.
args.why_useful: A daily “attention triage” saves time and reduces overwhelm, especially when the owner is on the move and can’t scan multiple apps.
args.model_tier: relay for voice; mac-planner for local sources; browser harness for authenticated web; cheaper model for ranking and summarization.
args.latency_budget: Quick acknowledgment, then a brief spoken summary within a few seconds; deeper evidence available on the Mac.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; dominated by reading sources (calendar/mail/browser) and summarization.
args.security_concerns: Needs strict source tagging and must show evidence on Mac. Should draft actions but not send or submit without explicit approval.
missing: Reliable authenticated browser session access without the Mac
Unified review queue with evidence and drafts
Scheduler for periodic checks if run unattended

args.user_asks: Prepare this form or message for me, show me exactly what will change, and wait for my go-ahead.
args.why_useful: This turns the assistant into a safe co-pilot: it can do the tedious parts and still keep the owner in control for irreversible steps.
args.model_tier: mac-planner/browser for extraction and drafting; relay for spoken confirmation; cheaper model for diffing and summarizing changes.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge fast; drafting may take longer. Final approval step must be explicit and reversible where possible.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; extraction and draft generation dominate, plus any browser automation.
args.security_concerns: Never submit without approval. Keep sensitive fields minimized in spoken output; show full diff in a secure review surface.
missing: Provenance-aware extraction and typed results from browser automation
Reliable command queue with irreversible-action checkpoints
UI for review and approval across devices

args.user_asks: When I say “pause the hive,” stop every in-flight Mac and browser action immediately, preserve exactly where each task was, and resume when I say “continue” — even if I am away from the Mac.
args.why_useful: The owner can interrupt an unsafe, mistaken, or socially inconvenient action from the wearable instead of racing to the keyboard. This is a cross-surface primitive: the pendant supplies the urgent signal, the relay fans it out, and Mac/browser workers must cooperatively cancel and checkpoint work.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only classifies the short voice command; cancellation, checkpointing, and resume are deterministic worker behavior.
args.latency_budget: The stop signal should reach every worker in under 500 ms; resume can take a few seconds while workers restore checkpoints.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for a command; engineering/storage cost is a durable cancellation token and per-action checkpoints, not inference.
args.security_concerns: A false wake or speech recognition could interrupt work, so require the physical pendant button plus the spoken phrase for the global variant. Checkpoints must exclude secrets and never serialize browser credentials. Resume must be idempotent to avoid duplicate mutations.
missing: relay-wide cancellation broadcast and durable run state
cooperative cancellation hooks in Mac planner/vision and browser extension
pendant button-plus-voice emergency command
idempotent checkpoint/resume protocol and owner-visible pause receipt

args.user_asks: While I am at my desk, let me say “remember this page for me.” Later, away from the Mac, let me ask the pendant “what did that page say about the renewal date?” and get a cited answer without reopening the site or exposing my browser cookies.
args.why_useful: This turns authenticated browser access into a safe, portable memory rather than requiring the owner to be at the computer every time. The browser keeps the session and emits only an explicitly requested, expiring excerpt; the relay can answer from that sealed fact while the Mac is offline.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to extract and normalize the explicitly selected page excerpt; use realtime only for the later short spoken lookup.
args.latency_budget: Capture confirmation under 2 seconds; an away-from-Mac lookup under 3 seconds if the sealed excerpt is local to the relay.
args.cost_estimate: One small extraction call per saved excerpt and a small lookup call later; storage is a few KB per fact, dominated by model extraction rather than transport.
args.security_concerns: Never copy cookies, DOM broadly, or unrestricted page text. Require an explicit spoken/button save, encrypt the excerpt, attach source URL, timestamp, scope, and expiry, and support immediate revoke. Sensitive fields should be redacted locally before upload.
missing: browser-extension command to create a narrowly scoped signed excerpt
encrypted relay vault with expiry and revocation
citation-aware retrieval over owner-approved excerpts
pendant UX for naming, querying, and deleting saved facts

args.latency_impact: No meaningful added latency; posture is local and attached before transcription routing.

args.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial handoff and final spoken status; cheaper Mac/browser tiers do the work.
args.latency_budget: Handoff under a second; execution can take minutes; status retrieval must be instant when asked.
args.cost_estimate: Low per handoff; the expensive part is downstream tool usage and any page reads, not the relay conversation.

args.user_asks: “Mark this moment.” Have the pendant capture a short audio excerpt and, if the Mac is reachable, attach the active screen/browser state; later let me ask “what did I mark at lunch?” and get a time-ordered, source-cited answer.
args.why_useful: The owner can preserve fleeting ideas, decisions, and things visible on a screen without opening an app or remembering to take notes. The worn button/audio path supplies the moment, the Mac supplies inaccessible visual context, and the relay makes the record retrievable when the owner is away.
args.model_tier: Realtime model handles the immediate marker acknowledgment and entity/time normalization; a cheaper background model performs transcription, screen/browser summarization, indexing, and later retrieval.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the mark in under 500 ms; capture can complete asynchronously within 10 seconds. Retrieval should return a spoken answer in 2–4 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per marked minute plus a few cents per retrieval, dominated by audio transcription and optional screen image/OCR processing.

missing: A pendant event/audio upload endpoint that accepts a bounded clip
A Mac snapshot endpoint returning active-window metadata and an optionally user-enabled screenshot
An encrypted episodic index with time/source citations and deletion
A joiner that correlates pendant timestamps with Mac/browser state

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving—give me a handoff.” The pendant should ask the Mac and browser for a fresh departure snapshot: unsaved work, running long jobs, active calls, private tabs, and anything that will need attention when I return, then speak a prioritized 20-second checklist.
args.why_useful: Today the owner can walk away from the Mac without knowing whether work is still running or a call/document is exposed. This turns the worn device into a reliable boundary between physical presence and unattended-machine state, using each node’s unique reach.
args.model_tier: Realtime model conducts the short spoken exchange and compresses results; cheaper background classification extracts unsaved/risky/long-running state from structured Mac and browser reports.
args.latency_budget: Snapshot collection under 3 seconds and spoken summary under 8 seconds; stale or unavailable surfaces must be explicitly named rather than silently omitted.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.02 per invocation; most cost is one short realtime turn, with no screenshot processing unless a state is ambiguous.
args.security_concerns: The report can reveal sensitive tabs and documents over audio. Require the pendant’s physical trigger or explicit wake phrase, redact titles by default, support a private LED/vibration-only mode, and discard the snapshot after delivery unless the owner saves it.
missing: A single authenticated departure-snapshot contract spanning Mac and browser
Mac inspection of unsaved documents, active calls, and process/job state with freshness timestamps
Browser extension report of tabs with sensitivity labels and pending downloads
A relay aggregator that distinguishes offline, stale, and confirmed-clear states

args.user_asks: “Check this before I send it.” Without changing anything, have the pendant inspect the focused draft on the Mac or browser, compare recipients, attachments, links, and claims against the surrounding document/context, and speak only concrete risks and a one-sentence suggested fix.
args.why_useful: A wearable can catch the expensive mistake at the last second even when the owner is not staring at the screen. The browser session knows authenticated recipients and attachments, the Mac knows the focused app/document, and the relay provides a fast spoken second opinion without taking over or silently sending.
args.model_tier: Realtime model performs intent recognition and delivers the concise risk summary; a cheaper structured/background model extracts draft, recipient, attachment, and link facts and runs deterministic checks before the realtime explanation.
args.latency_budget: Collect evidence in 2 seconds and answer in under 5 seconds for ordinary drafts; if evidence is stale or inaccessible, say so instead of guessing.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.08 per review, dominated by secure draft extraction and one realtime response; deterministic checks should avoid unnecessary model calls.
args.security_concerns: Drafts, recipients, and attachments are highly sensitive. Keep raw content on the Mac/extension where possible, send only hashes/extracted facts to the relay, encrypt any temporary payload, never auto-send or edit, and visibly state which surfaces were actually inspected.
missing: A read-only focused-draft adapter for common Mac apps and browser compose surfaces
A browser-extension inspection API for recipient/attachment/link metadata with session affinity
Deterministic checks for wrong recipient, external domain, secret/token patterns, broken links, and attachment mismatch
A provenance-bearing relay response that reports inspected timestamps and unavailable surfaces

args.change: Add a small ERM/LRA vibration motor and driver to the nRF9160 pendant, with a firmware pattern table for acknowledgment, urgent alert, capture-confirmed, and link-lost states. Keep the existing one-button/one-LED interface and make vibration locally triggerable without LTE or the Mac.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a discreet, unmistakable result while walking, in a meeting, or somewhere the pendant’s speaker/audio bridge is unavailable. It makes asynchronous cross-node work usable instead of requiring the owner to keep listening for speech.
args.effort: Moderate hardware revision and enclosure work; add a GPIO/PWM driver, four bounded patterns, battery testing, and relay-to-device event delivery. Prototype on the currently USB-connected pendant before spinning a board.
args.risk: Added current draw and mechanical noise could reduce battery life or annoy the wearer; cap duty cycle, expose intensity/off settings, and fall back to LED/audio. A lost link must never leave the motor running; enforce firmware timeouts.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$4 in components and under $0.05 per unit at volume; brief pulses add negligible average draw, while long alerts may add a few percent to daily consumption.
args.latency_impact: Local acknowledgment under 100 ms; remote alerts depend on link latency but remain useful when audio playback is unavailable.
args.security_impact: No new data exposure. Treat only authenticated, typed event codes as motor commands and reject arbitrary duration/waveform payloads.
depends_on: A device event/push channel that can deliver typed alert codes
Firmware support for a watchdog-bounded vibration driver
A relay policy mapping completion/urgency states to discreet patterns

args.user_asks: “Can I merge this?” From the focused repository and current diff, have the Mac run the relevant tests and inspect the actual changed files, then have the relay speak a short merge-readiness report: failing evidence first, behavior risks second, and exact commands or files behind each claim.
args.why_useful: The owner can get a trustworthy engineering checkpoint while away from the keyboard instead of relying on a green-looking editor or memory. The Mac has the repository and test runtime; the relay and pendant make the result available during a walk; the report is grounded in executable evidence rather than a generic code opinion.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background planner for repository/test discovery and deterministic diff/test collection; reserve realtime for interpreting the collected evidence and speaking the compact result.
args.latency_budget: Start immediately, provide an audible 'testing started' acknowledgment within 500 ms, and deliver a first result within 30 seconds; long suites should return incremental completed/failed counts rather than blocking.
args.cost_estimate: Typically $0.03–$0.15 per review, dominated by test execution and a short synthesis; no screenshot cost unless the focused diff is only visible in a GUI.
args.security_concerns: Source code and test output may contain secrets or proprietary data. Keep execution on the Mac, redact credentials and unrelated files, include exact evidence paths and timestamps, and never merge, push, or mutate the repository without a separate explicit command.
missing: A Mac-terminal job endpoint that runs a bounded test plan and streams typed progress
Repository/diff identity and clean-worktree checks in the result
A relay job-to-pendant progress and completion channel
A synthesis format that separates observed test evidence from model risk judgments

args.cost_impact: Minimal BOM change; some power/storage overhead.
args.latency_impact: None during capture; retries happen opportunistically.
args.security_impact: Sensitive audio at rest; should be encrypted and auto-expire.

Server support for resumable uploads
