args.change: Add a small coin-cell haptic actuator and a dedicated low-power driver to the pendant, with firmware patterns for acknowledgement, attention-needed, failure, and queued-message count. Keep audio and the existing single LED, but let the relay select haptic feedback when the owner is in a meeting or cannot hear the speaker.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know that a remote task completed, needs attention, or failed without taking out a phone, looking at the LED, or playing speech aloud. This makes asynchronous Mac/browser work usable in public and gives a dependable tactile confirmation for button presses and connectivity loss.
args.effort: Medium hardware revision: actuator, driver transistor, routing, enclosure/comfort validation, battery profiling, and firmware pattern/state arbitration with the existing LED and audio state machine.
args.risk: Vibration can become annoying or drain the battery; cap duty cycle, allow a silent mode, and rate-limit repeated events. A failed driver must not block recording or audio. Mechanical noise and false presses need testing on the worn enclosure.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $0.30–$1.50 in components plus board/enclosure revision; roughly 5–30 mA only during short pulses and negligible idle draw.
args.latency_impact: Immediate local feedback, typically under 50 ms, independent of LTE/Mac latency. It can also make dropped-link states apparent before a server response arrives.
args.security_impact: Patterns must not reveal sensitive content to bystanders; encode only category/count, never message text. Firmware update signing and a local disable setting are required.
depends_on: A relay event delivery path for asynchronous task outcomes
Firmware integration with offline_alert_inbox and spoken_status_interrupt
A persisted owner preference for silent/public mode
Battery and enclosure validation on the live nRF9160 pendant

args.user_asks: "I can't see the screen well right now—describe the current Mac or browser screen, tell me what is actionable, and carry out the next thing I say without losing my place."
args.why_useful: This makes the hive an accessibility surface rather than merely voice remote control. The pendant supplies continuous spoken orientation and interruption; mac-vision interprets visual layout; browser-extension preserves authenticated web context; mac-planner/action executes the owner’s follow-up while the relay maintains the referent ('the blue button', 'the second result').
args.model_tier: Use gpt-4.1-mini or an equivalent low-cost vision loop for screenshots and element grounding; use the planner only for multi-step actions; realtime handles short descriptions, disambiguation, and interruption.
args.latency_budget: First orientation in under 3 seconds, action acknowledgement under 1 second, and each requested UI transition under 5 seconds. The owner can interrupt at any point and ask for a shorter description.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.20 per screen/action cycle, dominated by screenshot tokens and repeated visual grounding; cache unchanged regions and send diffs where possible.
args.security_concerns: Screens may contain passwords, private messages, or financial data. Keep screenshots on the Mac when possible, redact password fields, expose the active app/domain before describing it, and never speak secrets aloud unless explicitly requested. Actions must be tied to the owner’s current referent and report the exact target.
missing: A live mac-vision computer-use loop (currently disabled)
Stable element identities across screenshots and browser DOM inspection
A relay-side referent/session state that survives spoken interruptions
An accessibility-oriented spoken layout contract rather than raw screenshot captions

args.user_asks: "Let me start a conversation at my desk over USB, walk away, and have it continue over LTE without repeating myself or losing the reply."
args.why_useful: The live pendant is testable over USB today but is worn and will eventually operate away from the Mac. Seamless migration removes the arbitrary boundary between desk testing and real wearable use: the relay keeps the voice turn, audio sequence, and downstream Mac job coherent while the pendant changes transport.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay remains the turn owner; transport and audio workers are deterministic. Use a cheaper background tier only to reconcile a partial transcript or summarize a job after a handoff.
args.latency_budget: USB-to-LTE handoff detection under 500 ms, no duplicate spoken sentence, and resume audio within 2 seconds where LTE is available. If handoff fails, preserve the turn and speak one concise retry state.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation; mostly protocol/storage engineering. Model cost is limited to a rare transcript reconciliation, under roughly $0.01–$0.05.
args.security_concerns: Bind both transports to the same authenticated pendant session and monotonic turn sequence; reject replayed audio or replies. Do not duplicate microphone chunks during overlap, and erase transient handoff buffers after acknowledgement.
missing: A transport-independent pendant session identity and resumable audio sequence protocol
USB serial bridge support in the relay path alongside LTE WebSocket
A bounded overlap/reconciliation buffer for in-flight Opus frames and transcript state
Mac job continuation keyed to the same turn rather than a transport connection

args.user_asks: If that thing I asked the Mac to do finishes, tell me what happened, even if I’m not still talking to you.
args.why_useful: It turns long-running tasks into a clean, wearable experience: the owner doesn’t have to remember to check back or keep a session open.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the spoken acknowledgement; cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarization.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledgement under a second; completion notification can arrive minutes later when the job ends.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job. Most cost is status polling and summarization; notification delivery should be a small payload.
args.security_concerns: Spoken status may expose task details audibly. Use short summaries, avoid sensitive content, and require confirmation before speaking highly sensitive results.
missing: A real implementation behind relay_event_push (or equivalent route) to deliver async events to the pendant/phone
A scheduler or job-completion watcher to monitor jobs after the session ends
A storage-safe way to queue pending spoken alerts without violating the SD failure-path rule
built_from: offline_alert_inbox (already implemented on device/browser side per system observations)

args.user_asks: Quickly check what’s actually open and active on my Mac and tell me if it’s safe to proceed before you start doing anything.
args.why_useful: Prevents accidental interference with work in progress, which is especially important when the owner is away and the Mac is unattended.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the brief spoken check; Mac tier for live state inspection.
args.latency_budget: 1–2 seconds for a short spoken status.
args.cost_estimate: Very low; one status read and a short spoken response.
args.security_concerns: Reveals what apps and documents are open; keep summaries minimal and avoid reading content unless asked.
missing: A reliable live status read path that doesn’t require executing actions (likely get_mac_status needs to be described and verified current)
A concise spoken status format that fits pendant audio well

args.user_asks: Start this job on my Mac and browser, and if it reaches a real ambiguity, ask me one precise question through the pendant; use my answer to continue without restarting or losing the authenticated session.
args.why_useful: Long computer tasks fail today at the first ambiguous dialog or missing choice. This would let the owner leave the Mac and still resolve only the decisions that genuinely require them, while preserving browser state and producing one coherent result rather than a dead job or a guessed action.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for the one short clarification exchange; mac-planner for orchestration; mac-vision/browser-extension for execution and evidence extraction.
args.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; clarification prompt within 5 seconds of a blocker; resume within 10 seconds of the owner's answer.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01-$0.08 per task depending on planner turns; the dominant cost is vision/planner retries, not the short relay utterances.
args.security_concerns: The relay must send only the blocker and minimal options, never arbitrary page contents. The owner answer is bound to the exact job, step, and browser session, with expiry and a visible receipt so a stale answer cannot affect a later task. No automatic choice should be made when the blocker is consequential.
missing: A durable clarification state machine that pauses an executing Mac/browser job and binds a single pendant answer to its step
A relay-to-pendant downlink prompt and answer endpoint that works after the original voice turn
Mac planner support for resumable checkpoints rather than terminal success/failure
A browser-session evidence envelope identifying the tab and URL at the blocker

args.user_asks: I think someone may have access to my computer. From the pendant, put the Mac into a privacy posture, stop any active browser automation, and tell me exactly what was changed and what remains open.
args.why_useful: A worn button is the only control surface the owner can reach when away from the desk. Today the relay can start work, but there is no single cross-surface response to a suspected compromise. This gives the owner a fast, understandable incident response instead of needing to find the Mac or remember several commands.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay interprets the short emergency utterance; a deterministic Mac action bundle performs the response; the planner/vision tiers only inspect and report residual state.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; issue lock/stop actions within 2 seconds when the Mac is online; speak a bounded outcome within 8 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 for the deterministic path; inspection and receipt generation dominate if the owner requests details.
args.security_concerns: This must not claim protection if the Mac is offline. It should stop relay-originated jobs, close or freeze extension control, lock the Mac, mute active audio, and record a tamper-evident receipt; destructive tab closure or credential revocation should be separately requested. The pendant command needs replay protection and a distinct emergency utterance/button gesture.
missing: A relay emergency-control endpoint that cancels queued/in-flight jobs and broadcasts a stop token
An idempotent Mac privacy action bundle (lock, mute, halt automation, freeze browser command intake) with honest per-action receipts
A pendant emergency gesture and offline LED acknowledgement
A browser extension kill-switch that refuses new commands until explicitly resumed

args.user_asks: Give me a spoken 'since last check-in' that combines what changed in my Mac project, authenticated browser work, and relay tasks, with links or names I can ask you to open next.
args.why_useful: The owner is often away from the Mac and currently has to remember which surface changed what. A cross-surface delta, grounded in actual receipts rather than a generic summary, turns the pendant into a trustworthy return point after an interruption or a day away.
args.model_tier: A cheap background summarizer builds the delta from structured receipts; realtime only compresses it into speech and handles a follow-up such as 'open the second item'.
args.latency_budget: Precompute on each completed job or check-in; spoken response under 3 seconds, with a two-sentence default and on-demand expansion.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005-$0.03 per delta; storage/indexing is negligible, while summarization of page diffs is the main cost.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated browser content must remain on the relay or be reduced to user-approved metadata; do not read an entire portal aloud in a public setting. Every item needs source, timestamp, and confidence, and unchanged items must be excluded to prevent false novelty.
missing: A per-owner checkpoint cursor spanning Mac receipts, browser inspections, and relay jobs
Structured before/after snapshots for files, app state, and browser pages instead of opaque action logs
A redaction/classification pass for sensitive browser content before persistence or speech
A pendant query that can select an item and route it back to the originating surface

args.user_asks: Let me walk from outside LTE coverage to my Mac without losing the conversation: when I plug in the pendant, move the live voice session and its pending task to the USB-connected Mac/audio bridge, then move it back when I leave.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has two disconnected realities: the pendant is useful while worn, while the physically connected hardware is testable at the Mac. A session handoff would make one continuous assistant instead of forcing the owner to repeat context, restart audio, or abandon a task at the doorway.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay maintains the conversational session and selects the active transport; a deterministic handoff coordinator moves audio and job ownership; planner/vision continue the task without re-planning.
args.latency_budget: Detect USB attach or LTE loss within 2 seconds; freeze and resume audio in under 1 second with no duplicate command; preserve the last 30 seconds of transcript/context.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.02 per handoff; protocol work and short-lived session state dominate, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Authenticate the exact USB serial device before treating it as the owner's local endpoint. Never expose a live session to an arbitrary Mac; revoke the old transport on handoff, sequence audio frames, and make command submission idempotent so reconnects cannot repeat an action.
missing: A pendant/relay transport registry that recognizes the live nRF9160 and ESP32 USB serial pair
A session migration protocol with epoch, frame sequence, transcript cursor, and idempotent command ownership
Mac-side USB audio/serial adapter that can join an existing relay session rather than starting a new one
Explicit LTE-to-USB and USB-to-LTE transition signals in the firmware and relay

The first three are intentionally differentiated from completion notifications: they require pausing at a decision, active containment, and source-grounded change detection respectively.

args.user_asks: Tell me when that’s done, even after I stop talking.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing for a wearable assistant: you can ask for a task, go about your day, and get a completion cue without babysitting a screen.
args.model_tier: Cheaper background tier for monitoring; realtime only for the initial confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge the request; completion notification can arrive later.

args.user_asks: If I say something that sounds like a command, route it to the right place and tell me what you’re doing.
args.why_useful: Reduces friction. The owner can speak naturally and the system chooses Mac actions, browser work, or a web search without manual switching.
args.model_tier: Realtime for intent detection and confirmation; mac-planner handles multi-step plans.
args.latency_budget: Under 1 second to confirm the route for simple tasks; complex planning can take longer but should be handed off.
args.cost_estimate: Small per utterance. Cost dominated by planning when tasks are complex.

args.user_asks: Read out what’s happening right now with my system, briefly.
args.why_useful: Quick, hands-free status at a glance: queued jobs, failures, connectivity hints, and what’s waiting for review.
args.model_tier: Realtime for spoken summary; perception/planner for aggregation.
args.latency_budget: 1-2 seconds for a short summary; longer details only on request.
args.cost_estimate: Low. Dominated by pulling job summaries and any needed snapshots.

A way to request terse vs detailed summaries consistently across surfaces

args.risk: Low. Mostly introspection. Risk is leaking internal details; mitigate by returning only what agents need.
args.cost_impact: Low API cost; small storage and compute overhead.
args.latency_impact: Improves routing decisions; negligible runtime overhead.
args.security_impact: Ensure the inventory is bearer-protected and redacts secrets, internal paths, and tokens.

args.user_asks: "I just saw something wrong on my computer—find the exact problem, fix it if it is safe, and tell me what you changed."
args.why_useful: The owner can report a problem from the pendant without walking to the Mac or reconstructing which window, tab, or error they meant. The wearable supplies the utterance and timing; the Mac supplies the live screen, logs, and authenticated state; the relay fuses them into one bounded repair and an audible explanation.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for the short clarification and final spoken answer; gpt-5.6-luna mac-planner for diagnosis and reversible repair; gpt-4.1-mini mac-vision only when visual evidence is required; no expensive model for receipt summarization.

args.security_concerns: Screen images, logs, and browser contents may leave the Mac for model inference. Default evidence should be limited to the implicated app and the last few seconds, with explicit redaction of secrets. Reversible edits can run automatically under the owner's maximum-access policy; deletion, sending, or external publication must be reported before execution. A full action receipt and undo reference must be spoken or available on the pendant.

args.user_asks: "Save this thought exactly where it belongs: identify the project from what is open on my Mac, turn my voice into a structured note with action items, and link it to the relevant tab or file."
args.why_useful: A one-button spoken thought becomes useful project memory rather than an orphaned audio memo. The pendant is available at the moment of insight, while the Mac can identify the active project and write into the owner's existing tools; the owner does not need to remember the thought or later sort it.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for capture acknowledgement and a cheap transcription/normalization pass; background gpt-5.6-luna only for project attribution and structured extraction when the Mac context is available.
args.latency_budget: Store the utterance immediately in under 1 s; classify and file it within 15 s when the Mac is online. If offline, retain the typed payload and complete filing on reconnection without recording beyond the button-held interval.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per note, dominated by transcription and one planner classification call; retries should be idempotent and nearly free.
args.security_concerns: The note may contain confidential work or personal material. Keep raw audio on the existing failure-only path, send only the transcript plus narrowly scoped active-project context, and never attach a whole screen by default. Filing is a local reversible write; external sharing is out of scope and must never be inferred.

args.user_asks: "Before I leave, make sure the work I was doing is recoverable: summarize the exact state of my open project, save a restart checklist, and tell me the one next action."
args.why_useful: The wearable can turn an abrupt physical departure into a reliable handoff. The Mac contributes open files, tabs, diffs, terminal state, and unsent drafts; the relay compresses that into a spoken next step and a durable checkpoint the owner can resume later, preventing lost context rather than merely reporting status.

args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately, snapshot in 3 s, and provide the one-next-action summary within 8 s. Checkpoint persistence must complete before claiming success; otherwise say it is only a draft.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.10 per checkpoint, mostly planner context from diffs/tabs and optional summarization; deterministic persistence is negligible.
args.security_concerns: Open documents, code diffs, and browser tabs can contain secrets. Snapshot only the focused project and omit credentials, cookies, and raw terminal environment variables. Saving locally is reversible and should be automatic; the spoken response must distinguish saved checkpoint, failed save, and partial capture.
missing: A scoped workspace snapshot that captures open files, git diff, terminal cwd/command context, browser tabs, and unsent draft status

args.user_asks: "Handle this when my Mac is reachable again: use the context I gave you now, finish the task later, and tell me only when it actually succeeded or needs me."
args.why_useful: Today a worn owner must repeat a request or poll after losing the Mac link. This creates a durable, consent-scoped intent—not merely an audio memo—that can resume across relay, Mac, and browser availability, then deliver a truthful result to the pendant. args.model_tier: Realtime relay extracts and confirms the intent in one short turn; a cheap background worker retries transport and readiness checks; gpt-5.6-luna plans only when execution becomes possible; mac-vision is invoked only for visual ambiguity.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge escrow in under 1 s. Resume within 10 s of Mac/browser availability. Completion delivery should be eventual, with no repeated model calls while a dependency is unavailable.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.08 per task, dominated by one planner call and any vision/browser step; retries and event delivery should be sub-cent operations.
args.security_concerns: The escrow must expire, show its exact scope, and never broaden from the original utterance. Persist transcript/context encrypted with a redaction boundary; do not retain browser credentials. Reversible local work may proceed automatically under owner policy, but sending, purchasing, deleting, or publishing must enter needs_attention and explain why. Completion must include an execution receipt, not a guessed success.

args.change: Build a durable cross-surface Intent Escrow, not another job list: on pendant release, persist a normalized intent, evidence references, allowed action envelope, expiry, and idempotency key; a Durable Object alarm retries only the unmet dependency (Mac offline, browser unavailable, or planner failure), and completion is accepted only from an execution receipt whose observed state matches the requested outcome. On reconnect, the escrow hands the same intent to the Mac planner and emits one pending/completed/needs-attention event to the pendant inbox.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask once while walking away and trust that the work will either finish later or clearly come back as needing them. They stop losing tasks merely because the Mac was asleep, and they hear a truthful outcome instead of having to poll or repeat themselves.
args.effort: High: new Durable Object/alarm state machine, reconnect hooks from Mac and browser, idempotent planner handoff, receipt verification, expiry UI/voice wording, and firmware inbox integration.
args.risk: A stale or duplicated escrow could act at the wrong time. Recover with short expiries, immutable original utterance, idempotency keys, cancellation, visible pending records, and receipt-gated completion. If verification fails, stop and report needs_attention rather than retrying mutations blindly.
args.cost_impact: Low steady-state storage and alarm cost; roughly one background Worker invocation per dependency transition plus the existing planner/model call. No new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Immediate escrow acknowledgement; deferred execution latency becomes availability-bound. Normal online tasks add under 200 ms for persistence, while offline tasks wait safely rather than burning retries.
args.security_impact: Adds durable storage of user intent and scoped context. Encrypt it, redact secrets before persistence, bind it to the owner's session, and enforce expiry and cancellation. Never persist browser cookies or credentials.
depends_on: Cloudflare Durable Object or Cron alarm wiring (currently absent)
A Mac/browser availability callback
A stable receipt schema with observed-state verification
The existing pendant inbox/event delivery path

args.user_asks: “Put this browser task on a bookmark: save the exact page and form state I’m looking at, and later restore it or tell me precisely what changed.”

Show an audit record of extracted fields and allow the owner to disable cloud answering per site. A wrong redaction is a privacy failure, so uncertain fields should be omitted and the answer should say so.

Site-aware sensitive-field detection and a hard byte/token budget for relay payloads

args.user_asks: “Watch me do this browser task once, turn it into a named voice command, and next time repeat it with the new values I dictate.”

Keep raw keystrokes and screenshots on-device, replace values with typed parameters, redact secrets, and require explicit opt-in at recording start. args.user_asks: “While my Mac is carrying out that long task, let me steer it from the pendant: pause at the next safe boundary, change one parameter, skip a step, or continue.”

No expensive re-planning is needed for a simple parameter edit.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge a steer request in under 500 ms. Pause or apply a parameter change at the next checkpoint within 5 seconds; if the Mac is offline, queue the request and tell the owner plainly.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per steering event; cost is dominated by a compact state snapshot, not a new full plan. A recovery re-plan may cost $0.05–$0.30.
args.security_concerns: The relay must bind controls to the owner’s active job and reject stale or ambiguous job references. Do not pretend a pause happened until the Mac acknowledges it. Keep a tamper-evident event log of requested, accepted, and applied edits; preserve the owner’s maximum-access policy, but never silently substitute a different target or value.
missing: A bidirectional job-control protocol with pause/resume/skip/edit operations and acknowledged sequence numbers
Planner checkpoints that describe the next reversible boundary and current parameters
A pendant-facing job selector for multiple concurrent jobs
Mac planner and browser/vision adapters that can apply edits without discarding completed work

args.latency_budget: Handoff should feel immediate (<1s). Completion can arrive minutes later; the owner only cares that it’s timely and reliable.

args.user_asks: “If I get stuck, listen for what I’m doing and suggest the next step.”
args.why_useful: This would feel like a real companion: if the owner hesitates or repeats themselves, the system can offer a gentle, context-aware nudge rather than forcing them to explicitly ask for help.
args.model_tier: Realtime for conversational glue; mac-vision/browser work is planned by mac-planner; suggestions come from a cheaper planning model.
args.latency_budget: Nudge should arrive within a couple seconds of a detected stall; otherwise remain silent.
args.cost_estimate: Mostly planning and occasional page/app inspection; keep inspections small and capped to avoid expensive loops.
args.security_concerns: Only inspect apps/tabs when there’s an explicit stuck signal (e.g., repeated request or explicit “help”), and avoid reading sensitive fields like passwords or tokens.
missing: A reliable stall signal (e.g., explicit “help” utterance or repeated failure detected in job receipts)

args.user_asks: When I arrive at a place, give me the right handoff for that place: read my pendant location, inspect the Mac and authenticated browser, and tell me only what is relevant now; if I say 'set up here', open the appropriate apps and tabs.
args.why_useful: The pendant is the only surface that knows where the owner physically is, while the Mac and browser know what work is waiting. This turns location changes into useful, timely context instead of requiring the owner to remember which tools to open.
args.model_tier: Background model for geofence classification and ranking; relay-realtime only for the spoken handoff; mac-planner for actions.
args.latency_budget: Speak an initial arrival summary within 3 seconds of a confirmed geofence event; setup actions may take up to 30 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01-$0.05 per arrival, dominated by one planner/context call; geofence evaluation is near-zero cost.

Store coarse place labels rather than raw tracks; require an explicit first-time place enrollment and provide an off switch. args.user_asks: Let me say 'watch this' about a live browser page or Mac task, then later tell me when the exact condition changes — for example a ticket is assigned, a price drops, or a deployment turns green — with a short spoken explanation and a link or action ready.
args.why_useful: Today the owner must repeatedly ask for status. A durable watch combines the browser's authenticated session, the Mac's local state, and the always-awake relay into a useful asynchronous capability that survives ending the voice session.
args.model_tier: Cheap background polling/diff model; relay-realtime only interprets the initial request and speaks the alert; use a stronger model only when a change needs explanation.
args.latency_budget: Create a watch acknowledgement in under 2 seconds; detect ordinary changes within 1-5 minutes; deliver the alert as soon as the condition is confirmed.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02-$0.20 per watch per day depending on polling frequency and page complexity; browser polling and model calls dominate.

browser and Mac polling worker while the owner is offline
semantic diff/condition evaluator for page and task state
reliable push delivery to the pendant and paired phone

args.user_asks: When I say 'recover my work', reconstruct the last coherent state of a task across my voice conversation, Mac actions, browser tabs, and job receipts, then give me a two-sentence resume point and offer the next concrete action.
args.why_useful: A dropped connection, context switch, or unfinished multi-step task currently forces the owner to remember what happened. This is the single most valuable everyday capability: the worn front door can recover intent, while the Mac/browser can recover actual state and receipts rather than guessing from conversation alone.
args.model_tier: Background synthesis over structured receipts and snapshots; relay-realtime performs only the short spoken summary and dispatches the selected next action.
args.latency_budget: Return a trustworthy resume point within 5 seconds; if state collection needs a live Mac/browser round trip, say what is known immediately and complete within 20 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03-$0.15 per recovery, dominated by state collection and synthesis; subsequent action planning is an additional planner call only if requested.

read-continuity snapshot that joins voice, plan, execute, browser, and Mac receipts
provenance-aware synthesis with confidence and stale-state labels

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Location-aware arrival handoffs** — the pendant’s location triggers a context-aware summary and optional Mac/browser setup for the place the owner has arrived.
2. **Durable cross-surface watches** — “watch this” monitors authenticated browser pages or Mac state and delivers a spoken alert when a meaningful condition changes.
3. **Work-state recovery** — “recover my work” reconstructs the last coherent task from voice history, Mac/browser state, plans, and receipts, then gives a trustworthy resume point.

The main missing pieces are durable background workers, pendant location/geofence events, unified cross-surface task identity, semantic state-diffing, provenance-aware synthesis, and reliable asynchronous delivery.
I’ll quickly inventory what’s available now and then I’ll suggest a few high-value capabilities and call out any missing pieces.

args.user_asks: “Watch that task and tell me when it’s done, even if I stop talking.”
args.why_useful: It turns the pendant into a true hands-free assistant for long-running Mac jobs. The owner doesn’t have to keep checking; it reports completion or failure later.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the initial voice interaction; cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarizing status.
args.latency_budget: Fast acknowledgement (<1s) that monitoring is set, then asynchronous delivery when the job changes state.
args.cost_estimate: Low for setup; ongoing cost is periodic status checks and a short audio render when state changes. Dominated by polling/receipts and TTS/rendering.
args.security_concerns: Must not expose job details to other users; should only speak a short, user-facing summary. Needs a clear stop/disable command. Avoid storing audio on-device except failure-path buffering.
missing: A real relay event delivery mechanism (relay_event_push is currently a schema without implementation)
A scheduler/heartbeat for monitoring without a live conversation

args.user_asks: “If I start a task, summarize what you’re doing in one sentence, then ask if I want more detail.”
args.why_useful: It keeps voice interactions calm and concise. The owner gets a quick mental model without being trapped in a long readout, and can opt into details when needed.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the summary and follow-up question; mac-planner for the underlying plan and execution.
args.latency_budget: Under a second for the summary; details only if the owner asks.
args.cost_estimate: Minimal incremental cost. Summary can be derived from the planned action list already produced.
args.security_concerns: The summary must avoid leaking sensitive content from documents or emails. If the plan touches private data, keep it generic.
missing: A stable, structured plan representation returned to the relay for summarization (or a relay-visible summary field).
A convention for details-on-demand that the mac-planner can fulfill without replaying sensitive content.

args.user_asks: “When I’m away from my Mac, check my authenticated sites and tell me if anything urgent needs action.”

args.model_tier: Background tier for periodic checks; realtime only to deliver a spoken alert.
args.latency_budget: Not interactive. Alerts can arrive within minutes of change, depending on polling interval.
args.cost_estimate: Dominated by headless browser sessions and authentication maintenance.

A scheduler or push mechanism for periodic checks
Session storage/rotation for authenticated sites

args.user_asks: When something I asked the system to do fails, tell me what actually went wrong, collect the relevant Mac and browser evidence, and offer a safe repair I can approve by voice—without making me repeat the original request.
args.why_useful: Today a failed job leaves the owner to reconstruct context and troubleshoot from a wearable. This would turn failures into recoverable conversations, especially while away from the Mac, while keeping the owner in control of consequential repairs.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for the short failure explanation and clarification; background mac-planner for evidence collection and repair planning; mac-vision/browser harness only where planner evidence shows UI state is necessary.
args.latency_budget: Speak an initial failure explanation within 2 seconds of a terminal error; evidence and repair proposal may take 10–30 seconds and arrive asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per incident, dominated by planner/vision calls; relay speech remains a short low-token response.
args.security_concerns: Evidence can include private screen text, authenticated pages, and command output; keep it in the existing authenticated session, redact secrets in the spoken summary, and require explicit voice confirmation before irreversible repair actions. A repair must carry the failed-job receipt and a bounded action diff.
missing: A failure-classification and evidence-bundle worker that correlates job receipts, Mac state, and browser inspection
A repair-plan/approval protocol with an idempotency key and action diff
A reliable asynchronous pendant delivery path for the proposal and final outcome

args.user_asks: Take the document or page I’m looking at, make a share-safe copy by finding and redacting secrets and personal data across the browser and my Mac, then tell me exactly what was removed before I send it.
args.why_useful: The owner can currently copy or send content, but cannot reliably notice credentials, tokens, private names, or local paths hidden in a mixed document. A wearable command could make safe sharing practical while away from the keyboard.
args.model_tier: Background planner performs extraction and deterministic scanning; a cheaper model classifies ambiguous spans; realtime relay only handles the request, a concise removal summary, and confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; produce a preview in 15–45 seconds for a normal document, with a spoken completion and a review URL.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.15 per document, dominated by OCR/vision and model review; local deterministic scanners should handle most text cheaply.
args.security_concerns: Raw content must stay on the Mac/relay session and never be sent to a third-party sharing endpoint without confirmation. Never overwrite the source; create a new artifact, preserve an audit manifest, and require explicit confirmation before upload or send.
missing: A local extraction/redaction engine covering text, PDFs, screenshots, and browser DOM
A span-level review artifact and spoken summary protocol
A final send/export action that accepts only the redacted artifact and records its receipt

args.user_asks: Answer a question by checking the current state of my Mac and any authenticated browser page, and include where each fact came from and when it was observed—then warn me if the sources disagree or are stale.
args.why_useful: A spoken answer that sounds certain is dangerous when the Mac, browser session, or a cached job has changed. The owner needs a provenance-aware answer they can trust while walking around, not merely a plausible synthesis.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay asks one focused clarification if needed and speaks the result; faculty-perception/planner gather source snapshots; a small synthesis model produces the answer and conflict report rather than spending realtime tokens on research.

args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.10 per query, mostly planner/browser inspection and synthesis; avoid vision unless DOM or screen-only evidence is required.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated content remains scoped to the owner’s existing sessions. Spoken output should minimize sensitive quotations and identify sources generically when in public. Every claim needs a source ID, observed timestamp, and freshness policy; never silently merge contradictory values.
missing: A unified observation envelope and freshness/conflict policy shared by Mac, browser, and relay
A provenance-aware synthesis endpoint that can cite claims in a compact spoken format
A pendant-friendly follow-up gesture or phrase to hear the underlying evidence without restarting collection

transcript.text:
Recorded four proposals. The highest-value missing capability is:

1. **Evidence-backed personal research**
   - The owner asks one spoken question.
   - Relay searches public sources, local Mac files, and authenticated browser sessions.
   - It returns a concise spoken answer distinguishing facts, uncertainty, contradictions, and source freshness.
   - Requires a cross-surface retrieval planner, provenance-carrying evidence objects, and bounded private-file/browser extraction.

2. **Voice-driven engineering repair loop**
   - The owner describes a coding problem.
   - Mac tiers inspect the project, reproduce the issue, consult browser documentation, make the smallest fix, run tests, and report the patch and test receipt.
   - Requires iterative terminal-to-planner feedback, browser-context integration, durable patch/test artifacts, and reliable completion delivery.

3. **Remote screen understanding with grounded follow-up**
   - The owner asks what is currently visible on the Mac.
   - Vision explains the relevant screen or browser control aloud; “do that” binds to the identified control rather than guessing.
   - Requires a live vision inspection route, persistent screen-grounding references between turns, DOM fallback, and sensitive-region redaction.

4. **Noisy-environment speech capture**
   - A two-microphone ESP32 bridge performs local beamforming and noise suppression while preserving press-to-talk consent and the existing 24 kHz path.
   - Requires a bridge hardware revision, acoustic calibration, local DSP, and measured noisy-environment benchmarks.
   - This would make the pendant usable outdoors, in kitchens, and in busy offices rather than only in quiet rooms.
I’ll quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll call out what’s missing and propose a few high-impact additions.

args.user_asks: Tell me when that long-running Mac task finishes, even after I stop talking.

args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the initial confirmation; cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarizing results.
args.latency_budget: Fast acknowledgment (under a second) that the task is being watched; completion can arrive minutes later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job: one status subscription and one short spoken summary. Most cost is downstream polling/receipts, not realtime conversation.
args.security_concerns: Spoken notifications could leak sensitive content if heard in public. Provide a privacy mode (generic completion) and avoid reading detailed results unless the owner asks for details.
missing: A real implementation for relay_event_push that can deliver to the pendant/phone without keeping the voice session open
A background watcher (Durable Object alarm or similar) to monitor jobs after the session ends
A policy for what gets spoken vs. queued silently

transcript.text:
Recorded four new capabilities:

1. **Spoken secret-exposure response** — investigate possible leaks across the Mac and authenticated browser, identify risk, and contain it.
2. **Portable task handoff** — preserve the exact task state when the owner walks away, then resume it from the pendant.
3. **Source-versus-draft preflight** — compare a draft with its source and report only unsupported, stale, privacy-sensitive, or materially changed claims.
4. **Cross-surface causal debugging** — trace a failed request through relay, Mac, browser, and pipeline evidence to identify the first actual fault.

What is still needed is not another isolated route. The existing jobs, receipts, browser inspections, pipeline status, and Mac actions need a **shared causal/evidence layer** carrying session IDs, job IDs, timestamps, surface, parent action, redacted evidence, and confidence. We also need:

- Secret detection and credential-containment adapters.
- Durable, encrypted task-handoff checkpoints with expiry.
- Structured claim extraction and citation comparison.
- A trace assembler/root-cause evaluator.
- Pendant-friendly summaries and a dashboard for evidence, diffs, and incident timelines.
- Explicit handling for sensitive data so raw page contents, drafts, credentials, and transcripts do not leave the relevant device unnecessarily.
I’ll quickly map what’s actually available right now, then I’ll point out the missing pieces that would unlock the most useful cross-device behavior.

args.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.08 per invocation, dominated by one planner call; terminal and browser actions are local.
args.security_concerns: The snapshot must exclude secrets and page contents, and restoration must be scoped to the same Mac/browser profile and session. If the Mac disappears, the relay must say the block was not established rather than pretending. Closing tabs or muting notifications is reversible, but the owner should be told which mutations were applied.

args.user_asks: Tell me when that’s done, even if I’m not talking to you anymore.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing: the owner can start a long task hands-free and trust the system to report completion later, instead of repeatedly checking status.
args.model_tier: Realtime only to accept the voice request; planning and monitoring should run on a cheaper background tier.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge the request; completion can arrive minutes later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per request; the expensive part is keeping context and monitoring, which should run off the realtime tier.
args.security_concerns: Must avoid false positives. Only announce completion when the job status is definitive. Avoid leaking job details; speak only what the job status tool returns as user-facing text.
missing: A working asynchronous event delivery path (tool or route) from relay to pendant/phone
A monitoring mechanism that can watch job state after the session ends (scheduler, durable object, or relay worker alarm)
A way to store minimal notification state across sessions
built_from: offline_alert_inbox (existing concept on device/bridge, if available)

args.user_asks: Summarize what I was doing on my Mac and what changed since I last asked.
args.why_useful: Gives the owner a quick, spoken situational awareness of ongoing work without needing a screen.
args.model_tier: Cheaper background tier to assemble the summary; realtime to speak it.
args.latency_budget: 1-3 seconds for a short spoken summary.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; depends on reading job logs and receipts.
args.security_concerns: May reveal sensitive content from apps. Provide a brief summary and avoid reading raw documents unless explicitly asked.
missing: A concise, user-sized summary generator that uses receipts/journal
A stable mapping from job outputs to user-facing summaries

args.user_asks: If I start a task that needs my browser, keep going when I step away and tell me what happened.
args.why_useful: Combines mac/browser reach with relay voice. The owner can initiate from voice, then leave; the system continues and reports back.
args.model_tier: Mac planner for workflows; relay only for voice front-door.
args.latency_budget: Fast acknowledgment; completion later.
args.cost_estimate: Higher; involves browser automation and monitoring.
args.security_concerns: Browser sessions are sensitive. Only access authenticated sessions with explicit user intent and keep summaries minimal.
missing: Reliable continuation when the Mac/browser is unavailable
Asynchronous notification delivery from relay to pendant
A durable job monitor

args.change: Add a relay-visible capability manifest endpoint (e.g., GET /relay/capabilities) plus a typed, enum-based intent routing tool schema that resolves to real plan/execute action types, and a job status receipt feed sized for spoken output.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The relay can reliably tell what it can do and route requests without guessing. That reduces misroutes and lets the owner ask for complex actions with confidence.
args.effort: Medium: define manifest, implement endpoint, align tooling schemas with existing action vocabulary.
args.risk: Low to medium: schema mismatch could break routing; mitigate with versioning and a compatibility alias table.
args.cost_impact: Low ongoing; one extra endpoint and schema maintenance.
args.latency_impact: Improves routing speed by reducing retries and misroutes.
args.security_impact: Requires careful scoping to avoid exposing sensitive internals; publish capability names and versions, not secrets.

args.change: Introduce a durable, cross-surface notification spine: a relay Durable Object (or equivalent) that tracks job subscriptions, stores minimal state, and delivers completion notifications to pendant/phone inboxes when they reconnect.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can start tasks and confidently get results later, even across disconnects, without re-asking.
args.effort: High: needs storage, subscription API, reconnect logic, and delivery semantics.
args.risk: Medium: duplicate or missed notifications; mitigate with idempotent receipts and expiry.
args.cost_impact: Moderate: storage and a small amount of always-on compute.
args.latency_impact: Completion delivery depends on reconnect; acknowledgement stays fast.
args.security_impact: Must enforce per-owner isolation and avoid leaking job metadata; store only what needs to be spoken.

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.change: Shift long-running monitoring and summarization to a cheaper background model tier, keeping the realtime relay model only for conversational control and immediate acknowledgements.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, more responsive voice interactions and lower cost, while still getting rich summaries and updates.
args.effort: Medium: add routing rules and job handoff logic.
args.risk: Low to medium: context drift between tiers; mitigate with explicit job references and minimal shared state.
args.cost_impact: Reduces spend on realtime tokens; adds cheaper background usage.
args.latency_impact: Improves conversational latency; background summaries can take longer.
args.security_impact: Ensure both tiers follow the same data access policy and audit logging.

args.user_asks: “I’m looking at something on my Mac or in a logged-in browser. Tell me exactly what matters, then carry out the safe next step.” The pendant should capture the current visual context, have the Mac/browser agent interpret it with the user’s spoken constraint, act when appropriate, and report what changed and what remains uncertain.
args.why_useful: Today the owner must separately describe what is on a screen and issue a second command; the wearable cannot see the thing they are referring to. This makes the pendant a genuinely remote control for the owner’s current visual context while preserving a concise spoken interaction.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the short utterance and final spoken summary; mac-vision performs screenshot/UI grounding; mac-planner executes the small action sequence; browser-extension supplies authenticated page state when the target is in Safari.
args.latency_budget: 5–8 seconds for a first answer; up to 20 seconds for a multi-step action, with an immediate spoken acknowledgement if it runs longer.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per invocation; screenshot interpretation and any browser page extraction dominate, while the relay turn remains short.
args.security_concerns: A screenshot and possibly authenticated page text leave the Mac for interpretation. Redact known secrets and exclude password fields by default; make destructive or externally visible actions explicit in the spoken plan, and return a receipt naming the app/page and action.
missing: A Mac capture/vision endpoint that can atomically capture the foreground window and expose UI coordinates to mac-vision
A relay-to-Mac visual-context request carrying the spoken referent and a freshness timestamp
A browser bridge that returns the currently focused tab plus an inspectable DOM snapshot
A compact receipt format that the pendant can speak

args.user_asks: “Make this a private handoff: move the thing I’m working on from the Mac/browser to my phone or pendant, and back later, without me explaining it again.” The system should package the current task, relevant files or links, exact position, and unresolved decision into a resumable handoff, then surface it through the wearable and restore it on another surface.
args.why_useful: The owner is often away from the Mac. Today context is stranded in an app, browser tab, or an interrupted voice turn. A durable, minimal handoff would let them leave mid-task and resume hands-free or on the Mac with the same state rather than reconstructing it.
args.model_tier: A cheap background model extracts a structured task capsule; realtime only speaks the capsule title and next decision. Mac-planner/browser-extension produce exact local/browser anchors and faculty-perception validates that they still exist on resume.
args.latency_budget: Under 4 seconds to create a capsule and speak confirmation; restoration may take 10 seconds and should provide progress asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per handoff; tokenized task metadata is cheap, while optional screenshot/file indexing dominates.
args.security_concerns: Capsules may contain private file names, URLs, or snippets. Encrypt at rest, retain only the minimum selected artifacts, expire capsules by default, and never copy file contents to the relay when a local reference suffices. Restoring a browser session must not expose its contents in spoken audio around others.
missing: A durable encrypted task-capsule store with owner-controlled expiry
Mac and browser adapters that record stable anchors (window, tab, document range, cursor/selection)
A pendant/phone inbox verb that can announce and select capsules
Resume validation and conflict handling when a file, tab, or selection changed

args.change: Add a two-channel spoken interaction protocol for the relay: every downstream request first emits a 1-sentence intent echo with a compact correlation token, then the final answer includes a machine-verifiable freshness/source/result class. The pendant should let a second press say “repeat source,” “stop,” or “that’s not what I meant,” and the relay should cancel or correct the active Mac/browser job rather than starting a new unrelated turn.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can currently lose track of whether the pendant heard the right referent, especially while away from the Mac. This would make remote actions recoverable in conversation: fewer silent wrong actions, clear distinction between current state and stale completion, and a fast way to abort without reaching for the Mac.
args.effort: Medium: relay session state and correlation tokens, cancellation propagation to Mac jobs, a small firmware gesture/state addition, and spoken receipt rendering.
args.risk: A dropped cancellation could leave a downstream action running; the relay must say cancellation is requested versus confirmed and use existing job undo/cancel paths where available. Recovery is a final status event and the existing inbox for offline delivery.
args.cost_impact: Negligible per-turn storage; one extra short TTS sentence can add roughly $0.001–$0.01 and modest audio latency.
args.latency_impact: Adds about 300–700 ms for the intent echo, but prevents much costlier retries and wrong actions.
args.security_impact: Correlation tokens must be unguessable and scoped to the owner’s session; spoken source labels should avoid leaking sensitive URLs or file names.
depends_on: A real relay job cancellation/abort propagation path
A durable per-session correlation record
A firmware gesture that distinguishes interrupt/cancel from ordinary playback

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.change: Ship a first-class USB-tethered operating mode: when the nRF9160 and ESP32 are attached to the Mac, a signed local bridge should carry the same press/audio/reply protocol as LTE, expose connection quality and device identity to the relay, and fail back cleanly to the existing offline outbox when the cable is removed. The mode must be selectable per session, not silently masquerade as LTE.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The real pendant is physically testable on the owner’s desk today, but it cannot currently behave like the worn product because it is not relay-registered over LTE. This would let the owner use and debug the actual button, microphone, speaker, LED, and 24 kHz path immediately, then walk away without losing queued work.
args.effort: Medium-high: USB serial framing/authentication on the Mac, a local-to-relay WebSocket or HTTPS bridge, device registration/lease handling, and firmware transport selection with reconnect tests.
args.risk: A stale cable bridge could report the pendant as online when it is not. Use explicit transport identity, heartbeats, monotonic sequence numbers, and replay-safe acknowledgements; on failure, preserve the existing upload-failure-only SD behavior and offline memo queue.
args.cost_impact: No per-invocation model cost beyond normal voice turns; negligible power change while tethered. Engineering cost is in the serial bridge and integration tests.
args.latency_impact: Should reduce desk-mode round-trip latency by roughly 50–150 ms by avoiding LTE, while LTE behavior remains unchanged.
args.security_impact: The local bridge becomes a powerful bearer of microphone audio and relay credentials. Pair it with a device key, bind it to the owner’s Mac session, use encrypted localhost transport, and refuse arbitrary serial clients.
depends_on: A real pendant registration/lease route on the relay
A Mac USB serial bridge for /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA
A transport-neutral audio/session protocol shared by LTE and USB
Integration tests for cable removal during capture, upload, and downlink playback

transcript.text:
Recorded four proposals:

1. **Visual-context command execution** — the pendant asks the Mac/browser what is currently on screen, interprets it, and performs the next safe action.
2. **Resumable task handoffs** — package the current Mac/browser task into an encrypted capsule that can be resumed from the pendant or another surface.
3. **Intent echo and cancellation protocol** — confirm what the relay understood before acting, expose freshness/source status, and support spoken cancellation or correction.
4. **USB-tethered pendant mode** — use the physically connected nRF9160 and ESP32 as a real local pendant session today, with authenticated relay bridging and clean LTE/offline fallback.

The largest missing pieces are the visual-context capture bridge, durable encrypted task capsules, downstream cancellation propagation, pendant gesture support for cancel/correct, and authenticated USB registration/transport.
Okay, I’ll quickly map what’s actually live now, then I’ll propose a few high-impact abilities and call out what’s still missing.

args.user_asks: Tell me when the thing I asked you to do is finished, even if I’ve stopped talking.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful “it just works” behavior: the owner can delegate a long task and go hands-free, then get a spoken result later without polling.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial conversation; a cheaper background tier should monitor jobs and compose the spoken result.
args.latency_budget: Instant acknowledgement when the request is handed off; completion can arrive minutes later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job for status polling, dominated by backend job record reads and text-to-speech rendering.
args.security_concerns: Spoken summaries must not reveal sensitive content to bystanders; include only what’s necessary and avoid reading full documents. Require explicit confirmation before speaking highly sensitive results.
missing: A real implementation of relay_event_push (currently schema-only) or an equivalent notification delivery route
A background job monitor (scheduler/worker) to watch job completion
A durable outbox/inbox path for notifications when the pendant is offline

args.user_asks: If I say a command and the Mac is asleep, queue it and do it when the Mac comes back.
args.why_useful: The owner is often away from the Mac. Queuing turns failures into eventual success without needing them to repeat themselves.
args.model_tier: Realtime to capture intent; cheaper planner to execute when available.
args.latency_budget: Immediate confirmation of queuing; execution whenever the Mac reconnects.
args.cost_estimate: Mostly storage and a retry loop; minimal compute per queued job.
args.security_concerns: Queued actions must be auditable and reversible where possible. Avoid queuing destructive actions without explicit confirmation.
missing: A durable job queue at the relay (not just in-memory)
Reconnect trigger from mac-bridge to drain the queue
Idempotency keys to prevent double execution
A policy for which actions are reversible and which require confirmation

args.user_asks: What am I in the middle of right now?
args.why_useful: A quick spoken snapshot reduces anxiety: what’s queued, what’s running, and what failed, without opening a laptop.
args.model_tier: Realtime, because it’s a quick conversational status check.
args.latency_budget: Under a second when job records are local; a few seconds if it requires Mac status.
args.cost_estimate: Low; a couple of job record reads and a short summary.
args.security_concerns: Avoid revealing sensitive task details; summarize at a high level and offer to drill down.
missing: A consolidated status endpoint that merges relay job records with any local queue state
Consistent job naming and categorization for spoken summaries

args.change: Publish a relay capability manifest endpoint (e.g. GET /relay/capabilities) that lists the relay’s own routes/tools and their schemas, plus a minimal health and version block. Add a matching tool inventory to the capability manifest so agents can discover what exists without probing unknown paths.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets faster progress and fewer dead ends. The relay agent can stop guessing what exists, which reduces bugs and makes new voice features land sooner.
args.effort: Medium: define schema, wire it to the Worker router, and keep it generated from the actual route/tool registry.
args.risk: Low: exposure risk if it leaks internal-only routes. Mitigate with a public vs privileged view and require auth for sensitive entries.
args.cost_impact: Minimal runtime cost; one small JSON response per discovery call.
args.latency_impact: Improves: fewer failed probes and faster routing decisions.
args.security_impact: Requires careful filtering and auth. Privileged entries should require the existing bearer token.
depends_on: A single source of truth for relay routes/tools in the Worker

result.why: This restates something the system already has, so it was not recorded.
result.alreadyHave: Publish a relay capability manifest endpoint (like the Mac’s /capabilities) so relay-realtime can inventory its own routes/tools instead of probing blind.
result.next: Propose something this does not already cover, or say what it should become that it is not today.

args.user_asks: When I say “take care of this” while I’m away from my Mac, use the pendant’s captured utterance plus the Mac’s current screen and authenticated browser context to complete the smallest safe interpretation, then tell me exactly what changed and let me undo it by voice.
args.why_useful: This is the core hive-mind experience: the pendant supplies intent and physical presence, the relay preserves the handoff, and the Mac/browser supply context and reach. Today the owner must spell out app, page, and steps, and cannot reliably resume an interrupted handoff.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for a one-sentence clarification and acknowledgement; mac-planner for planning; mac-vision/browser harness for observing the live UI; background worker for execution receipts and undo window.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; first context-grounded question in under 5 seconds; completion can take minutes with a spoken or queued result.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per handoff, dominated by planner calls and any vision frames; relay speech should remain one short turn.
args.security_concerns: Current screen contents, authenticated pages, and the owner’s utterance leave the Mac for planning. Redact secrets from screenshots, bind the handoff to the current Mac session, keep an append-only action journal, and expose a voice undo command; do not silently broaden an ambiguous request.
missing: A cross-surface handoff capsule with correlation ID, context snapshot, clarification state, and resumable execution
Mac vision loop enabled and able to return structured observations
A durable undoable action journal and relay-side clarification delivery

args.user_asks: Read the important parts of the page I’m looking at into my ear, in short sections; pause when I press the pendant, remember the exact paragraph, and continue when I press again—even if the page is behind my authenticated browser session.
args.why_useful: The owner can consume a private webpage hands-free while walking, without asking the relay to dump an entire page or losing their place. The pendant’s existing interrupt gesture and 24 kHz downlink make this materially better than a generic text summary.
args.model_tier: Browser extraction and section ranking on a cheaper background model; realtime relay only manages turn-taking, interruption, and concise spoken delivery; local browser agent retains the page and selection state.
args.latency_budget: First 2–3 sentence section within 3 seconds of the request; pause/resume acknowledgement under 300 ms; later sections may be prefetched.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per section, dominated by authenticated-page extraction and speech generation; prefetching should be capped.
args.security_concerns: Never send page contents to an untrusted cloud browser; extraction stays on the Mac/browser session and only selected text is sent for speech. Do not persist page text after the turn; bind resume tokens to the browser session and expire them.
missing: A browser action that returns semantic sections plus stable paragraph IDs instead of a raw page dump
A relay audio playlist/cursor protocol supporting pause, resume, and cancellation at packet boundaries
A session-scoped encrypted cursor store shared by browser and pendant

args.user_asks: While I’m in a meeting at my Mac, let me press the pendant to hear a private, rolling one-sentence summary of what has just been said, and let me ask “what was the decision?” or “what do I owe?” without interrupting the meeting audio for anyone else.
args.why_useful: The owner gets an unobtrusive second channel: the pendant can answer a clarification or recover a missed decision without announcing an assistant in the room. This requires the worn device, Mac-local audio, relay turn-taking, and speech generation together; none of those surfaces alone can provide it.
args.model_tier: Mac-local speech capture/transcription and a cheap rolling summarizer; realtime relay only handles the owner’s short query and delivers a tightly bounded answer; use a stronger model only for ambiguity around decisions or owners.
args.latency_budget: Rolling summaries every 10–20 seconds; a query answer within 2 seconds after the owner releases the button; stop all capture immediately on button release.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.12 per meeting hour depending on local versus hosted transcription; the dominant cost is continuous transcription, so local capture and periodic compact deltas are essential.
args.security_concerns: Meeting audio is extremely sensitive. Capture must be physically button-gated, visibly indicated on the Mac and pendant, never retained by default, and sent off-device only as short encrypted transcript deltas needed for the current answer. Provide a hard disconnect and automatic expiry at meeting end.
missing: A Mac-local meeting-audio capture and transcription surface with explicit consent lifecycle
A low-latency rolling-summary state machine that retains only bounded deltas
A private pendant query channel that can interrupt summary playback without stopping capture

args.change: Add a tiny coin vibration motor (or linear resonant actuator) with a dedicated low-side driver and one firmware PWM/GPIO, while keeping the existing LED and button. Define three tactile patterns: queued reply, clarification needed, and task complete/failed. The relay should be able to request a pattern even when the speaker is busy or muted.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can feel that a reply, question, or failed task is waiting without staring at the single LED or wearing headphones. This makes asynchronous Mac/browser work discoverable in the real world rather than silently stranded.
args.effort: Mechanical re-spin or a small pendant revision, driver transistor/MOSFET, firmware pattern scheduler, and relay event mapping; validate vibration strength through clothing and battery impact.
args.risk: Added vibration could annoy or wake the owner, and a stuck GPIO could drain the battery. Use a hard maximum pulse duration, watchdog shutdown, and a physical disable setting; retain LED/audio fallbacks. Recovered units can boot with the motor disabled if self-test fails.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $0.50–$2 in components and assembly, plus a few mA only during pulses; negligible idle draw if the driver is off.
args.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms tactile notification once the relay event reaches the device; no effect on audio codec latency.
args.security_impact: No new data exposure. Patterns must not encode sensitive content—only urgency/type—and should be suppressed for private notifications when configured.
depends_on: A real relay-to-pendant asynchronous event delivery path
Firmware event queue integration with the existing inbox and one-LED state machine
A battery/EMI validation pass

transcript.summary: Recorded four proposals: a context-grounded “take care of this” handoff, resumable private browser page reading, a button-gated private meeting sidecar, and a haptic notification upgrade. The owner still cannot have these today because the relay lacks a durable cross-surface handoff/cursor protocol, the Mac vision loop and local meeting-audio capture are unavailable, browser extraction has no semantic cursor, asynchronous event delivery is not live, and the pendant has no tactile actuator. The most valuable is the first: intent from the worn pendant plus current Mac/browser context, resumable execution, truthful receipt, and voice undo.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Which already-recorded backlog items implement or overlap the proposed handoff, page cursor, meeting sidecar, and haptic actuator; the recorder accepted all four but flagged each as adjacent, so they should be checked against the backlog before engineering starts.

transcript.text: I’m going to quickly inventory what’s actually available now, then I’ll highlight what’s still missing and propose a few high-impact next steps.

args.user_asks: “Track that task and tell me when it’s done, even if I stop talking.”
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful outcome for a wearable assistant: the owner can hand off a job and walk away, then get a spoken update later without polling.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the initial handoff; a cheaper background tier for monitoring and composing the final spoken update.
args.latency_budget: Fast initial acknowledgment (<1s). Completion notification can arrive whenever the job finishes.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job: one plan/execute cycle plus status checks. Dominated by Mac-side work and any browser session time, not relay compute.
args.security_concerns: Notifications must reflect true job state. Never claim success without a confirmed completion receipt. Keep spoken content minimal and avoid sensitive details unless the owner explicitly asked for them.
missing: A real implementation behind relay_event_push (or equivalent route) to deliver queued completion events
A persistence mechanism to store pending notifications until delivered (Durable Object, KV, or equivalent)
A bridge for the Mac to emit completion receipts the relay can subscribe to

args.user_asks: “Summarize what you’re about to do before you do it, and let me approve or change it.”
args.why_useful: When the system spans a wearable, a Mac, and browser sessions, a quick, spoken preflight summary helps prevent wrong turns and builds trust without requiring the owner to watch a screen.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the brief spoken preflight. Mac-planner handles the plan details.
args.latency_budget: Preflight should be under 2 seconds. Approval adds only the owner’s response time.
args.cost_estimate: Mostly planning cost; the spoken summary is lightweight.
args.security_concerns: Do not expose secrets from authenticated sessions. Summaries should be high-level and omit sensitive content unless the owner explicitly asked for it.
missing: A standardized plan preview format that is safe to speak
A reversible approval flow that can pause execution between plan and run
A relay-visible plan receipt so the correct job is approved

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: All 4 pieces you named already exist: /plan, /journal/:jobid, /jobs/:jobid, /execute. So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.user_asks: “If I sound lost, help me recover: suggest the next sensible step based on what I last asked and what’s actually happening.”
args.why_useful: In voice, confusion is expensive. A gentle recovery that uses recent context and real job state can prevent repeated commands and frustration.
args.model_tier: Realtime to detect confusion cues; cheaper tier to reason over context and propose next steps.
args.latency_budget: Short hint within ~1 second. Heavier reasoning deferred to a cheaper tier if needed.
args.cost_estimate: Low most of the time; occasional escalations to a larger model to resolve ambiguity.
args.security_concerns: Hints must not hallucinate job state. If state is unknown, say so and offer to check.
missing: A shared, low-cost context projection accessible across surfaces
A standardized confusion/repair signal emitted by the relay
A policy for when to auto-check status vs ask the owner

args.user_asks: “Handle this job until it is truly finished. If you hit an ambiguity, ask me one precise question through the pendant, use my answer, and keep going; when done, tell me exactly what changed and what remains.”
args.why_useful: Today a delegated Mac task either guesses through ambiguity or stops as an opaque job. This would make the worn device a genuinely interactive supervisor: the owner can walk away, answer a single spoken clarification later, and receive a truthful completion rather than restarting the whole request.
args.model_tier: Use relay-realtime only for the short clarification and final spoken turn; mac-planner handles planning and state, mac-vision/browser-extension perform UI work, and a slower background planner evaluates whether the clarification is actually necessary.
args.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 500 ms; clarification delivery within 2 s of the blocker; task continuation within 5 s after the answer. Long actions may run asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per task depending on planner turns; the dominant cost is repeated planner context and screenshots, not the relay clarification.
args.security_concerns: The planner must attach the exact blocked step, candidate interpretations, and evidence to each question so the owner is not approving an invisible action. The answer and resulting actions leave the pendant for the relay/Mac; no new secrets should be copied into the question. Reversible actions remain automatic under the owner's maximum-access policy.
missing: A planner-to-relay clarification event with a resumable job state
A pendant reply correlation to the blocked job
A durable state machine that can pause a Mac/browser job without losing session context
An end-to-end completion receipt that includes changed objects and unresolved steps

args.user_asks: “Before you act, reconcile what I said with what is actually open on my Mac and in my signed-in browser, then give me one spoken plan with the supporting evidence; if the two surfaces disagree, tell me the conflict instead of choosing silently.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has separate Mac and browser agents that can each act, but no owner-facing cross-surface truth pass. This prevents dangerous stale-tab or stale-file decisions and makes a spoken answer defensible: the pendant can say which tab, document, timestamp, or local state it relied on.
args.model_tier: faculty-perception or a cheap background model gathers and normalizes observations; faculty-judgement produces the compact recommendation; relay-realtime only speaks the result and routes an explicit action request.
args.latency_budget: Read-only reconciliation in 3–8 s; speak an initial conflict warning as soon as the first contradictory pair is found. Never block the owner on a full scan when a local, bounded evidence set is sufficient.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.12 per invocation; screenshots/page extraction and re-sent evidence dominate. Cache hashes and timestamps locally so unchanged surfaces are not resent.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated browser content and local files must remain scoped to the specific request and be redacted before cross-surface model calls. Return provenance and freshness timestamps. Acting on the recommendation must be a separate explicit downstream action, not an accidental side effect of inspection.
missing: A cross-surface observation envelope with source, timestamp, freshness, and confidence
Parallel read-only fan-out to Mac and browser with bounded scope
A conflict detector and spoken evidence/provenance formatter
A relay turn that can present the recommendation without invoking execution

args.change: Add a physical 'attention lease' protocol spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser: when a task begins, the pendant announces whether it is merely observing, waiting for the owner, or actively changing state; the lease expires unless the relay receives heartbeats from the executing surface, and expiry causes a spoken/LED interruption with the last verified checkpoint. A resumed button press renews the lease and continues from that checkpoint rather than replaying earlier actions.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can walk away knowing whether a request is safely waiting, still working, or has gone stale. If Wi‑Fi, the Mac, or a browser session dies, they hear the last fact that was actually verified instead of a confident but obsolete completion.
