transcript.text: I’m going to quickly inventory what I can see from this relay surface, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and any missing pieces to make them real.

args.user_asks: Keep an eye on that task and tell me when it finishes, even if I’ve stopped talking.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing for the owner: long-running Mac work becomes hands-free. They can walk away and still get a reliable, spoken completion update on the pendant.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the initial acknowledgment; cheaper background model for monitoring and composing the final spoken update.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm monitoring is set; completion notification can arrive whenever the job resolves.
args.cost_estimate: Low per request; dominant cost is background polling and text-to-speech rendering for a short spoken summary.
args.security_concerns: Spoken updates may expose task details in public. Use concise phrasing, avoid sensitive content in the spoken string, and require confirmation for high-risk or ambiguous summaries.
missing: A real implementation for relay_event_push (currently schema-only).
A background notification mechanism (cron/alarm or durable object) to monitor job status without a running voice session.
A sanctioned path to render and deliver audio to the pendant without storing audio routinely on-device.

args.user_asks: When I’m tethered over USB, sync everything that’s waiting and then summarize what changed.
args.why_useful: While LTE is unregistered, USB tether is the fastest reliable path. This makes the pendant feel dependable: queued memos, alerts, and receipts get reconciled and the owner hears what actually updated.
args.model_tier: Realtime for a quick spoken summary; mac-planner for the sync orchestration; cheaper model for reconciliation logic if it’s long-running.
args.latency_budget: A brief spoken acknowledgement immediately; sync can take seconds, then a short summary.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; dominated by device I/O and reconciliation, not LLM tokens.
args.security_concerns: USB sync touches local data and potentially credentials. Keep payloads minimal, encrypt where possible, and log receipts without leaking content.
missing: A stable relay route/state machine for USB sync and receipts (the mac-planner asked about this; it needs a real endpoint to target).
A typed manifest for outbox/inbox item kinds so we don’t invent multiple queues.
Clear receipt semantics for exactly-once delivery across relay and Mac.

args.user_asks: Give me a quick status snapshot: what’s connected, what’s queued, and what’s next.
args.why_useful: A single spoken snapshot reduces uncertainty. The owner doesn’t have to ask three different questions to understand if the system is healthy and what it’s doing.
args.model_tier: Realtime model to compose a concise spoken status from live counters.
args.latency_budget: Under a second when cached; a few seconds if it must query multiple sources.
args.cost_estimate: Low; dominated by a small number of status probes, not generation.
args.security_concerns: Status can reveal sensitive context (active job names, connected devices). Use generic labels and avoid reading detailed job content unless asked.
missing: A relay-visible status route for the relay surface itself (the relay can’t inventory its own capabilities).
A unified health snapshot that merges Mac, device, and relay counters into one response.

args.user_asks: “Why did you do that?” — For any recent action you took on my Mac or in my browser, give me a short spoken explanation grounded in the exact evidence you used (page text, tab/app state, and action receipt), and if it was wrong, undo it or tell me precisely why undo is unavailable.
args.why_useful: Trust is the limiting factor for a wearable that can act while the owner is away. Today receipts and undo are separate primitives; the owner cannot interrogate one coherent causal record from the pendant. This would make mistakes understandable and recoverable without opening the Mac.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the spoken question and a concise synthesis; cheap background summarization should index the existing evidence and receipts.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds to acknowledge, under 8 seconds for a first spoken explanation; undo should begin immediately after the owner says “undo it.”
args.cost_estimate: Roughly one realtime turn plus a small background summarization call; about $0.01–$0.05 per investigation, dominated by speech and evidence synthesis.
args.security_concerns: Evidence may contain private page text or command output. Keep raw evidence on the relay/Mac, send only the minimum quoted excerpts to the realtime model, and never claim an action was undone without a verified undo receipt.
missing: A durable causal evidence bundle linking plan inputs, observations, chosen actions, and outcomes
A relay query that resolves “that action” to a job and returns its evidence, not just its status
A spoken explanation/undo orchestrator that can call /jobs/:jobId/undo and verify the result

args.user_asks: “Give me a private handoff.” — While I am away from my Mac, let me dictate a sensitive task on the pendant, have the relay hold it encrypted, and release it to the Mac or authenticated browser only when the pendant and the intended device are both present again; then tell me exactly what was released and what remains sealed.
args.why_useful: A wearable is useful away from the desk, but sending sensitive dictated material immediately to a cloud relay or unattended Mac is often the wrong tradeoff. This creates a deliberate, physical-presence handoff rather than forcing the owner to choose between losing the task and exposing it.
args.model_tier: Realtime model extracts only a task envelope and sensitivity label; encryption, presence checks, and release policy are deterministic. Use a cheaper background model to summarize the sealed queue after release.
args.latency_budget: Immediate local acknowledgement in under 500 ms; release and confirmation within 5 seconds after the paired device is detected.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per task beyond one short realtime classification, roughly $0.002–$0.01; storage and cryptographic key management dominate engineering cost, not inference.
args.security_concerns: This is specifically about keeping secrets sealed. Use device-bound keys, nonce-protected records, expiry and explicit deletion, and never put plaintext dictated content in logs, analytics, or spoken notifications. Presence must be cryptographic pairing, not merely a network IP.
missing: Pendant-side encrypted sealed-record support and a physical release gesture
Relay encrypted-at-rest queue with device-bound key exchange and expiry
USB/LTE pairing and presence attestation for the real nRF9160 and ESP32-connected setup
Mac/browser release endpoints that acknowledge exact record hashes and receipt them

args.user_asks: “Run this as a reversible experiment.” — Before changing my files, settings, browser state, or messages, show me a spoken prediction of the observable changes and a rollback plan; execute in an isolated snapshot or transaction where possible, then report which predicted changes actually occurred and let me revert the whole experiment with one phrase.
args.why_useful: The owner wants maximum access, but maximum access without a way to understand blast radius is hard to trust. A whole-experiment boundary is more useful than a per-click confirmation: it preserves speed while making multi-step changes inspectable and collectively reversible.
args.model_tier: Realtime model frames the experiment and speaks the result; deterministic planners and shell/browser adapters perform snapshots, diffs, and rollback. Use a cheaper background model for large diffs.
args.latency_budget: Prediction in under 3 seconds for a short plan; execution can run asynchronously, with a compact pendant update as soon as the first verified receipt arrives.
args.cost_estimate: One realtime framing call plus optional background diff summarization, roughly $0.01–$0.08 depending on changed files/page state; storage for snapshots is the dominant cost.
args.security_concerns: Snapshots can duplicate secrets. Store locally where possible, encrypt relay-held artifacts, redact spoken diffs, expire snapshots, and make rollback idempotent. Do not pretend arbitrary external side effects (sent mail, purchases) are reversible; label them as irreversible before execution.
missing: Transaction/snapshot adapters for filesystem, macOS preferences, browser storage and app state
A cross-action experiment ID joining /plan, /execute, receipts, observations and rollback
A diff-and-rollback planner with explicit irreversible-side-effect detection
A pendant command path for “revert experiment <recent description>”

args.user_asks: “Use my personal lens for this.” — Let me switch, from the pendant, which private context the hive may use (personal, work, travel, or no-history), and have the relay enforce that lens consistently across its speech context, Mac actions, browser tabs, logs, and follow-up notifications until I switch it back.
args.why_useful: The owner cannot safely wear a context-free agent everywhere. A single spoken privacy mode should prevent accidental mixing of work and personal material, rather than relying on each downstream agent to remember a preference or on the owner to explain it every turn.
args.model_tier: Realtime model recognizes only the explicit lens switch and confirms it; enforcement is deterministic at the relay and adapters. No expensive model is needed for ordinary routing.
args.latency_budget: Mode change acknowledgement in under 1 second; enforcement must apply before the next transcript or action leaves the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost after setup; roughly $0.001 or less per switch. Engineering cost is policy propagation and audit testing.
args.security_concerns: A lens must fail closed when missing or stale, be visible in every spoken confirmation, and never be inferred from location or calendar. Redact excluded context at ingestion rather than merely hiding it in prompts; retain an audit trail of mode changes without retaining excluded content.
missing: A relay-owned, versioned context-lens state with TTL and explicit reset
Ingress filtering for audio/transcripts and egress filtering for Mac/browser actions and notifications
Mac/browser adapters that expose and enforce lens-scoped app/tab/session allowlists
Pendant LED/audio confirmation and offline persistence of the selected lens

args.change: Implement a first-class context-lens firewall at relay ingress/egress: a signed lens state (personal/work/travel/no-history) with TTL and explicit reset, applied before transcript persistence, model-context assembly, Mac/browser dispatch, and event-push text. Every job and receipt carries the lens version; adapters reject mismatched or absent versions. The pendant gets a compact state acknowledgement and retains the last lens offline until the owner changes it.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can wear the agent in mixed settings without accidentally exposing work material to a personal task or vice versa; one spoken mode change becomes a reliable boundary across the entire hive.
args.effort: High: relay state machine, redaction at ingestion, propagation through planner/browser/mac contracts, firmware acknowledgement, and adversarial tests for stale or missing lens state.
args.risk: A false or stale lens could suppress useful context or leak the wrong one. Fail closed on uncertainty, provide an explicit spoken reset, and preserve only metadata needed to diagnose enforcement—not excluded content.
args.cost_impact: Small ongoing storage and CPU cost; one extra short metadata object per job. No meaningful model cost after the explicit switch.
args.latency_impact: Under tens of milliseconds for policy checks; no additional model turn for ordinary requests.
args.security_impact: Strongly positive if filtering occurs before persistence and dispatch. Requires careful key/signature handling so a compromised adapter cannot silently change the lens.
depends_on: A durable relay session/context state route
Lens-aware Mac and browser adapters
Pendant-side acknowledgement and offline persistence of the selected lens

transcript.text:
Recorded four owner-facing capabilities and one relay change:

1. **Evidence-backed “Why did you do that?”**  
   The pendant explains recent Mac/browser actions using their actual evidence and can initiate verified undo.

2. **Private handoff**  
   Sensitive dictated tasks remain sealed until the pendant and intended Mac/browser are physically paired again.

3. **Reversible experiments**  
   Multi-step changes run within a snapshot/rollback boundary, with predicted-versus-actual results and one-phrase revert where possible.

4. **Spoken context lenses**  
   “Personal,” “work,” “travel,” or “no-history” becomes an enforced boundary across transcripts, model context, Mac actions, browser tabs, logs, and alerts.

5. **Relay context-lens firewall**  
   I recorded the implementation change needed to enforce those lenses before persistence or dispatch, with signed versions, TTLs, adapter enforcement, and pendant acknowledgement.

What remains needed is not another discovery pass: durable causal evidence bundles, encrypted device-bound handoff storage and pairing, transaction/snapshot adapters, and a relay-owned context firewall propagated through Mac/browser adapters and pendant firmware.
I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll point out the gaps and what I’d ask for next.

args.user_asks: Tell me when that task finishes.
args.why_useful: This is the most owner-visible improvement: long-running Mac actions don’t leave them guessing. They can walk away and still get a short spoken outcome.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the spoken notification; planning and execution stay on the Mac tier.
args.latency_budget: Notification should arrive within a few seconds of completion when online; otherwise it should be queued and delivered when the link returns.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job. The expensive part is the voice session; status checks are cheap and should be event-driven rather than polled.
args.security_concerns: The notification text must match job truth. No paraphrasing that changes meaning. Include only what’s necessary to identify the job to the owner.
missing: A real implementation of relay_event_push (currently a schema only).
A completion event source from the Mac job lifecycle to the relay (or a durable subscription mechanism).
A relay capability manifest so this surface can be inventoried and tested.

args.user_asks: What’s my system status right now?
args.why_useful: A quick spoken snapshot reduces confusion: is the Mac connected, is the bridge alive, is the browser session available, and what should the owner do next.
args.model_tier: Realtime for summarization; data collection should be from existing status endpoints.
args.latency_budget: Under a second for typical status calls when online.
args.cost_estimate: Very low. One or two status reads and a short spoken response.
args.security_concerns: Avoid leaking detailed environment info beyond what the owner asked. Keep it high-level.
missing: Reliable relay-visible status for the pendant/bridge and browser session in one place.
Inventory of relay endpoints so the status path can be maintained.

args.user_asks: Do that on the Mac, and if you need details, ask me.
args.why_useful: This is a smoother handoff for multi-step tasks: the relay captures intent, the Mac plans, and the owner only answers clarifying questions when necessary.
args.model_tier: Realtime for intent capture; mac-planner for the workflow.
args.latency_budget: Intent capture should be immediate; planning can take a few seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate: one plan call plus execution. Keep the relay’s role minimal.
args.security_concerns: Do not execute irreversible actions without a clear plan and receipts. Keep a job record for traceability.
missing: A resolvable intent-routing mechanism (relay_route_intent is currently unresolved).
An enum-based intent contract tied to real action types (so routing can resolve).
Relay capability manifest for discoverability.

args.change: Build a relay-visible capability manifest and health inventory endpoint (e.g., GET /relay/capabilities and GET /relay/health) so this surface can be discovered, tested, and monitored like the Mac agent. Include tool resolution status (live/resolved/unresolved), and expose whether event push is implemented.

args.risk: Low. Main risk is leaking internal details; mitigate by redacting secrets and returning only capability names and statuses.
args.cost_impact: Low. A small amount of extra metadata and an endpoint.
args.latency_impact: Negligible. Fetch only when asked.
args.security_impact: Positive if done carefully: explicit inventory reduces accidental exposure and makes access control auditable.

args.change: Replace the unresolved free-form relay_route_intent with an enum-based intent contract mapped to real action types (the same vocabulary used by /plan). Use per-enum resolution so some intents can go live before others. Provide a fallback to mac_delegate for complex tasks.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, more reliable voice control. The owner can say a simple thing and have it routed correctly without brittle heuristics.
args.effort: Medium to high. Requires schema design, resolver wiring, and coordination with mac-planner.
args.risk: Medium. Misrouting could launch the wrong action; mitigate with receipts and conservative defaults (ask before irreversible steps).
args.cost_impact: Low ongoing; moderate initial integration.
args.latency_impact: Improves routing speed by avoiding extra clarification turns.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by making routing explicit and auditable.

args.change: Implement asynchronous completion delivery using a durable subscription: Mac job lifecycle emits completion events to the relay; relay pushes a spoken summary to the pendant/phone if online, or stores a short alert in the existing inbox mechanism if offline. Use ttl and expiry semantics.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can start something and move on without babysitting. The system feels dependable.
args.effort: High. Needs event emission, relay delivery, and UI/voice handling.
args.risk: Medium. Duplicate or out-of-order events could confuse; mitigate with idempotent jobIds and receipts.
args.cost_impact: Moderate. Event channel plus storage for small alerts.
args.latency_impact: Low when online; eventual when offline.
args.security_impact: Must ensure summaries reflect truth and do not leak sensitive content. Use minimal phrasing and job scoping.

args.user_asks: “When my pendant is physically with my Mac, let this button press authorize the next powerful action I say—open the authenticated portal, send the prepared message, or change the setting—without another confirmation. If the pendant is not present, only prepare and report.”
args.why_useful: It gives the owner fast, deliberate control over high-impact remote actions while preventing a replayed voice request or a compromised relay session from acting later. The same wearable that hears the request becomes a short-lived physical authorization key.
args.model_tier: Realtime only parses the spoken request and reports the result; the Mac planner performs the action, while browser-extension handles authenticated browser state. No expensive model is needed for the cryptographic check.
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms to establish the challenge when USB-attached, then the normal 1–3 s action latency; the pendant should say “authorized” immediately and stream the result when complete.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one realtime turn plus one planner/action call, roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on the action; cryptographic challenge traffic is negligible.
args.security_concerns: A nonce-bound challenge must be signed by the pendant over USB or LTE and scoped to one normalized action, one Mac session, and a short expiry. Never treat mere historical pairing or an audio recording as authorization. Show a distinct LED pattern before commit and log the signed receipt; losing the pendant requires revocation.
missing: pendant challenge-response firmware and secure key storage
relay authorization verifier and nonce ledger
Mac/browser enforcement that refuses the commit without a fresh pendant signature
a physical-presence signal that works over the currently live USB serial links

args.user_asks: “Tell me what is actually true right now, even if the Mac, browser, and relay disagree—what changed, what is still a draft, and what evidence proves it.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has to trust a single completion message. This would reconcile independent observations: for example, the Mac reports a send attempt, the authenticated browser still shows a draft, and the relay has no receipt. It speaks the contradiction instead of confidently claiming success.
args.model_tier: A cheap background perception pass gathers structured observations; a judgment model compares timestamps, identities, and source reliability. Realtime only turns the final verdict into a short spoken answer.
args.latency_budget: 2–5 seconds for a normal live query, with an immediate “checking three sources” acknowledgement; never block the voice turn on an unavailable source.
args.cost_estimate: One small perception/judgment pass, approximately $0.01–$0.04 per query; browser and Mac reads dominate neither tokens nor bandwidth.
args.security_concerns: Only return content already authorized for the owner’s paired Mac/browser session. Preserve source timestamps and hashes rather than copying whole pages into relay memory. Explicitly say “unverified” when sources conflict or are stale; never synthesize a successful state from an action request alone.
missing: a common observation envelope with source, timestamp, object identity, and confidence
a reconciliation/judgment route that can request parallel Mac and browser reads
spoken provenance formatting and a contradiction receipt in the job ledger

args.user_asks: “Take this outcome, work across my Mac and my authenticated browser, and keep going through ordinary interruptions. If one step fails, use the partial result to continue, and come back with exactly what was done, what was not, and the one choice you need from me.”
args.why_useful: This is an outcome-level assistant rather than a brittle one-turn command: it can collect a file locally, use a logged-in web service, reconcile the returned identifiers, and recover from a dropped Mac or browser connection without making the owner repeat the whole request.
args.model_tier: Realtime extracts the goal and handles brief clarifications. A cheaper planner owns the durable state machine; use the vision model only for a browser/UI step that has no reliable structured action.
args.latency_budget: A spoken acknowledgement within 1 second; each step may take seconds or minutes. The owner can end the conversation and receive a concise completion or blocked-choice alert later.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.20 per multi-step outcome, dominated by planner iterations and occasional vision calls; retries should reuse observations rather than resend full context.
args.security_concerns: Persist only the minimum goal, action receipts, and opaque remote IDs. Every retry must be idempotency-keyed so reconnects cannot duplicate a send or purchase. A blocked destructive choice is reported, not guessed; all completed steps remain auditable and undo metadata is retained where available.
missing: durable cross-surface workflow state and idempotency keys
a coordinator that can resume after Mac/browser disconnects
event delivery to the pendant for completion or needs-attention
structured partial-result handoff between planner and browser session

args.change: Build a signed, one-shot authorization bridge: the pendant emits a nonce-bound challenge over the live USB serial transport (and later LTE), the relay binds that signature to a normalized /plan job and expiry, and the Mac/browser executor refuses commit unless the exact job receipt contains that signature. Return the signed receipt to the pendant and visibly distinguish authorized execution from mere preparation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely say “do it” while standing at the Mac and get immediate execution, while the same request cannot be replayed after they walk away or from an old audio transcript. It turns the wearable into a trustworthy physical control, not just a microphone.

What is still needed:

- A shared cross-surface task/artifact envelope.
- Durable background execution with retries, idempotency, and “needs owner” states.

args.user_asks: When you finish something on my behalf, let me say “undo that” and have you reverse the last reversible change, even if it touched both my Mac and a browser tab.
args.why_useful: A wearable assistant becomes safe to use at conversational speed when mistakes are recoverable without finding the right app or remembering what happened. The relay can identify the exact completed job, explain any irreversible portion, and dispatch compensating actions across surfaces.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the short undo utterance and selects the latest job; a cheaper background planner derives a compensation plan from action receipts; Mac/browser agents execute and verify it.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 500 ms; begin reversal within 2 s; completion may take as long as the original job, with a short pendant result and durable inbox fallback.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per undo depending on whether compensation needs planning; latency and cost are dominated by receipt interpretation and postcondition verification, not the spoken turn.
args.security_concerns: The system must never claim an irreversible send, purchase, deletion, or external side effect was undone. Every action needs before/after evidence, a reversibility class, and an explicit partial-undo report. Receipt data may contain URLs and document names, so dashboard retention should be bounded.
missing: A durable before-state/compensation record for each Mac and browser action
A compensation planner and verification loop
A single undo endpoint that can correlate the latest job across relay, Mac, and browser
A user-visible distinction between fully reversed, partially reversed, and irreversible

args.user_asks: What was the thing I saw about [topic]? Search my open and recently used browser pages and my Mac files, then tell me the answer with where each piece came from.
args.why_useful: Today web search can find public information, but the owner's useful context is often behind their own browser sessions or in local files. This would make the pendant a truthful memory of the owner's working world rather than a generic search box, while preserving citations so an uncertain match is obvious.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay extracts the topic and gives a concise answer; browser and Mac retrieval run in parallel with a cheaper model for ranking and deduplication; realtime is used only to narrate the final evidence-backed result.
args.latency_budget: Speak an acknowledgement immediately; return a first answer in 3–8 seconds and continue with a later alert if local indexing or a locked browser tab takes longer.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.12 per query, mostly retrieval/reranking and any Mac planner turn; a local text index would reduce both cost and latency after initial indexing.
args.security_concerns: Never send private page or file contents to public web search. Retrieval must be scoped to explicitly requested personal sources, redact secrets from the spoken summary, retain source URLs/paths only as long as needed, and clearly say when a source could not be opened.
missing: A Mac-side local full-text index with permission-aware file and browser-history connectors
A browser command to export searchable page text and timestamps from the owner's authenticated session
A relay retrieval/ranking endpoint that merges Mac and browser evidence with provenance
A compact spoken citation format and dashboard transcript showing exact excerpts

args.user_asks: Put me back into my work context from yesterday.
args.why_useful: The owner should be able to leave the Mac, use another machine, or recover after a crash without manually reconstructing apps, browser tabs, documents, and the exact page positions that mattered. A worn-device request can restore a meaningful working state while the owner is away, then report what could not be recovered.
args.model_tier: A background Mac agent captures and normalizes context snapshots; realtime only resolves the spoken snapshot name and gives a result. The Mac planner restores apps/files and the browser extension restores authenticated tabs, with computer vision reserved for pages whose URL/state is insufficient.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; restore the first useful state in 5–15 seconds and continue asynchronously for large sessions. Speak a compact list of restored and skipped items.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.20 per restore, dominated by planner/vision turns; snapshot storage and local indexing are the larger ongoing costs, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Snapshots can expose private URLs, document names, and scroll context. Store them encrypted on the Mac, keep only explicit named snapshots plus bounded retention, never replay passwords or form contents, and make the spoken result omit secrets. A restore must not silently submit or send anything.
missing: A Mac context snapshot service for app windows, file URLs, browser tabs, scroll/selection metadata, and timestamps
A named snapshot store and diff format shared by Mac and relay
Browser extension save/restore commands for authenticated tabs without serializing cookies
A restore planner with idempotent actions and per-item receipts
A pendant command/result path that can survive the owner walking away

args.user_asks: “Track that task and tell me when it’s done, even if I’m not talking anymore.”

args.model_tier: Realtime to acknowledge and set up tracking; cheaper background tier to monitor status and generate the final short summary.

args.user_asks: “If I say ‘that’s wrong’ right after you summarize a result, fix the task or roll it back.”
args.why_useful: Voice-first correction turns the pendant into a real control surface: the owner can recover from mistakes quickly without digging into apps or logs.
args.model_tier: Realtime for interpreting the correction; mac-planner for choosing a safe rollback or edit; cheaper tier for audit trail.
args.latency_budget: Under ~2 seconds to acknowledge; rollback execution depends on the job but should be queued immediately.

args.user_asks: “I’m away from my Mac. Tell me exactly what I was in the middle of, across my Mac, browser, and pendant, and let me say ‘continue’ to pick it back up.”
args.why_useful: The pendant currently starts new conversations, but it cannot reconstruct a truthful working set from the other surfaces. This would make the wearable a reliable handoff point: current app and window, active browser tab and page state, unfinished Mac jobs, recent owner-scoped facts, and device connectivity become one short spoken answer. “Continue” would resume the identified reversible workflow rather than forcing the owner to remember which surface held it.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the short spoken synthesis and disambiguation; a cheaper background planner should gather and normalize the context, while mac-planner performs the resumed workflow.
args.latency_budget: First answer under 3 seconds when Mac and browser are online; up to 10 seconds for a fresh cross-surface snapshot. Resume acknowledgement under 2 seconds, with asynchronous progress thereafter.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per handoff, dominated by one realtime turn; context gathering and job polling should use cheap non-realtime calls.
args.security_concerns: The answer must only include facts scoped to voice and the current owner session, never arbitrary browser page contents. Resuming must be limited to the previously identified workflow and produce an auditable job receipt; destructive or external-send steps should be surfaced as pending rather than silently inferred.
missing: A cross-surface context assembler that joins machine context, browser state, live jobs, and projected memory into a stable checkpoint
A durable checkpoint identity and resume endpoint mapping one spoken ‘continue’ to the exact planner goal and prior constraints
Mac/browser adapters that report the current task, not just raw tabs or installed applications

args.user_asks: “Don’t just tell me the Mac task finished—verify the result independently and tell me what is actually true.”
args.why_useful: Planner success is not the same as world-state success: an app may have rejected a save, a browser command may have acted on the wrong tab, or a network request may still be pending. The relay should commission a separate perception pass after an action, compare the observed state with the requested outcome, and speak a calibrated result such as verified, partially verified, or could not verify. This is the single most valuable trust feature because it prevents the owner from acting on a confident but false completion report while away from the screen.
args.model_tier: Cheap background perception and deterministic checks first; realtime is used only to explain the verdict in one sentence or ask a narrowly scoped follow-up.
args.latency_budget: Initial acknowledgement under 2 seconds; verification within 5–15 seconds depending on app/browser state, with an asynchronous pendant update for slower checks.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per verified action, dominated by screenshots or page extraction and only occasional model adjudication; deterministic receipts should handle the common case.
args.security_concerns: Verification may inspect private screens and authenticated pages, so retain only hashes, selected evidence, and redacted snippets. Never claim verified from a planner receipt alone. If evidence conflicts, say so and preserve both the requested intent and observed state for audit.
missing: A post-execution verification contract linking requested outcome assertions to concrete observable predicates
A faculty-perception endpoint that can inspect Mac/browser state after execution and return evidence with confidence
A relay-owned verdict record and pendant delivery path that distinguishes complete, partial, failed, and unverified

Store only the minimum excerpt, encrypt at rest, scope facts to voice/mac/browser, and never attach to a page or file based on a weak match without saying “I’m not sure what you meant.” Browser-originated content must remain a separate low-trust memory tier.

args.user_asks: Run a quick pendant-to-Mac audio check and tell me if the link is healthy.

args.model_tier: Realtime for guidance; diagnostics can be automated without heavy reasoning.
args.latency_budget: A few seconds end-to-end; short spoken steps if manual intervention is needed.
args.cost_estimate: Low. A small diagnostic payload and a brief report.
args.security_concerns: Diagnostics should avoid recording real content; use synthetic audio and discard it after the check.
missing: A defined diagnostic verb on the USB bridge and relay pipeline to run loopback tests
Permissioned endpoint to invoke bridge work when attached

args.change: Implement a real relay-side completion notification pipeline. Track jobId -> delivery targets (pendant/phone/dashboard), monitor status transitions using the existing job status read path, and emit alerts into the existing offline alert inbox flow when sessions end.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can fire off a task and get a spoken outcome later without babysitting the system.
args.effort: Medium. Requires a persistent mapping table, a watcher loop, and integration with the device inbox format.
args.risk: Alert spam or duplicate notifications. Mitigate with dedup receipts and per-job state machine.
args.cost_impact: Low. Polling is the main cost; bound it by exponential backoff and a hard cap per job.
args.latency_impact: Adds a small background delay; user-facing latency improves because they don’t wait in-session.
args.security_impact: Notification content could leak sensitive details; default to minimal summaries unless the owner opted in.
depends_on: job_completion_watch semantics clarified or replaced with a concrete watcher route
A real relay_event_push implementation or an alternative delivery verb

args.change: Wire the existing memory projection into the live conversation context builder, in place of the legacy prompt composition, to reduce per-turn token cost and keep status references stable.
args.why_useful_to_owner: More consistent context means fewer misunderstandings like “that thing” failing to resolve, and it reduces latency/cost per turn.
args.effort: Medium. One injection point change plus tests for ordering and budgets.
args.risk: Context regressions causing missing permissions or stale preferences. Mitigate with a rollout flag and telemetry.
args.cost_impact: Measured savings about 222 tokens/turn (≈59%).
args.latency_impact: Lower; less prompt churn and fewer retries.
args.security_impact: No new data leaves; it changes ordering and selection only.

args.change: Add a USB-attached diagnostics path: relay can invoke a bridge work command that generates synthetic audio, routes it through the pipeline, and returns measurable health (levels, packet loss, decode errors).
args.why_useful_to_owner: A quick “is it healthy?” check before a demo prevents embarrassing failures.
args.effort: Medium to high. Needs a new command verb and a small report schema.
args.risk: Could interfere with a real conversation if triggered at the wrong time. Require idle state and a clear spoken confirmation.
args.cost_impact: Low ongoing; occasional diagnostics only.
args.latency_impact: A few seconds per run.
args.security_impact: Must avoid capturing real speech; synthetic only and discard artifacts.
depends_on: Permission to POST /v1/bridge/work
A defined bridge command set

args.user_asks: Move this conversation to my Mac, keep the context and unfinished plan, and let me continue there (or bring the result back to my pendant).
args.why_useful: The owner should not have to repeat a long spoken request when they reach the Mac. This creates a real handoff between the worn front door and the machine with the browser session, rather than treating each surface as a separate chat.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the handoff command and a short acknowledgement; mac-planner performs the work; a cheaper background summarizer compresses the transcript and pending decisions.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant in under 1 second; make the Mac session available within 3 seconds; later work may be asynchronous.
args.cost_estimate: About one realtime turn plus one inexpensive summarization call per handoff; the dominant cost is the context compression, not the relay acknowledgement.
args.security_concerns: The handoff must preserve the owner's existing authorization but not broadcast private browser contents to an untrusted surface. Require an explicit target (Mac versus pendant), expire handoff tokens, and redact secrets from the summary. No destructive action should be inferred merely because a conversation moved surfaces.
missing: A durable conversation-handoff object containing transcript summary, unresolved questions, planned actions, and target surface
A Mac-side endpoint/UI to claim a handoff and return progress or a result
A pendant-visible return path for the final result, beyond ordinary job completion alerts

args.user_asks: Use my already-open browser session to check this, but do not send the page or its sensitive contents through the relay; tell me only the answer and what action, if any, is needed.
args.why_useful: The browser can reach authenticated information while the relay is the always-awake voice front door, but today a browser result is effectively treated as ordinary relay context. A privacy-preserving answer capsule would let the owner use private sessions without making the relay a copy of every page.
args.model_tier: A small local browser-side extractor computes a narrowly typed answer; the realtime relay only verbalizes that answer. Use the expensive model only when the extractor cannot map the page to the requested fields.
args.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds for a simple page predicate or field extraction; fall back to an asynchronous job for a complex page.
args.cost_estimate: Low for structured extraction; occasional model cost for ambiguous pages. Bandwidth and storage fall substantially because page HTML and screenshots do not leave the Mac.
args.security_concerns: The browser extension must enforce an allowlisted output schema and never return cookies, tokens, full DOM, screenshots, or unrelated nearby fields. Display an audit record locally showing exactly which fields were released. The owner must be able to revoke the capsule.
missing: A browser-local extraction primitive that returns typed fields or predicates rather than page text
A relay contract for schema-constrained, redacted result capsules
Per-session data-retention and revocation controls for browser capsules
built_from: browser_* action types including browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_read_page, browser_list_tabs

args.user_asks: Do not interrupt me for every update; learn my interruption rules and deliver one short, ranked digest when something truly matters, based on what I am doing on the Mac and what is waiting in my browser.
args.why_useful: The wearable is uniquely able to reach the owner while away, but unsolicited speech is costly and annoying. A policy-driven interrupt arbiter would combine job completions, page watches, and Mac state into one decision instead of making each subsystem compete for the pendant.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic urgency, quiet-hours, deduplication, and active-application rules first; use a cheap background model only to rank genuinely ambiguous items. Realtime is reserved for the final spoken digest.
args.latency_budget: New alerts should be classified in under 500 ms; a digest should be available on the next button press or within 2 seconds of a high-urgency event.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for rule-based events, with occasional low-cost ranking. This avoids paying a realtime turn for every background completion.
args.security_concerns: The arbiter must never infer that a low-priority browser or work item is safe to speak aloud in public. Store policies and sensitivity labels, expose a local audit trail, and make the owner able to mute or clear the queue physically. Do not silently change an action's execution policy.
missing: A single event bus that accepts job, watch, browser, and Mac-context events
A persistent interruption-policy model with quiet hours, sensitivity, deduplication, and escalation rules
A priority-aware delivery scheduler that can target the existing pendant inbox without speaking immediately
A feedback loop recording skip, replay, and interrupt outcomes without treating silence as consent

transcript.summary: Recorded three new owner-facing capabilities: cross-surface conversation handoff, privacy-preserving browser answer capsules, and a policy-driven interruption arbiter. The first two require new connective contracts despite existing sessions/actions; the third requires an event bus, policy store, and priority delivery scheduler. The owner still needs durable handoff state, browser-local redacted extraction, and unified alert arbitration before these are possible.

transcript.text: Got it — I’ll quickly map what’s available now, then I’ll tell you what’s still missing and what I’d ask for next.
I’m going to propose a few high-impact capabilities and a concrete change, then I’ll call out the gaps that still block them.

args.user_asks: Tell me what happened to the thing you sent to my Mac, and if it finishes later, let me know on the pendant.
args.why_useful: This turns long-running Mac tasks into a hands-free experience. The owner can stop talking and still get a clear outcome without polling.
args.model_tier: realtime for the initial question; cheaper background tier for completion watching
args.latency_budget: Immediate spoken status when asked; completion notification can arrive minutes later without keeping a voice session open.
args.cost_estimate: Low per status check via relay_job_status; completion watch cost dominated by job monitoring and delivery attempts.
args.security_concerns: Status may reveal sensitive task names. Spoken notifications should be short and avoid leaking details if multiple people are nearby. The owner must be able to disable pendant delivery.
missing: A working implementation of job_completion_watch that monitors a job after the session ends
A working implementation of relay_event_push delivery to pendant/phone
A relay capability inventory endpoint so the front door can see what it can do without probing

args.user_asks: If my Mac is online, use it to do the heavy lifting, but keep the voice interaction snappy.
args.why_useful: The owner gets fast conversational control without paying realtime costs for multi-step planning, browsing, or long workflows.
args.model_tier: realtime to interpret and hand off; planner tier for multi-step execution
args.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge and hand off; variable for completion.
args.cost_estimate: Dominated by Mac planning/execution; relay cost is minimal routing and status updates.
args.security_concerns: Handing off should preserve the owner’s wording and intent; avoid expanding scope. High-impact actions should still respect existing confirmation rules.
missing: A reliable, explicit relay routing tool that resolves to real action types/enums (current relay_route_intent schema is a stub)
A stable way to report the chosen plan back to the relay for logging and user confirmation in complex cases

args.user_asks: Run a quick pendant and bridge audio self-check over USB while I’m at my Mac, and tell me what’s broken.
args.why_useful: This is the fastest path to trust: a daily-wear device needs a one-minute confidence check that audio, decoding, and the USB chain are healthy.
args.model_tier: realtime for spoken guidance; local tools or firmware for measurements
args.latency_budget: Under a minute end-to-end; results summarized in one sentence.
args.cost_estimate: Low; dominated by a short capture/playback loop and metrics collection.
args.security_concerns: Audio captured during a test could contain speech. The test should use synthetic tones/loops and avoid storing user audio.
missing: A device skill to run a self-test and report measured counters (decode/encode timing, packet loss, tx_starved)
A Mac-side tool to command the bridge and gather results over USB serial
A relay-visible status endpoint for the test results

args.change: Add a relay /capabilities endpoint (or equivalent tool inventory) that lists shipped tools, supported delivery targets, and event delivery status. Make it the source of truth for this surface, like the Mac agent’s /capabilities.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer invisible failures. If the relay advertises what it can do, the voice agent can avoid promising features that aren’t implemented and can gracefully degrade.
args.effort: Medium: define a manifest, expose it via HTTP, and wire tool resolution to it.
args.risk: The manifest could drift from implementation. Mitigate with a startup self-check that validates tool bindings and routes.
args.cost_impact: Small. One lightweight endpoint and a manifest build step.
args.latency_impact: Improves responsiveness by reducing trial-and-error probing.
args.security_impact: Expose only capability names and versions; avoid secrets or internal URLs.
depends_on: A manifest format and build process shared across surfaces

args.change: Implement job completion delivery end-to-end: job_completion_watch emits events; relay_event_push (or pipeline events) delivers to pendant/phone/dashboard; acknowledgements prevent repeats.
args.why_useful_to_owner: This is the single most useful thing for a wearable assistant: you can ask for something, walk away, and be told when it’s done.
args.effort: Medium to high: eventing, persistence, and retry semantics.
args.risk: Duplicate or lost notifications. Mitigate with idempotent event IDs and receipt tracking.
args.cost_impact: Moderate ongoing cost for watches and delivery retries.
args.latency_impact: No impact on live conversation; adds asynchronous delivery.
args.security_impact: Notifications may contain sensitive content; keep them short and allow opt-out per target.
depends_on: A delivery target registry (pendant/phone/dashboard) and a receipt store

transcript.summary: Discovered current tools, surfaces, routes, and granted items. Proposed three capabilities: async status with completion notifications, fast relay-to-Mac handoff with clear status, and a USB audio self-test. Proposed changes: a relay capability manifest and end-to-end completion delivery. The standout capability is completion delivery after the voice session ends — it makes the pendant feel like a real assistant instead of a push-to-talk remote.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Which relay-side capabilities are truly implemented (job completion watch, event push, delivery targets) and how the relay can introspect its own tool inventory without probing. A relay /capabilities manifest would remove this uncertainty.

args.user_asks: Let me start a task on the pendant, pause it, and continue the exact same conversation on my Mac (or resume it on the pendant) without repeating myself or risking the action twice.
args.why_useful: The owner is often away from the Mac. Today a voice session and a Mac job are separate worlds: moving between them loses conversational state or invites duplicate execution. Seamless migration would make the wearable, relay, and Mac feel like one reliable assistant rather than three endpoints.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short spoken handoff and intent extraction; a cheaper background model summarizes the session and reconstructs context when the surface changes. The Mac planner remains responsible for planning and execution.
args.latency_budget: A handoff acknowledgement under 500 ms; migration state available within 2 s. No model call is needed for a simple resume if the prior normalized intent and job state are already stored.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per migration; dominated by one small background summarization call only when the context exceeds the compact transcript/state record.
args.security_concerns: The relay must bind a migrated session to the authenticated device/account and never expose the transcript to an unpaired surface. Every mutating action needs a stable idempotency key, with the user-visible state distinguishing planned, started, and completed rather than claiming success from a handoff.
missing: A durable session-migration record containing compact transcript, normalized intent, current surface, and action idempotency keys
A Mac-to-relay session attach/resume endpoint and pendant resume handshake over the currently USB-testable and eventual LTE paths
Execution deduplication that treats a replayed action key as a status read, not a second mutation
A UI/audio cue that says which surface currently owns the turn

args.user_asks: Read and summarize this authenticated page for me, but automatically hide passwords, access tokens, payment numbers, and private messages before anything leaves my browser or Mac; tell me what was redacted.
args.why_useful: The wearable makes it natural to ask about whatever is open, but sending an entire authenticated page to a model can leak secrets. The owner should get the convenience of cross-surface understanding without having to manually sanitize every page, and should receive an honest redaction notice instead of silently losing context.
args.model_tier: A deterministic local redaction engine (browser extension for DOM and Mac harness for screenshots/accessibility text) runs first. Realtime only speaks the request and result; a small model may classify borderline entities after local masking, never before it.
args.latency_budget: Mask common patterns in under 150 ms; return a spoken summary in under 3 s. If classification is uncertain, omit the span and say so rather than blocking the owner with a confirmation flow.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.005 for an ordinary page; most requests use local regex/entity detectors. A small classification call dominates the rare ambiguous case.
args.security_concerns: Raw page text, screenshots, and secrets must not be uploaded for classification. Redaction should happen in the extension/Mac process, with a visible count and categories of masked spans, provenance linking the answer to the sanitized snapshot, and a kill switch for pages that disallow extraction.
missing: A shared DOM/accessibility/screenshot sanitization library implemented in both the browser extension and Mac harness
Secret detectors for credentials, financial identifiers, private-message blocks, and user-defined patterns, with replacement tokens preserving useful structure
A relay request contract that accepts only the sanitized artifact plus redaction manifest, never the raw page
A spoken result that reports redaction categories and a dashboard inspection view

args.change: Add a low-profile haptic actuator and a side rotary encoder with a detent press, while retaining the existing primary voice button. The encoder would navigate/seek through a spoken response, switch between queued choices, and adjust reply verbosity; the haptic motor would provide distinct private pulses for listening, awaiting a decision, action started, and action result. Firmware should expose a small event vocabulary and preserve operation with the current single-button hardware.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can control and understand the assistant discreetly in public, while walking or when speaking is awkward: turn to skip a result, press to select, or feel that a task failed without relying on the one LED or an audible interruption. This makes the pendant genuinely wearable rather than a phone microphone on a lanyard.
args.effort: Medium hardware spin plus firmware input/debouncing, haptic pattern tests, enclosure and power redesign; prototype over the currently USB-connected pendant before committing to a jewellery enclosure.
args.risk: Added controls can cause accidental commands and haptic patterns can be misunderstood. Require a deliberate detent press for mutations, keep the existing button semantics unchanged, provide a firmware-disable setting, and fall back to the current LED/button path if the new component fails.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $3–10 in prototype components/PCB changes and perhaps 5–20 mA peak during haptic/encoder activity; negligible ongoing model/API cost.
args.latency_impact: Local feedback under 50 ms; no network round trip for navigation or acknowledgement.
args.security_impact: No new data leaves the device. The firmware must never treat a rotation alone as authorization for a high-impact external action.
depends_on: A revised pendant PCB/enclosure with space and a power budget for the actuator and encoder
A firmware event contract consumed by the relay and alert/audio playback state machine
A haptic/gesture interaction specification tested against the existing one-button meanings

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: Watch me perform this workflow once in my browser and Mac, then let me say “run my weekly expense check” and repeat it later, adapting to changed page layouts while telling me exactly what it did and where it stopped.
args.why_useful: The owner should not need an engineer for every personal routine. Demonstration-based teaching turns the Mac and browser agents' concrete actions into a reusable personal skill, while the relay makes that skill invokable from a worn device even when the owner is away from the desk.
args.model_tier: A background model converts a recorded demonstration into a parameterized workflow; mac-planner validates and executes it, and mac-vision/browser-extension supply grounded UI state. Realtime is used only for naming the skill, collecting a missing parameter, and speaking the result.
args.latency_budget: Start acknowledgement under 500 ms; skill compilation can take 10–30 s in the background. Each replay should stream step receipts and stop within 2 s of an unverifiable state rather than guessing.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.15 to compile a new workflow, dominated by screenshot/action summarization; replays cost <$0.01 plus ordinary planner inference.
args.security_concerns: Demonstrations may contain secrets and destructive actions. Store only semantic actions and masked targets where possible, encrypt the artifact, bind it to the owner's account, and provide a dashboard diff of the planned replay. Do not silently widen a learned workflow when a page changes; report the blocked step and preserve evidence.
missing: A demonstration recorder that pairs browser DOM/accessibility snapshots and Mac UI/action events with timestamps
A versioned workflow format supporting variables, assertions, retries, and explicit stop conditions rather than brittle coordinates
A compiler/evaluator that turns the recording into a planner-readable skill and tests it in dry-run mode
A skill registry, edit/delete UI, and per-run receipts linked to the originating demonstration
A relay invocation path that resolves a spoken skill name and collects only missing parameters

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 8 of 10 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /prepare, /approve. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

The most useful is session migration: it makes one task survive the owner's movement between wearable and computer without repetition or duplicate actions.

The key unresolved implementation questions are whether the existing session/job records can be extended with durable migration and idempotency fields, where browser/Mac raw capture is intercepted before relay upload, and the exact pendant PCB/power/enclosure budget for haptics and a rotary control.

transcript.text: Okay, I’ll quickly map what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few new high-impact abilities and call out what’s still missing.

args.user_asks: Keep an ear on that task and tell me when it finishes, even if I stop talking.
args.why_useful: This is the magic trick: the owner can start something on the Mac and walk away, and the system will deliver a short completion result later without needing polling.
args.model_tier: Start on realtime for the quick confirmation, then hand off monitoring to a cheaper background tier.
args.latency_budget: Under 1 second to acknowledge; completion delivery happens whenever the job ends.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation; dominant costs are job status polling and a short notification audio render.
args.security_concerns: Notifications can leak sensitive task names. Use the relay’s already-sized spoken field verbatim and keep details minimal; require confirmation for high-impact failures that would act on data.
missing: A working completion event pipeline from relay to pendant/phone (relay_event_push or a replacement)
A job monitor that actually runs after the voice turn ends (job_completion_watch needs implementation)

args.user_asks: If I’m away from my Mac, read my status and help me decide what to do next.
args.why_useful: A quick spoken triage that doesn’t require the Mac to be awake: what’s queued, what failed, what’s waiting for attention.
args.model_tier: Realtime for conversation; no need to wake the Mac.
args.latency_budget: About 1 second for a short summary.
args.cost_estimate: Very low; reads relay-side job state only.
args.security_concerns: Job descriptions may contain sensitive filenames or app names. Summarize only what is already present in the relay’s spoken field; avoid exposing paths.
missing: A relay-side intent to summarize latest jobs without a jobId (or a tool like relay_job_status that accepts 'latest')

args.user_asks: Use the pendant as a live voice front door to my browser sessions when my Mac is online, but fall back gracefully when it’s not.
args.why_useful: The owner can say what they want, and the system routes it to a browser session when possible; when the Mac is offline, it offers a read-only web path instead of failing silently.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for intent capture; hand over to mac-planner for multi-step browser work.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds to confirm routing; the actual browsing can take longer.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; main cost is the browser automation on the Mac.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated sessions are sensitive; never read or exfiltrate secrets. Confirm before sending messages or purchases.
missing: A reliable route to discover browser session availability from the relay without probing the Mac
A server-side browser fallback (server_browser_actions) if it’s implemented

args.name: relay_task_digest
args.why: Owners need a quick spoken triage of recent tasks without recalling job IDs. Today, relay_job_status requires a reference or job id, and GET /jobs is an HTTP route not guaranteed to be available as a low-latency voice tool.
args.why_existing_tools_insufficient: relay_job_status is great for a specific job but not for a quick overview. /jobs exists but is not exposed as a voice tool and may require probing permissions. This capability would summarize recent jobs into a single spoken sentence suitable for the pendant.

scope.description: Which set of jobs to summarize.

max_items.description: Upper bound on jobs included in the summary.

args.expected_output: A short spoken string and a structured list of the jobs included, with statuses and minimal labels.

result.note: Queued for the orchestrator. If it is granted, it will be resolved against the running system when you call it — real and read-only means it runs, anything else means you get a description or a refusal with the nearest real capabilities. Carry on with what you already have and do not wait on this.

args.change: Implement a real completion notification path by wiring job_completion_watch to relay_event_push and the existing inbox/alert mechanism, so job outcomes can be delivered after the voice session ends.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can start a task and move on, and still get a clear outcome later without polling or re-asking.
args.effort: Medium. Requires implementing the watch, event delivery, and a small policy for which outcomes deserve alerts.
args.risk: Alert spam or sensitive content leakage. Mitigate with throttling, minimal spoken summaries, and honoring existing confirmation rules for high-impact actions.
args.cost_impact: Low to moderate; main cost is occasional polling and message delivery.
args.latency_impact: No impact on conversational latency; work happens after handoff.
args.security_impact: Potential disclosure of task names in spoken alerts; use verbatim pre-sized spoken fields and avoid extra detail.
depends_on: A working relay_event_push implementation or equivalent event delivery route

args.change: Add a deterministic routing table for pendant voice intents that maps to existing tools (get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, mac_delegate, web_search) without free-form intent strings, and log the chosen route for observability.
args.why_useful_to_owner: More reliable voice behavior: less misrouting, fewer confusing failures, and better explainability when something goes wrong.
args.effort: Medium. Requires defining a small enum of intents and mapping rules, plus logging.
args.risk: Overly rigid routing could block novel commands. Mitigate by falling back to mac_delegate for ambiguous cases.
args.cost_impact: Low; mostly logic and logging.
args.latency_impact: Small improvement by avoiding misroutes and retries.
args.security_impact: Logging must avoid sensitive content; store intent class and tool used, not raw utterances.

args.user_asks: “Research this for me using whatever I already have open, my Mac files, and the web; give me the answer and leave me a source-linked dossier I can ask about later.”
args.why_useful: Today each surface is queried separately and the relay cannot combine authenticated browser context, local files, and public sources into one trustworthy result. This would make the pendant a practical research front door while preserving provenance and letting follow-up questions resolve to the exact evidence.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the spoken scope and a concise answer; background mac-planner and browser workers perform the fan-out and evidence extraction; a cheaper synthesis model builds the dossier.
args.latency_budget: A spoken acknowledgement within 1 s, first answer in 10–20 s, dossier completion within 60 s. Partial evidence should be speakable while slower sources finish.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.05–$0.30 per request; browser/file extraction and synthesis dominate, not the short realtime turn.
args.security_concerns: Local files and authenticated pages leave their surfaces only to the relay and authorized workers. Every claim needs a source pointer and an explicit unavailable-source marker; never imply a source was checked when Mac or browser was offline. Require confirmation before sharing the dossier externally.
missing: A fan-out job that can invoke Mac-local file search and the authenticated browser in one task
A provenance graph linking spoken claims to URLs, file paths, timestamps, and extraction snippets
A durable dossier store and a voice follow-up resolver over its claim graph
built_from: browser_* action types exposed by the Mac manifest

args.user_asks: “Watch for a problem that only becomes important when several things line up—like a meeting moving, a related email arriving, and the project page changing—and tell me only when the combination matters.”
args.why_useful: Single-source alerts are noisy and miss the meaning created by correlation. A cross-surface sentinel would turn the always-awake relay into a quiet personal early-warning system, especially while the owner is away from the Mac.
args.model_tier: Cheap scheduled/background workers collect diffs; a small judgement model scores cross-source correlation; realtime is used only to phrase a concise alert when a threshold is crossed.
args.latency_budget: Checks every 5–15 minutes when configured, with an alert within one check interval. No conversational wait is needed.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.10 per check depending on page and mail/calendar diff volume; correlation and authenticated browser reads dominate.
args.security_concerns: The sentinel must retain only hashes, extracted fields, and minimal snippets, not whole mail or pages. User-defined scopes and expiry are required. Alert text must avoid leaking sensitive details to anyone nearby; provide a terse mode and a button-press detail mode.

Connectors for Mac Calendar/Mail/files and authenticated browser sessions feeding normalized change events

args.user_asks: “When I say ‘make this understandable’, use the thing I’m looking at or working on, produce a plain-language explanation with examples, and let me ask follow-ups against the exact paragraph or screen.”
args.why_useful: The pendant currently hears a request but has no reliable shared referent for ‘this’. Joining the current Safari tab, focused Mac document, and a spoken pointer would make vague wearable commands useful without forcing the owner to dictate URLs, filenames, or copied text.
args.model_tier: Realtime resolves the utterance and asks at most one ambiguity question; mac-vision/browser extract the focused artifact; a cheaper model creates the explanation and anchored follow-up index.
args.latency_budget: Resolve the referent in under 2 s, speak a useful first explanation in 8–12 s, and support later paragraph-level follow-ups without re-reading the whole artifact.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.15 per explanation; screenshot/OCR or page extraction and the explanation context are the main costs.
args.security_concerns: The current screen may contain secrets. The relay must receive only the selected region/page text when possible, show which artifact was used, and discard unselected screen content. Never silently act on the artifact; explanation is read-only.

A referent resolver that binds pronouns and deictic phrases to an immutable artifact version

args.change: Add a coin/LRA haptic actuator and a dedicated haptic driver to the pendant, with firmware patterns for recording, staged reply, urgent inbox alert, failed delivery, and owner acknowledgement. Keep audio and the existing single LED, but move private state signalling to haptics; expose a small event API so the relay can select urgency and the pendant can acknowledge delivery locally.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know whether a request was accepted, waiting, failed, or urgently needs attention without listening aloud or looking at the pendant—especially in meetings and public places. It also removes the current single-LED ambiguity instead of adding more competing blink patterns.
args.effort: Moderate hardware revision plus firmware event/state work; prototype with a 10–12 mm LRA, driver, enclosure isolation, and measured patterns before committing the jewellery enclosure.
args.risk: Vibration can be distracting or audible against the body, and a bad state mapping could create false urgency. Make all patterns short, provide a quiet mode, rate-limit repeats, and fall back to the LED/audio semantics if the actuator self-test fails.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$6 in components and PCB/enclosure changes, with roughly 10–30 mA only during short pulses and negligible idle draw.
args.latency_impact: Immediate local feedback, typically under 50 ms after a firmware event; no relay round trip required for local states.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy because status can be conveyed without spoken audio. Do not encode sensitive content in patterns; use only urgency/state classes.
depends_on: A pendant event vocabulary shared with the relay inbox and staged-reply state
A firmware self-test and owner-configurable quiet schedule
Physical enclosure space and a revised power budget

transcript.text:
Recorded four new proposals:

1. **Cross-surface research dossiers** — combine the owner’s open browser session, Mac files, and public web sources into a sourced answer with durable follow-up references.
2. **Cross-surface anomaly sentinel** — alert only when multiple correlated changes become meaningful, rather than producing noisy single-source notifications.
3. **Deictic “this” understanding** — resolve phrases like “explain this” against the focused Mac document, browser page, or selected screen region, with anchored follow-ups.
4. **Private haptic status channel** — add an LRA haptic actuator so the pendant can signal task acceptance, failure, urgency, and delivery privately without spoken audio or ambiguous LED patterns.

The **cross-surface research dossier** is the most useful of these: it would make the pendant a genuine front door to the entire hive rather than another isolated voice interface.
Okay, I’ll quickly inventory what’s actually available now, then I’ll propose new owner-facing capabilities and call out the gaps that still need wiring.

args.user_asks: Keep an ear on the task I just started and tell me when it’s done, even if I stop talking.
args.why_useful: This is the “single most useful” pendant behavior: the owner can start something and walk away, then get a concise completion update without babysitting a screen.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial voice interaction; a cheaper background tier should poll and summarize.
args.latency_budget: Fast acknowledgment within a second; completion notification can be delayed but should arrive within a few seconds of job completion.
args.cost_estimate: Cheap per job: one status poll loop and one short spoken summary. Dominated by polling frequency and summary generation.
args.security_concerns: Must not read or speak sensitive content beyond a short summary. Any failures that involve private data should be summarized generically unless the owner explicitly asked for details.
missing: A real completion event delivery path from relay to pendant/phone (relay_event_push is a schema only).
A durable job watch mechanism that runs after the session ends (job_completion_watch resolves to a single job read today).

args.user_asks: “Before anything consequential leaves my Mac, read back exactly who it will reach and what it contains; if the browser or app’s actual state differs from what I asked, stop and tell me the mismatch.”
args.why_useful: This turns the pendant from a command microphone into a last-mile truth check. The relay hears the owner’s intended recipient, amount, attachment, or text; the Mac planner and browser extension inspect the rendered, authenticated UI immediately before submission; the owner hears a compact comparison rather than trusting a plan that may have drifted.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay only for extracting the owner’s constraints and speaking the verdict; a cheaper background planner performs the semantic comparison, while deterministic DOM/accessibility extraction supplies facts.
args.latency_budget: 3–8 seconds for an ordinary email/form; up to 15 seconds for a complex page. No model should narrate intermediate steps.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per check, dominated by one planner/comparison call; extraction and hashing are local and cheap.
args.security_concerns: The comparison must inspect authenticated page content and may see secrets, but should send only the fields being checked to the relay and retain a redacted receipt. A mismatch must be surfaced, not silently normalized. This is an observational safety check, not an arbitrary confirmation gate.
missing: A structured intent envelope carrying recipient/content/amount constraints from voice to the Mac planner
A browser/Mac pre-submit inspection action that returns normalized fields plus source locators
A semantic diff and redacted receipt route
A single spoken mismatch response that can leave the task paused without losing its browser session

args.user_asks: “Keep this task alive while I walk away. If the Mac or browser reaches a genuinely ambiguous choice, ask me one short question on the pendant, wait for my answer, and continue from the exact checkpoint instead of starting over.”
args.why_useful: Today a long delegated task can finish or fail, but an ambiguity discovered after the voice session has no natural conversational return path. This would let the owner leave the Mac, answer a single targeted question from anywhere, and preserve the authenticated browser session and already-completed work.
args.model_tier: Background Mac planner handles the workflow; realtime relay handles only the short clarification exchange; a small durable state machine, not a model, owns checkpoint and correlation.
args.latency_budget: The initial handoff should be immediate; clarification delivery within seconds of the planner pausing. The task may remain suspended for hours without consuming model turns.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per clarification, plus negligible durable-state storage; cost is dominated by the one short realtime turn.
args.security_concerns: The question must identify the task and show only the minimum choices. Answers must be bound to a nonce/job checkpoint so a late answer cannot affect a newer task. Authenticated browser state stays on the Mac; the relay stores only the checkpoint and answer.
missing: A durable WAITING_FOR_OWNER job state with checkpoint payload and expiry
A relay-to-pendant question inbox and answer endpoint distinct from completion alerts
Planner support for pausing and resuming at a named action boundary
A dashboard view of pending questions and expired checkpoints

args.user_asks: “For the next hour, treat everything I say as private scratchpad: use it to act right now if I ask, but do not put the words, page contents, or result into memory, browser findings, transcripts used for later turns, or Mac logs.”
args.why_useful: A worn microphone is present in intimate situations where durable memory is inappropriate. A spoken privacy mode would let the owner still control the Mac and authenticated browser while sharply limiting retention across every node, rather than relying on remembering which subsystem logs what.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay recognizes the mode and enforces it deterministically; downstream agents receive a short-lived capability token and do not need an expensive model to decide retention.
args.latency_budget: Mode activation and acknowledgement under one second; enforcement adds no meaningful task latency.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per invocation; storage deletion/audit is the dominant engineering cost, not inference.
args.security_concerns: This must be fail-closed: if a downstream surface cannot honor the token, the relay must refuse to forward sensitive content and say so. Existing provider logs and OS-level telemetry need explicit redaction limits; the owner should see a dashboard receipt of what was intentionally discarded, without retaining the content itself.
missing: An ephemeral-session/retention token understood by relay, Mac planner, browser extension, and memory service
A transcript and log redaction path covering voice runs, job receipts, browser findings, and planner prompts
A pendant gesture or spoken mode switch that remains active across a delegated job
A test harness proving no private payload reaches persistent memory or browser-finding routes
