transcript.text: I’m going to quickly map what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out what’s still missing.

args.user_asks: If the thing I asked you to do finishes later, tell me when it’s done and what happened.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful “don’t make me babysit it” feature: the owner can speak a request, walk away, and still get a completion result without polling.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for acknowledging the request; cheaper background model (mac-planner/faculty-action) for monitoring and summarizing.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm the watch is set; delivery time depends on job completion.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation; the expensive part is monitoring state changes. Polling should be done sparingly and off the realtime path.
args.security_concerns: Completion summaries must not leak sensitive content. Only a short, pre-approved spoken string should be delivered. If the outcome implies sending mail or other side effects, require confirmation before executing follow-up actions.
missing: A real event delivery mechanism to pendant/phone (relay_event_push is a schema only)
A durable job watch registry and change detector on the relay
A mapping from job state to short spoken summaries

args.user_asks: While I’m talking, keep track of what I meant, and if it’s ambiguous, ask a quick clarification instead of doing the wrong thing.
args.why_useful: Prevents costly mistakes and keeps the conversation smooth. It makes the pendant feel like a smart assistant, not a command parser.
args.model_tier: Realtime for detection and clarification; mac-planner for execution after intent is clear.
args.latency_budget: Clarification question must arrive within about a second to feel natural.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate: intent parsing is cheap; the expensive part is context carry and conversation length, which should be minimized.
args.security_concerns: Do not invent details; ask before acting. If destructive actions are implied, confirm explicitly.
missing: A reliable intent-to-actions bridge without inventing a protocol (relay_route_intent is unresolved)
Better shared context projection into the live prompt to reduce token cost and ambiguity

args.user_asks: Tell me what’s going on with my devices right now: is the Mac reachable, is the pendant connected, and what can you do from here?
args.why_useful: Helps the owner understand what’s possible in the moment and avoids confusion when something seems “silent.”
args.model_tier: Realtime for status readout; no heavy planning.
args.latency_budget: Under a second for cached relay status; a few seconds if the Mac must be queried.
args.cost_estimate: Low; mostly reads. Avoid repeated polling.
args.security_concerns: Status should be high-level, not a dump of sensitive data. Don’t expose user content.
missing: Reliable pendant connectivity status endpoint on relay (prior path was 404 for /v1/devices/status)
A unified status snapshot across relay/Mac/browser to avoid redundant checks

args.user_asks: “Take care of this across my Mac and browser, and if you get stuck, ask me one focused question on the pendant; otherwise keep going.”
args.why_useful: Today a long workflow either guesses through ambiguity or ends silently. This would let the owner start a real task while away, answer only the missing decision by voice, and have the same Mac/browser job resume with its prior state intact.
args.model_tier: Use relay-realtime only for the initial utterance and the one clarification; mac-planner handles planning and state, browser-extension performs authenticated browser steps, and a cheaper background model summarizes the blocked state.
args.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1.5 s; clarification prompt when a real blocker is reached; resume within 5 s of the owner's answer.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per workflow, dominated by planner calls and any vision/browser extraction; clarification adds one short realtime turn.
args.security_concerns: A blocked job must expose exactly what decision is missing and never silently broaden scope. The owner’s answer must be bound to that job and expire with it; browser page contents and pending action details leave the Mac only through the existing relay.
missing: A durable blocked-state record with a machine-readable question and resumable plan cursor
A relay-to-pendant question event and an answer endpoint that resumes the exact job
Mac/browser adapters that can checkpoint and restore authenticated workflow state

args.user_asks: “Pause the thing you’re doing on my Mac, keep any safe progress, and switch it to this new goal.”
args.why_useful: A delegated workflow is currently a one-way handoff: the owner cannot redirect it from the wearable without starting a competing job. This would make the pendant a genuine control surface for work already in flight, preserving completed artifacts while preventing stale instructions from continuing.
args.model_tier: Relay-realtime classifies the short control utterance; a deterministic job controller pauses/cancels safely, and mac-planner replans from the checkpoint. Use the realtime model only to resolve which active job “it” means.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge pause in under 1 s and stop issuing new actions within 2 s; replan after the new goal is captured.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per redirect, mostly one planner call; pause/cancel itself should be non-model work.
args.security_concerns: Stopping must be idempotent and leave a receipt of the last action. The controller must distinguish a paused job from one that already committed an irreversible external effect, and must never replay browser clicks or shell commands after resume.
missing: A job-control state machine with pause, cancel, supersede, and checkpoint semantics
A pendant command path that targets active jobs and resolves pronouns against the owner’s active-job list
Planner support for resumable checkpoints and an explicit artifact/side-effect ledger

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 6 of 7 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /ops/history. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: “Undo the last thing you did for me.”
args.why_useful: After a voice-initiated Mac/browser workflow, the owner currently has to remember which app or site changed and repair it manually. A cross-surface undo would turn mistakes into recoverable events: identify the exact recent action, perform its inverse where possible, and say plainly what could not be reversed.
args.model_tier: Use a deterministic receipt index to identify the latest owner-requested mutation; mac-planner generates a compensating plan, while browser-extension or Mac actions execute it. Relay-realtime only speaks the result or asks which action if several are equally recent.
args.latency_budget: Identify and acknowledge the target under 1 s; reversible local changes complete within 5 s. External-service compensation may become an asynchronous job with a spoken pending notice.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.06 per undo, dominated by compensation planning and browser inspection; receipt lookup and local reversals are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Undo must never pretend that deletion, sending, or third-party effects are reversible. Each compensation needs an audit link to the original receipt, idempotency protection, and an explicit spoken distinction between fully undone, partially compensated, and impossible.
missing: A normalized inverse-operation registry for Mac and browser action types
Receipt records that include before-state or enough information to construct a compensating action
A compensation executor with idempotency and partial-failure reporting

args.user_asks: “Show me on my Mac exactly what you found when I asked from the pendant.”
args.why_useful: The owner is often away from the Mac when asking, then returns to a computer with only a spoken summary and no way to inspect the evidence. This would turn a voice result into a handoff: reopen the relevant browser pages, files, and action receipts in a labeled workspace so the owner can verify rather than trust a compressed sentence.
args.model_tier: Relay-realtime records the request; a background handoff worker gathers the job’s evidence and mac-planner arranges it. No expensive realtime reasoning is needed except a short spoken acknowledgement.
args.latency_budget: Speak acknowledgement immediately; prepare the Mac workspace within 10 s for ordinary results, or notify the pendant when a large evidence bundle is ready.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per handoff, mainly extraction and one planner call; opening already-known URLs/files is cheap.
args.security_concerns: Do not expose sensitive page contents on a shared display without an explicit owner request. Workspace links must be scoped to the originating job, avoid leaking credentials, and clearly label stale or inferred evidence versus source material.
missing: A job-scoped evidence bundle containing source URLs, screenshots/text excerpts, files, and action receipts
A Mac handoff action that creates a temporary labeled workspace without disturbing unrelated work
A relay event that tells the pendant when the visual handoff is ready

transcript.summary: Recorded three non-identical capabilities: wearable control to pause/supersede an active Mac/browser job, cross-surface undo with compensating actions and receipts, and a pendant-to-Mac visual evidence handoff. The first proposed clarification flow was rejected as already present, so I did not count or restate it. These require durable job control/checkpoints, inverse-operation and before-state receipts, and job-scoped evidence/workspace handoff respectively.

transcript.text: I’m going to quickly map what’s actually available right now, then I’ll propose a few high-value capabilities and flag what’s still missing.

args.user_asks: Tell me when that Mac task finishes, even if I’ve stopped talking.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing for long-running actions: the owner can walk away and still get a clear outcome without polling or keeping a session open.
args.model_tier: Realtime only to accept the request; cheaper background tier to watch jobs and craft a short spoken summary.
args.latency_budget: Fast to register the watch (under a second); completion delivery can be minutes to hours later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation. The expensive part is the occasional job status read; everything else should be cached and event-driven.
args.security_concerns: Avoid leaking sensitive task details in the spoken summary. Only send a short status line. Require confirmation if the summary would include sensitive content.
missing: A real implementation behind job_completion_watch that emits events to delivery targets
A reliable delivery path to pendant/phone when the relay is idle
A storage mechanism for queued notifications if the device is offline
built_from: offline_alert_inbox (existing inbox queue behavior, as referenced)

args.user_asks: Keep an eye on my microphone and audio link quality during a conversation, and warn me if I’m likely to sound bad.
args.why_useful: The owner gets immediate feedback before a whole interaction is wasted due to clipping, packet loss, or bridge issues.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the spoken feedback; measurement should be on-device and in the bridge where the audio actually flows.
args.latency_budget: Continuous low-latency monitoring with brief spoken warnings (under a second) when thresholds are exceeded.
args.cost_estimate: Very low. Mostly counters and rolling averages; only tiny summaries cross the network.
args.security_concerns: Do not transmit raw audio. Only send metrics like packet loss, underruns, and clipping rate.
missing: Expose live audio health counters from pendant and ESP32 bridge to the relay
Threshold configuration and adaptive guidance logic
A small on-device diagnostic request path to run targeted tests
built_from: offline-reality-beacon (superset health report concept, as referenced)

args.user_asks: If I say “remember this preference,” store it and use it later, but keep memory small and relevant to the task.
args.why_useful: This makes the assistant feel personal without becoming a context blob. Preferences persist and show up only when they help.
args.model_tier: Realtime to capture the preference in the moment; cheaper context projection to decide what to include later.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge and store; no added latency during normal turns.
args.cost_estimate: Low. Small preference facts with strict TTLs and token budgets.
args.security_concerns: Preferences can reveal sensitive habits; store only what’s necessary, with clear scope and optional expiration.
missing: Wire the existing memory projection into the live prompt assembly so preferences are injected correctly
A voice command grammar for preference capture and confirmation

args.user_asks: “Find my keys (or another named object) and tell me where they are.” The pendant should start a search of the rooms visible to my Mac, ask me to move the camera only when confidence is low, and speak the best location with a confidence level.
args.why_useful: This solves a physical, everyday problem that neither a voice relay nor an unattended Mac can solve alone: the pendant supplies the request while the Mac supplies eyes. It avoids making the owner search manually and is useful even when they are away from the desk.
args.model_tier: Use the low-latency relay only to normalize the object name and speak progress; use a cheaper vision model on the Mac for frame-by-frame detection, with a stronger model only to disambiguate the top candidates.
args.latency_budget: First spoken acknowledgement under 1 second; first scan result in 10–20 seconds. A scan may take up to two minutes if the owner asks for more rooms.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per search depending on frames and whether disambiguation is needed; Mac camera capture and local image processing dominate latency, not relay speech.
args.security_concerns: Camera frames stay on the Mac by default and are deleted after the search. The relay should receive only object labels, candidate regions, confidence, and optional thumbnails. Require an explicit spoken opt-in per search; never run the camera continuously.
missing: A Mac-vision camera capture/room-scan action with a bounded frame retention policy
Object detection and candidate ranking across multiple frames
A relay-to-Mac streaming search session and a way for the owner to say “next room” or “stop”
Pendant speech output for confidence and location phrased as an uncertainty, not a fact

args.user_asks: “When this happens, do the thing I just described.” For example: when a new high-priority message appears in my authenticated browser, create a Mac reminder with its due date, and tell me on the pendant; let me pause or disable the rule by voice.
args.why_useful: It turns a one-shot voice request into a dependable cross-surface assistant: the browser session observes a private page, the relay evaluates the rule, the Mac performs the local action, and the pendant reports the result. Today each piece can be used manually, but no owner-defined event-to-action chain crosses them.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap deterministic matcher for known page fields and a background model only to extract structured fields from changed content. Use the realtime model only for creating or editing the rule conversationally and for short spoken alerts.
args.latency_budget: Rule creation should feel conversational (under 5 seconds). After an observed change, alert within 30 seconds and perform the Mac action within 60 seconds; missed checks must be reported as unknown rather than silently treated as no change.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for DOM diffs and rule evaluation; about $0.005–$0.03 per ambiguous extraction. Browser polling and Mac wake/transport are the dominant operational costs.
args.security_concerns: Rules can act on authenticated private content, so store selectors and extracted values encrypted and scope each rule to one origin/session. Show the exact action and target during creation. Keep the owner's maximum-access policy, but provide voice “pause rule” and an immutable execution log. Never send page bodies to the relay when a local extractor can produce the needed fields.
missing: A durable rule object that composes browser-watch diffs into typed Mac actions
A browser-extension trigger that can wake the relay on a real change rather than only being checked manually
A relay evaluator with deduplication, retry, and explicit unknown/error states
A Mac action executor that accepts extracted fields and reports a receipt
Rule lifecycle commands: list, pause, resume, edit, and delete by voice

args.user_asks: “Stop that,” “change the target to Alice,” or “only continue through the next step.” The pendant should interrupt an in-flight Mac or browser job, show me what has already happened, and resume from a safe checkpoint without losing the original conversation.
args.why_useful: Long-running remote work is currently effectively all-or-nothing from a wearable. A spoken interruption would let the owner correct a mistaken target or halt an expensive workflow while away from the Mac, instead of waiting for completion or relying on a later cleanup.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic job state, checkpoints, and cancellation on the relay/Mac. The realtime model parses the brief interruption and speaks the current checkpoint; do not spend the expensive model on ordinary polling.
args.latency_budget: A stop must be acknowledged in under 1 second and reach the executor within 2 seconds. Resume/re-target can take 5–15 seconds to re-plan from the checkpoint.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 for a normal stop/replan; the savings come from avoiding wasted downstream actions and model calls. Storage is a small append-only checkpoint and receipt record per job.
args.security_concerns: Cancellation must be idempotent and honored before the next action boundary. Record which actions completed and which were prevented. A stopped job must never auto-resume after reconnect; resuming requires a new explicit spoken command. Checkpoint data may contain private URLs or text, so retain it briefly and redact secrets.
missing: A real cancellation/interrupt endpoint shared by relay and Mac executor
Action-boundary checkpoints with resumable planner state for /plan and /execute
A streaming job-state channel to the relay, rather than polling only after the fact
Voice reference resolution for “that job” and “the last step”
Executor semantics for compensating or clearly reporting partially completed mutations

args.user_asks: “Put what we just discussed on my Mac.” The pendant should turn the current voice answer, links, decisions, and any relevant browser findings into a small visual workspace, open it on the Mac, and keep the pendant and screen synchronized when I say “next,” “highlight that,” or “send this.”
args.why_useful: A wearable is excellent for capture but poor for inspecting lists, links, and details. This gives the owner a seamless voice-to-screen handoff instead of making them repeat the request at the keyboard, and it works across the relay, memory, browser session, and Mac.
args.model_tier: The realtime model extracts the requested handoff and a cheap background formatter builds deterministic HTML/Markdown. Use the Mac planner only for opening the workspace and browser extension only when authenticated source links need to be embedded.
args.latency_budget: Speak acknowledgement immediately; open a usable workspace within 3 seconds. Incremental additions should appear within 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01: formatting and local persistence dominate, with no model call needed when the transcript and links are already structured.
args.security_concerns: The workspace may contain private conversation and authenticated URLs. Keep it on the local Mac, use a random unguessable session URL, expire it after a short period, and never publish it to a public cloud page. Let the owner say “erase that workspace.”
missing: A relay-owned handoff artifact with transcript, links, citations, and stable item IDs
A local Mac renderer that can open and update that artifact without exposing it publicly
Bidirectional pendant-to-screen focus events for next/highlight/send
A browser adapter that can attach authenticated findings without copying full page bodies to the relay

args.user_asks: “Make me a private take-home packet from this.” The system should gather the selected voice conversation, relevant local files, and authenticated browser pages into a cited, expiring bundle on my Mac, then speak a short inventory and let me ask for one item at a time.
args.why_useful: The owner can currently ask separate agents to read or act, but cannot reliably leave a coherent, auditable artifact for later work. This turns an ephemeral wearable conversation into a useful deliverable without sending the owner's whole workspace to a third party.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic collection and hashing first; use a slower model only to summarize and label the collected material. The realtime tier should only resolve “this,” “that page,” and speak the final inventory.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge under 1 second; begin collection immediately and provide a first item within 10 seconds. Large bundles may take several minutes, with progress delivered asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: $0.02–$0.20 depending on document volume and summarization; local file enumeration and browser extraction dominate data movement, not relay speech.
args.security_concerns: Default to local-only output, include source paths/URLs and timestamps, redact credentials and cookies, and expire the bundle automatically. Never silently include unrelated files; speak the inclusion list before collection when scope is ambiguous.
missing: A scope resolver that maps spoken references to concrete files, browser tabs, and transcript spans
A local bundle writer with manifest, hashes, citations, and expiry
A browser extraction adapter that exports readable content without session secrets
A relay job that can stream item-level progress and answer inventory questions after the voice turn

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Voice-defined browser-to-Mac automation rules** — authenticated browser changes trigger Mac actions and pendant alerts, with pause/resume/edit controls.
2. **Voice-to-screen handoff** — turn a pendant conversation into a synchronized visual workspace on the Mac.
3. **Private take-home packets** — gather selected voice context, local files, and authenticated pages into a cited, expiring local bundle.

The physical-object finder was rejected as already present in the backlog, so I did not restate it.
I’ll do a quick capability sweep first, then I’ll tell you what’s still missing and propose a few high-impact additions.

args.user_asks: “If that job finishes later, tell me what happened.”
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful behavior for a pendant assistant: you can start a task hands-free and then forget it. The system should remember and notify you when it completes, without requiring you to keep talking or keep checking a screen.
args.model_tier: Realtime to acknowledge the request, cheaper background tier to monitor, then relay-side delivery to the pendant.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm it’s being watched; completion notice can arrive whenever the job state changes.
args.cost_estimate: Cheap per request: one job-monitor registration and periodic status reads; cost dominated by polling frequency and any text-to-speech rendering for the spoken summary.
args.security_concerns: Notifications can reveal sensitive task results. Keep spoken summaries short, avoid including secrets, and require confirmation before reading detailed content aloud if it may contain private data.
missing: A real, implemented async delivery path for relay_event_push (or equivalent) to pendant/phone/dashboard
A watch/monitor mechanism that doesn’t depend on the user staying in-session
A policy for summarizing job results safely for speech

args.user_asks: "Take care of this until it is actually finished; if you get stuck, ask me one precise question."
args.why_useful: Today a delegated Mac task is effectively a single job with a result. The owner cannot walk away while a multi-step browser/Mac workflow survives partial completion, records exactly what changed, and resumes after an answer. A durable saga would make the pendant a real remote operator rather than a one-shot voice remote.
args.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture the goal and speak a question; use the cheaper planner/background workers for each checkpointed step.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; individual steps may take minutes, with a spoken or dashboard update only at checkpoints or when blocked.
args.cost_estimate: About one realtime turn for intake, then roughly one planner call per checkpoint; cost is dominated by repeated computer-use screenshots and browser operations, not the relay acknowledgement.
args.security_concerns: The saga can mutate many applications and may contain private browser state. Persist only action summaries and opaque session references, encrypt checkpoint data, and require explicit owner answers for irreversible or ambiguous branches; reversible actions can follow the owner's existing maximum-access policy.
missing: A durable saga/state-machine record distinct from the existing one-shot job
Planner checkpoint and compensation/resume protocol across mac-planner, mac-vision, and browser-extension
A relay question inbox that can pause a saga and deliver one targeted question through the pendant
Dashboard visualization of checkpoint, pending question, and exact receipts

args.user_asks: "Save the form I'm working on so I can finish it later, even if I leave my Mac."
args.why_useful: A half-completed authenticated form is currently trapped in a live browser tab. The owner cannot safely turn it into a resumable handoff from the pendant. This would preserve the exact page, entered-but-not-submitted fields, validation state, and next action, then restore it later without submitting anything accidentally.
args.model_tier: Use a small background model to summarize and redact field metadata; use realtime only for the owner's short save/resume command.
args.latency_budget: Save acknowledgement within 3 seconds; restore within 10 seconds when the Mac and browser are online.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation: one short relay turn plus browser DOM inspection/serialization; storage and browser session retention dominate rather than model tokens.
args.security_concerns: Form fields may include passwords, payment details, health data, or CSRF/session tokens. Never persist secrets or raw values by default; classify fields locally, encrypt an owner-approved draft, expire it, and require a fresh spoken confirmation immediately before any submit. The browser extension must visibly mark a restored draft as unsent.
missing: A browser-extension draft protocol that captures DOM/field identity and validation state without leaking secrets
Encrypted, expiring draft storage on the relay with per-draft owner association
A restore operation that re-finds the page and reports mismatches instead of blindly typing
A pendant inbox/resume command path and dashboard list of saved drafts

args.user_asks: "If I say the emergency phrase, get me help and keep trying until a real person acknowledges it."
args.why_useful: The worn pendant is the one surface available when the owner is away from the Mac, but today it cannot escalate beyond a relay conversation. A deliberate emergency phrase plus a physical confirmation could fan out through the relay, phone, and Mac, retrying delivery and telling the owner whether a human acknowledged it.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic phrase/button recognition and a durable background escalation worker; no expensive realtime reasoning should sit in the critical path.
args.latency_budget: Local confirmation immediately, first delivery attempt under 5 seconds, retries and acknowledgement tracking for hours.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost; telephony/SMS/push provider fees and an always-on durable worker dominate.
args.security_concerns: False positives and abuse are serious. Require a configured phrase plus deliberate button pattern, local audible/LED confirmation with a cancel window, encrypted emergency contacts and location, strict audit logs, and never expose contacts or location in normal transcripts.
missing: A configured emergency-contact and location consent store
iOS push/SMS/voice-call integration and delivery receipts
Durable escalation timers/retries and human-acknowledgement protocol
Firmware emergency gesture that survives a dropped LTE/Mac link and an operator dashboard

args.user_asks: "Don't interrupt me while I'm presenting or recording; if something urgent arrives, tell me at the first safe moment."
args.why_useful: The owner currently has no shared notion of attention across the worn pendant, Mac audio/apps, browser, and relay. Notifications can arrive while they are presenting, recording in Ableton, or speaking with someone, and the pendant cannot defer or prioritize them based on real activity. This would make the system helpful without becoming an interruption source.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic state collection and a cheap classifier for urgency; reserve realtime for the one-sentence alert when the safe window opens.
args.latency_budget: State refresh within 2 seconds; urgent events evaluated in under 5 seconds; deferred alerts delivered at the first detected safe window.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost if activity signals are structured; most work is event ingestion and a small durable deferred-notification queue.
args.security_concerns: Activity state reveals meetings, applications, and possibly document titles. Keep raw titles on the Mac, send only coarse states (presenting, recording, focused, idle), make urgency rules owner-editable, and provide an unmistakable cancel/snooze gesture.
missing: A Mac activity/privacy adapter for microphone, camera/presentation, Ableton recording, calls, and focused-app state
A shared relay attention-state and deferred-alert queue with coalescing and expiry
Browser and Mac event subscriptions rather than periodic polling alone
Firmware behavior for quiet/deferred/unread urgency using the existing inbox and LED semantics

A browser draft/resume idea was rejected as a duplicate of an existing backlog item, so I did not rephrase it. I do not need another tool this round; these proposals explicitly identify the missing durable orchestration, escalation integrations, activity adapters, and cross-surface event queues.

args.user_asks: Keep an ear on the task I just started and let me know when it’s done, even if I stop talking.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful everyday flow: the owner can start something from the pendant and then go back to life without babysitting a job list. Completion shows up as a short spoken update.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the initial handoff; cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarizing
args.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge the watch; completion can arrive minutes later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job: one watch registration plus periodic job status reads; the summary is tiny.
args.security_concerns: The spoken summary must not reveal sensitive content unless the original task context permits it. Delivery should respect device availability and user preferences.
missing: A real asynchronous event delivery path from relay to pendant/phone
An implemented completion-event emitter (relay_event_push is schema-only today)
A durable watch registry on the relay or a shared store

args.user_asks: If my Mac is asleep or I’m away, tell me what’s going on with my system and whether a task can run right now.
args.why_useful: Prevents frustrating failures: the owner can decide to wake the Mac, plug in, or try a different approach before issuing commands.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the quick spoken check; no background job needed.
args.latency_budget: A brief spoken answer within a second when possible; longer if a status probe is required.
args.cost_estimate: Very low: a small status read and a short spoken response.
args.security_concerns: Exposes device state (online/offline, battery, network). Keep it minimal and avoid sharing details beyond what the owner asked for.
missing: A reliable relay-visible device status endpoint for pendant and bridge, beyond Mac agent context
Clear mapping from relay job status to ‘can run now’ readiness

args.user_asks: Summarize what I was working on across my Mac and browser, and read the next important thing out loud.
args.why_useful: It turns the pendant into a quick daily navigator: what matters next, without a screen. This is only possible by combining browser session context, Mac project state, and the relay’s voice delivery.
args.model_tier: Cheaper planner for aggregation; realtime for the spoken summary.
args.latency_budget: A couple seconds for aggregation; then a short spoken summary.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate: reading several sources and generating a short summary; reuse cached context when possible.
args.security_concerns: Summaries may include sensitive content from mail, files, or pages. Use permissions and confirm before speaking anything potentially sensitive.
missing: A unified cross-surface context projection wired into the live prompt path
Clear permissions for reading browser and Mac sources in one request
Policy for what can be spoken aloud in shared spaces

args.change: Publish a relay capability manifest and self-describing routes (GET /capabilities for the relay surface), mirroring what the Mac agent already exposes, so relay-realtime can inventory its own surface instead of guessing or probing.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer failures and faster iteration: the voice agent can confidently route and explain what it can do, which makes the pendant feel reliable.
args.effort: Medium: add a route, build a manifest from the relay router, and keep it in sync with changes.
args.risk: Low. Main risk is exposing sensitive internal routes; mitigate by publishing only safe, high-level capability descriptions.
args.cost_impact: Low ongoing cost; small response payload.
args.latency_impact: None at runtime except when queried.
args.security_impact: Must avoid leaking internal admin/debug endpoints.

result.why: This restates something the system already has, so it was not recorded.

args.change: Wire the existing memory projection into live conversation context for all surfaces, so each turn receives a scoped, cached head of preferences/permissions plus only task-relevant facts instead of resending large blocks.
args.why_useful_to_owner: More accurate, less repetitive assistance and lower token cost, which means faster responses and more capability headroom.
args.effort: Medium: change the conversationContext build path to call projectContext and adjust tests.

args.change: Add a rule that the relay acknowledges commands, then hands long-running planning/aggregation to a cheaper model tier by default, retaining only the minimal state needed to answer quick spoken follow-ups.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Keeps the pendant responsive and reduces cost, without losing the thread of what was asked.
args.effort: Medium: routing logic and state handoff; requires a minimal shared job reference.
args.risk: Low to medium: follow-up questions could lose context; mitigate by storing job IDs and using status tools.

args.latency_impact: Improves conversational responsiveness.

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: When I say “save this moment,” capture exactly what I’m doing on the Mac and in the browser so I can say “restore the moment from this morning” later.
args.why_useful: The owner can leave a task without losing the precise working state: focused app, windows, tabs, document/selection where available, and the spoken label are preserved as one recoverable checkpoint. This is more useful than a bookmark because it reconnects the worn device, the acting Mac, and authenticated browser state.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for recognizing the short save/restore command; mac-planner and browser-extension do the capture/restore work asynchronously, with mac-vision inspecting UI when structured state is unavailable.
args.latency_budget: A save acknowledgement under 2 seconds; capture may take 5-15 seconds. Restore should speak a preview under 3 seconds and complete after explicit spoken selection if multiple checkpoints match.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01-$0.05 per save/restore depending on whether UI vision is needed; most structured Mac/browser captures should avoid the expensive vision tier.
args.security_concerns: Checkpoint metadata may include private tab titles, document names, and authenticated URLs. Store encrypted, scope browser contents to the owner, never read page bodies unless requested, and require confirmation before restoring a state that would type, submit, or alter data.
missing: A durable checkpoint schema and encrypted store joining Mac window state, browser tab/session identifiers, focused location, label, and timestamp
Mac actions to enumerate and restore windows/documents/selection rather than only opening apps/URLs
Browser extension support for serializing and restoring tab groups and session-bound page locations
A relay voice command resolver and checkpoint search/preview endpoint

args.user_asks: If a task gets stuck while I’m away, ask me one clear question on the pendant, wait for my answer, and continue exactly where you stopped.
args.why_useful: Today an unattended Mac task either guesses, fails, or waits for a live conversation. This makes long computer/browser work genuinely usable while the owner is walking around: the relay turns ambiguity into a durable, answerable interruption rather than losing the task context.
args.model_tier: Use the cheaper planner/worker for execution and question generation; use realtime only to recognize the owner’s short answer and bind it to the waiting job.
args.latency_budget: Question generation within 10 seconds of a blocked step; pendant delivery within seconds when connected and retained until answered. Resume within 5 seconds after the answer reaches the Mac.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02-$0.10 per blocked task, dominated by the planner context needed to summarize the ambiguity; no model call is needed while simply waiting.
args.security_concerns: The question must expose only the minimum relevant choices, not page secrets or unrelated tabs. Bind answers to an opaque job/question nonce, expire stale questions, and never interpret an answer for a different job. The owner’s existing maximum-access policy still applies to execution.
missing: A first-class WAITING_FOR_OWNER job state with a durable question record, allowed answer forms, expiry, and resume cursor
A relay-to-pendant interactive question delivery path and an answer upload path (the current inbox can surface alerts but cannot correlate a reply to a paused plan)
Mac planner support for checkpointing tool state and resuming from a validated answer
A conflict policy for answers arriving after the Mac has already timed out or changed state

args.user_asks: Before you upload or send something for me, tell me out loud what private details it contains and let me say “remove the phone number” or “send it” without opening the Mac.
args.why_useful: The owner gets a practical privacy checkpoint at the only moment that matters: immediately before data leaves a local file or authenticated browser. It combines Mac file access, browser session reach, relay reasoning, and the pendant’s hands-free approval; today those surfaces can act, but cannot produce a compact spoken disclosure-and-redaction loop.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper extraction/classification model for local candidate detection and a realtime turn only for the short spoken disclosure and owner’s redaction commands. Use the planner/browser tiers to apply edits and upload.
args.latency_budget: Initial disclosure in 3-8 seconds for a normal document; each redaction command acknowledged in under 2 seconds. Never submit until the owner’s explicit send instruction is bound to the exact content hash.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.02-$0.15 per document, mostly OCR/structured extraction and any vision needed for PDFs or screenshots; text-only files are cheaper.
args.security_concerns: The disclosure engine itself sees sensitive content, so processing should stay on the Mac whenever possible and send only entity labels/counts to the relay. Keep a content hash and immutable pre-send preview, redact locally, and prevent a stale spoken approval from authorizing changed content or a different recipient.
missing: A Mac-local sensitive-entity extractor covering text, PDFs, images, and clipboard data
A relay protocol for a spoken disclosure card with content hash, recipient, destination, and field-level redaction commands
Browser and Mac actions that transform a staged copy, recalculate its hash, and submit only the approved version
A durable pending-send record so a dropped pendant link cannot silently turn approval into submission

All three require new connective protocols rather than assuming current tools already provide them.

It needs a WAITING_FOR_OWNER job state, durable question/answer correlation, pendant delivery and answer upload, and planner resume cursors. Also recorded exact cross-surface work-state checkpoints, and a spoken pre-send privacy disclosure/redaction loop that hashes the approved content before submission. All three require new connective protocols rather than assuming current tools already provide them.

args.why_useful: Today the pendant can hand off a goal or a short action list, but it cannot turn the owner's private, already-authenticated page context into a durable, resumable job. This would make the worn device a real front door to work that spans browser sessions and Mac applications rather than merely a remote button.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for intent capture and one-sentence clarification; gpt-5.6-luna mac-planner for planning and recovery; gpt-4.1-mini computer-use only when visual interaction is unavoidable; cheap background model for extracting page state and checking whether a paused job can safely resume.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second, first page/task interpretation in 3-5 seconds, then background execution with spoken interruption available.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02-$0.10 for a normal task; planner calls and screenshots dominate, while relay speech should remain one short turn.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents and any resulting local data leave the Mac only through the relay's task context. The system must bind the job to the captured tab/session, redact secrets from receipts, re-check page identity after reconnect, and never silently continue after a material page or target change. Reversible actions may proceed under owner policy; irreversible external sends or purchases still need an explicit spoken checkpoint.
missing: A durable cross-surface job state machine with checkpointed browser identity, planner state, and reconnect recovery
A relay endpoint that can capture the current Safari tab and attach it to POST /plan rather than requiring a manually authored action list
Mac-side lease/heartbeat and safe resume semantics for jobs when the Mac or browser goes offline
A compact pendant interaction for answering an ambiguity and cancelling or resuming a paused job

args.user_asks: “Privacy curtain.” The pendant should immediately stop using browser-page context, cancel or suspend active computer-use jobs, clear transient spoken-task context from the relay, and tell me when the curtain is active; saying “resume” or a deliberate button gesture should restore normal operation.
args.why_useful: The owner wears the microphone away from the screen and may enter a sensitive conversation without being able to reach the Mac. There is currently no single, obvious physical or spoken action that makes the whole hive stop looking at private pages or continuing a job. This is a user-visible privacy control, not a tidying refactor.
args.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for activation: firmware event plus deterministic relay state. Use the realtime tier only to acknowledge; downstream agents consume a signed privacy-state event and stop immediately.
args.latency_budget: The pendant LED/acknowledgement in under 250 ms and downstream cancellation in under 1 second.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per invocation; this is mostly firmware and relay state propagation, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The curtain must be fail-closed on relay uncertainty, survive a dropped Mac link, and be visible in the dashboard. It should revoke browser inspection and job continuation leases, prevent new memory projection of browser findings, and avoid claiming that already-uploaded data was erased. Resume must require a deliberate physical gesture or an unambiguous spoken command after the owner knows the state.
missing: A relay-wide privacy epoch/token checked by browser and Mac agents before every read or action
Cancellation and lease revocation semantics in the job executor, including a truthful stopped-versus-unreachable receipt
A firmware gesture/state for curtain active that does not conflict with recording and inbox playback
A browser-extension hook that blocks page capture and clears its transient command context

args.user_asks: “Use the other account,” or “No, put it in Downloads instead.” While a Mac/browser job is running, the pendant should let me correct one parameter by voice, identify which active job I mean, validate the change against the current step, and continue without restarting the whole task.
args.why_useful: Long computer tasks fail today at the first wrong assumption: the owner must wait, cancel, and explain the entire goal again. A wearable is uniquely suited to low-latency steering while the owner is away from the Mac. This is not a completion notification; it changes an in-flight plan safely and preserves its progress.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay resolves the utterance to the active job and extracts a small patch; gpt-5.6-luna evaluates the patch against the planner state and replans only the remaining steps. Use a cheap classifier for whether the utterance is a steering correction, a new task, or a cancellation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the correction in under 1 second, show the affected step in under 3 seconds, and resume within 5 seconds when the patch is unambiguous.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01-$0.05 per correction, dominated by a targeted planner re-evaluation rather than a full task restart.
args.security_concerns: Never apply an ambiguous correction to the wrong job. The relay should speak back the selected job and changed target when needed, preserve an immutable before/after plan diff, and stop at an external-send boundary if the correction materially changes who receives data. The owner policy permits reversible actions without an extra gate, but the system must truthfully report if the job was already past the affected step.
missing: An active-job registry exposed to the realtime relay with owner-facing short names and current step
A versioned planner state plus patch/replan API; current plan/execute is effectively one-shot from this surface
A pendant protocol for a correction response and a compact disambiguation prompt
Receipts that distinguish applied, superseded, too-late, and rejected steering patches

args.cost_impact: Low runtime per message; storage cost scales with undelivered notifications. Development cost is the bigger piece.

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Private screen coach** — the Mac watches a selected app, detects actionable changes, and whispers concise alerts through the pendant.
2. **Ephemeral cross-source evidence brief** — combines local files and authenticated browser pages into a provenance-preserving, 24-hour evidence bundle for spoken follow-ups.
3. **Learn-by-demonstration workflows** — observes a workflow once, turns it into a parameterized command, and later replays it with postcondition verification.

The main missing pieces are a functioning Mac vision/observation loop, relay-side event throttling and delivery, ephemeral evidence storage with hard deletion, and versioned workflow recording/replay with secret exclusion. I also told mac-planner about the established handoff routes: `/workbench/jobs/:jobId/handoff`, `/journal/:jobId`, and job receipts.
I’ll do a quick capability sweep and then sketch what’s still missing for truly useful everyday behavior.

args.user_asks: “When I’m at my Mac, carry out this change; if I walk away before it is committed, stop and leave me a clear draft instead.”
args.why_useful: The pendant can become a physical-presence key for unattended-computer actions: the owner gets powerful automation without a task continuing after they leave the desk. This is materially different from a confirmation prompt because presence is continuously re-checked during a multi-step job, not guessed from the original voice turn.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the short spoken command and state changes; mac-planner performs the workflow; a cheap background verifier watches presence and job receipts. No expensive model is needed for the repeated heartbeat checks.
args.latency_budget: Under 300 ms to acknowledge presence and under 2 s to pause a running job after loss; initial planning may take 3–10 s.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly one realtime turn plus one planner invocation per job; verifier polling should be Worker-side and near-zero model cost.
args.security_concerns: A USB-connected pendant is evidence of proximity, not identity by itself; bind the session to an authenticated device key and fail closed on disconnect, stale heartbeat, or serial ambiguity. Do not delete or send anything merely because presence changed; pause, preserve the draft, and report exactly what was and was not committed.
missing: A signed pendant-presence lease with monotonic heartbeat and disconnect semantics
Planner/execute checkpoints that can pause between actions and emit a durable partial receipt
A relay policy that maps presence loss to pause rather than cancellation

args.user_asks: “While I’m working, notice when two apps or tabs contain conflicting versions of the same thing, tell me the conflict in one sentence, and let me choose which source wins.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner can ask the Mac or browser to read and edit, but has to know where inconsistency is hiding. A cross-surface reconciliation agent would compare local files, authenticated browser pages, and recent action receipts, then present a small decision on the pendant instead of silently overwriting one source.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for extraction and pairwise comparison; use realtime only to summarize the detected conflict and collect the owner’s winner choice. Mac-planner/browser actions then apply the selected patch.
args.latency_budget: Detection can take 30–120 s after a relevant job or on demand; the spoken conflict summary should arrive within 2 s once detected.
args.cost_estimate: One low-cost comparison per changed-source pair; realtime cost only when a conflict is surfaced or the owner asks for detail.
args.security_concerns: Read only by default. Preserve source snapshots and a field-level diff, never claim consistency if one source could not be read, and require an explicit spoken choice before overwriting either source. Authenticated page contents and private files leave their surfaces only as encrypted, scoped comparison inputs.
missing: A cross-surface content identity and canonicalization layer
A durable conflict record with source snapshots, field-level diff, and chosen winner
Browser and Mac adapters that return provenance rather than plain text
An inbox delivery path that carries a decision request, not merely a completion alert

args.user_asks: “Before I leave, ask me only about unfinished things that are blocked by my decision, and let me resolve each one by voice without reopening the Mac.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently receives task completion/status information, but no compact, decision-focused end-of-session sweep. This would turn abandoned Mac/browser work into a bounded voice queue: the relay identifies jobs that cannot proceed, the pendant asks one high-value question at a time, and the selected answer is handed back to the exact waiting workflow.
args.model_tier: A background classifier ranks blocked jobs and extracts the smallest missing decision; realtime handles the short interactive sweep; the planner resumes the original job after the answer.
args.latency_budget: Generate the queue in under 5 s; each question should be spoken within 1 s of the owner asking for the sweep. Resumption can be asynchronous.
args.cost_estimate: One cheap ranking pass per sweep and one realtime turn for the dialogue; reuse stored job receipts to avoid re-reading the Mac.
args.security_concerns: Only jobs owned by the current session/device may enter the queue. Show the originating app/site and proposed consequence before applying a choice. Never infer a choice from silence, and preserve the unanswered queue when the pendant disconnects.
missing: A first-class blocked/awaiting-owner state in job receipts
A durable decision-token linking one spoken answer to one exact pending action
A compact owner-facing queue distinct from generic completion notifications
Resume support in the Mac planner after a decision arrives

transcript.summary: Recorded three new owner-facing capabilities: (1) presence-bound execution that pauses when the worn pendant leaves the Mac, (2) cross-app/browser conflict detection with provenance and a spoken winner choice, and (3) a voice-resolvable queue of unfinished jobs blocked on the owner’s decision. The system still needs signed presence leases and checkpoint pause semantics; provenance-rich cross-surface comparison and durable conflict records; and first-class blocked-job decision tokens with resume support. Existing routes can carry much of the plumbing, but they do not provide those missing semantics.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the live Mac planner and browser adapters already expose enough per-action checkpoints and source provenance to implement these safely, or whether both need new contracts.

args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, cheaper, more consistent conversations. The pendant can remember relevant preferences and tasks without paying to resend bulky context every turn, which makes the assistant feel snappier and more reliable.

args.user_asks: "Handle this task all the way through, and only wake me if you hit a genuinely missing decision." The relay should let me delegate an ambiguous multi-step goal, have the Mac planner and browser work it, detect when a needed choice is truly unavoidable, ask one sharply scoped question on the pendant, then continue and report the result with evidence.
args.why_useful: Today delegation either ends at a plan or leaves the owner polling and re-explaining context. This would make the pendant a reliable front door for real work: the owner can walk away, answer only the one decision no agent can infer, and receive a truthful outcome rather than a vague 'done'.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial request and the one clarification; background orchestration and evidence summarization use a cheaper model.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; background steps may take minutes. Clarification delivery must survive an offline pendant and resume automatically after the answer.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02-$0.15 per task depending on planner/browser turns; realtime cost is dominated by clarification and final spoken summary, not idle watching.
args.security_concerns: The system must distinguish an unavailable fact from a preference it already knows, avoid asking for secrets aloud when a browser session can supply them, and include action receipts/evidence. Owner policy permits execution, but destructive or irreversible outcomes still need an explicit decision when the task itself is ambiguous.
missing: A durable state machine for paused-on-question jobs with a typed clarification payload and answer correlation
Relay-to-pendant delivery of a clarification request, not just a completion alert
Planner/browser checkpoints that record what was tried and why it cannot proceed
A resume endpoint that feeds the answer back into the exact paused job

args.user_asks: "Why are you saying that?" Give me a spoken, source-grounded explanation of any answer or action: which remembered preference, browser page, Mac state, and agent observation contributed, what was inferred, and what remains uncertain.
args.why_useful: A wearable assistant acts while the owner cannot see its screen. Without provenance, a wrong answer or surprising action is impossible to audit from the pendant. This would make the hive trustworthy: one short spoken explanation on demand, with a dashboard view for the full chain and direct links to the underlying evidence.
args.model_tier: Realtime generates the short spoken explanation from a prebuilt trace; a cheaper background model can compress long traces and cluster recurring uncertainty.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for the spoken summary when the trace already exists; full trace inspection may load in under 5 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005-$0.03 per explanation. Storage and indexing of structured receipts dominate; model cost is small if raw pages and action results are not resent wholesale.
args.security_concerns: Never speak secrets, tokens, private page contents, or full sensitive memory values by default. Store provenance with sensitivity labels and expose redacted source titles/fields first; require a deliberate request for sensitive detail. The trace must distinguish observed facts from model inferences and never manufacture citations.
missing: A shared append-only provenance graph spanning relay turns, memory facts, Mac actions, browser commands, and their outputs
Stable evidence IDs and sensitivity/redaction metadata on every action receipt
A spoken 'explain this' resolver that can bind 'that' to the last answer/action
Dashboard and browser deep links to the relevant evidence

args.user_asks: "Move this conversation to my Mac, keep the context, and show me the result there." Seamlessly hand a live pendant conversation to the Mac or authenticated browser when a visual surface is better, then let me return to the pendant without repeating myself.
args.why_useful: Speech is ideal while walking, but many tasks need a page, code, image, or a long result. Today the owner must choose a surface, repeat the request, and hope context survived. A true handoff would make the wearable and screens feel like one assistant rather than disconnected agents.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the handoff utterance and continuity summary; the target surface uses its normal planner/vision model, with a cheaper model maintaining the compact shared state.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the handoff in under 1 second and expose the target session in under 5 seconds. Returning to voice should resume in one turn without replaying the whole transcript.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01-$0.08 per handoff, dominated by one compact context summary and any target-surface model call. Persistent session metadata is inexpensive.
args.security_concerns: Only paired, currently authorized surfaces may receive a handoff. Redact sensitive voice context from dashboards and unrelated browser tabs; expire handoff tokens and make the target display visibly identify the active owner session. Never assume a nearby Mac is the owner's intended target if pairing is stale.

Bidirectional session event transport rather than one-way job completion
Context compaction that preserves referents, pending decisions, and tool state without replaying sensitive audio
A pendant gesture/utterance to choose or cancel the target and a target-surface resume affordance

args.user_asks: Follow that task and tell me when it’s done, even if I stop talking.
args.why_useful: This is the daily-driver feature: the owner can issue a command and go about their day, then get a completion alert without having to poll.
args.model_tier: Low-latency relay for the conversation; cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarizing
args.latency_budget: Start the watch immediately while the owner is present; completion delivery can be delayed until the job finishes.
args.cost_estimate: Small per-call cost to register a watch; the dominant cost is polling job status and generating a short spoken summary.
args.security_concerns: Only status and a short summary should leave the Mac; do not include sensitive content unless the user asked for detail. Confirm before delivering to shared devices.
missing: A real implementation behind job_completion_watch that can emit events and deliver to pendant/phone
A relay event delivery path that can queue and retry while devices are offline

args.user_asks: What’s going on with my Mac and browser right now?
args.why_useful: Quick situational awareness helps the owner avoid interrupting work in progress and makes voice commands safer.
args.model_tier: Low-latency for the spoken response; Mac/browser provide the state
args.latency_budget: Fast status snapshot under a second when available; fall back to last known state if offline.
args.cost_estimate: One status request plus a small spoken reply; cheap compared to planning and execution.
args.security_concerns: Status can reveal sensitive apps or pages; keep summaries generic unless the owner asks for specifics.
missing: A consolidated status snapshot endpoint that includes mac + browser + relay health in one response to reduce chatter

args.user_asks: Use the best place to do this: if it’s simple, do it now; if it’s complex, hand it to my Mac and keep me posted.
args.why_useful: The owner shouldn’t have to think about routing. This reduces friction and errors, especially while moving.
args.model_tier: Relay for intent capture; judgement/action tiers for routing; Mac/browser for execution
args.latency_budget: Fast initial acknowledgement; background planning for complex tasks.
args.cost_estimate: Cheap for simple reversible actions; higher for multi-step workflows and browser automation.
args.security_concerns: Complex workflows may touch mail or files; require confirmation for destructive actions and keep receipts.
missing: A reliable routing primitive (or plan endpoint) visible to the relay so it doesn’t invent a protocol
Better receipts/telemetry for routed actions to support spoken summaries

args.user_asks: When I say “take care of this” while wearing the pendant, have the system inspect the relevant authenticated browser page and my Mac, complete the whole task across both, and tell me exactly what changed—even if the Mac or browser drops offline halfway through.
args.why_useful: Today the owner must know which surface to address and manually recover interrupted work. This would make the pendant a genuinely reliable front door for real tasks spanning a Safari session and local applications, with truthful recovery rather than a confident but incomplete spoken answer.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for intent capture and one short clarification; gpt-5.6-luna mac-planner for decomposition; browser session agent for authenticated page work; background worker for retry/reconciliation; cheap summarizer for the final receipt.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second, begin work immediately, and deliver a short completion or failure event asynchronously. Multi-step work may take minutes.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.20 per task depending on browser screenshots and planner turns; most waiting time is tool execution, not realtime inference.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents and local files cross the relay boundary unless the browser agent can return redacted structured results. Secrets must stay in the browser session; spoken output must never quote tokens or private page text. Changes need an immutable before/after receipt and a clear partial-completion state.
missing: A durable cross-surface transaction/coordinator that records each step, retries only idempotent steps, and resumes after Mac/browser reconnect
A real browser-side authenticated execution worker that can participate in the existing job protocol
A receipt schema joining browser and Mac effects with redaction and causal ordering
Relay-side delivery of that receipt to the pendant after the voice turn

args.user_asks: Before you act, tell me when the world has changed underneath my request: “The page is no longer the same,” “that file was edited,” or “the amount changed.” Then show me the exact old and new value and continue only with the part that is still valid.
args.why_useful: A wearable assistant acting across a live browser and Mac can otherwise apply a stale plan to a changed page or document. The owner gets a trustworthy warning at the point of divergence, not a vague failure after a wrong click or overwritten value.
args.model_tier: Cheap structured diffing first; gpt-5.6-luna only to explain an ambiguous semantic conflict; realtime relay speaks the single urgent warning.
args.latency_budget: Detect divergence before every mutating step, adding under 500 ms for structured state and under 2 seconds for a screenshot/OCR comparison.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.05 per guarded step; the dominant cost is an occasional screenshot/vision comparison, not speech.
args.security_concerns: Diffs may expose private page or document contents. Keep raw snapshots local to the Mac/browser where possible, send only redacted changed fields, and expire evidence after the job. This is an advisory conflict detector, not a confirmation gate, matching the owner's maximum-access policy.
missing: A precondition/evidence field on every planned action
Browser DOM snapshots and Mac accessibility/screen snapshots normalized into comparable state
A semantic diff service that distinguishes harmless layout churn from value or identity changes
A partial-plan replanner that can continue safe steps after a conflict

args.user_asks: Make my pendant remember the conversation correctly: after I say “use the same editor,” “send it to him,” or “the one from yesterday,” resolve that reference from the relevant Mac, browser, and recent voice context without replaying my entire history or leaking unrelated facts.
args.why_useful: The owner can speak naturally instead of restating filenames, people, and prior decisions. This is especially valuable while away from the Mac, where the relay must resolve a short follow-up against the right task and surface rather than guess from a giant transcript.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for reference resolution; the existing projection and a cheap entity linker do retrieval; gpt-5.6-luna is invoked only when two candidates remain ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Resolve ordinary references in under 300 ms from the stable projection; ask one concise clarification within 1 second when confidence is low.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per turn because the projection is small; ambiguity may add one planner call.
args.security_concerns: Only surface-scoped facts should be injected. Browser-derived facts must remain task-matched, sensitive values must stay redacted, and unresolved ambiguity must be spoken rather than silently choosing the wrong person or file.
missing: Wire projectContext(surface, task) into conversationContext.js so the live voice prompt uses the measured projection instead of legacy memory blocks
Persist short-lived conversation entities and pronoun links with expiry and confidence
Return provenance for each resolved reference so the relay can explain “I mean the Outlook draft from yesterday” without exposing unrelated memory

args.user_asks: While my Mac is asleep or offline, let me say “check my logged-in dashboard,” “download the invoice,” or “tell me if anything changed,” and have the relay use my already-authenticated browser session safely, then speak the result on the pendant when I am walking.
args.why_useful: The browser holds sessions the relay cannot currently reach unless the owner's Mac is online. This is the clearest everyday gap between a wearable and an ordinary voice assistant: the owner should not have to wake a laptop to read a page they are already signed into.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for the utterance; a low-cost browser worker for navigation/extraction; gpt-5.6-luna only for page interpretation or a multi-step task; background execution for long downloads.
args.latency_budget: Speak an acknowledgement in under 1 second, return a simple reading in under 10 seconds, and queue longer work with an asynchronous pendant alert.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.10 per request, dominated by browser rendering and OCR for visually complex pages; text-only extraction should be cheap.
args.security_concerns: This requires moving capability, not passwords: store session cookies in an encrypted, owner-scoped browser vault and never send them to the model. Require explicit device pairing and revocation, isolate each site, redact page data in logs, and make downloads/results expire. High-impact actions such as sending, purchasing, or deleting remain visibly reported as such.
missing: A Cloudflare Browser Rendering or equivalent worker with persistent encrypted per-owner sessions
A pairing/import flow from the existing Safari extension that transfers an authenticated session without exposing cookies to the relay model
Browser action execution and extraction routes that work with the Mac absent, plus download storage and expiry
A durable relay-to-pendant inbox path for spoken results and failures

The third is the highest-value missing capability: it needs a paired encrypted browser-session worker, safe browser execution/extraction, and durable pendant delivery.
