transcript.text: I’m going to quickly map what’s actually available now, then I’ll highlight what’s still missing and propose a few high-impact next steps.

args.user_asks: Watch that job and tell me when it finishes, even if I’m not talking to you anymore.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing: the owner can hand off a task, walk away, and still get a concise completion update without polling.
args.model_tier: cheap background tier for the watch; realtime only for the spoken notification when it arrives
args.latency_budget: Watch setup should be fast (<1s). Notification delivery depends on network and device availability; spoken update should start within ~1s of delivery.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job to register a watch and poll state; cost dominated by job status checks and audio rendering when needed.
args.security_concerns: Notification content is sensitive. Only short, user-facing summaries should be delivered; avoid including secrets. Require confirmation before speaking anything that could expose private data in public.
missing: A real implementation behind relay_event_push or job_completion_watch that schedules/maintains watches after the voice session ends
A delivery path to the pendant/phone with durable offline queueing and TTL semantics

args.user_asks: If I say something like ‘open the thing I was working on’, figure out the right place to handle it and do it.
args.why_useful: Reduces friction. The owner can speak naturally and the system routes to Mac or browser without manual tool selection.
args.model_tier: realtime for intent classification; mac-local planner for execution
args.latency_budget: Classification must be sub-second; execution depends on the chosen surface.
args.cost_estimate: Low classification cost; execution cost depends on app/browser actions.
args.security_concerns: Misrouting could cause unintended actions. Prefer reversible operations and confirmations for destructive ones. Keep utterance handling minimal and avoid logging sensitive content unnecessarily.
missing: An implemented routing tool or enum-based intent resolver at the relay
A relay capability inventory endpoint to avoid blind routing assumptions

args.user_asks: Tell me what’s going on with my system right now, and keep it short unless I ask for details.
args.why_useful: A quick spoken status check is ideal for a wearable. It saves opening the Mac and lets the owner decide whether to dig deeper.
args.model_tier: realtime for the spoken summary; cheaper tier for assembling a longer report if requested
args.latency_budget: Quick status should be <1s when cached; a detailed follow-up can take longer.
args.cost_estimate: Low; dominated by a small number of status reads.
args.security_concerns: Status can reveal sensitive info (apps, network, calendar). Keep summaries high-level and avoid reading content unless asked.
missing: A unified status aggregator that composes Mac status, job state, and device health into a single spoken summary

args.user_asks: “Take care of this end to end while I’m away from my Mac. Use my open browser session and Mac apps, make the routine choices from what you know about me, and interrupt me only if the next step is genuinely ambiguous or consequential.”
args.why_useful: Today the pendant can hand off a goal or a short action list, but the owner still has to manage the boundary between planning, browser state, Mac state, and follow-up. This would turn a spoken goal into a durable, resumable piece of work that progresses across all reachable surfaces and asks one focused question only when it cannot safely infer the answer.
args.model_tier: relay-realtime for intent extraction and concise clarification; mac-planner for the long workflow; mac-vision only when semantic UI state is needed; browser-extension for authenticated page state; cheaper background model for checkpoint reconciliation and final summarization.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; first action within 3 seconds; checkpoint updates asynchronously. A clarification should arrive only at a true branch, not during every action.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.15 per ordinary workflow depending on planner turns and screenshots; browser and vision observations dominate, not the short relay exchange.
args.security_concerns: The workflow can act in authenticated sessions and mutate files or web data. It must preserve the owner’s maximum-access preference while recording a typed action trail and exact checkpoint evidence; the owner should be able to say stop or undo the current reversible checkpoint. Secrets stay on the Mac/browser surfaces and are not copied into the spoken prompt.
missing: A durable cross-surface workflow/checkpoint coordinator that can pause and resume a POST /plan or POST /execute job when a clarification is needed
A standard handoff envelope carrying goal, memory projection, current browser evidence, Mac state, checkpoint, and pending question
A real completion/clarification delivery path to the pendant, beyond the currently unresolved event-push promise

args.user_asks: “Before I submit this, tell me whether it matches what I intended.”
args.why_useful: The owner often needs a second set of eyes rather than another automation. The system should combine the authenticated browser’s actual form/page, the Mac’s visible app state, and the spoken intent, then report mismatches such as wrong recipient, amount, attachment, date, or environment before submission. This is a new evidence-and-intent comparison, not a generic page read or action confirmation.
args.model_tier: relay-realtime extracts the intended constraints; browser-extension supplies DOM/text evidence; mac-vision supplies rendered-state evidence when the DOM is insufficient; a slower judgement model compares them and returns a short spoken verdict with cited fields.
args.latency_budget: Under 4 seconds for text/DOM checks and under 8 seconds when a screenshot or vision pass is required; no mutation occurs while checking.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.06 per check; vision screenshot analysis is the dominant cost.
args.security_concerns: Evidence may contain private mail, financial, or health data. Keep raw evidence on the owning surface, pass only selected fields to judgement, redact secrets, and retain a short-lived receipt. This is a read-only preflight and should not block ordinary browsing.
missing: A cross-surface intent-vs-evidence schema with field extraction and confidence
A browser action that can pause exactly before a submit and expose the candidate mutation without clicking it
A relay response format that can speak a concise mismatch list and link it to the pending job

args.change: Replace the live-turn legacy memory assembly in conversationContext.js with the existing contextProjection.projectContext(surface, task, budgetTokens) output, preserving the stable preference/permission prefix and task-scoped tail; include the projection’s droppedForBudget metadata in internal receipts rather than spoken output.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would stop repeating stale project context and start remembering the owner’s actual editor, permissions, reply style, and current task with much shorter prompts. Responses become more personal and faster while spending less context on every turn.
args.effort: Small but high-leverage: wire one injection point, map relay task text to the projection query, add regression tests for follow-ups and sensitive facts, then measure with the existing context-projection script.
args.risk: A bad surface/task mapping could omit a relevant fact or expose a browser-derived fact in an unrelated conversation. Recover by falling back to the legacy formatter on projection failure and by honoring the projection’s existing sensitivity and surface filters.
args.cost_impact: No new API dependency; reduces prompt tokens materially (the measured example saves about 222 tokens/turn, 59.4%).
args.latency_impact: One local store read, likely lower total latency because the prompt is shorter; stable-prefix caching improves across turns.
args.security_impact: Improves security if the projection is the sole live path because it enforces surface scoping, sensitivity gating, and browser-fact task matching; remove the parallel legacy path to avoid accidental leakage.
depends_on: The existing GET /memory/projection contract and contextProjection implementation
A reliable relay surface identifier and current utterance/task string in conversationContext.js

args.user_asks: “Show me proof that it really happened everywhere I asked.”
args.why_useful: A spoken “done” is not enough when a Mac file, a browser account, and the relay can disagree or one surface can silently fail. The owner should receive one concise spoken result plus a durable receipt showing the before/after evidence for each requested surface, and a clear distinction between completed, observed, and merely queued.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay gives the immediate one-sentence answer; mac-planner and browser-extension perform the requested work; a cheaper background verifier compares postconditions and assembles the evidence receipt; mac-vision is used only when rendered UI is the only proof.
args.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; ordinary verification under 10 seconds; long verification can finish asynchronously and alert the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.10 per request, dominated by a second browser/Mac read or screenshot rather than generation.
args.security_concerns: Receipts can contain private page text and filenames. Store hashes, selected fields, and redacted evidence by default, with raw captures expiring quickly. Never claim success from an action response alone; require an observed postcondition or explicitly say unverifiable.
missing: A postcondition/verifier schema attached to each planned action, rather than a free-form goal only
Cross-surface receipts that correlate Mac, browser, and relay evidence under one job
A spoken distinction between queued, executed, observed, and verified, delivered after the voice session

transcript.summary: Recorded three owner-facing capabilities: a durable cross-surface task executor that pauses only for genuine ambiguity, an intent-versus-evidence preflight before submission, and proof-backed verification that distinguishes queued/executed/observed/verified. The first and third are especially important because the owner can walk away from the Mac; all three require connective work between existing plan/execute, browser, Mac, job, receipt, memory, and event surfaces. The live memory-projection wiring proposal was rejected as already in the backlog, so I did not count it.
transcript.biggest_unknown: The exact durable handoff and postcondition schemas do not exist yet; the existing job receipts and pipeline events need to be inspected and extended rather than treated as sufficient.

transcript.text: Got it — I’ll do a fresh capability sweep, then I’ll point out what’s still missing or unclear and what I’d ask for next.

args.user_asks: “Track that task and tell me when it’s done.”
args.why_useful: This is the everyday killer feature: you can start something hands-free, walk away, and still get a clear completion ping without babysitting it.
args.model_tier: Realtime only to acknowledge the request; cheaper background tier (Mac/relay) should monitor and notify.
args.latency_budget: Under 1s to confirm it’s being tracked; completion notification can arrive later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per request. The expensive part is unnecessary polling; use evented status when available and fall back to periodic checks sparingly.
args.security_concerns: Notifications can leak task names. Keep spoken summaries short and avoid sensitive details unless explicitly requested. Always reflect the true job state; never infer success.
missing: A real completion event delivery mechanism (relay_event_push is currently unresolved).
A durable job watch that survives voice session end and can emit to pendant/phone/dashboard.
A small notification queue on relay/paired app to handle offline delivery and dedupe.

args.user_asks: “Tell me what’s happening right now with my devices and connection.”
args.why_useful: When speech feels glitchy or a command seems slow, the owner needs a quick, trustworthy status snapshot without digging into logs.
args.model_tier: Realtime (relay) for the spoken summary; Mac only if a live check is needed.
args.latency_budget: 1-2 seconds for a basic snapshot; deeper diagnostics can take longer but should be announced.
args.cost_estimate: Low. Prefer cached relay/device health signals and only query the Mac when necessary.
args.security_concerns: Status may reveal identifiers and environment details. Keep it minimal and avoid serial numbers or sensitive network info unless explicitly asked.
missing: A single consolidated health endpoint for relay-visible device and link state (USB, audio bridge, pendant, Mac agent).
Standardized fields for audio pipeline health, packet loss, and last error.
Permissions to read any additional state not already exposed via /v1/state/* or /v1/ops/*.

args.user_asks: “Summarize what changed since the last time I asked.”
args.why_useful: This reduces cognitive load. The owner gets a concise delta instead of a full re-briefing, which is perfect for a wearable voice interface.
args.model_tier: Cheaper background tier to compute and store deltas; realtime only to speak them.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds to speak a short summary once the delta is prepared.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate if it requires reading many sources; keep it bounded with watched sources and sampling.
args.security_concerns: Changes may include sensitive content (mail, files, tabs). Require explicit scope and confirmation for sensitive sources.
missing: A cross-surface change journal keyed by source (mail/files/browser/jobs).
A diffing format that is stable enough to store and replay.
A user-level preference for verbosity and scope.

args.user_asks: “Warn me, through the pendant, when I am about to make a consequential mistake on the Mac—but never block me.” The warning should understand that I am composing an email, editing code, buying something in a browser, or deleting a file, and explain the specific mismatch with my stated project or preferences.
args.why_useful: The pendant is the one surface that can interrupt attention while the Mac is in front of the owner. This turns the system from a passive executor into a second pair of eyes without imposing the rejected confirmation-gate policy. It could catch an accidental production edit, an email to the wrong person, or a purchase that conflicts with a remembered constraint.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for a one-sentence alert; a cheap background model on the Mac for continuous local classification and comparison against projected memory. Escalate only ambiguous/high-impact observations to the planner.
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms from a Mac event to an alert when possible; otherwise batch at natural UI boundaries (field blur, navigation, save). Never speak more than one alert per cooldown window unless the owner presses for detail.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero incremental API cost with local event classification; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per escalated reasoning check. The dominant cost is vision/model calls for screenshots, so use accessibility metadata and DOM text first.
args.security_concerns: Screen text, browser content, and drafts may leave the Mac only for an escalated check. Default to local redaction of secrets and credentials. Alerts are advisory and must not silently alter, block, or send anything.
missing: A Mac event stream for active-app/accessibility/DOM changes rather than only request/response actions
A durable, debounced policy evaluator joining current UI evidence with memory projection
A relay-to-pendant alert path that is actually implemented (the existing inbox shape is the right destination)
A Mac vision fallback for UI states with no useful accessibility metadata

args.user_asks: “Find the thing I saw before—search my authenticated browser history, open tabs, Mac files, and voice notes, then tell me where it came from and reopen the exact source.” I should be able to describe it approximately (“the paper about the battery test from last month”), and the pendant should speak a ranked answer with a citation, not pretend a fuzzy match is certain.
args.why_useful: Today each surface knows only its own slice, so the owner must remember whether an item was in Safari, a local file, or a prior conversation. A provenance-preserving federated search would recover lost work while keeping uncertainty explicit and would work especially well when the owner is away from the desk and only has the pendant.
args.model_tier: Cheap retrieval/reranking on the Mac and relay; use the expensive realtime model only to resolve the spoken description and summarize the top result. Do not send full corpora to the realtime tier.
args.latency_budget: Speak an initial top match in 2 seconds, then optionally refine. A slow authenticated-browser search may return as an inbox update rather than holding the voice turn.
args.cost_estimate: A local index makes ordinary queries <$0.001; occasional embedding/index refresh and one concise synthesis are the dominant costs, roughly $0.002–$0.02 per query.
args.security_concerns: Browser history, private pages, files, and voice transcripts are sensitive. Index and search locally on the Mac; return only the selected snippets and URLs. Respect per-source sensitivity and never expose a private result merely because its text matches a public query.
missing: A unified local index over browser history/tabs, files, memory facts, and voice-run transcripts with stable provenance IDs
Browser-extension access to history and authenticated page metadata, not only active-page commands
A search route that can query the Mac while the owner is away and return ranked evidence
A compact pendant spoken-result protocol supporting citation, confidence, and “open this” follow-up

args.user_asks: “Before you change anything, rehearse the whole operation against a disposable copy and tell me exactly what would happen.” For a code change, use a temporary git worktree and test it; for a browser workflow, use a preview/draft path where available; for a file operation, use a snapshot. Let me say “apply that rehearsal” from the pendant to commit the already-reviewed result.
args.why_useful: The owner wants maximum access and does not want needless permission prompts, but a spoken preview is valuable when an operation has broad or irreversible consequences. This gives them confidence without turning the system into a confirmation gate for ordinary reversible actions, and it makes multi-step Mac/browser automation inspectable before it touches real state.
args.model_tier: Use the Mac planner and local shell for deterministic cloning, snapshots, dry-runs, and tests. Use realtime only to translate the spoken goal and summarize the resulting diff; use a cheaper background model for large diffs or logs.
args.latency_budget: Return a plan and first risk summary within 3 seconds; let tests continue asynchronously and deliver a short pendant inbox result. Applying an unchanged, owner-requested rehearsal should begin immediately after the explicit spoken command.
args.cost_estimate: Local filesystem snapshots and git worktrees are cheap; model cost is roughly $0.005–$0.05 per rehearsal depending on diff/log size. Browser preview support is the expensive portion because some sites have no draft or transaction mode.
args.security_concerns: A rehearsal must be hermetic: no production credentials, network writes, mail sends, purchases, or destructive commands may escape the sandbox. The apply step must verify that the real target has not changed since rehearsal and should refuse stale patches rather than silently merging.
missing: A first-class sandbox/rehearsal action type in the Mac agent with resource and network isolation
Snapshot/diff adapters for arbitrary files and app state, plus git worktree support
Browser transaction or draft adapters and an explicit classification of sites that cannot be safely rehearsed
A durable rehearsal artifact keyed to the exact goal, inputs, diff, tests, and target revision
A pendant command to select and apply a named rehearsal without replaying the entire conversation

args.user_asks: “Stop the thing you just started.” A deliberate long press on the pendant should cancel the currently running Mac or browser job, close or undo only the actions that job owns where that is safe, and tell me exactly what was stopped and what could not be undone.
args.why_useful: When the owner is away from the Mac or notices an automation going wrong, waiting for a spoken turn or finding the right window is too slow. A physical abort path is the wearable's unique value: it can halt a runaway loop, accidental browser navigation, or an unexpectedly broad file operation before the owner reaches the keyboard.
args.model_tier: No expensive reasoning is needed for the first stop signal: relay forwards a signed cancellation to the owning job and the Mac agent enforces it. Use a cheap model only to summarize partial receipts; use realtime for the immediate spoken acknowledgement.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge locally within 150 ms and deliver the cancellation to the Mac/browser within 500 ms when connected. If disconnected, the pendant must show a distinct abort-pending state and the relay must not claim success until a receipt arrives.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; the engineering cost is cancellation propagation and compensating actions. A short final summary is <$0.001 per incident.
args.security_concerns: The gesture must be hard to trigger accidentally and must never be treated as a general delete/undo command. Cancellation should be idempotent, scoped to the active job, logged with a receipt, and conservative about compensation: stop first, undo only operations with an explicit inverse.
missing: A physical long-press/double-confirm abort gesture distinct from normal record/stop behavior
Cancellation tokens propagated from relay jobs through planner, shell, vision, and browser command queues
Cooperative cancellation checks in long-running Mac/browser actions
Per-action inverse metadata and a partial-completion receipt
A relay-to-pendant immediate status signal for abort-pending, stopped, and unable-to-undo

args.user_asks: Tell me what happened with that thing I asked the Mac to do.
args.why_useful: The owner gets a quick, reliable status update without waking the Mac or re-running the task, perfect for on-the-go voice interactions.
args.model_tier: realtime for status lookup; no need to route to a heavier model
args.latency_budget: Under a second when the job exists; dominated by relay record lookup.
args.cost_estimate: Low. One job-status read; no downstream execution.
args.security_concerns: Avoid inventing details. Speak the returned status verbatim. Do not expose sensitive job payloads beyond the canned spoken summary.

args.user_asks: “I’m in a meeting and missed that last point—tell me the key thing they just said, and draft a reply I can approve by voice.”
args.why_useful: The owner can recover from a missed spoken moment without opening a laptop or making the meeting stop. It combines the worn microphone, the authenticated meeting/browser surface, and the Mac’s drafting ability in a way no one node can provide.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the short spoken request and confirmation; a cheaper background model extracts the latest caption/transcript window and drafts the reply. Use the expensive tier only for ambiguity and the final concise answer.
args.latency_budget: Initial acknowledgement under 500 ms; caption retrieval and summary in 3–8 seconds; draft in under 15 seconds. If captions are unavailable, say so rather than pretending to have heard the meeting.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per use, dominated by transcript/caption extraction and draft generation; near-zero when the browser already exposes a small recent caption window.
args.security_concerns: Meeting text and the proposed reply leave the browser/Mac only to the relay/model. Require an explicit spoken confirmation before sending anything; never infer permission to send from a request to draft. Mask unrelated participant text and retain the transcript slice only ephemerally.
missing: A browser-extension action that exposes the most recent caption/transcript segment from the active meeting tab with timestamps
A relay session binding that keeps the request associated with the active meeting tab
A voice confirmation path that can return a drafted reply to the browser without sending it

args.user_asks: “Find the thing I was looking at yesterday about the pendant, tell me which tab or file it was, and put me back exactly there.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets continuity across a fragmented day: the pendant supplies the vague natural-language clue while the Mac and browser search their distinct histories and reopen the exact source. This is more useful than a generic web search because it recovers the owner’s own prior context.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background retrieval/ranking model over browser history, open tabs, recent files, and scoped memory; realtime only resolves the owner’s short clarification and speaks the winning provenance.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately, rank candidates within 5 seconds, and reopen the selected source within 10 seconds. If there are multiple plausible matches, speak at most three discriminating choices.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.04 per invocation, dominated by embedding/ranking or summarizing candidate metadata; document contents should not be sent unless needed.
args.security_concerns: Search only the owner’s local browser and Mac metadata by default; do not upload full file contents or private page bodies to the model. Report provenance (app, title, timestamp, URL/path) so the owner can detect a wrong match. Opening a source is reversible; do not edit it.
missing: A unified, read-only recent-context index joining Safari/browser history, open tabs, and Mac recent documents
A local Mac action for opening a ranked provenance result by stable ID rather than by guessed title
A relay-side short-lived candidate cache so a follow-up like “the second one” is unambiguous

args.user_asks: “I’m away from my Mac. Turn this spoken idea into a working experiment: create the project note, run the smallest safe test, and tell me what happened when it’s actually done.”
args.why_useful: This is the system’s highest-value end-to-end promise: a thought captured while worn becomes a verifiable artifact and execution result without the owner sitting at the computer. The relay handles ambiguity, the Mac edits and runs, and the pendant delivers a truthful completion or failure later.
args.model_tier: Realtime converts speech into a compact goal and asks only essential clarifying questions. mac-planner performs the multi-step plan; a cheaper verifier checks receipts, test output, and changed files. Realtime returns only the final short spoken status.
args.latency_budget: Capture and acknowledgement under 1 second; planning under 10 seconds; execution may take minutes. Completion must be pushed asynchronously and remain available if the pendant is temporarily offline.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.30 per experiment, dominated by planner/verifier turns and any long command output; token cost is reduced by passing structured receipts and diffs instead of full transcripts.
args.security_concerns: The owner has granted broad access, but the system must still be truthful: distinguish queued, running, passed, failed, and not-run. Include command/file receipts and a compact diff in the dashboard. Never claim completion from a planner response alone; destructive or externally visible steps should be surfaced for the owner’s explicit approval.
missing: A durable experiment job record containing goal, plan, commands, outputs, changed paths, and verification state
A planner-to-relay completion callback wired to the existing pendant inbox/event delivery, including offline retention
A verifier that can rerun or inspect tests independently and mark a job failed when the claimed artifact is absent
A Mac-local workspace lease so unattended jobs do not interfere with active work

args.change: Add a meeting-context capture primitive to the browser extension: for the active tab only, expose a bounded rolling window of visible captions/transcript lines with speaker labels and monotonic timestamps, plus a tab/session identifier. The relay can request that window, but the extension must never silently capture microphone or hidden-tab content.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner misses a sentence while wearing the pendant, the system can answer from the meeting’s actual visible words and draft a response instead of guessing or requiring them to rewind manually.
args.effort: Medium: extension content-script adapters for supported meeting UIs, a normalized caption schema, relay endpoint, and tests against DOM changes and caption absence.
args.risk: Meeting sites can change their DOM or captions can be incomplete; return an explicit unavailable result. Limit the window and active-tab scope, and recover by asking the owner to repeat or open the transcript. Do not send or post a reply automatically.
args.cost_impact: Low per request; only a small caption window is transferred. Engineering cost is the adapter maintenance across meeting sites.
args.latency_impact: Caption retrieval should add under 1 second; normalization is local to the extension.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy over full-tab capture by limiting data to visible captions and a bounded time window. Still treat meeting text as sensitive and avoid durable storage by default.
depends_on: A relay endpoint that can associate a request with the active browser session
The meeting-companion capability’s draft-only confirmation flow

transcript.text:
Recorded four items:

1. **Pendant meeting recovery and reply drafting** — retrieve recent visible captions from the active meeting tab, summarize what was missed, and draft (but never send) a reply for spoken approval.
2. **Cross-surface personal-context recovery** — find a document, tab, or file the owner previously viewed using vague clues, report provenance, and reopen the exact source.
3. **Verified spoken-to-experiment execution** — turn an idea spoken away from the Mac into a planned, executed, independently verified experiment with durable receipts and truthful asynchronous completion.
4. **Browser meeting-context capture primitive** — add a bounded, active-tab-only rolling caption window with speaker labels and timestamps for reliable meeting recovery.

The most important is #3: it is the clearest path from “I had an idea” to “the system actually made and tested something,” while preserving truthful status when work is queued, running, failed, or complete.

Biggest remaining unknown: which meeting applications expose captions in a stable DOM/API, and whether the current browser extension can identify the active meeting session without adding a new pairing protocol.
I’ll do a quick capability sweep first, then I’ll flag what’s missing and propose the most useful next steps.

args.user_asks: “Watch that task and tell me when it’s done, even if I’ve stopped talking.”
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing for a wearable voice assistant: you can start a long task hands-free, walk away, and still get a clear completion notice without polling.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief confirmation; background monitoring should run on a cheaper tier tied to job state.
args.latency_budget: < 1s to confirm the watch is set. Completion delivery can be minutes-hours, depending on the job.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation. The expensive part is LLM time if used to summarize results; job state polling should be lightweight and event-driven where possible.
args.security_concerns: Completion notices must not claim success unless the job state says so. Notifications should be short and avoid leaking sensitive content; include only what’s needed to act.
missing: A reliable completion-event path from job state to a delivery target (pendant/phone/dashboard) that works after the voice session ends.
A working implementation of job watchers/events in the relay surface, wired to real routes.
A delivery mechanism that respects the pendant’s storage rule (no routine audio stored on SD; queue text/metadata only).

args.user_asks: “Tell me what I was doing and what’s next.”
args.why_useful: A quick spoken ‘working memory’ is perfect for a pendant: it reduces context switching and helps resume work after interruptions.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the spoken summary; deeper reconstruction should run on the Mac/browser tier using cheaper models and local context.
args.latency_budget: 1-3 seconds for a short summary; longer details only if asked.
args.cost_estimate: Low to moderate. Most cost comes from retrieving and summarizing context; keep the default reply short.
args.security_concerns: Avoid reading sensitive content aloud by default. Summaries should name sources (mail/calendar/files) and require confirmation before opening or sending anything.

A cross-surface task model that merges Mac job history and browser findings into a single ‘what’s next’ list.

args.user_asks: “Test the pendant connection and audio path right now.”
args.why_useful: When something sounds off, the owner needs a one-shot diagnostic they can run without opening a laptop. It’s immediate confidence, not a spreadsheet.
args.model_tier: Realtime to guide the user; the actual test routine should run on-device and/or on the Mac without LLM involvement.
args.latency_budget: Fast: a few seconds for loopback checks; longer if a recording needs analysis.
args.cost_estimate: Low. Mostly device and bridge operations; minimal model tokens.
args.security_concerns: Diagnostics should not capture or store user speech beyond what’s needed for the test; no routine SD writes.
missing: A callable diagnostic endpoint for the bridge/pendant path (today it’s only indirectly testable).
A standard report format that can be spoken and also logged for later analysis.

args.change: Wire the existing memory projection into the live conversation context so the relay gets a compact, stable head of preferences/permissions and a task-scoped tail, instead of resending legacy blocks every turn.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, cheaper, and more consistent responses. The owner gets snappier voice interactions and fewer ‘I forgot what we were doing’ moments.
args.effort: Medium. Replace the prompt assembly path to call projectContext(surface, task) and adjust the downstream formatting.
args.risk: Projection bugs could hide relevant facts. Mitigate by logging dropped-for-budget and allowing a fallback verbose mode for debugging.
args.cost_impact: Measured savings are large (hundreds of tokens per turn).
args.latency_impact: Lower latency from smaller prompts and more cacheable context.
args.security_impact: Better scoping reduces accidental leakage of browser-derived facts into voice conversations.
depends_on: Confirm the projection route and parameters; add tests for surface scoping and budget behavior.

args.change: Publish a relay capability manifest route (e.g., GET /capabilities) so this surface can inventory its own routes and event endpoints, just like the Mac agent.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer blind spots mean fewer failures mid-conversation. The system can self-diagnose and route work more reliably.
args.effort: Medium. Add a route that enumerates relay routes and tool endpoints with versioning.
args.risk: Exposing too much internal detail could expand attack surface; mitigate with auth and minimal output.
args.cost_impact: Low ongoing cost; small implementation effort.
args.latency_impact: No runtime latency impact; improves debugging speed.
args.security_impact: Requires strict auth and redaction of secrets.

args.change: Implement a job completion pipeline: when a Mac job reaches a terminal state, emit a relay event, queue a short alert (text/metadata) for delivery, and render audio only at delivery time — never store routine audio on SD.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can start a task and walk away, then get a clear, timely update on the pendant without babysitting the job.
args.effort: High. Needs relay event emission, a delivery queue, and integration with the existing alert inbox shape.
args.risk: Duplicate or missing notifications if state transitions are mishandled. Use idempotent job receipts and retries.
args.cost_impact: Moderate build cost; low per-job runtime cost if event-driven.
args.latency_impact: Near real-time when event-driven; acceptable delay if fallback polling is used.
args.security_impact: Short messages reduce leakage; confirmation required for sensitive results.
depends_on: A reliable job state source (GET /jobs/:jobId) and a working event/watch implementation.

args.user_asks: When I ask “where was I?”, tell me exactly what I was doing on my Mac and in my browser, what is unfinished, and give me a one-sentence way back into it through the pendant.
args.why_useful: A worn assistant should restore the owner’s working context without requiring them to remember which app, tab, or job held it. This is a cross-node reconstruction, not merely a history list: live Mac state, authenticated browser state, outstanding jobs, and durable task memory are reconciled into a spoken answer.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to clarify the spoken request and speak the compact result; use faculty-perception or a background planner to rank and reconcile state, because the owner is waiting for a short answer rather than a long computer-use loop.
args.latency_budget: Under 4 seconds for the first spoken sentence; continue collecting state in the background for up to 15 seconds and replace the answer only if confidence materially improves.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly one realtime turn plus one cheap synthesis turn; the dominant cost is browser and Mac state collection, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: Browser titles, document names, and window contents can be sensitive. Send only extracted task candidates to the relay, redact page text by default, and require an explicit “show me the details” follow-up before reading private content aloud.
missing: A single state snapshot API that joins live Mac windows, browser tabs, active jobs, and task memory with timestamps
A reconciliation/ranking worker that marks evidence as current, stale, or conflicting
A spoken disambiguation response when two work contexts are equally plausible

args.user_asks: Let me say “hold this thought” while away from my Mac, then later say “continue that” and have the system reopen the exact working context, quote the last saved thought, and ask only the one missing question before acting.
args.why_useful: This turns a fleeting wearable utterance into a resumable handoff rather than a dead-end memo. The owner can leave a meeting or walk away from the desk and return to a precise, bounded continuation with the relevant browser page, Mac app, and pending intent restored.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles capture confirmation and the later one-question clarification. A background planner extracts a compact continuation record and resolves it against Mac/browser state when the owner returns.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge capture in under 1 second; on resume, speak the proposed context in under 3 seconds, then wait for confirmation before any mutation.
args.cost_estimate: One short realtime exchange at capture and one at resume; background extraction is a low-cost model. State snapshots and browser inspection dominate operational cost.
args.security_concerns: Continuation records may contain secrets or sensitive page titles. Store a minimal encrypted record with expiry, never store raw audio after transcription, and require confirmation for reopening or acting on a different account/session than the original.
missing: A first-class continuation record with source anchors, expiry, and confidence
Mac and browser commands to restore a recorded app/window/tab context without replaying destructive actions
A conflict resolver for stale or changed pages

args.user_asks: Tell me “what can I safely do right now?” and have the pendant answer using my current Mac activity, browser session, audio state, and pending jobs—then offer one useful action that will not interrupt work already in progress.
args.why_useful: The owner should not have to know whether an action belongs to the Mac, browser, relay, or a queued job. This creates a truthful availability view for a worn device: it distinguishes idle, busy, disconnected, stale, and safe-to-interrupt, and converts that into one actionable suggestion.
args.model_tier: Faculty-perception gathers and classifies state; a cheap planner selects a reversible suggestion; realtime only asks a clarification or speaks the result. The computer-use loop is not needed unless the owner accepts the suggestion.
args.latency_budget: First answer in 2–3 seconds from cached state; refresh uncertain sources within 8 seconds and say explicitly when a source is stale.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation if state snapshots are cached; occasional Mac/browser probes and one small synthesis call are the main costs.
args.security_concerns: The answer itself may reveal private work titles or browser sessions. Speak app-level categories by default, keep content redacted, and make detailed disclosure a separate request. Do not infer that disconnected means safe.
missing: A shared freshness-aware availability schema across relay, Mac, browser, and jobs
A non-interference classifier that understands active calls, presentations, audio playback, and unsaved work
A cache with explicit stale/error states rather than silently treating missing data as idle

args.user_asks: Keep private answers private: when I ask the pendant for sensitive information, decide whether it is safe to speak aloud from my current context; if not, send the answer to the least intrusive available surface and tell me only that it is ready.
args.why_useful: A wearable is inherently public. Without output-aware privacy, the assistant can disclose passwords, finances, health, or private messages to everyone nearby. This lets the owner use voice anywhere while preserving the convenience of a spoken answer for harmless information.
args.model_tier: A low-cost policy model classifies sensitivity and chooses a delivery surface; realtime handles the request and speaks only a safe acknowledgement. The actual answer is rendered on the selected trusted surface.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 2 seconds. Sensitive delivery may take up to 10 seconds if it must wait for a paired private surface; never stall the spoken interaction while probing every surface.
args.cost_estimate: One small classification call plus whichever Mac/browser retrieval is needed; delivery rendering is cheap. Cost is dominated by source retrieval, not the privacy decision.
args.security_concerns: This is security-critical: default to withholding rather than guessing, bind trusted surfaces to the owner, expire undelivered answers, avoid logging plaintext, and distinguish 'could not verify privacy' from 'safe.' The pendant must never read a secret merely because the owner asked while in public.
missing: An output-sensitivity classifier with a closed set of delivery policies
Presence/proximity and acoustic privacy signals from the pendant and paired devices
Encrypted, single-use delivery envelopes for Mac, browser, phone, and dashboard
A confirmation-free but auditable policy for harmless versus sensitive speech

args.user_asks: Give me a “one safe next move” whenever I am stuck: infer the smallest reversible action that advances the task from my current Mac/browser state, explain why it is next, and do it only after I say “go.”
args.why_useful: The system becomes useful in moments of uncertainty rather than only when the owner already knows the command. It combines perception of the actual work state with judgement and a bounded action, while preserving the owner’s control over the decision.
args.model_tier: Faculty-perception reads the current state, faculty-judgement proposes one reversible next move, and realtime presents it in one sentence. mac-planner or browser executes only after the owner’s explicit “go”; no expensive realtime reasoning is spent on execution.
args.latency_budget: Propose within 5 seconds; execution receipt within 8 seconds for a short action. If state is stale or conflicting, say so instead of fabricating a move.
args.cost_estimate: One perception pass and one cheap planning pass per request, with Mac/browser inspection as the dominant variable cost; realtime output is short.
args.security_concerns: The proposal must include the exact target and predicted effect, never silently mutate state, and attach a before/after receipt. Avoid proposing actions on unsaved or high-impact work without surfacing that fact.
missing: A state-to-next-action evaluator that scores reversibility and expected progress
A compact spoken proposal schema with target, effect, and confidence
A precondition check and postcondition receipt spanning Mac and browser

args.change: Build a cross-surface evidence graph that records facts about the same task from pendant utterances, Mac observations, browser observations, and action receipts as timestamped claims with provenance, freshness, and contradictions; expose a task-scoped view to the realtime relay and downstream agents instead of passing unrelated raw context.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets answers grounded in what actually happened, even when the Mac, browser, and pendant disagree or one went offline. It prevents the assistant from confidently acting on yesterday’s tab, an old transcript, or a job that silently failed.
args.effort: High: define claim identity and provenance, add adapters for each surface, implement freshness/conflict resolution, and integrate the task view into conversation context and action planning.
args.risk: Bad entity matching could merge two projects or hide a real conflict. Keep original claims and provenance, expose uncertainty, and fall back to asking the owner rather than resolving high-impact conflicts automatically.
args.cost_impact: Moderate storage and a small background reconciliation model; lower realtime prompt cost once only task-relevant claims are injected.
args.latency_impact: Cached task views can be sub-second; a cold reconciliation adds 2–6 seconds and should produce an immediate stale/collecting acknowledgement.
args.security_impact: Provenance and sensitive fields need encryption and surface scoping. Do not replicate browser content to the relay unless the task explicitly requires it.
depends_on: Wire GET /memory/projection into conversationContext.js
Add adapters over GET /machine-context, GET /browser/inspect, GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts, and POST /execute receipts
Define surface-scoped redaction and claim retention rules

args.user_asks: Pick up where we left off on my computer.
args.why_useful: The owner can start a thought on the pendant and continue on the Mac or browser with the right context already loaded, saving time and mental load.
args.model_tier: Realtime to capture intent, then handoff to the Mac planner/browser for the heavy lifting.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm the handoff; the Mac workflow can proceed at normal speed.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; dominated by context packaging and downstream planning/execution.
args.security_concerns: Context may include sensitive memory. Only project what’s relevant to the task and avoid leaking browser-derived facts unless explicitly included.
missing: Live wiring to use the memory projection output in the conversation context instead of legacy blocks.
A standard handoff envelope for task context and constraints across surfaces.

args.user_asks: “Search everywhere I can reach for the thing I’m thinking of, tell me which source is authoritative, and put the right result into the app I name.” For example: “Find the latest invoice from Acme across my Mac files, logged-in browser, and relay history, tell me which one is current, and attach it to the draft in Outlook.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner must know which surface contains information and manually shuttle results between them. This would make the worn pendant a single, source-aware front door: it searches local files, authenticated browser sessions, and relay memory, resolves conflicts by freshness and provenance, speaks a short answer, and performs the final placement on the Mac/browser. The result is useful specifically because no single node can see all three stores.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles intent extraction and a one-sentence answer; a cheaper background planner performs federated retrieval and provenance ranking, while mac-planner/browser-extension execute the destination action.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 500 ms; first answer in 5–8 s; placement may continue asynchronously with a spoken completion notice.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per request depending on document/page count; retrieval, OCR, and browser snapshots dominate rather than the realtime turn.
args.security_concerns: Search results can contain sensitive mail, files, and logged-in pages. Keep raw content on the Mac/relay where possible, send only ranked excerpts to the realtime model, show source names in the spoken answer, and record an evidence receipt. Placement into a destination must be explicitly named by the owner; never infer a recipient or attachment target from a vague phrase.
missing: A federated search contract spanning Mac files, browser sessions, relay memory, and job receipts
Content extraction and provenance IDs for local files and authenticated pages
A destination adapter that can attach or insert a selected artifact, not merely type text
A compact spoken disambiguation protocol when two sources are equally current

args.user_asks: “Watch this authenticated page and, if my exact condition becomes true, carry out the whole follow-up.” For example: “When this limited-run item is back under $80, buy one, use my saved shipping details, and tell me what happened.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently can ask for a page check or a one-off Mac action, but cannot express a durable, conditional objective that bridges a logged-in browser, a scheduled relay watch, and a Mac-side receipt. This turns the pendant into an agent that can act while the owner is away instead of requiring them to remember to ask again.
args.model_tier: Realtime only captures the condition and summarizes the resulting decision. A low-cost scheduled worker evaluates the page and deterministic predicates; the browser extension performs the authenticated transaction; mac-planner handles local receipt/storage and exception recovery.
args.latency_budget: Immediate confirmation of the registered condition in under 2 s; checks within the requested cadence; completion alert within 30 s of a positive match.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per check depending on page extraction and frequency, plus one planner call on a match. Browser session uptime and page polling dominate.
args.security_concerns: This can create financial or contractual side effects. Store the exact predicate, item identity, maximum quantity/price, and expiry as an immutable plan; refuse if the page differs materially. The owner’s explicit spoken instruction authorizes the specified transaction, but the system must not broaden it. Keep credentials in the browser session, never in relay prompts, and emit a receipt containing before/after evidence, price, and timestamp.
missing: A durable conditional-workflow record with exact predicates, expiry, idempotency, and retry state
A scheduler/worker that can run browser watches even when the Mac agent is temporarily offline
Authenticated browser execution that can return structured checkout evidence
A safe transaction adapter for saved details and a durable completion/exception notification

args.user_asks: “Finish the task I started, even if the connection dropped, and tell me exactly what was already done versus what still needs doing.” For example: “I started sending the rent spreadsheet to Alex; reconcile the browser and Mac state, avoid sending twice, finish the missing steps, and give me one truthful summary.”
args.why_useful: A dropped link currently leaves the owner guessing whether an action happened, especially when a browser submission or Mac mutation may have succeeded before the relay lost its response. This would make interrupted tasks recoverable rather than duplicated or abandoned, using the pendant as the place to resume and the Mac/browser as the sources of truth.
args.model_tier: A cheap reconciliation worker compares action receipts with live Mac/browser state and builds an idempotent continuation plan; realtime only asks a narrowly scoped clarification when state is genuinely ambiguous and speaks the result.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge recovery intent in under 500 ms; produce a state classification in 3–10 s; long repair runs continue asynchronously and notify the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per recovery, dominated by live browser/Mac inspection and occasional planner calls. Most unambiguous cases should be rule-based with no expensive model invocation.
args.security_concerns: Never infer that a side effect happened from a timeout alone. Maintain a per-step idempotency key, inspect destination state before retrying, and distinguish confirmed, probably-completed, and unknown. For unknown high-impact effects, report the uncertainty instead of repeating them. Receipts should include redacted evidence and be retained only as long as needed for recovery.
missing: A durable step-level action journal with idempotency keys and pre/post observations across Mac and browser surfaces
Adapters that can inspect whether a specific send/upload/form submission already occurred
A continuation planner that can safely skip confirmed steps and retry only unresolved ones
A user-facing reconciliation vocabulary for the pendant: completed, resumed, blocked, or unknown

transcript.summary: Recorded three distinct owner-facing capabilities: federated source-aware search and placement across relay/Mac/browser; durable conditional actions against authenticated pages; and interruption-safe reconciliation that resumes tasks without duplicate side effects. The most broadly useful is the first: it makes the pendant a single front door to information and action across otherwise isolated surfaces.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the existing watch, receipt, and browser routes already expose enough structured state to implement the proposed conditional workflows and reconciliation without new durable worker/journal primitives; I was instructed not to discover further this round.

transcript.text: Alright, I’ll quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll call out what’s still missing and propose a few high-impact additions.

args.user_asks: Watch the thing I just asked you to do, and tell me when it finishes—even after we stop talking.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful behavior: the owner can hand off a task and walk away. No polling, no checking later—just a clear completion cue when it’s done or needs attention.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the handoff sentence; cheaper background tier for watch polling and summarization.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge the watch request; completion delivery happens asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: Low per minute while watching; dominated by job status polling and a tiny summary generation when state changes.
args.security_concerns: Completion summaries must reflect job truth verbatim and avoid leaking sensitive task details; if the task touches mail/files, only a short outcome should be spoken. Delivery should require an authenticated pairing to the owner’s pendant/phone.
missing: A resolvable completion delivery mechanism (relay_event_push is currently unresolved)
A durable watch registration and lifecycle (create/cancel) on the relay
A delivery path to the existing offline inbox queue without storing routine audio on-device
built_from: job_completion_watch (schema resolves to job status today)

args.user_asks: If I say something like “handle the Outlook thing,” figure out what I meant and route it to the right place without me naming the tool.
args.why_useful: The owner talks naturally. The system should turn that into the correct action type and destination without exposing internal tool names.
args.model_tier: Realtime to classify intent fast, then planner tier to expand into actions.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm the interpretation; planning can take a few seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low per request; dominated by planning and execution on the Mac.
args.security_concerns: Misrouting is the risk. The relay should confirm high-impact interpretations and require explicit confirmation for destructive operations.
missing: A real implemented routing tool or schema-to-action bridge (relay_route_intent is unresolved)
Integration with the existing plan/execute action vocabulary to avoid free-form intents

args.user_asks: Remember what we’re working on right now and keep future turns focused on that, without me repeating context every time.
args.why_useful: Reduces friction and cost: the owner shouldn’t pay for the same context every turn, and the assistant stays on-task.
args.model_tier: Realtime uses a compact projection head; heavier retrieval happens on the Mac when needed.
args.latency_budget: No noticeable delay; must be under a second.
args.cost_estimate: Saves tokens per turn by sending a stable, small context head; costs are occasional projection reads.
args.security_concerns: Projection must honor sensitivity and scope rules; only relevant facts for the current surface and task should be included.
missing: Wire the existing memory projection into the live conversation context builder
A task label from the relay for better relevance scoring
built_from: conversationContext.js injection point (buildConversationContext) if exposed via a route

args.user_asks: When I tap the pendant and say “bookmark this,” capture exactly what I was doing on the Mac and browser, then later let me say “take me back to that” and restore the relevant app, tab, document, selection, and a one-sentence reason.
args.why_useful: A physical tap is a reliable interruption boundary. The owner could leave the desk, return hours later, and recover the precise work context rather than remembering which window, tab, or text mattered. This is more useful than a note because it restores state across the Mac and authenticated browser.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the two short utterances; a cheaper background planner should assemble and restore the context, with mac-vision used only when the active UI needs visual interpretation.
args.latency_budget: Bookmark acknowledgement under 2 seconds; capture under 10 seconds; restore under 15 seconds, with a spoken fallback if a tab or app is no longer available.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per bookmark/restore, dominated by one vision snapshot and planner context; most bookmarks need no large model call.
args.security_concerns: The snapshot may include authenticated pages, clipboard text, and window contents. Encrypt the bookmark, retain it for a user-selected TTL, redact passwords/credit-card fields, and never speak captured sensitive text unless explicitly requested.
missing: A first-class cross-surface bookmark record containing app/document/tab identity, selection, screenshot reference, transcript, and provenance
Mac actions to capture active window, caret/selection, and browser tab identity in one atomic snapshot
A restore planner that validates targets before changing the Mac and reports what could not be restored
Pendant utterance routing for bookmark/create versus restore/reopen

args.user_asks: If a task gets stuck because you need an answer from me, ask the question on the pendant, keep the work paused safely, and continue automatically when I answer—even if that answer comes hours later or from a different place.
args.why_useful: Today an agent either guesses, blocks a live turn, or leaves the owner to rediscover the unfinished job. This makes long, ambiguous work genuinely delegable: the pendant becomes an asynchronous question channel while the Mac and browser preserve the exact checkpoint.
args.model_tier: Use the cheaper background planner for task execution and checkpoint recovery; use realtime only to phrase the short question and acknowledge the answer.
args.latency_budget: Question delivery within 5 seconds of detecting a block; answer acknowledgement under 2 seconds; resume within 30 seconds after the owner replies.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.20 per blocked/resumed task, dominated by planner rehydration and any browser vision; idle waiting should cost nothing.
args.security_concerns: Persisted questions and checkpoints can contain private page data. Encrypt job state, scope each question to its originating job, expire abandoned jobs, and require an explicit owner answer for consequential ambiguity without imposing a blanket execution gate.
missing: A durable blocked state with a typed pending question and checkpointed action plan
A relay-to-pendant question delivery path distinct from completion alerts, plus answer correlation to the waiting job
Planner support for suspend/resume and idempotent replay after Mac or browser reconnect
A job journal that stores the minimum redacted context needed to continue

args.user_asks: When I say “what did I leave unfinished?”, search my recent voice sessions, Mac jobs, browser work, and saved task facts, rank the unfinished threads, and let me say “continue the second one” to resume the exact next step.
args.why_useful: The owner should not have to remember whether an abandoned intention lived in a voice memo, a failed Mac action, or a logged-in browser tab. A single spoken backlog turns scattered partial work into actionable continuity and is especially valuable when the pendant is worn away from the desk.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background summarizer/ranker over structured job and memory records; realtime only reads the short ranked list and routes the chosen continuation.
args.latency_budget: Ranked answer in under 4 seconds; continuation starts within 10 seconds after selection.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per query, mostly context retrieval and a small ranking call; continuation costs the normal planner/browser execution budget.
args.security_concerns: Only surface records scoped to the owner and current surface; do not read arbitrary browser content merely to build the list. Show provenance (“from yesterday’s Mac job”) and allow deletion of a thread from the pendant.
missing: A unified unfinished-thread index joining voice runs, jobs, receipts, browser findings, and task facts without duplicating their source data
Thread identity and deduplication across retries and handoffs
A continuation endpoint that rehydrates a selected thread into the correct Mac/browser agent with stale-state checks
A compact spoken disambiguation format and pendant-side selection gesture

args.user_asks: When you do something for me, let me ask “why did you choose that?” and hear a short, honest explanation that separates what the system observed, what it inferred, what it changed, and what remains uncertain—across the Mac, browser, and relay.
args.why_useful: A single completion receipt says what happened, but not whether the decision was based on a page observation, an owner preference, or a guess. This would let the owner audit an action from the pendant without reopening the Mac, catch mistaken assumptions, and correct the underlying preference rather than merely undoing one result.
args.model_tier: Record structured observation/decision/action provenance during execution; use a cheap summarizer for the explanation and realtime only for the spoken answer. Escalate to vision or planner logs only when the owner asks for detail.
args.latency_budget: A short explanation in under 3 seconds from cached provenance; detailed reconstruction under 15 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 for a cached short explanation; $0.03–$0.15 when reconstructing multiple agent traces or page evidence.
args.security_concerns: Explanations can quote private page text or commands. Redact secrets and limit the default to actor, evidence class, confidence, and outcome; expose raw evidence only after an explicit request and enforce the same owner/session scope as the source job.
missing: A causality/provenance record linking perception evidence, judgement, selected action, and observed result across agents
A stable spoken reference to the last action or a selected job from the pendant
A redaction and confidence policy that distinguishes observed facts from model rationale
A route that gathers the linked Mac, browser, and relay records into a compact explanation

transcript.summary: Recorded three owner-facing capabilities: (1) a cross-surface work bookmark that captures Mac/browser state and restores it later, (2) a unified unfinished-thread spoken backlog that resumes selected work, and (3) source-grounded explanations of what the agents observed, inferred, changed, and still do not know. The blocked-task question/answer channel was proposed but rejected as an existing backlog item, so it was not counted. The first needs an atomic state snapshot and restore planner; the second needs a unified thread index and continuation endpoint; the third needs linked provenance across perception, judgement, action, and result records.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the existing /ops/history and voice-run records already expose enough structured provenance and active-window identity to implement the recorded ideas, or whether those fields must be added at their source.
