args.user_asks: “When I’m on a call, translate what the other person says into my ear, and translate my reply back in their language.”
args.why_useful: This would turn the worn pendant into a private, low-latency interpreter for calls and in-person conversations: the Mac supplies the active call or meeting audio, while the pendant supplies the owner’s speech and discreet translated playback. The owner can participate without staring at a screen or handing a phone around.
args.model_tier: Realtime for speech segmentation, translation, and short turn-taking; a cheaper background model may detect language and maintain a glossary between turns.
args.latency_budget: Under 1.5 seconds from the end of the other speaker’s utterance to translated playback; under 800 ms for language identification after the first phrase.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per minute depending on realtime audio-token pricing; Mac audio capture and Opus transport dominate bandwidth, not model context.
args.security_concerns: Call audio and the owner’s replies leave the Mac and relay. The active call identity, language pair, and a visible/on-device listening indicator must be explicit; never keep raw call audio after the turn unless the owner asks. Translation can be wrong, so the owner needs a button interruption path and a short confidence caveat for uncertain phrases.
missing: A Mac system-audio capture and source-selection action that can feed the active call into the relay without recording unrelated applications
A duplex low-latency audio stream distinct from the current press-to-speak request/response turn
A translation session state machine with language detection, glossary, interruption, and echo suppression
A relay-to-pendant audio channel that can interleave translated speech with the owner’s normal assistant reply

args.user_asks: “Make this a handoff: I’ll start explaining on the pendant, then put the full context and the next step on my Mac so I can continue there without repeating myself.”
args.why_useful: The owner can begin a thought while walking and continue at the desk with the exact transcript, unresolved entities, decisions, and proposed next action visible in the right Mac app. This removes the costly failure mode where a useful wearable conversation disappears when the owner reaches the computer.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the spoken capture and a compact handoff summary; a cheaper background model extracts entities, open questions, and app-specific placement after the turn.
args.latency_budget: A spoken acknowledgement in under 500 ms; a usable Mac handoff within 3 seconds of the owner releasing the button.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per handoff, dominated by transcription and the summary; the stable memory projection should avoid resending the whole history.
args.security_concerns: The handoff may contain private speech and must be scoped to the owner’s selected destination. Show the source transcript and generated action separately so an invented detail cannot silently become a task. Do not place secrets into an app chosen only by inference.
missing: A first-class handoff object tying a voice run to transcript, summary, destination, and acknowledgement
A Mac action that opens or focuses the selected destination and presents the handoff atomically rather than typing fragments into whichever app is frontmost
A pendant command or button gesture to request handoff completion and a durable failure notice if the Mac is asleep

args.change: Build a cross-device 'presence and intent lease' shared by the pendant, relay, Mac planner, and browser harness. A voice turn receives a short-lived lease containing the owner’s explicit target (active call, selected browser tab, named app, or no target), origin timestamp, and cancellation state. Mac/browser actions must report which lease they consumed, and the pendant must be able to cancel it with one press. On reconnect, the relay reconciles leases and emits one truthful outcome instead of replaying stale actions.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “use this tab” or “stop that” while away from the keyboard and know the action applies to the intended screen—not a later tab or a different app—and that a dropped connection will not cause a stale command to fire hours afterward.
args.effort: High: protocol and storage changes in relay, Mac planner, browser command queue, and pendant firmware, plus race-condition tests for sleep, reconnect, and cancellation.
args.risk: A lease could expire while an action is mid-flight or cancellation could arrive after a mutation. Every action needs a visible consumed/expired/cancelled receipt, and existing undo paths must remain available. Recovery is to surface the uncertain state rather than claim success.
args.cost_impact: Low API cost; one small lease record and receipt per turn. Engineering cost is concentrated in concurrency and integration testing.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 100 ms for lease validation locally; reconnect reconciliation may take seconds and must be spoken as pending rather than hidden.
args.security_impact: Improves isolation by binding actions to an explicit target and expiry, but the target metadata itself can reveal app/site usage. Encrypt it in transit and redact it from general logs.
depends_on: A real relay capability manifest so lease consumers can be validated rather than inferred
A Mac/browser acknowledgement route carrying action receipts and target identity
Pendant firmware support for a cancel event without ending or corrupting the current audio session

Capture only the frontmost window or an owner-selected region, discard the image after the answer, and redact known credential fields before relay upload. Acting must be separately represented from describing, with an explicit spoken “do it” turn.

A vision-loop result contract that returns grounded regions, OCR text, and uncertainty rather than only free-form prose

A way for the pendant to interrupt a long visual explanation and request only the next actionable sentence

This would make the pendant a reliable handoff point across away/home transitions: the owner can leave without memorizing state, and return to a truthful, compact continuation rather than a generic completion alert.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial capture and final short spoken summary; background Mac planner and browser work use a cheaper slower model, with deterministic state reconciliation in the relay.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; checkpoint on each completed subtask; final result may take minutes and is delivered asynchronously when the pendant reconnects.
args.cost_estimate: About 1 realtime turn plus 3–10 background planner/browser calls per workflow; dominant cost is computer-use perception, not the spoken acknowledgement.

args.user_asks: “Turn this thought into a finished, filed result later—research it, draft it in the right app, and tell me what you decided to leave unresolved.”
args.why_useful: Offline voice memos can preserve words, but today they do not become useful work. This would bridge the worn device's fleeting capture to authenticated browser research and Mac artifact creation, while preserving uncertainty instead of silently producing a half-finished document.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only capture confirmation and a one-sentence result; background uses a cheaper planner/research model, with the Mac/browser agents doing local authenticated actions.
args.latency_budget: Capture confirmation under 1 second; owner need not remain connected. First progress event within 30 seconds of a worker becoming available; completion is asynchronous.
args.cost_estimate: One short realtime call, then typically 2–6 background research/planning calls and a few browser/Mac actions. Browser computer-use screenshots dominate cost.

missing: A durable memo-to-work item promotion path with provenance from the pendant recording
Background worker execution for queued work (not merely a user-facing reminder)
Artifact provenance linking each draft claim to browser/page evidence and each mutation to a receipt
A relay inbox payload that can carry a concise result plus unresolved items

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can currently hear that work finished, but cannot interrogate the result from the pendant. This makes autonomous action understandable while walking or away from the Mac, and catches wrong assumptions before they become forgotten state.
args.effort: Medium: normalize plan/action/receipt evidence into a decision trace, add a job-linked spoken query path, and render a dashboard drill-down. No new physical hardware required.

args.cost_impact: One inexpensive summarization call per inquiry; no continuous inference or audio storage.
args.latency_impact: Target under 2 seconds for a short trace from existing receipts; dashboard detail can load asynchronously.
args.security_impact: Adds a new way to expose action evidence through voice, so apply existing surface scoping and redact secrets, tokens, and page text.

args.user_asks: When I say “take care of this,” have the pendant, relay, Mac, and my logged-in browser collaborate until the real-world result is verified—not merely until an action was attempted—and tell me exactly what remains if verification fails.
args.why_useful: Today the owner can hand work to one downstream surface and later ask for a job status, but cannot get a single accountable loop spanning a Mac app and an authenticated browser. This would turn vague spoken delegation into a trustworthy outcome, especially when the owner is away from the Mac.
args.model_tier: Use relay-realtime only to clarify the initial utterance and narrate concise updates; use the cheaper Mac planner for planning, browser harness for authenticated web state, and a background verification worker for retries and reconciliation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; first plan in 5–10 seconds; completion may take minutes. The owner should be able to stop talking and receive a later pendant alert.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per delegated task depending on planner retries and browser verification; verification and retries dominate, not the spoken turn.
args.security_concerns: The browser session may expose private data to the planner and relay. Keep page contents scoped to the task, retain only a redacted receipt, and require an explicit owner policy for irreversible external effects. Never claim success from a click receipt alone.
missing: A durable cross-surface task state machine with plan, execute, verify, retry, and compensating-action states
A browser-side verification contract that returns evidence rather than only action success
A background worker/alarm that continues the loop while the Mac is offline and resumes when it returns
A single pendant-facing completion event containing evidence and an actionable failure reason

args.user_asks: Save my current work moment when I press the pendant: include what I said, the Mac's open apps and windows, and the browser's logged-in tabs; later say “restore the moment from yesterday” and put me back where I was, without reopening anything that has become unsafe or stale.
args.why_useful: A wearable can mark the instant an interruption happens, but today a spoken note, Mac state, and browser session are separate and not restorable as one unit. This would make the pendant a genuine interruption-and-recovery device for the owner's real work.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the short spoken label. Use a cheaper background model to summarize and redact the snapshot, and deterministic Mac/browser adapters to capture and restore state.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 1 second and snapshot completion under 10 seconds. Restore should begin immediately, with a concise report of stale or unavailable items.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per snapshot/restore; screenshots, browser metadata, and model summarization dominate storage and cost.
args.security_concerns: Logged-in URLs, window titles, and screenshots can contain secrets. Encrypt snapshots, default to metadata rather than page bodies, apply a per-surface retention period, and show the owner exactly which tabs/apps will be restored before any destructive replacement.
missing: A versioned workspace-snapshot schema shared by Mac and browser adapters
Mac actions to enumerate and restore window/app state, including safe stale-state checks
Browser extension export/import of tab groups and session identifiers without sending page contents
A durable encrypted snapshot store and a pendant gesture/voice command to select snapshots

args.user_asks: While a delegated task is running, let me press the pendant and say a correction like “skip that site and use the second result”; resume the existing Mac/browser job from its checkpoint, preserving useful work instead of starting over.
args.why_useful: Today the pendant can interrupt speech, and the owner can learn a job's status, but cannot safely steer an in-flight multi-step task. A correction currently means abandoning the context or waiting for a wrong workflow to finish. This gives the owner practical control while away from the Mac.
args.model_tier: Use relay-realtime for the short correction and intent extraction; use a cheaper planner to compute a delta against the checkpoint; let deterministic adapters execute only the changed suffix.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the correction in under 2 seconds, checkpoint in under 5 seconds, and resume within 15 seconds. The owner should hear whether the old branch was cancelled, preserved, or already irreversible.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per correction, mostly planner context and any browser reinspection; materially cheaper than replanning the entire task.
args.security_concerns: Cancellation races can leave partial external changes. Persist an action journal, mark irreversible steps as already committed, never replay them, and include the exact checkpoint and affected surfaces in the spoken receipt. The owner’s correction and page evidence should have bounded retention.
missing: Cooperative pause/cancel/checkpoint semantics in the Mac planner and browser command queue
A job action journal with idempotency keys and a dependency graph of completed steps
Relay routing that can associate a new utterance with the active job without inventing a second protocol
A planner mode that produces a minimal delta plan and explicitly reports irreversible steps

args.user_asks: Tell me when that Mac job finishes, even if I stop talking.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing: the owner can hand off a task and walk away, and still get a concise, timely result without polling.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the quick confirmation; cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarizing completion.
args.latency_budget: Immediate spoken confirmation within a second; completion notice can arrive minutes later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job; cost dominated by job polling on the Mac/relay side and short audio delivery.
args.security_concerns: Completion summaries may contain sensitive filenames or content; keep messages short, avoid quoting full data, and require confirmation for destructive actions.

args.user_asks: What’s going on with my system right now?
args.why_useful: A fast health snapshot reduces confusion when the Mac, browser, and wearable disagree. It’s a quick sanity check before deeper troubleshooting.
args.model_tier: Realtime to summarize; background tiers to gather details if needed.
args.latency_budget: Under a second for a summary; a deeper report can be deferred.
args.cost_estimate: Low; mostly reads like status endpoints and job summaries.
args.security_concerns: Status can reveal app names, URLs, or device presence; keep the default summary high level.
missing: A unified relay-side status aggregator; today status is scattered across Mac endpoints and job logs.
A consistent presence signal for the pendant when LTE is unregistered (USB-attached is real today).

args.user_asks: Summarize and prioritize the notifications and results you’ve queued for me.
args.why_useful: When the owner returns after a busy day, they need one coherent digest instead of a stream of unrelated pings.
args.model_tier: Background model for ranking and summarization; Realtime only for the spoken top items.
args.latency_budget: Digest generation can take seconds; spoken top summary should be brief.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; dominated by summarization tokens and reading multiple sources.
args.security_concerns: Digesting across sources risks mixing contexts; keep sources labeled and avoid exposing sensitive content without confirmation.
missing: A unified queue model across existing inbox/outbox mechanisms; today they’re implemented as separate subsystems.
A standard schema for priority, expiry, and source labeling across alerts, job results, and memos.

args.change: Expose a relay capability manifest endpoint (e.g., GET /capabilities) for the relay surface itself, mirroring what the Mac publishes, so the relay agent can inventory its own routes and tools without blind probing.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer routing mistakes and less wasted time means faster, more reliable voice interactions.
args.effort: Medium: implement endpoint, wire it to the relay router/tool registry, add tests.
args.risk: Low: disclosure risk if it exposes sensitive internals; mitigate with auth and redaction.
args.cost_impact: Minimal runtime cost; small development cost.
args.latency_impact: Improves routing decisions; negligible overhead.
args.security_impact: Requires strict auth and output filtering to avoid leaking secrets.

result.why: This restates something the system already has, so it was not recorded.
result.alreadyHave: Publish a relay capability manifest endpoint (like the Mac’s /capabilities) so relay-realtime can inventory its own routes/tools instead of probing blind.
result.next: Propose something this does not already cover, or say what it should become that it is not today.

args.change: Implement a real completion-notification pipeline: job watcher emits state transitions, relay formats a short spoken summary, and delivers via the existing inbox model to pendant/phone/dashboard. Use TTL and idempotent delivery.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can trust the system to finish work and report back without babysitting it.
args.effort: High: needs watcher, formatter, delivery, and storage semantics.
args.risk: Medium: duplicate or missing notifications; mitigate with receipts, retries, and idempotency keys.
args.cost_impact: Moderate; polling and delivery/storage dominate.
args.latency_impact: Completion can be delayed by polling interval; acceptable for background work.
args.security_impact: Summaries may contain sensitive info; default to minimal content and label sources.

args.change: Wire the existing memory projection into the live conversation context builder so each turn sends a small, stable head plus task-relevant tail instead of the legacy blocks.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Responses get more relevant, and the system becomes cheaper and faster without losing important preferences.
args.effort: Medium: replace context assembly call site and validate output.
args.risk: Low to medium: wrong projection could omit critical facts; mitigate with tests and fallbacks.
args.cost_impact: Measured savings ~222 tokens/turn (59.4%); large cost reduction at scale.
args.latency_impact: Lower prompt size improves responsiveness.
args.security_impact: Projection already enforces scoped surfaces and sensitivity rules; keep them.

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving my desk—make a work capsule for this, and let me resume it from the pendant later exactly where I left off.”
args.why_useful: Today a spoken request can be handed to the Mac, but the handoff loses the page, window, selection, and unfinished reasoning that made the task understandable. A durable capsule would let the owner leave the Mac, continue by voice, and return to the same browser/Mac state rather than restarting or explaining everything.
args.model_tier: Realtime extracts a compact goal and asks one clarifying question at most; a cheaper background planner assembles the capsule and reconciles it when the Mac or browser reconnects.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; capsule creation under 10 seconds; reconnection and reconciliation can take 1–3 minutes.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per handoff depending on whether a background planner must summarize screenshots/page state; storage and polling dominate, not realtime inference.
args.security_concerns: Capsules may contain authenticated page text and private documents. Encrypt at rest, scope each artifact to its originating surface, expire stale page snapshots, and never read a page merely because it is in a capsule without the owner asking to resume.
missing: A first-class capsule schema containing goal, transcript excerpt, browser tab/page snapshot, Mac window/app state, pending actions, and provenance
A reconnect reconciler that can detect stale UI and ask the owner instead of blindly replaying clicks
A pendant command to list/resume/abandon capsules

args.user_asks: “Is that actually done? Check everywhere you can, show me the evidence, and fix it if it isn’t.”
args.why_useful: The current system can report a queued job or inspect one surface, but it cannot establish truth when a task spans a browser portal, a local file, a Mac application, and a relay job. This gives the owner an evidence-backed answer and an optional repair, instead of a confident stale-memory reply.
args.model_tier: Realtime only classifies the question and speaks a short verdict; background perception gathers independent evidence and a judgement/action tier resolves contradictions or proposes the smallest repair.
args.latency_budget: Speak “checking” immediately; first verdict in 5–15 seconds, with late evidence pushed to the pendant and dashboard.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.03–$0.20 per check; browser snapshots and Mac round trips dominate, with a cheap model sufficient for evidence normalization.
args.security_concerns: Evidence can expose mail, documents, and authenticated portals. Keep raw evidence on its source surface, transmit hashes/excerpts by default, record provenance and timestamps, and require explicit confirmation before any repair that sends, deletes, buys, or publishes.
missing: A cross-surface claim/evidence model with freshness, authority, and contradiction fields
A verifier that queries Mac and browser in parallel and distinguishes “not found” from “could not check”
A repair planner that links each proposed mutation to the contradictory evidence and emits a receipt

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 7 of 8 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /watches/reports. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: “Approve this one sensitive action with my pendant.”
args.why_useful: A spoken approval can be overheard or replayed, and a Mac session can remain unlocked after the owner walks away. A deliberate physical press on the worn device would bind approval to the owner’s current challenge, while still allowing the owner’s stated maximum-access policy for ordinary reversible work.
args.model_tier: Realtime presents the exact pending action and challenge; firmware performs the physical confirmation; the relay verifies the signed response; the Mac/browser executes only the matching action hash.
args.latency_budget: Challenge to spoken confirmation under 2 seconds; physical approval to execution under 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per approval in inference; engineering is dominated by firmware cryptography, replay protection, and Mac/browser adapters.
args.security_concerns: This is an authorization primitive, not a generic confirmation dialog. Use device-bound keys, nonce and action-hash binding, short expiry, monotonic counters, cancellation on changed parameters, and an audit receipt. Never speak secrets in the challenge; require a fresh press for each high-impact action.
missing: Secure key provisioning and signed challenge-response support in the nRF9160 firmware
Relay endpoint for nonce issuance, verification, expiry, and replay detection
Mac and browser executors that refuse an action whose hash differs from the approved one
A clear pendant interaction pattern using the existing single button/LED without delaying ordinary presses

args.user_asks: “Use my pendant normally even when LTE is unavailable—fall back to the Mac’s USB serial link, then switch back to LTE without losing the conversation.”
args.why_useful: The wearable is physically connected and testable today, but an unregistered pendant cannot be a live voice front door. A transparent tethered mode would make the product usable at home and in development now, while preserving the same button, speaker, relay session, and queued delivery semantics when the owner walks away.
args.model_tier: Realtime stays on the relay; the Mac USB companion only transports framed audio/control and never becomes a second conversational model. A small local connectivity supervisor chooses USB or LTE and resumes the same session on link change.
args.latency_budget: USB press-to-first-audio should remain under 500 ms; link failover should be detected in under 2 seconds, with no more than one audio frame lost.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per-turn model cost beyond current realtime inference; implementation is primarily serial framing, reconnect state, and a Mac launch agent. No recurring cloud browser cost.
args.security_concerns: USB must be authenticated to the paired Mac, not accepted from arbitrary serial devices. Bind a session to a device identity, protect audio/control framing against injection, and visibly indicate which transport is active without exposing transcripts to unrelated local users.
missing: A Mac USB companion that terminates the nRF9160 serial protocol and forwards the existing audio pipeline
Relay session transport abstraction with resumable sequence numbers and duplicate-frame suppression
Firmware link arbitration and a clear tethered-versus-LTE status indication using the existing LED patterns

transcript.summary: Recorded four owner-facing proposals: resumable cross-surface work capsules, evidence-backed “is it done?” verification with optional repair, physical pendant-bound approval for sensitive actions, and USB/LTE-transparent live voice continuity. The strongest near-term value is tethered live voice: it makes the physically connected pendant usable today, while the strongest long-term safety/value is action approval bound to a real press on the worn device. Several proposals were flagged as close to backlog items, so they should be deduplicated rather than rephrased.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Which existing relay routes actually terminate the live USB serial/audio path and whether /approve is already a complete execution gate; the tool inventory is gone this round, so I cannot distinguish an unwired connector from a genuinely missing subsystem.

transcript.text: I’ll quickly inventory what’s available now and then I’ll tell you what’s missing and what to ask for next.

args.user_asks: Tell me when that Mac task finishes, even after I’m done talking.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing for long-running work: the owner can speak a request, walk away, and still get a short completion result without polling.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the initial acknowledgement; a cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarizing job output.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm monitoring is set, then asynchronous delivery minutes or hours later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job to register; ongoing cost dominated by periodic status checks and summary generation, not realtime speech.
args.security_concerns: Summaries may contain sensitive info from the Mac. Default to a short, non-detailed spoken result and avoid reading private notification bodies. Require confirmation before speaking detailed content to shared devices.
missing: A real relay event delivery mechanism for pendant/phone
A durable watch that triggers on job state changes rather than ad-hoc polling
A compact, privacy-filtered summarizer for job results

args.user_asks: If a task fails, tell me what went wrong and offer the shortest safe next step.
args.why_useful: Failure handling is where assistants feel real. The owner hears a brief diagnosis and can choose to retry, open the relevant app, or send a note—without digging through logs.
args.model_tier: Realtime for triage phrasing; cheaper tier for log/receipt analysis.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to acknowledge, then a brief spoken summary once the failure is detected.
args.cost_estimate: Dominated by retrieving receipts/logs and summarizing them; minimal realtime cost.
args.security_concerns: Receipts may contain sensitive text. Use redaction and default to high-level explanations; ask before reading detailed content aloud.
missing: A reliable way to detect failure states and map them to user-facing categories
Redaction rules for spoken summaries
An intent path to trigger the shortest safe next action

args.change: Implement a real job completion delivery path: when a job transitions to complete/failed/needs_attention, emit a durable, privacy-filtered notification to the pendant and/or phone. Use a watch abstraction for state change detection, and deliver via a relay-visible endpoint instead of relying on tools that are only schemas.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can stop babysitting tasks and still get a trustworthy, brief update on what happened.
args.effort: Medium to high: needs a state-change watcher, a delivery pipeline, retries, and a storage policy for undelivered notifications.
args.risk: Speaking sensitive content aloud or delivering to the wrong device. Mitigate with short default summaries, explicit device targeting, and opt-in detail.
args.cost_impact: Moderate. Overhead comes from job state checks and delivery retries; realtime cost stays low.
args.latency_impact: No impact on normal conversation; asynchronous completion adds a small delay but removes user polling.
args.security_impact: High if done poorly. Needs strict redaction, device targeting, and audit logs.
depends_on: A relay capability manifest or equivalent route discovery for the relay surface
A durable delivery queue (reusing existing inbox/outbox mechanisms where possible)

args.user_asks: “Is this invoice actually paid?” Reconcile the evidence across my email/files on the Mac, my authenticated browser portal, and my iPhone, then tell me the answer, confidence, and exactly which sources disagree.
args.why_useful: Today each surface can be queried separately, but nobody can establish a trustworthy answer when systems disagree. This turns the pendant into a cross-system fact checker rather than a launcher.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay handles the short spoken question; faculty-perception extracts dated evidence from Mac, browser, and iPhone in parallel; a cheaper background judge model normalizes entities, detects contradictions, and computes confidence; relay speaks only the conclusion and offers the source trail.
args.latency_budget: First acknowledgement under 500 ms; parallel evidence within 10 s; if a portal is slow, speak a provisional result and push a corrected result when the watch completes.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.03–$0.15 per investigation, dominated by browser/iPhone screenshots and the judge pass; no expensive realtime generation beyond the final sentence.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents, mail, files, and phone data leave their surfaces to the relay/judge. Keep raw evidence encrypted and short-lived, redact unrelated message bodies, show source names and timestamps, and require confirmation before any suggested payment or correction.
missing: A cross-surface evidence envelope with entity IDs, timestamps, provenance, and contradiction links
Parallel Mac/browser/iOS evidence collection under one investigation job
A confidence-and-disagreement judge and a spoken/source-trail result format
Explicit retention and redaction policy for investigation evidence

args.user_asks: “Save exactly where I am and get me back here tomorrow.” Later, when I press the pendant, restore the relevant Mac app and browser tabs, reopen the right document or message, and briefly remind me what I was trying to do.
args.why_useful: People lose work not because files vanish, but because the surrounding state vanishes. A durable, cross-device return point would let the owner leave the Mac without reconstructing a task from memory.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay records the intent and gives a one-sentence acknowledgement. A background state-capture model turns active Mac/browser/iPhone state into a minimal semantic resume packet; on return, mac-planner executes restoration and relay summarizes differences before speaking.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 1 s. Save within 5 s. Restoration may take up to 20 s, with a short progress alert and a final spoken summary.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per save/restore, mostly screenshot summarization and one planning pass; storage is small JSON plus references, not copied documents.
args.security_concerns: Resume packets may contain document titles, URLs, selected text, and private app state. Encrypt them, allow per-packet expiry/deletion, never store passwords or page bodies, and require confirmation before reopening a sensitive app or sending anything.
missing: A first-class resume-packet schema with semantic intent, app/window identity, tab references, selection anchors, and expiry
Mac and browser snapshot adapters plus iPhone Mirroring state capture
A restoration engine that tolerates changed tabs/documents and reports what could not be restored
A pendant gesture/voice command and durable packet listing

args.user_asks: “Why didn’t that work?” After any failed or partial request, reconstruct a causal timeline across my pendant audio, relay job, Mac actions, browser commands, and iPhone actions, identify the first failure and what state each surface was left in, then offer the safest recovery.
args.why_useful: Today a failure is reported as a vague job error and the owner has to interrogate every node manually. A causal timeline would make the hive accountable and recoverable, especially when one device succeeded while another timed out.
args.model_tier: A cheap background correlator joins append-only operation receipts and device telemetry by operation ID; faculty-perception classifies the first fault versus downstream symptoms; realtime relay gives a short explanation, while the dashboard exposes the detailed timeline.
args.latency_budget: Speak an immediate “I’m tracing it” acknowledgement under 500 ms; initial diagnosis in 3 s; deeper correlation and recovery plan within 15 s.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.04 per diagnosis, dominated by log retrieval and an inexpensive correlation model; no browser or screenshot work unless the evidence requires it.
args.security_concerns: Logs can contain URLs, filenames, transcripts, and device identifiers. Redact payloads by default, retain hashes and metadata longer than raw content, bind records to an owner-visible operation ID, and never silently retry a consequential action.
missing: A shared operation ID propagated from pendant capture through relay, planner, browser, and iOS
Append-only receipts with start/end, retries, partial effects, and device health snapshots
A causal correlator that distinguishes first failure from timeout cascades
A recovery planner that can verify current state before proposing or executing repair

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Cross-surface evidence reconciliation** — ask “Is this invoice actually paid?” and have the system reconcile Mac files/email, authenticated browser data, and iPhone evidence, including disagreements and confidence.

2. **Durable cross-device resume points** — say “Save exactly where I am,” then later restore the relevant Mac app, browser tabs, document, and task context from the pendant.

3. **Causal failure diagnosis** — ask “Why didn’t that work?” and receive a timeline across pendant audio, relay jobs, Mac actions, browser commands, and iPhone actions, identifying the first failure and any partial side effects.

The single most useful is likely **causal failure diagnosis**: a distributed assistant must explain not only what it intended, but what actually happened.

What these still need:

- A shared operation ID propagated across every node.
- Structured receipts containing timing, retries, partial effects, and device health.
- Cross-surface evidence and state schemas.
- A background correlation/judgment step separate from realtime speech.
- Recovery planning that verifies current state before retrying.
- Privacy-preserving retention and redaction for URLs, documents, transcripts, and phone data.
- For resume points, semantic snapshots and restoration tolerant of changed tabs or documents.
I’ll take a quick look at what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few big, useful capabilities and call out what’s missing to make them real.

args.user_asks: “Tell me when that’s done, even after I stop talking.”
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful behavior for a wearable assistant: you can hand off a task, walk away, and still get a clear completion update without babysitting a screen.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the initial acknowledgement, cheaper background model for monitoring and summarizing updates.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm the watch is set; completion delivery can be seconds to minutes later depending on the task.
args.cost_estimate: Low per request. The expensive part is polling job status; that should run on a cheaper tier and only send a short notification back to the relay.
args.security_concerns: Notifications must not reveal sensitive content on a shared speaker. Use short summaries, redact details, and require confirmation before speaking anything that looks like secrets or financial info.
missing: A real job-completion watcher that runs without an active voice session
A delivery mechanism to pendant/phone (device inbox) that can store and surface short text safely
A bridge to render spoken audio without storing it on-device by default
built_from: offline_alert_inbox (existing pattern, not a new queue)
mac_delegate (for tasks that need complex planning)

args.user_asks: “Bookmark this moment and attach it to what I’m working on.”
args.why_useful: The owner can capture a quick thought while away from the Mac and later find the exact file, tab, or project state it refers to, without rummaging through notes.
args.model_tier: Realtime for capture; mac-bridge/browser for context binding; cheaper tier for indexing/search later.
args.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm capture; binding may take a few seconds depending on Mac/browser state.
args.cost_estimate: Low ongoing cost. The main cost is capturing context snapshots (browser tabs, open files) when binding, which should happen only when the owner asks.
args.security_concerns: Context binding can expose sensitive URLs, document paths, or content. Store minimal references (IDs, titles, hashes) and require confirmation before including sensitive text.
missing: A typed capture payload that can represent voice memo, bookmark, or text note as items in the existing outbox/inbox queue
Reliable context snapshot/restore for browser and workspace state
A unified index so voice search can find captures by project/task
built_from: GET /sessions and POST /sessions for context linkage
memory store/projection (once wired into live prompts)

args.user_asks: “Move this conversation and unfinished task to my Mac when I sit down, without making me repeat anything.” The pendant should hand an active voice task to the Mac, where the owner can continue it with the exact spoken context, discovered artifacts, pending plan, and current uncertainty.
args.why_useful: The pendant is the only surface available while away and the Mac is the only surface with rich control. Today the owner must restart or remember what was said; a true task baton would make the system feel like one assistant rather than disconnected sessions.
args.model_tier: Realtime model handles the short handoff summary and spoken continuity; mac-planner performs the work; mac-vision/browser supply current UI state; a cheaper background model can compress the transcript and artifacts.
args.latency_budget: Handoff acknowledgement under 2 seconds; Mac rehydration under 10 seconds after the Mac is detected. The owner should hear one sentence immediately, not wait for the whole task.
args.cost_estimate: About one realtime turn for the handoff plus a cheap summarization call, typically under $0.03; the dominant cost is rehydrating large browser/UI artifacts, which should be content-addressed rather than resent.
args.security_concerns: The baton must be bound to the owner’s paired devices and expire. It must carry artifact references and action scope, not blindly replay credentials or stale UI actions. The owner should be able to revoke a baton from the pendant or dashboard; no new confirmation gate is required for reversible work.
missing: A paired-device presence/discovery signal that can announce the Mac is available
A durable handoff record containing transcript, artifact references, plan, and uncertainty
Mac-side session rehydration that can resume a task rather than start a new planner run
A continuation UI on the Mac and a compact pendant acknowledgement

args.user_asks: “Keep working until you hit a real ambiguity, then ask me exactly one useful question.” The assistant should run a multi-step Mac/browser task autonomously, pause only when observations create materially different next actions, speak the smallest discriminating question through the pendant, and resume with the answer.
args.why_useful: Long tasks fail today either by guessing through ambiguity or by dumping a whole plan on the owner. This would let the owner stay away from the Mac while still steering the few decisions that genuinely require human intent.
args.model_tier: mac-planner does ordinary planning and execution; mac-vision/browser provide observations; realtime is used only for the short ambiguity question and answer normalization; a cheaper judge model scores whether a question is actually decision-changing.
args.latency_budget: Continue automatically for ordinary steps. When blocked, surface a question within 3 seconds and resume within 5 seconds of the owner’s reply.
args.cost_estimate: One inexpensive judge call per suspected ambiguity and one realtime exchange only when needed, roughly $0.01–$0.05 per task; savings come from not invoking realtime for routine progress.
args.security_concerns: The system must show the evidence that caused the pause and record the selected branch. It must distinguish ambiguity from a high-impact action; this is an interaction mechanism, not an authorization gate. Stale observations must invalidate the pending question rather than silently applying the answer to a changed page.
missing: A planner protocol for typed pause/resume checkpoints with competing branches and evidence
A relay-to-pendant question/answer exchange that survives the normal turn ending
A stale-observation/version check across Mac and browser actions
A compact owner-visible decision log

args.user_asks: “At the end of the day, tell me what actually changed because of my assistant, what is still uncertain, and let me correct the record by voice.” The system should build an evidence-backed personal activity ledger from Mac action receipts, browser outcomes, relay conversations, and offline pendant notes, then speak a concise discrepancy-focused digest.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has scattered logs and no trustworthy answer to “what did it do?” or “what did I tell it that it failed to do?”. A ledger with provenance and corrections would make automation accountable and improve future decisions without pretending that an attempted action succeeded.
args.model_tier: A cheap background model clusters receipts and detects contradictions; realtime only conducts the short spoken review and applies explicit corrections; Mac/browser agents remain sources of evidence, not narrators of their own success.
args.latency_budget: Generate asynchronously in under a minute after the chosen cutoff; spoken review should begin in under 2 seconds when requested and fit in 30–60 seconds unless the owner asks for detail.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one background summarization call, about $0.01–$0.05 per digest; storage/indexing and receipt normalization dominate engineering cost, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Every claim needs provenance, timestamp, target surface, and confidence. Private browser content must be excluded unless explicitly included; corrections must be versioned rather than overwrite evidence. The digest should clearly separate completed, attempted, failed, and unknown.
missing: A cross-surface append-only activity ledger joining voice turns to Mac/browser job IDs
Receipt normalization and contradiction detection
A user-correction endpoint that creates scoped memory facts with provenance
A routine trigger and durable spoken delivery using the existing inbox semantics

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Portable task baton** — move an active pendant conversation and unfinished task to the Mac with its transcript, artifacts, plan, and uncertainty intact. Requires paired-device discovery, durable handoff records, and Mac-side session rehydration.

2. **Ambiguity-aware autonomous work** — let Mac/browser agents continue independently and interrupt the owner only when a genuinely decision-changing ambiguity appears, with one concise question and evidence. Requires pause/resume checkpoints, stale-observation checks, and a durable decision log.

3. **Evidence-backed activity ledger** — provide an end-of-day account of what actually changed, what failed, and what remains uncertain, using Mac/browser receipts and pendant conversations; allow corrections by voice. Requires an append-only cross-surface ledger, contradiction detection, provenance-preserving corrections, and routine delivery.
I’ll quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll suggest the next capabilities to add and what blockers remain.

args.user_asks: Tell me when the thing I asked the Mac to do finishes, even if I’m not talking to you anymore.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful “it just works” behavior: the owner can start a long task hands-free, walk away, and still get a concise completion signal instead of polling.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial voice; background monitoring should be a cheaper tier behind the relay.
args.latency_budget: Start monitoring immediately; delivery can be delayed by network, but should arrive as soon as the job state changes.
args.cost_estimate: Low per job: one status lookup plus an event delivery; dominant cost is job polling and audio delivery, not the initial voice turn.
args.security_concerns: Completion text can leak task intent. Keep spoken summaries short and avoid sensitive content. Confirm before speaking potentially sensitive details when possible.
missing: A real implementation for relay_event_push or an equivalent delivery route to pendant/phone
A durable job watcher that can emit events after the session ends (or wiring job_completion_watch to a real emitter)
Permission to post completion events if a new route is introduced

args.user_asks: What’s going on with my Mac right now?
args.why_useful: Quick status checks are a perfect pendant use: battery, wifi, and frontmost app help the owner decide whether to continue a task without touching the Mac.
args.model_tier: Realtime, because the owner is waiting for an answer.
args.latency_budget: Under a second for cached/fast paths; otherwise as fast as the Mac can respond.
args.cost_estimate: Very low; one status call per request.
args.security_concerns: Status is personal. Don’t over-collect; fetch only the fields asked for.

args.user_asks: Find the best way to do this, even if it means using my browser or multiple apps.
args.why_useful: This uses the hive mind: the relay captures the intent, the Mac planner executes, and the browser/OS surfaces do the fiddly work. It’s useful when the owner can’t predict the steps.
args.model_tier: Realtime to capture intent, then mac-planner for the multi-step workflow.
args.latency_budget: Seconds to plan, longer for execution; keep the spoken confirmation short.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; planning and multi-surface actions dominate.
args.security_concerns: May touch authenticated sessions and send messages. Use receipts and confirmations for high-impact actions.

args.change: Publish a relay capability manifest route, equivalent to the Mac agent’s /capabilities, so the relay can inventory its own routes and tools without blind probing.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, more reliable voice behavior: fewer wasted requests, better routing, and fewer “I can’t see my own endpoints” failures.
args.effort: Medium: implement a read-only endpoint that enumerates relay routes and tool schemas.
args.risk: Low; exposure is informational but should exclude secrets and internal-only routes.
args.cost_impact: Low ongoing cost; one small JSON response when requested.
args.latency_impact: Improves: less probing means lower latency overall.
args.security_impact: Must redact sensitive configuration and auth details.
depends_on: internal route registration metadata

result.why: This restates something the system already has, so it was not recorded.
result.alreadyHave: Publish a relay capability manifest endpoint (like the Mac’s /capabilities) so relay-realtime can inventory its own routes/tools instead of probing blind.
result.next: Propose something this does not already cover, or say what it should become that it is not today.

args.change: Add an enum-based routing tool for relay intents that maps directly onto real action types (the same vocabulary used by /plan and /execute), so routing is explicit and resolvable.
args.why_useful_to_owner: More accurate and predictable behavior from voice commands; fewer misroutes and less back-and-forth.
args.effort: Medium: define an enum schema and resolver that targets mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, or mac_delegate.
args.risk: Medium: misconfiguration could route actions incorrectly; mitigate with receipts and safe defaults.
args.cost_impact: Low; routing itself is cheap.
args.latency_impact: Improves by avoiding trial-and-error.
args.security_impact: Needs strict validation to prevent privilege escalation.
depends_on: existing action-type vocabulary from /plan and /execute

args.change: Wire the existing memory projection into the live conversation context builder so only relevant facts are injected per surface/task, reducing token cost and context churn.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster responses and fewer hallucinations because the assistant gets a cleaner, more relevant context.
args.effort: Medium: replace the legacy context composition with projectContext(surface, task).
args.risk: Medium: could omit needed context; mitigate with budget tuning and telemetry.
args.cost_impact: Improves: measured token savings per turn are significant.
args.latency_impact: Improves due to smaller prompts.
args.security_impact: Neutral; scope rules already exist.
depends_on: contextProjection.js already present
conversationContext.js injection point

args.user_asks: “I’m away from my Mac. Find the cheapest nonstop flight that fits my constraints, use my logged-in browser only for the final comparison, and tell me the best option with the exact tradeoffs.”
args.why_useful: This would turn the worn pendant into a trustworthy remote research agent: the relay captures constraints conversationally, the Mac planner searches broadly, and the authenticated browser session is used only where public tools cannot reach. The owner gets a decision-ready answer without manually shuttling links between devices.
args.model_tier: Realtime for constraint capture and a one-sentence clarification; mac-planner/background tier for search and comparison; browser harness only for authenticated pages; realtime again for the final spoken synthesis.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; 10–60 seconds for public search and logged-in comparison; push a concise result when complete, with a dashboard evidence trail.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.03–$0.20 per request depending on planner iterations and page extraction; browser calls and planner context dominate, not the short voice turns.
args.security_concerns: Search constraints and any authenticated page excerpts leave the pendant for relay/Mac processing. Never expose credentials to the model; retain only cited result snippets and URLs; require explicit confirmation before booking or purchasing.
missing: A durable cross-surface research job that can combine web_search/read_web_page with the owner's authenticated browser session
A result schema containing normalized options, constraints satisfied/violated, citations, and confidence
A relay completion path that can deliver the result after the voice turn without making the owner poll

args.user_asks: “When I say ‘quiet mode,’ make the whole hive private: stop speaking sensitive details, mute or lock the Mac/browser surfaces, and keep only a short confirmation on the pendant. When I say ‘resume,’ restore the previous state.”
args.why_useful: The owner can wear the device in public or around other people and change the privacy posture in one spoken command. It coordinates the pendant, relay, Mac audio/display, and browser rather than relying on one surface's local mute switch.
args.model_tier: Realtime intent recognition and immediate acknowledgement; deterministic Mac/browser state capture and restoration; no expensive model after the state transition.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge and begin enforcement in under 500 ms; complete surface changes within 2 seconds; if a surface is offline, state exactly which one remains unprotected.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01 per toggle; cost is dominated by one state snapshot and a few Mac/browser actions, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The privacy mode must fail closed for spoken content: if relay cannot verify a surface's state, it must not claim privacy. Store a signed pre-toggle snapshot, never log sensitive transcript text in the confirmation, and make resume restore only the states this command changed.
missing: A first-class privacy posture record spanning pendant, relay, Mac audio/notifications, and browser tabs
Atomic or compensating state transitions with per-surface acknowledgement and an offline-safe pendant indicator
A redacted status/result contract so the relay can confirm protection without repeating secrets

args.user_asks: “Remember this as a reusable way of working: whenever I ask for a client update, gather the latest project facts, draft a short email in my editor, and leave it ready for me to review—but never send it.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets a personalized command that compounds over time instead of repeating a multi-step workflow. The pendant supplies the trigger while the relay retrieves only relevant memory, the Mac gathers current material and drafts, and the browser can add context from an authenticated project page. The safety boundary is useful: preparation is automatic, sending remains impossible by construction.
args.model_tier: Realtime to capture and confirm the reusable recipe; background planner to execute each invocation; cheap deterministic memory projection and action validation; realtime only for the spoken result.
args.latency_budget: Recipe creation under 3 seconds; invocation acknowledgement under 1 second and draft completion within 30 seconds; push a completion alert if the owner walks away.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.10 per invocation depending on browser/planner steps; memory retrieval is cheap, while authenticated page extraction and drafting dominate.
args.security_concerns: Persist the recipe as a structured template, not unrestricted prompt text. Scope facts by surface/task, redact secrets, and enforce a hard no-send terminal action. Show source links and the draft location in the dashboard; deletion must remove both recipe and derived sensitive artifacts.
missing: A user-facing routine/recipe layer that stores parameterized multi-surface workflows rather than only fixed schedules
Binding from a spoken alias to a validated plan with current memory projection and browser findings
A no-send draft artifact contract and completion receipt that the Mac and relay both honor

args.change: Replace the live-turn prompt assembly in conversationContext.js with the existing surface/task-aware projectContext() projection, while preserving the stable preference/permission prefix and passing the current utterance as the task query. Add a compact projection hash and droppedForBudget count to the turn trace so downstream agents can explain which facts were actually supplied.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant will stop making the owner repeat editor, permission, timezone, and active-project facts, while irrelevant browser discoveries stop leaking into unrelated conversations. Follow-up commands like “send it to him” become more reliable and responses get shorter because the model receives the right context instead of a duplicated historical block.
args.effort: Small integration change plus regression tests across voice, Mac, and browser surfaces; validate with the existing measure-context-projection script and real follow-up turns.
args.risk: A too-narrow task match could omit a needed entity. Recover by retaining the projection fallback to freshest facts, logging dropped facts, and allowing a deliberate reveal-sensitive/debug path; keep the legacy formatter behind a feature flag for rollback.
args.cost_impact: Reduces prompt context by the measured ~222 tokens per turn (about 59% in the current store), lowering recurring inference cost; negligible runtime storage cost.
args.latency_impact: Slightly faster prompt construction and model generation due to fewer tokens; projection lookup is local.
args.security_impact: Improves least-privilege context because browser-sourced facts join only for matching tasks and sensitive facts remain gated by revealSensitive; audit the projection hash without recording values.
depends_on: The existing GET /memory/projection contract and contextProjection.js implementation
A task/surface value available at live-turn construction time

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving now. Keep working on the task I just started, and if it finishes, tell me the result; if it needs a decision, ask me one precise question on the pendant. I should also be able to say ‘cancel that’ or ‘undo the last change’ from anywhere.”
args.why_useful: The owner can physically walk away without abandoning work or babysitting a browser. This is more than a completion ping: the relay becomes a durable control surface for an active Mac/browser job, translating only actionable blockers into a short voice exchange and exposing cancellation/undo when available.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the initial handoff, blocker question, and cancel/undo intent; background planner and deterministic job monitor for execution; no expensive model while merely waiting.
args.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; blocker alerts within 5 seconds of detection; cancellation request acknowledged under 2 seconds; final summary delivered asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per delegated task outside the planner's normal execution cost; monitoring is mostly polling/event infrastructure, with inference only on blocker summaries.
args.security_concerns: A spoken cancel/undo must be bound to the owner's active session and job identity, not a vague historical reference. Do not claim completion without a receipt; if undo is unavailable, say so and preserve the exact failure state. Pending questions must expire rather than silently authorizing a mutation.
missing: A durable voice-owned job lease linking a pendant session to one or more Mac/browser jobs
A blocker protocol that pauses safely, asks one constrained question, and resumes with the answer
Real asynchronous delivery from job state changes to the pendant, plus authenticated cancel/undo resolution for spoken references

args.user_asks: “Tell me what changed in my work since yesterday, but only after checking the project page in my logged-in browser and the local files on my Mac. Cite each change, flag contradictions, and say what I should do next.”
args.why_useful: This gives the owner a single spoken situation report assembled from sources that no one node can reach alone: authenticated browser state, local Mac files, and the relay's remembered project context. Contradiction detection prevents a polished but false summary, which is especially valuable when the owner is away from the screen.
args.model_tier: Background planner gathers and normalizes sources; a judgement tier compares claims and ranks next actions; realtime only asks for scope and speaks the short result.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; deliver within 30–90 seconds; provide a dashboard evidence view while the pendant speaks only the top changes and contradictions.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.25 per report; Mac file inspection, authenticated browser extraction, and claim comparison dominate.
args.security_concerns: Limit file paths and browser pages to the named project; preserve source URLs and file timestamps; do not read unrelated mail or secrets. Mark stale/blocked sources explicitly and never infer ‘no change’ from an unavailable surface.
missing: A cross-surface snapshot job with a shared cutoff time and source freshness metadata
A normalized claim/evidence format and contradiction detector spanning browser text and Mac artifacts
A spoken compression policy that retains uncertainty and cites evidence in the dashboard

transcript.summary: Recorded four owner-facing proposals: cross-surface authenticated research with tradeoffs, a coordinated whole-hive privacy posture, reusable spoken workflows that produce drafts without sending, and a durable walk-away job lease with blocker questions/cancel/undo. Also recorded a cross-surface evidence report that compares authenticated browser state with local Mac artifacts and flags contradictions. The strongest immediate value is walk-away control: the owner can leave the desk while retaining truthful, voice-level control over work. The required changes are durable job ownership, blocker/resume semantics, evidence normalization, and real asynchronous delivery to the pendant—not another local action wrapper.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the existing job_completion_watch and relay_event_push paths are actually wired end-to-end to a live pendant, and whether /workbench/contexts can provide source snapshots suitable for cross-surface evidence comparison. The proposal recorder accepted these as missing or unverified rather than assuming they exist.

transcript.text: I’ll quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out what’s still missing.

args.user_asks: Tell me when that finishes.
args.why_useful: This is the big one: the owner can start a long Mac task, walk away, and still get a spoken update later without babysitting a screen.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the initial confirmation; background polling should be a cheaper model in the Mac/relay tier.
args.latency_budget: Under 1 second to acknowledge the request; completion notification can arrive minutes later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per request. The expensive part is repeated job status checks, so it should back off and stop once terminal.
args.security_concerns: Notifications could leak task names. Keep text short, avoid sensitive content, and require confirmation before speaking if the task might contain secrets.
missing: A real completion-event delivery path to the pendant/phone (relay_event_push is unresolved).
A background watcher that can run after the session ends, with a store for subscriptions and backoff.
A way to render and deliver audio safely without storing routine audio on-device.

args.user_asks: If I say something like 'the Outlook thing', check its status.
args.why_useful: Voice references are fuzzy; this lets the owner talk naturally and still get accurate status without re-identifying job IDs.
args.model_tier: Realtime, because the owner is waiting on a spoken answer.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a spoken status.
args.cost_estimate: Very low; a single read of relay job records.
args.security_concerns: Must not invent success. Speak the tool’s spoken field verbatim, and avoid adding details.
missing: None for basic status; but richer receipts would benefit from structured job metadata.

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: All 3 pieces you named already exist: relay_job_status, /jobs/:jobid, /jobs/:jobid/receipts. So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.user_asks: File a bug report from the pendant logs.
args.why_useful: Turns real-world failures into actionable reports automatically, which is huge for a wearable under development.
args.model_tier: Realtime to confirm capture; Mac/relay to assemble and file the report.
args.latency_budget: Capture should be immediate; filing can take longer and be asynchronous.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate; log upload plus report generation. Dominated by transport and any attachments.
args.security_concerns: Logs may contain sensitive info. Redact secrets and require confirmation before sending externally.
missing: A standardized UART log ingestion route from relay to Mac.
A report generator that can attach firmware version, timestamps, and minimal reproduction.
A safe destination (issue tracker integration) with credentials managed on the Mac.

args.change: Implement a real completion notification pipeline that persists subscriptions, polls job state with exponential backoff, and emits a minimal event to the pendant/phone. Replace the unresolved relay_event_push with a concrete route and delivery mechanism.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can start something, leave, and hear the result later — the most useful “always-on” behavior for a wearable assistant.
args.effort: Medium to high. Needs a small subscription store, a polling worker, and a delivery adapter.
args.risk: Duplicate notifications or missing terminal events. Mitigate with idempotent receipts and terminal-state checks.
args.cost_impact: Low ongoing cost if polling is backoff-based; storage cost is tiny.
args.latency_impact: Adds delay between completion and notification depending on polling cadence.
args.security_impact: Task names may be sensitive; keep messages short and avoid including secrets.
depends_on: A delivery path to pendant/phone (or reuse an existing inbox mechanism).
A place to run background polling after the voice session ends.

args.change: Standardize a UART log capture path: relay collects pendant/bridge logs during a session, forwards to the Mac, and the Mac can attach them to bug reports. Include firmware version, build ID, and timestamps.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When something breaks in the field, they get a ready-to-file report instead of a vague complaint.
args.effort: Medium. Needs a streaming/rotation format and a small ingestion route.
args.risk: Logs can be large or contain secrets. Mitigate with size limits, redaction, and owner confirmation before upload.
args.cost_impact: Low to moderate; dominated by upload size.
args.latency_impact: Capture is streaming; upload may delay report creation.
args.security_impact: Potential data leakage; default to local-only until confirmed.

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.change: Wire the existing memory projection into the live conversation context builder so the relay sends stable preference/permission headers and task-relevant tail, reducing repeated tokens and improving responsiveness.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, cheaper turns and more consistent behavior without needing to repeat themselves.
args.effort: Low to medium. It is a targeted wiring change in conversationContext.js.
args.risk: Context regressions if the projection differs from legacy blocks. Mitigate with side-by-side checks and token budget telemetry.
args.cost_impact: Reduces per-turn token cost (already measured ~59% savings).
args.latency_impact: Lower latency from smaller prompts.
args.security_impact: No new data leaves; projection already enforces surface scoping.

args.user_asks: Call my dentist and reschedule me for the earliest slot next week; handle the conversation and interrupt me only when you need a decision.
args.why_useful: The owner can delegate a real-world phone task while walking, without sitting at the Mac or manually relaying what the other person says. This is a genuinely cross-surface capability: the pendant supplies intent and decisions, the Mac/iPhone places the call, and the relay remains the low-latency conversational coach.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for the owner's short decisions and turn-taking; gpt-5.6-luna for call planning and extraction; gpt-4.1-mini vision only for phone UI state.
args.latency_budget: Initial call setup under 10 seconds; spoken decision requests under 2 seconds; otherwise the phone conversation proceeds in real time.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.05-$0.30 per call depending on duration and transcription; telephony audio streaming and model inference dominate.
args.security_concerns: The counterpart's voice and potentially health or financial details leave the phone and pass through the relay. The owner must explicitly start the call, hear who is being called, and be able to stop it immediately; do not silently record or send commitments beyond the requested constraint.
missing: A bidirectional iPhone telephony-audio bridge exposed to the Mac agent (iPhone Mirroring UI alone cannot safely provide counterpart audio to the relay)
Call-state and hangup controls with a hard physical stop from the pendant
Streaming speech-to-text/text-to-speech turn exchange and explicit recording disclosure
A durable call transcript/result receipt tied to the job, with sensitive-data retention controls

args.user_asks: I'm away from my desk. Look at the thing open on my Mac, explain what it is in one sentence, and if it is broken, repair it and tell me exactly what changed.
args.why_useful: This makes the worn pendant a remote pair of eyes and hands rather than merely a command microphone. It combines current-screen perception, terminal/browser action, and a concise spoken explanation, allowing the owner to recover from a stuck app or broken development task without returning to the Mac.
args.model_tier: gpt-4.1-mini for rapid screenshots and UI grounding; gpt-5.6-luna for diagnosis, repair planning, and change summary; realtime relay only for the conversation.
args.latency_budget: First spoken diagnosis within 5 seconds; repair may run asynchronously with a completion alert.
args.cost_estimate: $0.02-$0.15 per investigation depending on screenshot count and shell output; vision calls dominate.
args.security_concerns: Screenshots may contain passwords, private messages, or source code. The Mac agent must redact known secrets before sending frames, keep raw screenshots ephemeral, and report every mutation. The owner has approved broad access, but a physical stop and truthful failed-state report remain essential.
missing: Re-enable and expose the currently disabled computer-use/vision loop
A relay-visible screenshot and incremental observation stream rather than only a final Mac job result
Structured before/after file, app, and process diffs for an honest change report
A pendant interrupt that cancels an in-flight repair, not merely shortens speech

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 7 of 8 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /vision-loop/plan. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: Find the answer in my private Mac, browser, or phone data, and say the answer plus where you found it; if the sources disagree, ask me instead of guessing.
args.why_useful: The owner gets a trustworthy spoken answer while away, grounded in the private surfaces that public search cannot reach. The source disagreement behavior is more valuable than a generic assistant answer for questions like dates, commitments, account status, or the latest version of a document.
args.model_tier: Cheap retrieval and ranking first; gpt-5.6-luna only to reconcile evidence and formulate the short spoken answer; realtime relay handles follow-up clarification.
args.latency_budget: First answer in 3-8 seconds for indexed data; live browser/iPhone checks may take up to 20 seconds and should stream a brief progress cue.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01-$0.08 per query; embedding/search is cheap, while live browser or iPhone inspection and reconciliation dominate.
args.security_concerns: Private mail, notes, browser pages, and phone content must not be mixed into unrelated prompts or persisted as broad memories. Return source labels and timestamps, retain only the answer provenance, and require the owner to explicitly name a sensitive surface when appropriate.
missing: A unified cross-surface retrieval API over Mac files/mail/calendar, authenticated browser sessions, and mirrored iPhone state
Freshness metadata and conflict detection across results rather than selecting the highest-scoring snippet
A spoken provenance format that remains understandable in one sentence
Live-turn wiring of the existing scoped memory projection so stable preferences and task context are not resent as legacy blocks
