transcript.text: I’ll check what’s available now, then I’ll suggest concrete next capabilities and call out anything missing.

args.user_asks: Keep working on that after I walk away, and tell me what happened when it finishes.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful thing: the owner can start a task while speaking, then stop listening and still get a clear outcome without babysitting a screen.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the initial voice intent; a cheaper background tier for monitoring and summarizing while the owner is away.
args.latency_budget: Fast handoff (sub-second) to start the task; completion alert can arrive seconds to hours later.
args.cost_estimate: Low per check if polling is batched; biggest cost is keeping job context and producing a good spoken summary when it ends.
args.security_concerns: Alerts must be truthful and derived from job status, not guesswork. Anything that can send messages to a device should include authentication and avoid leaking sensitive task details in spoken form.
missing: A real completion-event delivery mechanism tied to GET /jobs/:jobId
A durable watch/notification path for pendant and phone targets
A policy for when to summarize details vs. only state

args.user_asks: If I lose my connection, save what I was trying to do and resume it when I’m back online.
args.why_useful: This makes the system feel reliable. The owner doesn’t have to re-say or re-issue commands after a drop; work resumes when the Mac or browser becomes available.
args.model_tier: Realtime to capture the intent; background tier to resume when connectivity returns.
args.latency_budget: Capture should be instant. Resume can wait for the next availability event.
args.cost_estimate: Mostly storage and reconciliation; compute is small, dominated by retries and idempotency checks.
args.security_concerns: Must not replay destructive actions without explicit confirmation. Needs idempotency keys and a safe checkpoint before irreversible steps.
missing: A cross-surface command ledger with idempotency and replay protection
Connectivity-change triggers and a resume policy
A way to serialize intent safely for later execution

args.user_asks: Tell me what’s going on with my devices right now.
args.why_useful: The owner can quickly understand whether the pendant, Mac bridge, and browser are online, and what’s available for action.
args.model_tier: Realtime voice response; no need for a heavy planner.
args.latency_budget: Under a second if status is cached or locally available; otherwise a quick relay lookup.
args.cost_estimate: Small; the dominant cost is any live status probes.
args.security_concerns: Status should avoid exposing sensitive identifiers; only report availability and basic health.
missing: A stable device status endpoint for relay to read without guessing paths
A consistent vocabulary for state (online/offline/stale/unknown) across surfaces

args.user_asks: If I say “save this for the project” while looking at a logged-in web page, have the pendant capture the page I mean, ask only if there are multiple plausible targets, and produce a durable project note on my Mac with the source URL, title, timestamp, and a short spoken confirmation—even if I walk away before it finishes.
args.why_useful: Today the owner must manually bridge the pendant, authenticated browser, and Mac. This turns a fleeting spoken reference into a traceable artifact without making them repeat URLs or stay near the laptop.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for intent and one clarification; background mac-planner for extraction, filing, and receipt generation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 1 s; clarification within 3 s; complete in under 30 s when browser and Mac are online. Queue the result for later pendant playback if the owner leaves.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per invocation depending on page extraction and planner turns; browser/Mac execution dominates latency, not speech.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and the resulting note leave the browser/Mac only through the existing relay job path. Never read arbitrary tabs without a target match; include URL and capture time in the receipt. Creating the note is reversible, but sending or sharing it must remain a separate explicit action.
missing: A cross-surface target-resolution operation that can inspect the active browser tab and current Mac project context, rank candidates, and ask one spoken disambiguation question.
A durable artifact writer that stores source provenance and links it to the relay job receipt.
A live wiring of the context projection into conversationContext.js so the relay knows project/editor preferences without resending legacy memory.

args.user_asks: Give me a “panic button” phrase or two-press gesture that immediately locks my Mac, pauses active browser sessions, and tells me on the pendant exactly which protections succeeded or failed.
args.why_useful: When the owner is away from the laptop, they currently cannot reliably contain an exposed or unattended session from the one device they are wearing. A single spoken/physical emergency action would reduce the time from noticing risk to containment.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for recognition and status; deterministic Mac/browser action broker for containment; no expensive model after the command is classified.
args.latency_budget: Begin containment within 1 s, report first results within 5 s, and continue collecting receipts asynchronously. The pendant must announce partial failure rather than claiming success.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per event; dominated by Mac wake/link latency. No browser-model inference is needed for the fixed sequence.
args.security_concerns: This is intentionally high impact and must require a deliberate physical gesture or a pre-enrolled spoken phrase plus a current pendant session nonce. It should lock, not shut down or delete data. Browser session pausing must be scoped to the owner's registered browser, and every action needs an immutable success/failure receipt.
missing: A firmware/relay emergency command path that survives an ordinary voice-turn timeout and cannot be confused with normal dictation.
A Mac action for lock-screen and a browser action for revoking/pausing registered sessions, with idempotent execution and per-step receipts.
A prioritized alert delivery path that can distinguish complete, partial, and failed containment and surface it through the existing pendant inbox.

args.user_asks: Let me say “what am I looking at?” and have the pendant answer with a compact, confidence-ranked explanation assembled from the active Mac window, the selected text, and the current browser page—then let me say “that one” to act on the exact item it just described.
args.why_useful: The owner is often away from the screen or cannot comfortably read it while wearing the pendant. Today the available computer-use pieces do not preserve a shared referent between perception, spoken explanation, and a follow-up action.
args.model_tier: gpt-4.1-mini vision loop for screenshot/OCR grounding; realtime relay only handles the two short turns; mac-planner executes the confirmed follow-up.
args.latency_budget: Return a 1–2 sentence description in 3 s; retain the ranked referents for 60 s; execute “that one” in under 5 s.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per inspection depending on screenshot/OCR size; follow-up actions are cheap. The dominant cost is image tokens.
args.security_concerns: Screenshots may contain private data and must remain scoped to the active window or explicitly selected tab. Do not infer sensitive content aloud unless requested. The follow-up must use the exact referent ID from the inspection receipt, not a fresh guess.
missing: A currently enabled Mac vision/computer-use loop with a stable screenshot/OCR endpoint and referent IDs.
A short-lived cross-turn referent store shared by relay and Mac agents, including expiry and confidence.
A voice-turn resolver that maps pronouns such as “that one” to the prior referent and rejects stale or ambiguous IDs.

args.user_asks: Answer “what changed because of me today?” with a spoken, trustworthy digest of every Mac and browser mutation made through the hive, grouped by task, with the exact app/site and a one-word status; let me say “undo the last one” to reverse only a reversible change.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has to inspect scattered job records and cannot tell whether a spoken request caused one change, several partial changes, or none. A concise end-of-day accountability view makes automation safe enough to trust when the owner was away.
args.model_tier: Cheaper background summarizer over structured receipts; realtime relay only resolves the time range and the selected receipt for undo.
args.latency_budget: Digest in under 5 s from cached receipts; undo acknowledgement in 1 s and completion within 10 s.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.02 per digest; receipt retrieval and compact summarization dominate.
args.security_concerns: Only include actions attributable to this owner and this pendant/session. Never summarize page contents by default, only metadata and declared action results. Undo must target a receipt ID, be idempotent, and refuse if state has diverged.
missing: A unified immutable mutation ledger joining Mac, browser, and relay receipts with actor, target, before/after summary, and reversibility.
A receipt query and spoken grouping endpoint; current job receipts are per-job rather than a cross-surface audit view.

transcript.text:
Recorded four proposals:

1. **Cross-surface action explanations** — ask “Why did you do that?” and receive the evidence, reasoning, result, uncertainty, and possible undo.
2. **Mid-flight plan editing** — interrupt a running Mac/browser/iOS workflow, change one step, and resume from a durable checkpoint.
3. **Per-turn private mode** — execute one request without retaining audio, transcript, screenshots, browser findings, journals, or memory.
4. **USB-local pendant operating mode** — use the physically connected nRF9160 and ESP32 as a real voice endpoint today, even without LTE registration.

What still needs to change:

- A causal receipt format joining utterance, context, plan, evidence, actions, and resulting state.
- Cooperative cancellation, checkpoints, idempotency, and replay-safe suffix execution across downstream agents.
- A retention lease propagated through every storage-producing surface, with post-turn verification.
- A signed USB serial bridge and relay transport that distinguishes USB-local sessions from LTE sessions.
- Persistent session identity and health reporting shared by both transport modes.
Okay, I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll point out the gaps that still need wiring or access.

result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

args.user_asks: When I say “fill this out from my voice,” have the pendant capture a structured answer, the relay validate and normalize it, and my Mac’s authenticated browser fill the current form field-by-field, read back a compact receipt of every value and leave the form unsent until I explicitly say “submit.”

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

args.user_asks: Be my eyes for what’s happening on my Mac and tell me only the important changes while I’m away.
args.why_useful: This is the kind of thing only a multi-surface assistant can do: the Mac can observe and summarize, the relay can speak it, and the pendant makes it effortless to receive. It cuts down on constant checking and helps the owner focus.
args.model_tier: Mac planner/observation loop for change detection and summarization; relay only for low-latency delivery.
args.latency_budget: Observation runs in the background; spoken delivery should be under a second once an alert is ready.
args.cost_estimate: Most cost sits on the Mac observation and summarization. Relay cost is a short spoken delivery.

args.user_asks: If I say “undo that” right after a remote action, reverse the last change on my Mac or in the browser—even if I am no longer looking at the screen—and tell me exactly what was restored and what cannot be undone.
